items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: The credit for construction of not only temples but also the carving styles of sculpture goes to which of the below mentioned dynasties?
items.x: The Pallavas pioneered structural and rock-cut temples (Mahabalipuram rathas, Shore Temple, Kailasanatha) and a distinct style of carved sculpture (Arjuna's Penance).

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Kokili belongs to which dynasty?
items.x: Kokkili (Kokkili Vikramaditya, 8th c.) was an Eastern Chalukya king of Vengi who briefly succeeded Vishnuvardhana III and was overthrown. He was not a Pallava, Ganga or Chola ruler.

items.s: Gramadevata temples belong to which tradition?
items.x: Gramadevata (village goddess) shrines belong to the Shakta (Sakteya) tradition of mother-goddess worship.

items.src: Asst. B.C. Welfare Officer, Asst. Social Welfare Officer & A
items.s: Who was conferred the title Gandharva-vidya-visarada in the Chalukyan Court?
items.x: Chellavva, court singer and dancer of Chalukya Bhima I, received the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada and the village Attili.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which religious sect enjoyed great popularity under eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
items.x: Saivism dominated under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: kings built Shiva temples (Biccavolu, Draksharama), and Buddharamas became Saiva shrines. Jainism and Buddhism declined.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: Which one of the following religions was not prevalent at the time of Chalukayas?
items.x: Hinduism (Saivism, Vaishnavism), Buddhism and Jainism all existed under the Chalukyas, but Judaism had no place in their realm. So Judaism was the religion not prevalent.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien

items.x: Nedumbi Basadi was a Jain basadi built at Bezawada (Vijayawada) by Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of the Eastern Chalukya Kubja Vishnuvardhana, so it is in Andhra Pradesh.

items.s: What were the Ashtadasha Tirthas in the Eastern Chalukya administration of Vengi?
items.x: The Ashtadasha Tirthas were the 18 departments; the Yuvaraja was a partner in governance and councils were called Varagoshti.

items.s: What were the councils of the Eastern Chalukya administration called?
items.x: The Eastern Chalukyas had 18 departments (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and councils called Varagoshti.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20

items.x: The Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama, built by Chalukya Bhima I, is a Shiva temple (one of the Pancharamas).

items.x: Chalukya Bhima I, who fought 360 battles, is said to have built 360 temples including the Pancharamas and the Bhimeswara temples.

items.x: The Bhimeswara temple of Draksharama (Dakshina Kasi) was built by Chalukya Bhima I; Ganga Mahadevi only added a mandapa later.

items.x: Chalukya Bhima I founded the Pancharama tradition of five Shiva temples (Draksharama, Kumararama, Somarama, Ksheerarama, Amararama).

items.x: The Bhimeswara temples on the Godavari (Draksharama, Samalkot) were built by Chalukya Bhima I ('Chalukya-I' = Chalukya Bhima I). items.x: The Ambapuram and Adavi Nekkalam hills north-east of Vijayawada hold rock-cut Jain caves (7th–8th century, Eastern Chalukya period), including the Ambapuram cave temple with Mahavira.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s:
Which of the following statements about Durjayas of Velanadu is/are correct?

A. They supported the Chalukya-Chola dynasty after the decline of Eastern Chalukyas.

B. They belonged to the 'Chaturthanvya' or the fourth caste, i.e., the Sudras.
items.x: Both are correct: the Velanati Durjaya chiefs were loyal feudatories of the Chalukya-Cholas after the Eastern Chalukya decline, and they called themselves Chaturthanvaya (fourth-caste, i.e. Sudra) lineage.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: The combined forces of the rulers Velanadu, Giripaschima, Konakandravada joined hands with Kulottunga II and defeated the Western Chalukyas in the
items.x: Vikrama Chola sent his son Kulottunga II to Vengi; the Velanati Chodas and other chiefs (Giripaschima, Konakandravadi) joined him and drove out the Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas in the battle of Manneru, ending their occupation of Vengi (c. 1135).

items.s: Who formed the slave society in Andhra?
items.x: Brahma Naidu of Palnadu formed the Dasa Samajam (Chapa Koodu), with inter-caste dining.

items.x: Brahma Naidu of Palnadu, founder of the Chapa Koodu (Dasa Samaj), opened the Chennakesava temple at Macherla to all.

items.s: During whose times did local self government institutions flourish in South India?
items.x: Village self-government (ur, sabha, nagaram, the Uttaramerur inscriptions) flourished under the Cholas; the Cheras, Pandyas and Kakatiyas are not known for it.

Rudramadevi (reign 1262-1289) is one of the most prominent Kakatiya rulers. Her inscriptions call her 'Rudradeva Maharaja', in the male form, which shows she was accepted as a full sovereign, so R explains A.

items.x: Rudrama Devi's sons-in-law were Mahadeva (Mummadamma's husband, father of Prataparudra), Annayadeva (Annayamatya) and the Chalukya Ellanadeva. Prasaditya Nayaka was her Recherla general and protector, not a son-in-law.

items.x: Ganapati Deva had no son, so his daughter Rudramba (Rudrama Devi) succeeded him in 1262 despite opposition from many nobles.

items.x: Prataparudra (II) faced the first invasion of Warangal sent by Alauddin Khalji in 1303; his generals defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna at Upparapalli. Ganapati and Rudrama ruled earlier. (Moved to the Kakatiya row.)

items.x: Siddhanta Shikhamani (Veera Saiva Siddhanta Shikhamani) of Shivayogi Shivacharya is regarded as the complete and standard scripture of Veerashaivism; Basava Puranam is a biography of Basava, not the doctrinal text.

items.x: C and D hold: Uddandarayunipalem (Amaravati) bears the name of Uddanda Raya, and Rudramba (Rudramadevi) of the Kakatiyas was a devotee of Shiva. Amuktamalyada is a Vaishnava Telugu poem of Krishnadevaraya, not a Buddhist discourse, and Kalachakra is a Buddhist tantra, not linked to Harihara Raya. (Moved: Andhra history.)

items.s: The temple at Arasavalli is dedicated to which deity?
items.x: Arasavalli is famous for its Surya (Sun) temple.

items.s: Which was the popular religion during the time of the Reddy Rajas?
items.x: Veerashaivism was the popular religion of the Reddy period; the Reddi kings also patronised Pasupata Shaivism, but Veerashaivam predominated.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: 'Perantaallu' means
o: A sati practice in Kakatiya period
An evil social practice of Telugu Choda times
Women who committed sati were elevated to the status of demi goddesses and were worshipped as perantallu during the rule of Reddis in Andhra
Inviting women by applying Kumkuma to the religious ceremonies
items.x: In Reddi-period Andhra women who died as sati were deified and worshipped as Perantallu (Parantas, local deities); this was not a Kakatiya or Telugu Choda practice, nor the kumkum invitation custom.

items.s: Who among the following poets adorned the court of Pedakomati Vemareddy?
items.x: Srinatha served at Kondaveedu as Vidyadhikari in the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy. Potana did not seek royal patrons, and Tikkana and Bhimakavi belong to earlier courts.

items.s: Which of the following books was not written by Srinatha?
items.x: Madanavilasabanam is not Srinatha's (it is credited to Naganatha); Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam and Palnati Veera Charitra are his works.

items.src: Asst. B.C. Welfare Officer, Asst. Social Welfare Officer & A
items.s: The poet who gave a graphic description of the socio-economic life of the Palnadu people was
items.x: Srinatha wrote Palnati Veera Charitra, describing the life of the Palnadu people.

items.s: At whose court did Srinatha serve as Vidyadhikari (education minister)?
items.x: Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at the Kondaveedu court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and wrote the king's Sanskrit inscriptions. Under Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry he wrote Bhimakhandam and Kasikhandam; at Devaraya II's court he won the title Kavi Sarvabhauma; Sarvajna Singabhupala is linked with Potana's refusal of patronage.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajahmundry — Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya
items.x: After Kondaveedu fell in 1424, Srinatha went to Rajahmundry under Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya. The other pairs confuse patrons or places.

items.s: Which statement about Srinatha is correct?
o: He pioneered the Prabandha style, and his age is known as the Kavya Yuga.
He founded the Tallapaka tradition of sankirtana.
He was the composer of the Pancharatna Kritis.
He was the first Telugu woman poet and composed Bhogini Dandakam.
items.x: Srinatha is regarded as a pioneer of the Prabandha style, and his period is called the Kavya Yuga. The other statements refer to different literary or musical figures.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Srinatha's works and their dedications?
items.x: Sringara Naishadhamu was dedicated to the minister Mamidi, or Madiki, Singana. Haravilasamu was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, while Sivaratri Mahatmyam was dedicated to Mummadi Santayya.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Srinatha's Haravilasamu?
o: It was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti
It is chiefly a source on the military organisation of the Vijayanagara Empire
It describes Reddi-period sea trade, including imports and exports
items.x: Haravilasamu, dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, is valued as a source on Reddi-period sea trade, imports and exports, not on Vijayanagara military organisation.

items.s: After the fall of Rajahmundry, Srinatha's chatu verses chiefly portrayed which condition?
o: The maritime wealth of Avachi Tippaya Setti
The religious debates at the Vijayanagara court
The prosperity of the Gajapati court
The hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu
items.x: After Rajahmundry fell in 1448, Srinatha lived in poverty in Palnadu. His chatu verses provide a literary picture of its hardship and coarse food.

items.s: At whose court did Srinatha receive the title Kavi Sarvabhauma?
items.x: At Vijayanagara Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta before Devaraya II and won Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

items.s: In which year was the Palnadu war, the subject of the dvipada ballad Palnati Veera Charitra, fought?
items.x: Palnati Veera Charitra describes the Palnadu war of 1182.

items.s: In which year did Kondaveedu fall, after which Srinatha moved to the Rajahmundry court?
items.x: Kondaveedu fell in 1424 and Srinatha went to Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry; Rajahmundry itself fell in 1448.

items.s: Which of the following works is NOT by Srinatha?
items.x: Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam and Palnati Veera Charitra are credited to Srinatha; the APPSC Group 2 Mains 2025 key made Madanavilasa Bhanam the 'not by Srinatha' answer.

items.s: To whom did Srinatha dedicate Sringara Naishadhamu?
items.x: Sringara Naishadhamu went to minister Mamidi (Madiki) Singana; Haravilasamu to Avachi Tippaya Setti and Sivaratri Mahatmyam to Mummadi Santayya.

items.s: Who among the following made the first reference to paper as a writing material in Andhra?
items.x: Srinatha's writings give the first reference to paper as writing material in Andhra.

items.s: Whom did Srinatha defeat in a literary debate at the court of Devaraya II?
items.x: At Devaraya II's court in Vijayanagara, Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta, was given Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

items.s: Who among the following Telugu poets was honoured with Kanakabhishekam at the court of Devaraya II?
items.x: After defeating Gauda Dindima Bhatta at Devaraya II's court, Srinatha received Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

items.s: At whose court in Rajahmundry did Srinatha write Bhimakhandamu and Kasikhandamu?
items.x: After Kondaveedu fell in 1424, Srinatha moved to the Rajahmundry court of Veerabhadra Reddy, where he wrote Bhimakhandamu and Kasikhandamu.

items.s: Who led the confederacy of the post-Kakatiya liberation movement?
items.x: Prolaya Nayaka led the post-Kakatiya liberation confederacy.

items.s: Anantavarman Chodaganga belonged to which of the following provincial kingdom?
items.x: Anantavarman Chodaganga (1078-1147) was the Eastern Ganga king of Kalinga (Orissa) who began the Jagannath temple at Puri.

items.s: Who succeeded Yudhishtira to the throne?
items.x: In the Mahabharata Yudhishthira crowned Parikshit, Abhimanyu's son, before going on his last journey; Janamejaya was Parikshit's son.

items.x: Nannaya Bhatta's Andhra Mahabharatam (11th century, Rajaraja Narendra's court) is the earliest extant work of Telugu literature; the other works are of the 15th–16th centuries.

items.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Rajputs of 8th to 14th Centuries :

A. The term Rajput is derived from "Rajaputra", meaning the son of a ruler.

B. They were a group of warriors who claimed Kshatriya caste status.
The correct statements are
items.x: 'Rajput' comes from 'Rajaputra' (son of a ruler), and the Rajputs were warrior lineages claiming Kshatriya status, so both are true. Moved.

items.s: Which scholar came to India with Mahmud Ghazni –
items.x: Al-Biruni of Khwarizm came with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind). Ibn Battuta came under Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Khusrau and Ferishta were later writers.

items.s:
What is the sequence of arrival of these travellers?
1. Ibn Battuta
2. Tavernier
3. Al-Biruni
4. Manucci
items.x: Al-Biruni (with Mahmud, early 11th c.) → Ibn Battuta (1333) → Tavernier (from 1640s) → Manucci (1656). So 3, 1, 2, 4.

items.s: Who devastated Chola dynasty eventually?
items.x:
Most books and keys: Malik Kafur. Strictly the Chola line had already ended in 1279 under the Pandyas; Kafur's 1311 raid struck the Pandyas of Madurai.
Books key Malik Kafur, whose 1311 southern raid devastated the far south; Bakhtiyar Khalji worked in Bihar-Bengal and Mahmud and Ghori never reached the Tamil country.

items.s: Royal palace consisting of thousand pillars was constructed by the following ruler
items.x: The royal palace of a thousand pillars (Qasr-i-Hazar Sutun, at Siri) was built by Alauddin Khalji. The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda is a Kakatiya temple (Rudradeva), not Ganapati Deva's palace. (Moved to the Khalji row.)

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A

Taxes collected on Agriculture by rulers
Export of Spices, textiles and Indigo from Delhi

items.s: Who founded the Bahmani Empire?
items.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

items.x: Ala-ud-din Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu, Zafar Khan), a Tughlaq officer, revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347; Alauddin Khilji was a Delhi Sultan and Mujahid Shah a later Bahmani. (Moved to the Bahmani row.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

R is true: named design varieties (NextGen lists 'Farishkani' and 'Ashunkhani'; the exam lists Bulbandi, Nabashkhany, Gopalraokhany) were made in Andhra.

items.s: How was Bhakta Ramadasu related to Madanna and Akkanna?
items.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.

items.s: Which Golconda ruler granted the village of Kuchipudi to its dancers?
items.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah granted Kuchipudi village to the dancers of the form that grew under Siddhendra Yogi. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Char Minar and was the first Urdu poet with a diwan; Abdullah Qutb Shah's era is called the Golden Age of Urdu; Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah is a distractor.

items.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, with whom is the growth of Kuchipudi associated?
items.x: Kuchipudi's growth is associated with Siddhendra Yogi; Persian was the official language and Telugu the people's language.

items.s: What was the philosophy of Vidyaranya Swamy?
items.x: Vidyaranya, the Sringeri pontiff who blessed Harihara and Bukka, was an Advaita philosopher (Jivanmukti Viveka). (Moved: foundation of Vijayanagara.)

items.s: The fortress of Vijayanagara was located on the bank of the river
items.x: Vijayanagara (Hampi) stood on the south bank of the Tungabhadra.

items.s: Who wrote Madhuravijayam?
items.x: Madhuravijayam is by Gangadevi; Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam.

items.s: During the time of Sri Krishna Devaraya
items.x: Krishnadevaraya (1509-29) was a contemporary of Babur, who won at Panipat in 1526. Akbar came later; Firoz Tughlaq and Alauddin Khalji were 14th-century Sultans.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: ____ founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his mother.
items.x: Krishnadevaraya founded Nagalapuram near Vijayanagara in honour of his mother Nagala Devi. The other options are not Vijayanagara kings.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Who wrote 'Amuktamalyada'?
items.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya wrote the Telugu Amuktamalyada (Vishnuchittiyam). Devaraya II wrote the Sanskrit Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Pothana wrote the Telugu Bhagavatam.

items.s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva dynasty?
items.x: Vira (Veera) Narasimha, son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1505 after killing Immadi Narasimha. Krishnadevaraya and Achyutaraya were his younger brothers; Vidyaranya was a sage.

items.s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva Dynasty?
items.x: Vira (Veera) Narasimha, son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1505 after killing Immadi Narasimha. Krishnadevaraya and Achyutaraya were his younger brothers; Vidyaranya was a sage.

items.s: Timmarasu was the minister to
items.x: Saluva Timmarasu (Appaji) was the prime minister of Krishnadevaraya. Rajaraja Narendra was an Eastern Chalukya king, Kataya Vema a Reddi, and Saluva Narasimha an earlier king.

items.s: Who is the author of Jaimini Bharatham?
items.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu, a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha. Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam; Jaimini Maharshi is the sage of the original story.

items.s: Who is the author of "Jaimini Bharatam"?
items.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu, a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha. Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam; Jaimini Maharshi is the sage of the original story.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Which of the Kingdoms was defeated by Sri Krishnadevaraya and Coastal Andhra and Odisha were annexed from that Kingdom?
items.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated the Gajapati king Prataparudra of Odisha and took coastal Andhra up to Simhachalam. The Hoysalas, Chalukyas and Kakatiyas had long ended.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20

items.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya ('establisher of the Yavana kingdom') for restoring the Bahmani Sultan. Kulottunga and the Gonka rajas are earlier dynasties.

items.x: Krishnadevaraya took the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya ('establisher of the Yavana kingdom') for restoring the Bahmani Sultan. Kulottunga and the Gonka rajas are earlier dynasties.

items.s: In the following which Telugu work describes the daily life of Krishna Devaraya?
items.x: Rayavachakam, a Telugu prose work by Sthanapati, describes Krishnadevaraya's court and daily life. Manucharitra is Peddana's poem and Amuktamalyada is the king's own work.

items.s: Krishnadevaraya was a contemporary of whom?
items.x: Krishnadevaraya (1509-29) was a contemporary of Babur (Panipat 1526), who praised him in the Baburnama; Firoz Tughlaq and Alauddin were 14th-century, Akbar later.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s:
Read the given statements of
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) carefully and select the correct option.
(A): Telugu language is believed to have become a prominent literary language during the Vijayanagara Empire.
(R): The Vijayanagara ruler's patronage encouraged the development of Telugu literature, leading to the creation of many significant classical works in Telugu.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.x: Both true and linked: Telugu reached its classical peak (the Prabandha age) under Vijayanagara, because rulers such as Krishnadevaraya – himself author of Amuktamalyada – patronised the Ashtadiggajas.

items.s: The president of the imperial council of the empire of Vijayanagar was:
items.x: The Vijayanagara council of ministers that advised the Raya was presided over by the Sabhanayaka; the king was not its president, and the Pradhani/Mahapradhana and Mahadandanayaka were members.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagar Empire.

I. Vijaynagar was noted for its markets dealing in spices, textiles and precious stones.

II. Krishnadeva Raya’s rule was characterised by the strain within the imperial structure.

III. The amara-nayakas were military commanders who were given territories to be governed by the Rayas.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
items.x: I and III: Vijayanagara's markets dealt in spices, textiles and precious stones, and the amara-nayakas were military commanders given territories by the Rayas. II is wrong – Krishnadeva Raya's reign was one of expansion and consolidation; strain came after him (NCERT).

items.s:
Regarding the taxation system of Krishna Devaraya, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements:

A. The tax rate on land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.

B. Private owners of workshops paid an industries tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Both are correct: Krishnadevaraya's land tax varied with the quality of land, and private owners of workshops paid an industries tax (UPSC 2016 key: both). (Moved: Vijayanagara administration and revenue, book 1 row 121.)

items.s: The crop known to people of Vijayanagara Empire is:
items.x: Coconut is native to the Indian coasts and was grown in Vijayanagara times; groundnut, tobacco and red chilli are American crops brought later by the Portuguese. (Moved: Vijayanagara economy.)

items.s: Whose help did Vijayanagaradhisas take in the construction of dams?
items.x: Nuniz records that a Portuguese engineer helped Krishnadevaraya build the great tank (dam) near the capital, so the Vijayanagara kings took Portuguese help. (Moved to Vijayanagara.)

items.s: Who wrote 'A Forgotten Empire' on Vijayanagara?
items.x: 'A Forgotten Empire' on Vijayanagara was written by Robert Sewell.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Who built the Balakrishna Temple in Hampi?
items.x: Krishnadevaraya brought the Balakrishna idol from Udayagiri fort (1513) and built the Balakrishna temple at Hampi to house it. Narasa Nayaka, Devaraya II and Tirumala Raya did not.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III ANM/Ward Health Secreta
items.s: Which Ruler of Vijayanagar had built the Hajara Ram Temple?
items.x:
Most books and keys: Krishnadevaraya. Strictly: the temple was begun in the early 15th century under Devaraya I (Wikipedia, Hampi inscriptions) and enlarged later; the printed key gives Devaraya II.
Most books and the NextGen notes credit the Hazara Rama temple at Hampi to Krishnadevaraya, so he is keyed; the printed key Devaraya II is not supported by the sources. Harihara II and Venkata II did not build it.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: Hazara Ramaswamy temple was built by
items.x: The Hazara Rama temple at Hampi (Vijayanagara) was built by Sri Krishnadevaraya. Venkata (Aravidu), Sri Ranga and Lingama Nayaka are not its builders.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: 'Lavani' Dance is from the state of
items.x: Lavani is the folk dance-song form of Maharashtra (with the dholki), often part of Tamasha folk theatre – a culture fact, not geography.

items.s: Hathras and Kanpur traditions relate to
items.x: Hathras and Kanpur are the two schools of Nautanki, a folk theatre of Uttar Pradesh, so theatre.

items.s: With which of the following areas of Rajasthan the Alibaksh Khyal is associated?
items.x: Ali Bakhshi khyal was founded by Ali Bakhsh of Mandawar in the Alwar state, so Alwar.

items.s: Mohiniattam is the classical dance form from:
items.x: Mohiniyattam is the classical dance of Kerala.

items.s: Who wrote 'Abhinava Darpanam'?
items.x: Abhinaya Darpanam, the Sanskrit treatise on gesture in dance, is by Nandikeshvara. Bharata wrote the Natyashastra and Jayapa Senani the Nritta Ratnavali; Vidyaranya was the Sringeri sage of Vijayanagara.

items.s: Who is the father of Kathak?
items.x: Of the names given, only Pandit Birju Maharaj (Lucknow gharana) is a Kathak dancer and he is widely called the face or father of modern Kathak; Rajan Mishra and Jasraj were vocalists.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: "Tamasha" performance belongs to which state?
items.x: Tamasha is the traditional folk theatre of Maharashtra (Lavani-based).

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies

items.x: Giddha is a women's folk dance of Punjab, not Gujarat, so that pair is wrong. A folk-dance item, moved.

items.s: Out of the following, which tribal religious festival was declared as a State festival during 2016?
o: Sri Sri Sri Modakondamma Talli Jatara
Sri Sri Sri Talupulamma Talli Jatara
Sri Sri Sri Tirupatamma Talli Jatara
Sri Sri Sri Mavullamma Talli Jatara
items.x: The keyed answer: the Modakondamma Talli Jatara of Paderu (tribal festival) was declared a state festival in 2016. (Moved to the AP festivals row.)

items.s: In which of these cities Kumbh mela is celebrated?
items.x: The Kumbh Mela is held at Prayagraj (Allahabad), Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik; of the options only Allahabad. Off-topic here.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: The Jamdani 'Sari' style is one of the Geographical indications from Andhra Pradesh
items.x: Uppada (East Godavari coast) is famous for its Jamdani silk sarees, a GI product of Andhra Pradesh.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III ANM/Ward Health Secreta
items.s: Sangidiraallu, a sport which involved balancing stones is identified with which of the following areas of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: The printed key links the stone-lifting sport Sangidi rallu with Vizianagaram, known for village weightlifters (Konda Velagada); no library source covers it.

items.s: In which of these months Onam is celebrated?
items.x: Onam, Kerala's harvest festival, falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam, i.e. August–September.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: In which one of the following Districts of Andhra Pradesh, "Butta Bommalu"- famous handicrafts is available?
o: East Godavari and West Godavari districts
items.x: Butta Bommalu (light wooden toys) are made at Tanuku, West Godavari – the Godavari districts.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: The famous Bargarh Dhanu Jatra (Yatra) is celebrated in the state of
items.x: Bargarh Dhanu Jatra, an open-air theatre festival on Krishna and Kansa, is held every year in Bargarh, western Odisha.

items.s: Simhachala Narasimha Swamy is worshipped with Sandal wood paste on this day.
items.x: At Simhachalam, the deity's sandal paste is removed for Nijaroopa darshan and fresh sandalwood paste applied during Chandanotsavam on Akshaya Tritiya (Vaisakha Shuddha Tadiya).

items.s: For what is Uppada on the Andhra coast known?
items.x: Uppada is known for Jamdani silk sarees; Kalamkari is Machilipatnam's and salt Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam's.

items.s: Which of the following pairs (centre - product) is correctly matched?
items.x: Machilipatnam is known for Kalamkari; Uppada for Jamdani and Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam for salt.

items.s: Vijayanagara kingdom completely disappeared with this battle
items.x: After Talikota (1565) the Aravidus survived at Penugonda and Chandragiri; the civil-war Battle of Toppur (Topuru, 1616) broke up what was left, after which the empire disintegrated completely. Penugonda and Chandragiri were capitals, not the decisive battles.

items.s: In 1565 the Vijayanagar empire fell as a result of the war
items.x: The Vijayanagara empire's power was broken at the Battle of Tallikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565, by the Deccan Sultans; the capital then moved to Penugonda.

items.s: In the year 1565 the battle of Tallikota was fought between them?
o: The kings of Vijayanagara and the Sultanate of Golconda
Vijayanagar kings and Kondaveeti Reddy kings
Deccan Sultans and Kondaveeti Reddy Kings
items.x: Tallikota (1565) was fought between Vijayanagara under Rama Raya and the combined Deccan Sultans (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) – not Golconda alone and not the Kondaveedu Reddis, who had gone long before.

items.s: The Sufi saint of Naqshbandiya order, Ubaidullah Ahrar was followed by which among the following Mughal Emperor?
items.x: Babur was a follower of the Naqshbandi saint Khwaja Ubaidullah Ahrar; the order came to India with him.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor wrote his own autobiography?
items.x: Babur wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in Turki; Akbar, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb did not write autobiographies.

items.s: In which language was the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama) written?
items.x: The Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish; Persian was the Mughal court language.

items.s: Of which origin was the Rumi method of warfare used by Babur?
items.x: The Rumi method (carts linked as a barrier for matchlockmen and artillery) was Ottoman; Tulughma was Uzbek.

items.s: Where did Babur build the Kabuli Bagh Mosque to commemorate his 1526 victory?
items.x: The Kabuli Bagh Mosque is at Panipat and marks the 1526 victory; Ram Bagh was at Agra.

items.s: Which inviter of Babur was the Governor of Punjab?
items.x: Daulat Khan Lodi, Governor of Punjab, invited Babur along with Alam Khan and Rana Sanga.

items.s: What was Alam Khan, one of those who invited Babur, to Ibrahim Lodi?
items.x: Alam Khan was Ibrahim Lodi's uncle; Daulat Khan Lodi was the Governor of Punjab.

items.s: Of which origin was Babur's tulughma tactic, in which flanks wheel round to encircle the enemy?
items.x: Tulughma was Uzbek; the Rumi (araba) method was Ottoman.

items.s: Which cities did Babur occupy after the First Battle of Panipat?
items.x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.

items.s: In which year did Babur take the title 'Padshah' at Kabul?
items.x: Babur became Padshah at Kabul in 1507 and took the title Ghazi after Khanwa in 1527.

items.s: After which battle did Babur take the title 'Ghazi'?
items.x: Babur took the title Ghazi after Khanwa (1527) and the title Padshah at Kabul in 1507.

items.s: During whose reign did the Mughal empire become a political fact and a factor in the life of India, influencing her ever since?
items.x: Under Akbar's long reign (1556-1605) the Mughal empire was consolidated by conquest, mansabdari and Rajput policy and became a lasting political fact in India.

items.s: During Akbar period, land revenue system “ Ain-i- Dahsala” was developed by :
items.x: Raja Todar Mal devised the Ain-i-Dahsala (1580), helped by Khwaja Shah Mansoor and Muzaffar Khan Turbati.

items.s: Who among the following was the connecting link between Sher Shah and Akbar in land revenue administrative measures ?
items.x: Raja Todar Mal served Sher Shah's revenue administration and then devised Akbar's zabt, so he was the link between the two.

items.s: With reference to Mughal period’s revenue collection system, ‘Zabti’ means
items.x:
Most keys: 1/3rd of total yield. Strictly zabt means the measurement-based cash assessment; one-third was the state's share under it.
Zabti assessed revenue on measured land at crop rates, with the state demand fixed at one-third of the average yield, hence the printed key. 'Estimate' describes kankut.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor abolished the Persian Court Custom of ‘Sijda’ which was begun by Balban?
items.x: Shah Jahan abolished the court custom of sijda (prostration) begun by Balban, replacing it with the chahar taslim.

items.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
items.x: Jahangir wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian; Babur's Tuzuk-i-Baburi was in Turki.

items.s: The Mughal Emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was
items.x: Jahangir banned tobacco smoking (1617), as he records in his memoirs; Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb did not.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor Started Hijri Samvat in India by replacing Illahi samvat?
items.x: Shah Jahan gave up Akbar's solar Ilahi era and restored the Hijri (lunar) reckoning for regnal years.

items.s: Which Mughal emperor abolished sijda (prostration before the emperor)?
items.x: Sijda, begun by Balban, was ended by Shah Jahan.

items.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Babur adopted the title Zinda Pir.
Shah Jahan received the title 'Shah Jahan' from Jahangir.
Aurangzeb was known as Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir.
items.x: Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title 'Shah Jahan'. Alamgir and Zinda Pir were associated with Aurangzeb, while Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir was Jahangir's title.

items.s: Which of the following describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
items.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.

items.s: Which Mughal emperor, slightly more orthodox than Akbar, destroyed some newly built temples yet kept many Hindu nobles?
items.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples but continued to employ many Hindu nobles.

items.s: Which traditions does Dara Shikoh's Majma-ul-Bahrain bring together?
items.x: Majma-ul-Bahrain ('mingling of two oceans') compares Sufism and Vedanta.

items.s: Of which text is Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) a Persian translation?
items.x: Sirr-i-Akbar is the Persian Upanishads (1657); the Mahabharata became the Razmnama under Akbar.

items.s: What is the meaning of the title ‘Shah Jahan’?
items.x: Shah Jahan means King of the World, a title Prince Khurram took on his accession. Alamgir means Conqueror of the World, Sakari Saka-conqueror and Devanampiya Beloved of the Gods.

items.s: Which one of the following emperors had the highest number of Hindu Generals in the Mughal army:
items.x: The Hindu share in the nobility was highest under Aurangzeb (about 31.6%, mostly Marathas from the Deccan wars), against about 22.5% under Akbar.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
items.x: Aurangzeb, simple and orthodox in his personal life, was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint).

items.s: Who of the following Mughal Emperor was coronated twice?
items.x: Aurangzeb was crowned twice - at Delhi on 21 July 1658 and again on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

items.s: The Mughal Emperor who appointed the maximum number of Hindu officials was –
items.x: Aurangzeb had the largest number of Hindu officials (about 31.6% of the nobility), mainly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

items.s: Under Aurangzeb's jizya, children below what age were exempted?
items.x: Children below 14 were exempt, along with women, slaves, beggars and the unemployed.

items.s: Under which emperor did the Mughal Empire reach its maximum territorial extent?
items.x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.

items.s: Under which Mughal emperor was the share of Hindu nobles in the nobility the highest?
items.x: Hindu nobles formed about 31.6% under Aurangzeb, against about 22.5% under Akbar.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about Hindu nobles in Mughal service:
1. Their share under Aurangzeb was higher than under Akbar.
2. Most Hindu nobles added under Aurangzeb were Marathas from the Deccan wars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Under Aurangzeb Hindu nobles rose to about 31.6%, mostly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

items.s: Which Mughal emperor banned the celebration of Navroz?
items.x: Aurangzeb, who also reimposed jizya in 1679, banned Navroz.

items.s: In which year did Aurangzeb annex Golconda as the 21st Mughal suba?
items.x: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda on 3 October 1687; 1679 is the year jizya was revived.

items.s: What does Aurangzeb's title 'Alamgir' mean?
items.x: Alamgir means 'Conqueror of the World'; Shah Jahan means 'King of the World'.

items.s: ‘Radha Govind Sangeet Sar’ the renowned classical music composition is the creation of-
items.x:
Most books and keys: Sawai Pratap Singh. Some Rajasthan books credit its actual composition to his court scholar Devarshi Brajpal Bhatt.
The Radha Govind Sangeet Sar, a large music treatise, was produced at the Jaipur court of Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh (r. 1778-1803), himself a poet ('Brajnidhi'). Chatur Lal Sen and Hiranand Vyas are not linked to it.

items.s: For about how many years did Aurangzeb campaign in the Deccan at the end of his reign, draining the treasury?
items.x: Aurangzeb spent roughly the last twenty-seven years of his reign campaigning in the Deccan against the Marathas, which drained the Mughal treasury.

items.s: Which groups did Aurangzeb's reimposition of jizya in 1679 particularly alienate?
items.x: The religious policy, including the reimposition of jizya in 1679, alienated important groups such as the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.

items.s: With whose help were the Sayyid brothers, Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan, overthrown?
items.x: They were overthrown with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk, not Murshid Quli Khan.

items.s: Who became Mughal emperor immediately after Aurangzeb in 1707?
items.x: Bahadur Shah I (1707-1712) was the first emperor after Aurangzeb, followed by Jahandar Shah.

items.s: Whom did Saadatullah Khan name as his successor, making the Carnatic nawabship hereditary?
items.x: Saadatullah Khan, founder of Arcot, named his nephew Dost Ali successor without the Nizam's approval.

items.s: On which date did Ahmad Shah Abdali win the Third Battle of Panipat?
items.x: Abdali defeated the Marathas at Third Panipat on 14 January 1761; Karnal (24 February 1739) was Nadir Shah's victory.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal successor states:
1. Murshid Quli Khan founded the Bengal state.
2. Saadatullah Khan founded the Awadh state.
3. Nizam-ul-Mulk became autonomous after defeating Mubariz Khan at Shakarkheda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Murshid Quli Khan founded Bengal and Nizam-ul-Mulk won at Shakarkheda in 1724; Awadh was founded by Saadat Khan, while Saadatullah Khan founded Arcot.

items.s: Which of the following about Nadir Shah is NOT correct?
o: He was the Afsharid ruler of Iran
He defeated Muhammad Shah at Karnal in 1739
He carried away Shah Jahan's Peacock Throne
He won the Third Battle of Panipat
items.x: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was won by Ahmad Shah Abdali, a commander of Nadir Shah.

items.s: Who was the immediate predecessor of Farrukhsiyar on the Mughal throne?
items.x: Farrukhsiyar, with the Sayyid Brothers, killed Jahandar Shah (1712-1713) and took the throne in 1713.

items.s:
Arrange the following Later Mughals in chronological order:
1. Muhammad Shah
2. Bahadur Shah I
3. Shah Alam II
4. Farrukhsiyar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
items.x: Bahadur Shah I (1707) came first, then Farrukhsiyar (1713), Muhammad Shah (1719) and Shah Alam II (1759).

items.s: Which Mughal emperor granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the British by the Treaty of Allahabad?
items.x: After Buxar, Shah Alam II gave the Diwani to the Company by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

items.s: Who founded the Mughal successor state of Awadh?
items.x: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk, governor from 1722, founded Awadh; Saadatullah Khan founded Arcot.

items.s: Where was Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the revolt of 1857?
items.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal, was exiled to Rangoon and died there in 1862.

items.s: The first fort that was captured by Sivaji
items.x: Torna (Prachandagad) was the first fort Shivaji captured, in 1646, at about 16; Kondana (Sinhagad), Purandar and Rajgad came later.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: "Treaty of Mungi - Shevagaon" was agreed upon between
o: The Nizam and The Hyder Ali
items.x: The Treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon (1728), after the Battle of Palkhed, was between the Marathas (Peshwa Baji Rao I) and the Nizam (Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah), who accepted Shahu's chauth and sardeshmukhi. (Off-topic; moved to the Peshwas row.)

items.s: Divya Prabandhas are authored by
items.x: The Divya Prabandham (Nalayira Divya Prabandham) is the canon of hymns of the 12 Alvars, the Tamil Vaishnava saints. Haridasas were later Kannada Vaishnava singers.

items.s: Who among the following was not an ‘Alvar Saint’?
items.x: Poigai, Pudam (Bhutam) and Thirumangai were Alvars; 'Tirugyan' (Tirugnana Sambandar) was a Shaiva Nayanar, not an Alvar.

items.s: The collection of the writings of the Saivite saints is considered as Fifth Veda. What is the name of the above collection?
items.x: The Tirumurai, the 12-volume Tamil Shaiva canon of the Nayanars, is called the 'Fifth Veda'. Tolkappiyam is a grammar; Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are Sangam-age epics.

items.s: Vaishnavism was propagated by Alvar saints of Tamil Nadu. Who was the only female Sadhvi among the Alvar saints?
items.x: Andal was the only woman among the 12 Alvars. Nammalvar, Poigai and Thirumangai were male Alvars.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: The Tirumurai is a 12-volume Tamil Shaiva canon compiled between the 7th and 12th centuries and called the Fifth Veda; Alvar hymns were in Tamil.

items.s: What is the traditional number of Alvars and Nayanars respectively?
items.x: There are traditionally 12 Alvars (Vaishnava, devotees of Vishnu) and 63 Nayanars (Shaiva, devotees of Shiva). '63 and 12' reverses them, and the other two options give both groups the same number.

items.s: Which of the following was a Nayanar saint?
items.x: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar are notable Nayanars; Nammalvar, Andal and Tirumangai were Alvars.

items.s: Where did Rajaraja I consecrate bronzes of all 63 Nayanmars?
items.x: Rajaraja I consecrated the bronzes at Chidambaram; Parantaka I had installed statues of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.

items.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
items.x: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Shaiva woman saint associated with the Nayanars. Andal, not Karaikkal Ammaiyar, was the only female Alvar.

items.s: What is the canon of the Alvar hymns known as?
items.x: The Alvar hymns form the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; Tevaram and Tirumurai are Nayanar (Shaiva) collections.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Alvars and Nayanars:
1. The Alvars were Vaishnavas, traditionally 12 in number.
2. The Nayanars were Shaivas, traditionally 63 in number.
3. Their hymns were composed in Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Alvars (12) worshipped Vishnu and Nayanars (63) Shiva; their hymns were in Tamil, not Sanskrit.

items.s: Karaikkal Ammaiyar, known for extreme asceticism, belonged to which group of saints?
items.x: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Nayanar; Andal was the only female Alvar.

items.s: The Tirumurai, the Tamil Shaiva canon, consists of how many volumes?
items.x: The Tirumurai has 12 volumes, of which the Tevaram is the earliest and most sacred part.

items.s: Which is the earliest and most sacred part of the Tirumurai, the canon of the Nayanars?
items.x: Tevaram is the earliest and most sacred part of the Tirumurai, the Tamil Shaiva canon of the Nayanars.

items.s: Which Philosophy propagated by Shri Raghavendra Swami?
items.x: Raghavendra Swami of Mantralayam was a saint of Madhvacharya's Dvaita (dualist) school, not of Advaita or Shivadvaita.

items.s: Which philosophy did Ramanuja preach?
items.x: Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and stressed the worship of Narayana and Lakshmi.

items.s: Which philosophy did Nimbarka preach?
items.x: Nimbarka preached Dvaitadvaita; Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.

items.s: Which philosophy did Shankaracharya preach?
items.x: Shankaracharya taught Advaita (non-dualism); Madhva taught Dvaita and Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: Mira Bai belonged to the Royal family of
items.x: Mirabai belonged to the Rathore royal family of Merta, Rajasthan, and married into the Sisodia house of Mewar.

items.s:
Verses ascribed to poet-saint Kabir have been compiled in which of the following traditions?

I. Bijak in Varanasi

II. Kabir Granthavali in Rajasthan

III. Adi Granth Sahib
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: Kabir's verses survive in three overlapping traditions: the Bijak preserved by the Kabirpanth in Varanasi, the Kabir Granthavali of the Dadupanth in Rajasthan, and the Adi Granth Sahib. So all three are correct. (Moved to the Kabir row.)

items.s: Whose disciple was Kabir?
items.x: Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda, not Guru Nanak; his followers are the Kabirpanthis.

items.s: Which of the following was Kabir’s religious teaching?
o: Caste hierarchy is necessary for spiritual progress.
One God may be called by names such as Ram, Rahim, Allah and Hari.
Only one religious community can attain salvation.
Rituals of both Hinduism and Islam are indispensable.
items.x: Kabir taught belief in one God known by many names and condemned the rituals of both faiths, advocating Hindu–Muslim unity.

items.s: Identify the odd man out:
items.x: Maharajapuram Viswanatha Iyer, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and Musiri Subramania Iyer were Carnatic vocalists. T.R. Mahalingam was a flautist, so he is the odd one out.

items.s: In the opinion of some, Ottimitta is whose birthplace?
items.x: Ottimitta (Kadapa) is held by some to be the birthplace of Bammera Pothana, author of the Andhra Mahabhagavatam. (Moved to the Bhakti in Andhra row.)

items.s: Renowned keerthanakara in Telugu
items.x: Thyagaraja (1767-1847) composed his kirtanas mainly in Telugu; Vijayadasa composed in Kannada and the Alvars in Tamil.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was a contemporary of Akbar and Jahangir.
2. Shaikh Salim Chishti was a contemporary of Akbar.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (1564-1624) lived under Akbar and Jahangir, and Shaikh Salim Chishti (1478-1572) was Akbar's spiritual guide at Sikri.

items.s: Shaikh Salim Chishti (1478–1572) was the spiritual guide of which ruler at Sikri?
items.x: Shaikh Salim Chishti was Akbar's spiritual guide at Sikri.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. Janabai was associated with Namdev, Mardana with Guru Nanak and Surdas with Vallabhacharya.

items.s: Who compiled the Adi Granth (Guru Granth Sahib)?
items.x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth and installed it at Amritsar in 1604; Guru Gobind Singh declared it the Guru in 1706.

items.s: Which Sikh Guru standardised the Gurmukhi script?
items.x: Guru Angad (Lehna), Nanak's successor, standardised Gurmukhi and systematised the langar.

items.s: In which year was the Adi Granth installed in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar?
items.x: Guru Arjan Dev completed and installed the Adi Granth in the Harmandir Sahib in 1604.

items.s: Which Sikh Guru declared the Adi Granth to be the Guru?
items.x: Guru Gobind Singh added Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns and declared the Granth the Guru.

items.s: Who introduced the Gurmukhi script?
items.x: Guru Nanak used Punjabi; his successor Guru Angad introduced the Gurmukhi script.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: What were the taxes extracted by Church during late eighteenth century in the French Society called?
items.x: The tithe was the tax (about one-tenth of produce) that the Church collected in pre-revolutionary France. The taille was a direct tax paid to the state, the livre was the currency, and jizya was a Muslim poll tax.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Which of the following was discovered by Columbus?
items.x: Columbus (1492) reached the Americas while seeking a western route to India; India's sea route was found by Vasco da Gama in 1498. Moved to history.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: ---------- was the person who discovered new sea route to India via coast of South Africa on 20th May 1498.
items.x: Vasco da Gama rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut on 20 May 1498, opening the sea route to India. Moved to history.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: Where did the February Revolution take place?
items.x: Russia's February Revolution (1917) began in Petrograd (St Petersburg), the capital.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: As per the Gregorian calendar, the Bolshevik Revolution (October Revolution) occurred on
items.x: The October Revolution of 25 October 1917 (Julian calendar) fell on 7 November 1917 in the Gregorian calendar.

items.s: In India, Tobacco crop was first introduced by
items.x: The Portuguese brought tobacco to India, along with chilli, potato, pineapple and groundnut. (Moved to the Portuguese row.)

items.s: In which year did Albuquerque capture Goa for the Portuguese?
items.x: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510; Almeida's Blue Water Policy was an earlier, separate strategy.

items.s: With whom is the 'Blue Water Policy' associated?
items.x: Francisco de Almeida followed the Blue Water Policy; Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Where was Fort St. David built in 1690
items.x: Fort St. David was the English fort at Devanampatnam (Tegnapatnam) near Cuddalore, bought in 1690; Madras had Fort St. George, and Masulipatnam and Nagapatnam were other factories. (Moved to the English East India Company row.)

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: Which Governor of Bombay approved the building of the great sea wall to prevent flooding of low lying areas?
items.x: William Hornby, Governor of Bombay (1771-84), approved the Hornby Vellard sea wall (completed 1784) that closed the Worli breach. (Moved to the Bombay row.)

items.s: Which was the main trade centre for Portuguese in A.P.?
items.x: The Portuguese had their Andhra factory at Machilipatnam (c. 1570s; NextGen says 1670); Pulicat became the Dutch centre, and Kakinada and Rajahmundry were not Portuguese posts. (Moved: Advent of Europeans in Andhra.)

items.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
items.s: What major economic activity was dominant in the Andhra region during the pre-colonial period, which contributed significantly to the economy?
items.x: Pre-colonial Andhra was famous for textile production and export, such as the Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) chintz and calico trade. Coal mining began only in the colonial era.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: The Port of Masulipatnam rose to the prominence as a centre of maritime trade during last quarter of sixteenth century.
R: Portugese were the first to recieve the farman from Golkonda rulers to establish the factory at Masulipatnam.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: A is true: Masulipatnam rose as the Qutb Shahi kingdom's chief port in the last quarter of the 16th century. R is false: the Dutch were the first to get a Golconda farman for a factory at Masulipatnam (1605-06), followed by the English (1611); the Portuguese never had such a factory there.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: The Carnatic Wars were fought between the English and the French in India.
R: These wars were a result of the war of succession among the rulers of Carnatic.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: A is true. R is false as a general cause: the Carnatic Wars arose from Anglo-French rivalry and the European wars (the First Carnatic War came from the War of Austrian Succession), with succession disputes only exploited later. Moved to History.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s:
Which of the following statements is/are incorrect regarding the Dual system of administration prevalent in Bengal in the 18th century?

a. The Nawab controlled the defence of Bengal, while the East India Company controlled its finances.

b. The system was advantageous to the East India Company as it had power without responsibility.

c. The weaving industry of Bengal mostly suffered due to the dual system of administration.

d. The separation of power resulted in efficient administration and checked the drain of wealth.
items.x: Under the dual system (1765-72) the Company held the diwani and, through the deputy subahdar, the nizamat; it controlled the army, so (a) 'the Nawab controlled defence' is wrong, and (d) is wrong because the system ruined administration. (b) and (c) are correct. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.src: APPSC AEE Civil & Mechanical Engineering General Studies & M
items.s:
Which of the following statements is/are incorrect regarding the Dual system of administration prevalent in Bengal in the 18th century?

a. The Nawab controlled the defence of Bengal, while the East India Company controlled its finances

b. The system was advantageous to the East India Company as it had power without responsibility

c. The weaving industry of Bengal mostly suffered due to the dual system of administration

d. The separation of power resulted in efficient administration and checked the drain of wealth
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: Under the dual system the Company controlled both the revenues and the army (the Nawab depended on it for funds and forces), so (a) is incorrect; (d) is incorrect because the system caused an administrative breakdown. (b) power without responsibility and (c) ruin of the weavers are correct. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.s: The dual system of governance in Bengal was enforced by :
items.x: Robert Clive set up the Dual Government in Bengal (1765); Warren Hastings abolished it in 1772. (Moved to the Dual Government row.)

items.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), which ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu Sultan:
o: was killed and Mysore was partitioned
gave up half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and sent two sons as hostages
accepted a subsidiary alliance and restored the Wodeyars
returned all conquests under mutual restitution
items.x: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam, Tipu gave up half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and handed over two sons as hostages to the British, Marathas and Nizam, who were allied against him. Tipu was killed and Mysore partitioned in 1799, in the Fourth war, when the Wodeyars were restored. Mutual restitution was agreed in the Treaty of Madras of 1769.

items.s: What did the Treaty of Madras (1769), which ended the First Anglo-Mysore War, provide for?
o: cession of half of Mysore's territory
mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance
items.x: The Treaty of Madras gave mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.

items.s: Tipu Sultan's attack on Travancore in 1789 was significant because Travancore was
o: a Maratha dependency controlling the Tungabhadra
the capital of the Nizam's dominions
a French possession and Mysore's principal naval base
a British ally and the Company's only pepper supplier
items.x: Travancore was a British ally and the East India Company's only pepper supplier. Tipu's attack helped precipitate the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

items.s: Where is Tipu Sultan said to have planted a 'Tree of Liberty'?
items.x: The Tree of Liberty was planted at Srirangapatnam, his capital; Dindigul is where Haidar Ali set up an arsenal in 1755.

items.s: Which of the following correctly states the British concern behind the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
o: Warren Hastings feared Haidar Ali's control of Mahe.
Lord Cornwallis feared a Maratha alliance with France.
The Madras Government feared the restoration of the Wodeyars.
Lord Wellesley feared Tipu Sultan's alliance with Napoleon.
items.x: Lord Wellesley feared Tipu Sultan's alliance with Napoleon, which contributed to the decision to wage the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

items.s: Mysore's control over which Malabar spices was a factor in the British conflicts with Mysore?
items.x: The British were concerned about Mysore's control of Malabar pepper and cardamom, its threat to Madras and its French ties.

items.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, against whom were the Nizam, the Marathas and the British allied?
items.x: In the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam, the Marathas and the British formed an alliance against Haidar Ali.

items.s: Who defeated Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781)?
items.x: Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali at Porto Novo on 1 July 1781.

items.s: Where did Haidar Ali set up a modern arsenal with French help in 1755?
items.x: Haidar Ali built a modern arsenal at Dindigul (1755) with French help.

items.s: Which treaty ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
items.x: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Second war on the basis of status quo.

items.s: Which Anglo-Mysore War ended without a treaty?
items.x: The Fourth war (1799) ended with Tipu killed and Mysore partitioned, without a treaty.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about Tipu Sultan:
1. He sent ambassadors to France to obtain European technology.
2. He built a navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Tipu sent ambassadors to France for European technology and also built a navy.

items.s: Which French revolutionary club is Tipu Sultan said to have joined?
items.x: Tipu Sultan is said to have joined the Jacobin Club and planted a 'Tree of Liberty' at Srirangapatnam.

items.s: The Mulki rule agitation took place during the rule of
items.x: Mulki conditions (local candidates for state posts) were introduced in 1888 under the 6th Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, and made stricter by Mir Osman Ali Khan's farman of 1919. (Off-topic; moved to the Nizam row.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s: In which century did the English East India Company gain control over the Northern Circars?
items.x: The English got the Northern Circars in the 18th century: by Shah Alam II's grant (1765) and the treaty with the Nizam of Hyderabad (1766). (Moved: Northern Circars row.)

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s: Who among the following pressured the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam to issue a Farman ceding all the Northern Circars to the English?
items.x: Robert Clive obtained Shah Alam II's farman of 1765 granting the Northern Circars (confirmed by the Nizam in 1766). (Moved to the Northern Circars row.)

items.s: Who is Salarjung-I?
items.x: Turab Ali Khan, Salar Jung I, was appointed Diwan (Prime Minister) of Hyderabad in 1853 and served three Nizams till 1883.

items.s: On what charge were the lands of the Carnatic Nawab in Nellore and Chittoor annexed in 1801?
items.x: Nellore and Chittoor were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801 on the charge of collusion with Tipu Sultan, an early pretext annexation.

items.s: What were the Ceded Districts, given up by the Nizam in 1800, called?
items.x: Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, ceded in 1800, were called the Ceded Districts or Dattamandalalu.

items.s: Under which treaty did Nizam Ali get back Bellary, Gandikota and Kadapa from Tipu Sultan?
items.x: After the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Nizam Ali got back half the Rayalaseema lands under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: The Vijayanagaram estate was handed over to Narayana Babu after negotiations with the Company.
R: He agreed to pay arrears amounting to 5 lakh rupees.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: After Vijayarama Raju II fell at Padmanabham (1794), the Company restored the Vizianagaram estate to his son Narayana Babu on terms that included the arrears of revenue. The key follows the printed answer that both are true but R is not the explanation. Moved to History.

items.s: Due to whose efforts an anicut across the Godavari river at Dowaleshwaram was completed in 1849?
items.x: The Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram (1847-52) was designed and built by Sir Arthur Cotton; Munro, Macpherson and Barlow were governors. (Moved to the Andhra-under-the-Company row.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh during colonial rule are correct?

1. The British annexed the Northern Circars region from the French in the late 18th century and brought it under the Madras Presidency.

2. The 1857 Revolt had no significant impact in Andhra Pradesh, as there were no major uprisings in the region.

3. The Non-Cooperation Movement and Civil Disobedience Movement saw active participation from leaders and people in Andhra Pradesh.

4. The Andhra Mahasabha played a crucial role in mobilising people against British rule and later contributed to the formation of the Andhra State.
items.x: Statement 2 is false: Andhra did see uprisings in 1857-58 (e.g. a tribal rising in Gulugonda, Vizag district). Statements 1, 3 and 4 are taken as correct: the Circars passed from French control to the British (1759-66) under Madras; Andhra joined NCM and CDM; the Andhra Mahasabha/Andhra movement led towards the Andhra State.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: Even though the British East India Company occupied the region, during their rule they focused extensively on irrigation infrastructure to boost agricultural productivity.
R: Significant irrigational works undertaken by the Company were the construction of anicuts over the rivers Godavari and Krishna in 1847 and 1853 respectively.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: A is false: the Company's rule was revenue-driven and irrigation was neglected for long; R is true: Arthur Cotton's anicuts on the Godavari (Dowleswaram, from 1847) and the Krishna (from 1852-53) were the major exceptions.

items.s: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Avadh?
items.x: Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Awadh, deposed and exiled to Calcutta when Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856; Shuja-ud-Daula, Asaf-ud-Daula and Saadat Ali Khan were earlier Nawabs. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: Which Governor-General is associated with the ' Doctrine of Lapse '?
items.x: Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) applied the Doctrine of Lapse, annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir (Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur); Cornwallis, Ripon and Curzon are not linked to it. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: Who among the following formulated and implemented the ‘Doctrine of Lapse’?
items.x: The Doctrine of Lapse is credited to Lord Dalhousie, who enforced it with zeal (Satara 1848 onwards); Wellesley = Subsidiary Alliance, Hastings and Clive came earlier. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s:
Consider the following Indian states:
I. Awadh
II. Jhansi
III. Satara
IV. Nagpur
V. Sindh
Which of the above states were annexed by the British due to the policy of Doctrine of Lapse?
items.x: Jhansi, Satara and Nagpur lapsed; Awadh was annexed for misgovernment (1856) and Sindh by conquest (1843), so II, III and IV. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: Which of the following Princely States was not annexed by the British?
items.x: Gwalior (Sindhia) was never annexed and stayed a princely state; Sind (1843), Awadh (1856) and Satara (1848) were annexed. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: Oudh was amalgamated into the British dominion in the year–
items.x: Dalhousie annexed Oudh (Awadh) in February 1856 on the ground of misgovernment. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: Who among the following was the British residence in Awadh at the time of its annexation into British Dominion?
items.x: James Outram succeeded Sleeman as Resident in Awadh in 1854 and his report supported annexation in 1856; Sleeman was the earlier Resident. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: The ruler of which one of the following states was removed from power by the British on the pretext of misgovernance?
items.x: Awadh's Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was deposed on the pretext of misgovernment (1856); Jhansi, Nagpur and Satara were taken under the Doctrine of Lapse. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s: The policy of annexation devised by the British East India Company was called:
items.x: The annexation policy of the Company was the Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie): a state whose ruler left no natural heir passed to the paramount power. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s:
Consider the following Princely States of the British rule in India:
1. Jhansi
2. Sambalpur
3. Satara The correct chronological order in which they were annexed by the British is:
items.x: Satara lapsed in 1848, Sambalpur in 1849 and Jhansi in 1853-54, so 3-2-1. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.s:
Consider the annexation of the following States under 'Doctrine of Lapse' and arrange them into chronological order :

Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

items.x: Satara 1848, Baghat 1850, Udaipur (Chhattisgarh) 1852, Jhansi 1853-54: 1, 3, 4, 2. (Moved: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations row.)

items.x: Rani Chennamma led the Kittur revolt (1824); Nana Sahib, Dadu Miyan and Phadke belong to other risings. (Moved to the Doctrine of Lapse row.)

o: Awadh — 1856 — annexation due to absence of a natural heir
Satara — 1848 — first annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Punjab — 1849 — annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse

Arrange the following states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in chronological order:

B. Satara

items.x: The correct sequence is Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1849), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).

items.x: Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur and Jhansi were all annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.

items.s: Which of the following states was annexed on the ground of maladministration, rather than under the Doctrine of Lapse?
items.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration, based on Outram's reports. Nagpur, Jhansi and Sambalpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.

items.s: Whom did the lapse annexations and the takeover of Awadh alienate, helping to cause the Revolt of 1857?
items.x: The annexations and Awadh takeover turned rulers, taluqdars and sepoys against the Company, contributing to the revolt.

items.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

items.s: On what ground was Punjab annexed in 1849?
items.x: Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, and Duleep Singh was deposed.

items.s: Lord Dalhousie abolished the titles and pensions of the rulers of which states?
items.x: Dalhousie abolished the titles and pensions of the rulers of Tanjore and the Carnatic.

items.s: Which state was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1849?
items.x: Jaitpur lapsed in 1849; Jaipur was not a lapse case and Gwalior was never annexed.

items.s: On what ground was Berar taken from the Nizam in 1853?
items.x: Berar was taken from the Nizam in 1853 for arrears of the subsidy, not under lapse.

items.s: Under which Governor-General was Sindh annexed by conquest in 1843?
items.x: Sindh was conquered in 1843 under Ellenborough (1842-44), before Dalhousie's time.

items.s: Whose adopted son was not recognised by Dalhousie when Jhansi was annexed in 1853?
items.x: Raja Gangadhar Rao of Jhansi died in 1853; his adopted son Damodar Rao was not recognised and Jhansi lapsed.

items.s: What was the name of the adopted son of Raja Gangadhar Rao, who was not recognised when Jhansi was annexed?
items.x: Dalhousie refused to recognise Damodar Rao, the adopted heir, and annexed Jhansi under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1853.

items.s: Who was the Nawab of Awadh when it was annexed in 1856 on the ground of misgovernment?
items.x: Awadh was annexed in February 1856 on grounds of misgovernment; its Nawab was Wajid Ali Shah.

items.s: The annexation of Awadh in 1856 was based on the reports of which British officers?
items.x: Reports of Sleeman and Outram on misgovernment were used to justify the annexation of Awadh in 1856.

items.s: In which year was Nagpur annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse after Raghuji III died without an heir?
items.x: Raghuji III of Nagpur died heirless and the state was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1854.

items.s: Which Sikh ruler was deposed when Punjab was annexed in 1849?
items.x: Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1849) and Duleep Singh was deposed.

items.x: The Charter Act of 1853 let the Company keep its territories 'in trust for Her Majesty' without fixing any period; the Regulating Act was 1773, and the other two are commercial laws.

A: The Textile Industry of Andhra which flourished during 17th-18th centuries witnessed a decline in the 19th century in both foreign and local markets.
R: In the foreign markets it declined because of competition with machine made goods while in local markets it declined because of high tariffs.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

items.s: Why Calico Act was passed by British Government in 1721?
o: To prescribe sizes for books bound with Calico
To regulate the price of Calico Cloth
To levy import tariffs on Calico Cloth
To ban imports of printed cotton textiles
items.x:
Most books and keys: the 1721 Act banned imports of printed cotton textiles. Strictly: the 1700 Act banned imports of printed calicoes; the 1721 Act went further and banned the sale and wearing of most cotton cloth (general knowledge, not checked).
The British Calico Acts protected English wool and silk makers against Indian printed cottons; the option 'to ban imports of printed cotton textiles' is the keyed purpose.

items.s: As part of the British law in India, an act was enacted that stated that 'any person protesting or criticizing the British Government could be arrested without due trial'. Which act is being mentioned here?
items.x:
Most keys: Sedition Act of 1870 (Section 124A IPC). Strictly: 'arrest without trial' describes the Rowlatt Act of 1919 (not an option); sedition under 124A still needed a trial.
Of the options only the sedition law of 1870 (Section 124A, IPC) was a measure against criticism of the government; the 1773 and 1784 Acts and the '1786 Act' are constitutional Acts of the Company. Strictly, arrest and detention without trial was the Rowlatt Act of 1919, which is not offered.

1. Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the "Grand Old Man of India" and authored the book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

2. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was famously called the "Lokmanya" and popularized the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."

3. Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March in 1930 to protest the British salt tax.

4. Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc and led the Indian National Army (INA) with the slogan "Jai Hind."
Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.x: All four are correct: Naoroji (Grand Old Man; Poverty and Un-British Rule), Tilak (Lokmanya; 'Swaraj is my birthright'), Gandhi (Dandi March 1930 against the salt tax), Bose (Forward Bloc; INA; 'Jai Hind').

items.s: In 1907, Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay under which law?

items.s: Which event of 1906 preceded the grant of separate electorates for Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms?
items.x: The Simla Deputation of 1906 asked for separate electorates, granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
