items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Assembly bomb of 8 April 1929?
o: It protested against the Public Safety Bill
It protested against the Trade Disputes Bill
The bombs were meant to kill members of the Assembly
The bombs were thrown by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
items.x: The bombs were deliberately non-lethal, 'to make the deaf hear', aiming at arrest and a trial for propaganda.

items.s: Jatin Das died after how many days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929?
items.x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929 and was regarded as the first martyr of that strike.

items.s: The Saunders killing of 1928 was meant to avenge the lathi-charge on whom?
items.x: The Saunders killing was planned in retaliation for the lathi-charge on Lala Lajpat Rai during the anti-Simon Commission protest. The intended target was James A. Scott, while Rajguru fired first.

items.s: In which year did the Chittagong Armoury Raid take place?
items.x: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was in 1930.

items.s: Which book was written by Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee?
items.x: Jogesh Chatterjee wrote In Search of Freedom; Bandi Jiwan was by Sachindranath Sanyal.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about birth years of revolutionaries:
1. Bhagat Singh was born in 1907.
2. Chandrashekhar Azad was born in 1906.
3. Khudiram Bose was born in 1889.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: All are correct: Bhagat Singh 28 Sep 1907, Azad 23 Jul 1906, Khudiram 3 Dec 1889.

items.s: Who was the intended target in the Saunders killing of 1928?
items.x: The revolutionaries aimed at James A. Scott to avenge the lathi-charge on Lajpat Rai; Saunders was killed instead.

items.s: Who among the following was hanged in the Kakori case?
items.x: Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged for Kakori; Jogesh Chatterjee got life and Azad escaped.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ram Prasad Bismil was born on 11 June 1897.
2. Sukhdev was born at Ludhiana in 1907.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Bismil was born on 11 June 1897 and Sukhdev on 15 May 1907 at Ludhiana.

items.s: Who wrote 'Why I am an Atheist'?
items.x: Bhagat Singh wrote Why I am an Atheist; Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb.

items.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Kakori train action
2. Hindustan Republican Association
3. Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
4. Naujawan Bharat Sabha
items.x: HRA 1924, Kakori 1925, Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926, HSRA 1928.

items.s: Alluri Sita Rama Raju was killed by the British at
items.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was captured by Jamedar Kunchu Menon, taken to Koyyur and shot dead (7 May 1924).

items.s: Who established an organisation called 'Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshti'?
items.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah set up the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshti at Chirala in 1920.

items.s: Against which Act did Alluri Sita Rama Raju lead a tribal protest against the British rule?
items.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa rebellion (1922-24) was against the restrictions of the Madras Forest Act, 1882 (podu ban, forest dues).

items.s: Who were the lieutenants associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora
items.x: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora were associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju as lieutenants. Scott Coward and Haytes were officers killed during the rebellion.

items.s: Which one of the following statements about the Rampa Rebellion is NOT correct?
o: Scott Coward and Haytes were killed during the rebellion.
The Malabar Special Police was brought in against the rebels.
Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1922.
A direct battle took place at Panjerighat.
items.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922. The other three statements are correct.

items.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju's armed struggle is said to have troubled the British more than which movement?
items.x: Raju was not linked to the INC, but his armed struggle troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.

items.s: When was Alluri Sitarama Raju killed?
items.x: Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922; 22 August 1922 was his first attack, on Chintapalli.

items.s: Against what was the Rampa Rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju directed?
items.x: Raju rose against the Muttadari system, the forest laws and Tahsildar Bastian.

items.s: Which police station did Alluri Sitarama Raju attack first, on 22 August 1922?
items.x: The Rampa Rebellion began with the raid on Chintapalli police station on 22 August 1922; Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi followed.

items.s: Where did Alluri Sitarama Raju meet Bengal revolutionaries in 1921?
items.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju met Bengal revolutionaries at Chittagong in 1921, before the Rampa Rebellion.

items.s: Which police station was attacked first during the Rampa Rebellion?
items.x: The Rampa Rebellion began on August 22, 1922, when Alluri Sitarama Raju's men raided the Chintapalli police station. Kanikapadu and Nidubrolu are linked with N.G. Ranga.

items.s: On which date did the Rampa Rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju begin?
items.x: The Rampa Rebellion began on 22 August 1922 with a raid on Chintapalli police station.

items.s: Which tribes mainly took part in the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
items.x: The Rampa Rebellion in the Godavari agency was fought by Koyas and Konda Doras.

items.s: Which police station was attacked first by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
items.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju began the Rampa revolt of 1922 by attacking the Chintapalli police station first. Palnadu is linked with the Forest Satyagraha and Kakinada with the Vandemataram riot case.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017

items.x: Tripuraneni Gopichand wrote the novel 'Asamarthuni Jeevita Yatra'.

Non-violent reform and propaganda for Swaraj
Armed revolutionary training and military recruitment

items.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to give all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund?
items.x: Maganti Annapurnamma gave all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund and burnt foreign goods.

items.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras in 1938?
items.x: Durgabai, who translated Gandhi's speech at Kakinada in April 1921, founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (Madras, 1938).

items.x: Yamini Purna Tilakam is linked with the Guntur hartals.

items.x: During the protest against the Simon Commission in Madras, T. Prakasam bared his chest to the police and dared them to shoot – earning the title 'Andhra Kesari'. (Moved to the Prakasam row.)

items.x: After the 1946 elections Tanguturi Prakasam headed the Congress ministry of Madras Presidency (1946-47).

Andhra Pradesh Gandhiji – Nanduri Subba Rao

items.s: Who wrote 'Andhra Pradesh Gandhiji'?
items.x: 'Andhra Pradesh Gandhiji' was written by Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya.

items.x: The Bengal peasants' revolt of 1859-60 (Indigo Revolt) was against forced indigo cultivation for European planters; afterwards indigo shifted to Bihar.

items.s: What was the name of the contract farming system in British India in which a farmer signed a contract with a planter to cultivate Indigo on his farm?
items.x: Under the ryoti system the planter made the ryot sign a contract to grow indigo; nij was cultivation on the planter's own land. Moved to the indigo/peasant movements row.

items.s: Whose killing set off the Telangana armed struggle?
items.x: The killing of Doddi Komaraiah in 1946 helped set off the Telangana armed struggle.

items.s: When was the Telangana armed struggle (1946-51) withdrawn?
items.x: The struggle, led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha, was withdrawn in October 1951, not right after Operation Polo.

items.s: Which organisation, along with the Communists, led the Telangana armed struggle (1946–51)?
items.x: The struggle was led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha against the Nizam, the deshmukhs and later the Razakars.

items.s: First Rythu Sangha was established in Guntur by
items.x: Prof. N.G. Ranga founded the first ryots' association (Rythu Sangham) in Guntur district (Nidubrolu, 1923).

items.s: In 1939, who established a "Rajakeeya Pathashala" (political school) at Kankipadu?
items.x: N.G. Ranga ran the 'School of Politics' (Rajakeeya Pathashala) at Kankipadu in 1939, after his Kisan school at Nidubrolu.

items.src: Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, As

items.x: Amritlal Vithaldas Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa) founded the Bhil Seva Mandal at Dahod in 1922. C.F. Andrews, Karve and Vinoba had no part in it.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Birsa Munda, an Indian tribal independence activist and folk hero, led a tribal religious millenarian movement in which of the following present-day states?
items.x: Birsa Munda led the Munda rising (Ulgulan) of 1899–1900 in Chotanagpur, which is now in Jharkhand; it led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: For which of the following reasons, Pahariyas were against British?
o: British to take them as slaves
Tribals were killed in hunting expeditions
Tribals could not communicate with British
The shifting cultivation of tribals was affected
items.x: The Paharias of the Rajmahal hills lived by shifting cultivation and forest produce; British-backed settled farming (Santhals, zamindars) encroached on their land, so they resisted.

items.x: The 1940 Babijheri (Jodeghat) revolt in Adilabad was led by the Gond leader Komaram Bheem.

o: Adivasi Seva Mandal and Chotanagpur Seva Kendra
Mairakhed Ashram and Bhil Seva Mandal
Bhil Seva Mandal and Adivasi Seva Mandal
Mairakhed Ashram and Chotanagpur Seva Kendra
items.x: Thakkar Bapa (A.V. Thakkar) founded the Bhil Seva Mandal (1922) for the Bhils of Panchmahals and worked through the Adivasi seva bodies; Mairakhed Ashram and Chotanagpur Seva Kendra are distractors. Off-topic, moved to tribal history.

items.s: Who presided over the first session of the "Nizam Andhra Mahasabha"?
items.x: The first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha (Jogipet, Medak, 1930) was presided over by Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.

items.s: The first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha was presided by:
items.x: Suravaram Pratapa Reddy presided over the first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha at Jogipet in 1930.

items.s: "Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham" was formed in 1923 at which place?
items.x: The Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham was formed in 1923 at Hanamkonda.

items.x: The Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham was formed in 1923 at Hanamkonda; Hyderabad was the seat of the Andhra Jana Sangham (1921–22) (official key: Hyderabad).

items.s: Andhrapithamaha?
items.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was called 'Andhra Pitamaha'.

items.s: The Vandemataram Struggle of 1938 was associated with which university?
items.x: The 1938 Vandemataram Struggle took place at Osmania University, when students sang Vandemataram against the Nizam's ban.

items.src: Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fisheries
items.s: What was the subject of Nehru Report of 1928?
o: Action of Congress on Khilafat Conference
Preparation of Agenda for Civil Disobedience Movement
Memorandum for outline of draft Constitution for Dominion status
items.x: The Nehru Report (1928) was a memorandum outlining a draft constitution for India based on Dominion Status, prepared by an All Parties Conference committee under Motilal Nehru.

items.s: At which session of Indian National Congress, the decision to boycott the Simon Commission was taken?
items.x: The Madras session (1927, M.A. Ansari) decided to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage and in every form.

items.s: Which of the following is/are not true in relation to Congress Annual Session in 1927? (i) This session was presided by Dr. M.A. Ansari. (ii) This session passed a resolution against sending Indian Army to fight war in China and Japan. (iii)In this session, resolution on 'Purna Swaraj' was adopted.
items.x:
Coaching keys: (ii) and (iii), because the formal Purna Swaraj resolution came at Lahore 1929. CGPSC key: only (ii) – Madras 1927 passed Nehru's complete-independence resolution (PMF Part 4 p.178).
Only (ii) is untrue: Madras 1927 objected to sending Indian troops to China, Mesopotamia and Persia (not Japan). (i) Ansari presided, and (iii) Nehru's independence resolution calling for Poorna Swaraj was passed there.

items.s: Under whose chairmanship did the committee of the All Parties Conference prepare the Nehru Report of 1928?
items.x: The committee that prepared the Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.

items.s: What did the Nehru Report (1928) ask for India?
items.x: The Nehru Report proposed a constitution based on Dominion Status.

items.s: Who was the secretary of the committee that prepared the Nehru Report (1928)?
items.x: Motilal Nehru was chairman and Jawaharlal Nehru was secretary.

items.s: Which one of the following is not a feature of the Government of India Act of 1935?
o: Dyarchy at the Centre as well as in the Provinces
items.x: The 1935 Act provided dyarchy at the Centre but abolished it in the provinces (provincial autonomy), so "dyarchy at the Centre as well as in the Provinces" is not a feature. It had a bicameral legislature and an All-India Federation.

items.s:
Identify the following reforms that were introduced in India by the Government of India Act, 1935

A. Dyarchy in the provinces

B. Bi-cameral legislature at the central level

C. Provincial Autonomy

D. Establishment of Federal Court
items.x: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy (C) and set up the Federal Court (D). Dyarchy in the provinces was abolished by it, and a bicameral central legislature already existed under the 1919 Act.

items.s: The real intention of the British to include the Princely States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to –
o: Exercise more direct political and administrative
Involve the princes actively in the administration of
Finally effect the complete political and administrative
Use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist
items.x: The British included the princes in the proposed federation so that the loyal, nominated princely bloc would counter-balance the nationalists. The federation never came into being.

items.s: Which one of the following Act reserved seats for women in Legislatures in accordance with the allocation of seats for different communities?
items.x: The 1935 Act reserved seats for women in the legislatures along the communal allocation (the Communal Award also gave women separate seats). The 1858, 1909 and 1919 Acts did not.

items.s: The distribution of powers between the Centre and States in the Indian Constitution is based on the scheme provided in the
items.x: The Centre-State division of powers in the Constitution follows the federal scheme of the 1935 Act, the Constitution's largest single source.

items.s: Which among the following introduced the Provincial Autonomy in British India?
items.x: Provincial autonomy came with the GoI Act, 1935 (in force April 1937), which abolished provincial dyarchy; the Simon Commission only recommended it.

items.s: Who amongst the following had called the Government of India Act, 1935 as the “Charter of Slavery”?
items.x: Jawaharlal Nehru called the 1935 Act a "Charter of Slavery" (also "a machine with strong brakes but no engine").

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s: The Directive Principles resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' enumerated in which Government of India Act?
items.x: The Directive Principles resemble the Instrument of Instructions of the Government of India Act, 1935.

items.s: The ‘Instrumentation of Instructions” contained in the Government of India Act, 1935 have been incorporated in the Constitution of India in the year 1950 as–
o: Extent of Executive Power of State
Conduct of Business of the Government of India
items.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the 1935 Act was reborn in 1950 as the Directive Principles of State Policy.

items.s: Why the Government of India Act, 1935 is important?
o: It is a main source of the Indian Constitution
Division of India is described in it
End of the Princely States by this
items.x: The 1935 Act is the main source of the Indian Constitution (federal scheme, governors, emergency powers, PSCs). It neither gave freedom nor partitioned India, and it did not end the princely states.

items.s: In the first Madras Legislative Assembly, 1937 elections, which of the following parties came into power?
items.x: In the 1937 elections the Congress won a majority in Madras and C. Rajagopalachari formed the ministry, ending the Justice Party's dominance.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: When was the Temple Entry Authorisation and Indemnity Bill introduced in the Madras Legislative Assembly?
items.x: The printed key (4 August 1939) is kept. The Madras Temple Entry Authorisation and Indemnity Act of Rajaji's ministry followed the Madurai Meenakshi temple entry of 8 July 1939 and got assent on 4 September 1939, but the introduction date could not be verified.

items.s: Why did the Congress ministries resign in October-November 1939?
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
items.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.

items.s: How many sections and schedules did the Government of India Act, 1935, the longest British Act on India, contain?
items.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; some references describe it as having 14 parts and 321 articles.

items.s: On which date did the Muslim League observe the 'Day of Deliverance' after the Congress ministries resigned?
items.x: The League observed 22 December 1939 as the Day of Deliverance after the Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939.

items.s: When did provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 begin?
items.x: Provincial autonomy, which replaced dyarchy in the provinces, began in April 1937.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Federal Public Service Commission — 1935 Act — Calcutta, 1937
Provincial Public Service Commissions — 1909 Act — Delhi, 1910
items.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935. The Act also provided for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs.

items.s: After the 1937 provincial elections, who became the Congress Premier of Madras?
items.x: Rajaji headed Madras's first Congress ministry after the 1937 elections under the 1935 Act.

items.s: In which year was the Federal Court under the Government of India Act, 1935 set up at Delhi?
items.x: The Federal Court began at Delhi in 1937.

items.s: On whose recommendation was the Reserve Bank of India set up?
items.x: The RBI Act, 1934 followed the Hilton Young Commission (1926); the RBI started on 1 April 1935.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India:
1. It started functioning on 1 April 1935.
2. It was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: The RBI started on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934 and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

items.s: Which function of the Governor did Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 deal with?
items.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.

items.s: The Instrument of Instructions in the Government of India Act, 1935 became which part of the Constitution?
items.x: The Instrument of Instructions became the Directive Principles (APPSC 2023), not Fundamental Rights.

items.s: Which pair (feature of the 1935 Act – counterpart in the Constitution) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Federal scheme and PSCs – Union-State structure and UPSC/State PSCs
items.x: The Instrument of Instructions corresponds to the Directive Principles of State Policy, not the Fundamental Rights.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017

o: Dividing the country into different provinces and ruling them
Encouraging Hindus and Muslims to fight against one another
Separating administration of cities and villages
Discrimination of Indians against the British citizens
items.x: Divide and rule meant setting communities – above all Hindus and Muslims – against one another (separate electorates, partition of Bengal). Off-topic (modern history), moved.

items.x: 'The future of India lies in its villages' is Gandhi's, from his idea of village self-rule.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: In India party less Democracy was first advocated by
items.x:

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Whose philosophy is reflected in the current primary education of India?
items.x:
Printed key: Tagore. Most books and keys tie primary (basic) education to Gandhi's Nai Talim (general knowledge, not checked).
Gandhi's Basic Education (Nai Talim, Wardha scheme 1937) of learning through work is the philosophy usually said to underlie India's primary education; Tagore's Santiniketan model is a distractor.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in A.P BC We
items.s: Women's education was strongly supported and the 'purdah' system was opposed by?
items.x: Gandhi strongly supported women's education and opposed the purdah system, calling for women's equal role in the national movement. Among the options he is the reformer known for this campaign.

items.s: After which incident, Mahatma Gandhi had called Non-cooperation Movement as his “Himalayan Blunder?
items.x:

Books and keys link the 'Himalayan blunder' to the withdrawal of Non-Cooperation after Chauri Chaura (1922). Gandhi in fact used the phrase about the Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 (see the dispute line).

items.s: Chauri Chaura Incident led to calling off of
items.x: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 (CWC at Bardoli, 12 February 1922). Swadeshi (1905), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Quit India (1942) were other movements.

Boycott of Government schools and colleges
Boycott of public transport and communication system

items.s: Who said in 1942 that if Congress fails to support immediate struggle against British, he would create a movement, out of the sands of India, 'which would be larger than the Congress itself'?
items.x: It was Gandhi who said in 1942, while pressing for the Quit India struggle, that if the Congress did not support him he would build a movement 'out of the sands of India' larger than the Congress itself.

items.s: Who gave the call 'Do or Die' in 1942?
items.x: 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942; Meherally coined 'Quit India' and Bose's war cry was 'Dilli Chalo'.

items.s: Which of the following was associated with the underground leadership of the Quit India Movement?
items.x: Lohia, with Jayaprakash Narayan, Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik, was part of the underground network; Desai and Sapru were linked to the INA trial defence.

o: Organising the Prati Sarkar in Satara
Running the secret Congress Radio in Bombay
items.x: Usha Mehta ran the secret Congress Radio in Bombay during the Quit India movement.

items.s: Which development immediately triggered the Quit India Movement?
o: The conclusion of the Shimla Conference in 1945
The resignation of Congress ministries in November 1939 alone
Failure of the Cripps Mission in March 1942
The formation of the INA in 1943
items.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942), which offered no immediate self-government, was the immediate trigger for Quit India; Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque'. The Simla Conference (1945) and the INA's revival (1943) came later, and the 1939 ministry resignations were only background.

items.s: Who coined the phrase 'Quit India', while Gandhi gave the call for the movement?
items.x: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by Yusuf Meherally. Gandhi subsequently gave the call for the movement.

items.s: On which date was the Quit India Resolution passed at Bombay?
items.x: The Quit India Resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942; the Wardha CWC met on 14 July and the leaders were arrested on 9 August.

items.s: Where was the parallel government 'Prati Sarkar' set up during the Quit India Movement?
items.x: Prati Sarkar was at Satara under Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil.

items.s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
items.x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia (UP) parallel government.

items.s: Which of the following pairs of parallel government and place is correctly matched?

items.x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

items.s: Where was Gandhi detained after the Quit India Resolution?
items.x: Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune; the CWC was held at Ahmednagar Fort.

items.s: To which province did Kanaklata Barua, shot at 17 while leading a flag procession in 1942, belong?
items.x: Kanaklata Barua was from Assam; Matangini Hazra was from Tamluk, Bengal.

items.s: On which date did the Congress Working Committee meet at Wardha in 1942?
items.x: The Wardha CWC met on 14 July 1942; the AICC met at Bombay on 8 August.

items.x: Tenali and Bhimavaram saw firings in 1942.

items.s: The Bonded labour system was abolished from

The printed options did not include the correct answer (25th October, 1975); it is added as option 5.
The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Ordinance was promulgated on 24 October 1975 and the Act of 1976 (assent 9 Feb 1976) is deemed in force from 25 October 1975 – the date from which the system stands abolished. 24 Oct 1975 is only the Ordinance date and both 1976 dates are wrong; 25 Nov 1975 is unrelated.

items.s: A sale of immovable property of an endowment institution is void as per Section 81 of the Endowments Act if
o: it has taken place prior to the commencement of Act 30/1987, with the permission of the Government
it has taken place prior to the commencement of Act 30/1987, with the permission of the Commissioner
it has taken place without the permission of the Government or Commissioner, either prior to or after the commencement of Act 30/1987
items.x: Under Section 81 of the AP Endowments Act 30 of 1987, a sale of endowment immovable property made without the sanction of the Government/Commissioner – before or after the Act – is void.

items.s: Which authority has to initiate action in case of group encroachment on Endowments lands?
items.x: Key as printed: under the AP Endowments Act 1987 the Deputy Commissioner initiates action against group encroachment of endowment lands.

items.s: Who is the competent authority to sanction budget to the temples published under 6-C category?
items.x: Key as printed: the Assistant Commissioner sanctions the budgets of 6(c) institutions (lowest-income temples) under the AP Endowments Act.

items.s: Who is competent to file petition for eviction of an encroacher before the Endowments Tribunal?
items.x: Key as printed: the Assistant Commissioner files the eviction petition before the Endowments Tribunal against encroachers.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: In which year the committee on 'Religious and Moral Instruction' was appointed by the Govt of India?
items.x: The Committee on Religious and Moral Instruction (Sri Prakasa Committee) was appointed in 1959 and reported in 1960.

items.s: Who has to represent the institution/ temple in the legal proceedings before the Court of Law?
items.x: Under the AP Endowments Act the Executive Officer manages the temple and represents the institution in legal proceedings.

items.s: Who is competent to grant permission for sale of land of a temple by way of public auction?
items.x: Printed key kept: under the AP Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, sale of temple land by public auction needs the Commissioner of Endowments' sanction; not verified in the library.

items.s: The power to constitute groups of institutions for the purpose of appointing a single Executive Officer to each group is vested with
items.x: Printed key kept: the Commissioner of Endowments may group institutions to appoint a single Executive Officer for each group (AP Endowments Act, 1987); not verified in the library.

items.s: Who is the competent authority to grant permission for purchase of an immovable property by a temple?
items.x: Under Section 79 of the AP Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, no immovable property may be purchased for an institution without the prior sanction of the Commissioner. The Executive Officer only manages; the Government sanctions some alienations under Sec 80, not purchases.

items.s: Which one of the following authorities is responsible for implementing the order passed by the Endowments Tribunal in an eviction petition?
items.x: Under the AP Endowments Act, the order of the Endowments Tribunal in an eviction petition is implemented by the Assistant Commissioner (printed key kept).

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC Welfare Officer in AP BC Welfare Service, Roy
items.s: In which year was the bill related to abolishing bonded labour passed?
items.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was passed in 1976 (it replaced the ordinance of 1975), giving effect to Article 23.

items.s: With regard to the sale of immovable property of a temple, which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Before issuing permission orders for sale, objections must be called from the public
Only after disposal of such objections received, permission can be issued for the sale of land
Before putting the land for public auction, the E.O. has to seek permission from the competent authority
E.O. can go for public auction of land straight away, and later, he can seek approval of Commissioner
items.x: Under the AP Endowments rules, objections are called and disposed of and permission obtained before an auction; an E.O. cannot auction first and seek approval later. Off-topic (religious endowments), moved.

items.s: A small farmer who is continuing in possession of temple land by the time of commencement of Act 30/1987, is entitled to continue as tenant on payment of the following amount
items.x: Under Sec. 82 of AP Endowments Act 30/1987, a small/marginal farmer who cannot buy the temple land may continue as tenant by paying at least two-thirds of the market rent. Off-topic (endowments law), moved.

items.s: Which one of the following is not a source of income to the temple?
items.x: Temples earn from hundis, devotees' offerings and their immovable properties; government grants are not a regular source of temple income (Art. 27 bars taxes to promote a religion). (Moved: freedom of religion, book 2 row 12.)

items.s: The posts of Executive Officers in other than RJC, DC and AC cadres are classified into how many grades?
items.x: Executive Officers below the RJC, DC and AC cadres are classified into three grades (Grade I, II and III) in the AP Endowments Department.

items.s: Under Article 30(1), to whom does the right to establish and administer educational institutions belong?
items.x: Article 30(1) covers all minorities, religious or linguistic.

items.s: What does Article 29(1) protect the right of a section of citizens to conserve?
items.x: Article 29(1) protects a distinct language, script or culture.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: Kerala Education Bill was decided in 1958; T.M.A. Pai had 11 judges, P.A. Inamdar 7, and St. Xavier's was 1974.

items.s: In which case did a nine-judge bench in 1974 lay down limits on State control over a minority college's management?
items.x: St. Xavier's College (Ahmedabad), 1974, a nine-judge bench, limited State control over minority college management.

items.s: Who called Article 32 of Indian Constitution as "the fundamental of the Fundamental Rights" and "the heart and soul of the Constitution"?
items.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution in the Constituent Assembly. Moved to the Article 32 row.

items.s: ........ Article in Indian Constitution deals with free legal aid to economically backward classes of people.
items.x: Equal justice and free legal aid is Article 39A (DPSP, added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976). There is no Article 14-A. (The printed key was missing.)

items.src: Assistant BC, Social, Tribal Welfare Officer Screening Test
items.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution places a duty upon the State to provide a lawyer to any citizen who is unable to engage one due to poverty or other disability?
items.x: Art. 39A (DPSP, 42nd Amendment) directs the State to provide equal justice and free legal aid.

items.s: Which part of the Indian constitution elaborates the concept of a welfare state?
items.x: The Directive Principles (Part IV) set out the welfare-State ideal of social and economic democracy; the Preamble only names the goals. (No printed key.)

items.s: Which Article of the Directive Principles of the Constitution mentions about empowering Village Panchayats?
items.x: Article 40 (DPSP) directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government; Article 39 is the source of plan objectives.

items.s: In the event of non-enforcement of Directive Principles of State Policy by the Government, the citizen can approach
o: No court – DPSPs are not enforceable by any court
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (No court – DPSPs are not enforceable by any court); it is added as option 5.
Art. 37 makes DPSPs non-justiciable, so no court – district, High, Supreme or one of choice – will enforce them; the printed key 'any court of his choice' is wrong.

items.s: Which article in the constitution of India mentions about Panchayat Raj?
items.x: Article 40 (DPSP) directs the State to organise village panchayats; Art. 20 = protection in conviction, Art. 30 = minority institutions, Art. 16 = equal opportunity in public employment.

items.s: 'Uniform Civil Code' Incorporated in Indian Constitution was to secure
items.x: The Uniform Civil Code (Art. 44, a DPSP) aims at national integration: the Supreme Court in Shah Bano held that it 'will help the cause of national integration by removing disparate loyalties to laws'.

items.s: Protection of which one of the following is a Fundamental Duty in India?
items.x: Protecting and improving the natural environment, including wildlife, is an FD under Art. 51A(g). Respecting the National Flag is an FD under 51A(a), but protecting it is not; village panchayats (40) and SCs/STs (46) are DPSPs.

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates environmental protection as a fundamental duty of every citizen of India?
items.x: Protecting the environment is a Fundamental Duty of citizens under Art. 51A(g); Art. 48A is the State's Directive Principle, Art. 51 is international peace.

items.s: A 'good citizen' is one who
o: Casts vote and pays taxes regularly
items.x: A good citizen is one who is conscious of his social obligations (the spirit of Fundamental Duties, Art. 51A); voting and paying taxes are only parts of it, and education or knowing the Constitution alone does not make a good citizen.

items.s: Protection of which of the following is a fundamental duty in India?
items.x: Art. 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life; respecting the National Flag is 51A(a), but 'protection' of the flag is not the duty's wording.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Fundamental Duties?
o: They are sacrosanct in nature and cannot be amended.
The Supreme Court has an original and exclusive jurisdiction in case of enforcement of Fundamental duty.
They operate as checks on the tyranny of both executive and the Legislature.
The 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002 made it the fundamental duty of parents of children from 6-14 years of age to provide them education.
items.x: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Art. 51A(k), the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child aged 6-14. Fundamental Duties can be amended, are not enforceable by writ, and check citizens rather than the State. (Fundamental Duties; moved.)

items.s: An amendment to the Constitution of India can be initiated by
o: The Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
items.x: An amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament (LS or RS), not in a State Legislature, and needs no prior permission of the President (Art. 368(2)).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Where can an initiative to amend the constitution be taken?
items.x: An amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament (Art. 368(2)) – not only the LS and never in a State Assembly.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: An amendment of the Constitution of India may be initiated by the introduction of a Bill:
o: In either House of Parliament or in state legislatures
items.x: Art. 368(2): an amendment can be initiated only by a Bill in either House of Parliament – not in State legislatures.

items.s: Identify the wrong statement with regard to a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368 of Indian Constitution
o: The bill requires no previous consent of the President
The bill must be first introduced in the Lok Sabha
The bill requires 2/3rd majority in both the Houses of Parliament
No joint session of Parliament can be convened for passing the bill
items.x: An Art. 368 Bill needs no prior presidential consent, a special majority in each House and has no joint sitting – but it can be introduced in either House, so 'must be first introduced in the LS' is wrong.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: The role of the Indian States in the constitutional amendment process is:
o: greater than that of the Indian Parliament
greater than the Lok Sabha but limited in comparison to the Rajya Sabha
items.x: States take part only in amending federal provisions (ratification by half the States, Art. 368(2) proviso) and cannot initiate amendments – their role is limited.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: In which of the following scenarios, does a bill have to be ratified by the legislature of at least half of the states?
o: When certain provisions of the bill affect Fundamental Rights.
When certain provisions of the bill affect Fundamental duties.
When certain provisions of the bill affect central services.
When certain provisions of the bill affect the federal structure.
items.x: Amendments affecting the federal structure (Centre-State relations, judiciary, representation of States) need ratification by at least half the State Legislatures; FRs, duties and central services do not.

items.s: Which amendment of the Constitution limited the role of the President?
items.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers (Art. 74(1)).

items.s: Identify the odd man out
items.x: The 8th (1959), 23rd (1969) and 45th (1980, extending to 1990) Amendments extended SC/ST/Anglo-Indian reservation in legislatures; the 61st (1989) lowered the voting age to 18.

items.s: The 62nd Amendment Bill of the Indian Constitution deals with
o: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes
items.x: The 62nd Amendment (1989) extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies (Art. 334) for ten more years; Nagarpalika and Panchayati Raj were the 65th/64th Bills.

items.s: Which amendment of the constitution of India reduced the age limit to vote?
items.x: The 61st Amendment (1988, in force 1989) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 (Art. 326).

items.s: 85th Amendment Act of Indian Constitution provides for the promotion of
items.x: The 85th Amendment (2001) amended Art. 16(4A) to give consequential seniority in promotions to SCs and STs.

items.s: The First Amendment in the Indian Constitution was made in the year
items.x: The First Amendment Act was passed in 1951 (Art. 15(4), Ninth Schedule, restrictions on Art. 19).

items.s:
Consider the following statements concerning the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016:

A. The Act introduced Goods and Service Tax (GST).

B. The Act amended Sixth and Seventh Schedules of Indian Constitution.

C. The Act empowered Karnataka Governor to take steps for developing Hyderabad-Karnataka region.

D. The Act provided for the composition and function of National Judicial Appointments Commission.
Choose the correct answer from the following:
o: Both A and B are correct
A, B, C and D are correct
items.x: The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced GST and amended the Sixth and Seventh Schedules. Statement C is the 98th Amendment (2012, Art. 371J) and D the 99th (2014, NJAC).

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: In which of the following landmark cases, did the Supreme Court propound the doctrine of basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India
A.K. Gopalan vs State of Madras
State of Haryana vs Bhajan Lal
Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
items.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13 judges) propounded the basic structure doctrine; Maneka Gandhi and Gopalan are Art. 21 cases, Bhajan Lal is about quashing FIRs.

items.s: In the following case, Supreme Court of India gave a judgement that the Parliament has no power to amend the basic features of the Indian Constitution.
items.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but not its basic structure; Golaknath (1967) barred amending FRs altogether.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
items.s: Following Constitutional amendment Acts were declared as unconstitutional, except
items.x: Struck down (wholly or partly): 25th (second part of Art. 31C, Kesavananda), 32nd (Art. 371D(5), Sambamurthy 1987). Neither the 7th nor the 12th Amendment was ever declared unconstitutional, so two options fit 'except' – question defective.

items.s: The concept of "National rights" was emphasised by
items.x: 'National rights' is a misprint for natural rights: John Locke made the natural rights of life, liberty and property the basis of government; Dalton, Leacock and Bryce did not.

items.s: Who among the following proposed the theory of 'Civil Legitimacy'?
items.x: Unkeyed: 'civil legitimacy' is not a standard theory name. Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau all grounded the legitimacy of civil government in a social contract, and no source attributes the phrase to one of them, so no option can be fixed.

items.s: Who among the following got the Bharat Ratna Award before becoming the president of India?
o: Both Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Both Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam); it is added as option 5.
Two options qualify: Dr S. Radhakrishnan got the Bharat Ratna in 1954, before becoming President in 1962, and Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam got it in 1997, before becoming President in 2002 (official key: Radhakrishnan). Prasad (1962) and Giri (1975) got it after their terms, so the question is defective. (Moved to the President row.)

items.s: President of India with longest tenure
items.x: Dr Rajendra Prasad was President for about 12 years (1950-62), the longest tenure; he is the only President elected twice. (Moved to the President row.)

items.s: The book My Presidential Years was written by
items.x: 'My Presidential Years' was written by R. Venkataraman. (Moved to the President row.)

items.s:
Match the following
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer
List-I:
A. Chief Minister
B. President of India
C. Vice President
D. Governor
List-II: i. Head of the Nation ii. Head of the State Government iii. Constitutional Head of the State iv. Chairperson of Rajya Sabha
items.x: Chief Minister – head of the State government (ii); President – head of the nation (i); Vice-President – Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (iv); Governor – constitutional head of the State (iii) → A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii.

items.s: Among the following presidents of India, who was also the Secretary General of Non-Aligned Movement for some period?
items.x: Giani Zail Singh, as President (1982-87), headed the Non-Aligned Movement as its Chairman/Secretary-General from 1983 to 1986, after India hosted the 1983 New Delhi summit.

items.s: Who decides the salary and allowances of the President of India?
items.x: Article 59(4): the President's emoluments and allowances are determined by Parliament by law (now the President's Emoluments and Pension Act, 1951), not by the SC or the PM.

items.s: The President of India is eligible to seek re-election
items.x: Article 57: a person who holds or has held the office of President is eligible for re-election, with no limit on the number of terms.

items.s: Who is considered to be the first citizen of India?
items.x: The President is the first citizen of India and the symbol of the nation's unity; the VP, PM and Home Minister rank below.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: According to the Indian constitution who is the first citizen of the country?
items.x: The President is regarded as the first citizen of India; the Speaker, PM and CJI rank below in the order of precedence.

items.s: The Constitution of India does not expressly give any discretionary powers to the
items.x:
Printed key: Cabinet. Strictly the PM, the Cabinet and the President all lack express discretion; the books' contrast is Governor (express discretion, Art. 163) vs President (none), so the President is keyed.
Only the Governor is given express (constitutional) discretion (Art. 163(1)-(2)); the President has no constitutional discretion, only situational discretion. The PM and Cabinet are advisers and hold no discretionary powers in this sense either, but the question tests the Governor-President contrast, so 'President' is the better key.

items.s: The tenure of the Indian President is
items.x: The President holds office for five years from entering office (Art. 56).

items.s: The Elected Members of the legislative Assemblies of which Union Territories have right to vote in the election of President of India are
items.x: Article 54 (Explanation, 70th Amendment) includes the NCT of Delhi and Puducherry in the electoral college for the President. (Whether the UT of J&K's MLAs vote is unsettled.)

items.s: The Constitution of India does not contain any provision for the impeachment of –
items.x:
Most books and keys: the Governor. Strictly: the Constitution uses 'impeachment' only for the President (Art. 61); the VP (Art. 67(b)) and the CJI (Art. 124(4)) are 'removed', not impeached.
The Governor holds office during the President's pleasure (Art. 156) and has no impeachment procedure; the President is impeached (Art. 61), and the CJI and VP have removal procedures.

items.s: Who acts as returning officer for the election of Rashtrapati?
o: Secretary General, Lok Sabha and Secretary General, Rajya Sabha by rotation
items.x: For the Presidential election the ECI appoints the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha or of the Rajya Sabha as Returning Officer, by rotation (alternately) – not one of them always, nor the CEC.

items.s: In the matter of impeachment motion against the President in any of the two houses, the following is not correct
o: Not less than 1/4th of the members of the House shall sign on the notice
14 days notice needs to be given to the President
Not less than 1/2 of membership of the house shall pass the motion
The motion needs to be passed by both the Houses
items.x: Under Art. 61 the impeachment charge needs a notice signed by at least one-fourth of the House's members and 14 days' notice to the President, and must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership in each House – so 'not less than one-half' is not correct.

items.s: The President of India can be removed from office through
items.x: The President is removed only by impeachment under Art. 61 for violation of the Constitution. A no-confidence motion applies to the Council of Ministers, and there is no judicial removal.

items.s: A resolution for impeaching the president can be moved after at least fourteen days notice signed by
o: not less than 50 members of the house
not less than 1/3rd of the total number of members of the house
not less than 1/4th of the total number of members of the house
At least 100 members of Lok Sabha and 50 members of Rajya Sabha
items.x: Under Art. 61(2), the impeachment charge is preferred by a resolution moved after at least 14 days' notice signed by not less than one-fourth of the total members of the House.

items.s: Who is the former President of India who was referred to as the 'Messiah of the Downtrodden'?
items.x: K.R. Narayanan, India's first Dalit President (1997-2002), was hailed as a 'messiah of the downtrodden'; Shankar Dayal Sharma, Venkataraman and Sanjiva Reddy were not given this epithet.

items.s: Who was the sixth President of Independent India?
items.x: The sixth President was Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1977-82), after Rajendra Prasad, Radhakrishnan, Zakir Husain, V.V. Giri and Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.

items.s: Who was the second president of India? He is also a Bharat Ratna Award winner.
items.x: The second President was Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1962-67), awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954. V.V. Giri was the fourth President and Sanjiva Reddy the sixth; Abul Kalam Azad was never President.

items.s: The President of India who also held the office of the Speaker of Lok Sabha was
items.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Lok Sabha Speaker (1967-69, 1977) before becoming President in 1977; Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, V.V. Giri and K.R. Narayanan were not Speakers.

items.s: President of India from 25.7.1977 to 25.7.1982
items.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was President from 25 July 1977 to 25 July 1982; B.D. Jatti was acting President in 1977 and Zail Singh followed in 1982.

items.s: The formula by which the vote value of the member of a State Legislative Assembly decided in the election of the President of India.
o: Total voter population of the state / Total Elected Members of State Legislative Assembly x 1/1000
Total population of the state / Total Elected Members of State Legislative Assembly
Total voter population of the state / Total Elected Members of State Legislative Assembly
Total population of the state / Total Elected Members of State Legislative Assembly x 1/1000
items.x: Value of an MLA's vote = total population of the State ÷ elected MLAs × 1/1000 (1971 population); voter population is not used.

items.s:
The following is / are not voters in the Election of President of India

A. Vice-president of India

B. Elected Member of Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly

C. Elected Member of a State Legislative council

D. Nominated member of Rajya Sabha
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (A, C & D); it is added as option 5.
The Vice-President (A), elected MLCs (C) and nominated Rajya Sabha members (D) do not vote; elected MLAs of J&K (B) do (Art. 54, then a State; the UT Assembly too since 2019). Every printed option wrongly includes B.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: On what date in 2017 are next elections for the post of President of India going to be held?
items.x: The 2017 Presidential election was held on 17 July 2017 (counting 20 July); Ram Nath Kovind won.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer in Women & CW 2012
items.s: According to which Article of Indian Constitution there is no limit on the number of times a person can become the President
items.x: Art. 57: a President is eligible for re-election, with no limit on terms. Art. 54 = election, 55 = manner, 56 = term.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: The birth place of President Ram Nath Kovind is
items.x: President Ram Nath Kovind was born at Paraunkh village, Kanpur Dehat district (UP), on 1 Oct 1945.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: In the context of election to the post of President, the following post held by contestant is treated as "Office of Profit".
items.x: Under Art. 58 the offices of President, Vice-President, Governor and Minister are not offices of profit for the presidential election, so the CAG's post is one.

items.src: APPSC Common GS for ADTP, ADILIS, IFS, ATT 2012
items.s: Who acts as the President of India when neither the President nor the Vice-President are available?
items.x: Under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969, when both the President's and Vice-President's offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India (or, failing him, the senior-most SC judge) acts as President.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: When President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by the:
items.x: Under Art. 61 impeachment charges are preferred by either House of Parliament – not by the CBI, CVC or NIA.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017
items.s: What is true about the impeachment of the President?
o: It is quasi-Judicial as well as Political
items.x: Impeachment of the President (Art. 61) is a quasi-judicial procedure in Parliament with a political character – one House charges, the other investigates.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: The President of India is a/an:
items.x: The office of the President is created by the Constitution (Art. 52), so the President is a constitutional authority, not a statutory or merely administrative one.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economics & Statistics Servic
items.s: When both President and Vice President are absent, who will perform their duties?
items.x: When both the President and the Vice-President are absent, the Chief Justice of India (or else the senior-most SC judge) discharges the President's functions (President (Discharge of Functions) Act 1969). Moved.

items.s: Who among the following serves as the constitutional head of India?
items.x: The President is the constitutional (nominal) head of India; the Prime Minister is the real executive head. Moved to the President row.

items.s: President addressed joint session of two houses of Indian Parliament on
items.x: President Pratibha Patil addressed the joint session of Parliament opening the Budget Session on 12 March 2012. (President; moved.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Who is the President of India as of February 2020?
items.x: Ram Nath Kovind was President from 25 July 2017 to 25 July 2022, so in February 2020. (Off-topic PYQ: moved to Polity – President.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017
items.s: What is not true about President's power to grant pardon?
o: It is exercised on the advice of the Central Government
He can pardon a Court Martialed convict
It's not subject to Judicial Review
He can scrutinize the evidence on record
items.x: Not true: pardon is subject to limited judicial review (Epuru Sudhakar 2006; mala fide, arbitrary or irrelevant grounds). It is exercised on the Union government's advice, covers court-martial cases, and the President may examine evidence afresh (Kehar Singh).

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: Who among the following can pardon punishments of sentences inflicted by court martial?
items.x: Only the President can pardon sentences by a court martial (Art. 72(1)(a)); the Governor cannot. (No printed key.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
items.s: President of India has certain powers of pardon. In relation to these powers choose the wrong answer
o: Pardon means absolve the offender from all punishments
Reprieve means a stay of execution of a sentence and conviction
Remission means reduce the amount of sentence without changing its character
Respite means changing one punishment to other
items.x: Respite means awarding a lesser sentence for special reasons; changing one punishment for another is commutation, so 4 is wrong.

items.s: Regarding the pardoning powers, choose the correct answer.
o: Both the President and Governor can pardon a death sentence
The only authority for pardoning a sentence of death is the President
The Supreme Court can pardon a death sentence
The Governor can pardon a death sentence in his state
items.x: Only the President can pardon a death sentence; the Governor can suspend, remit or commute it but not pardon it.

items.s: With regard to power of pardon available to President and Governer under the Constitution?
o: The power of the President and Governor are one and same
For Offences under concurrent lists, without the role of State, President alone has the pardoning power
The only authority for pardoning a sentence of death is the President
As regard suspension and remission, the Governor does not have concurrent jurisdiction with the President
items.x: The only authority for pardoning a death sentence is the President; the Governor shares the power to suspend and remit, and the powers are not the same.

items.s:
Match the following:
List I:

(a) Reprieve

(b) Respite

(c) Remission

(d) Commutation
List II:

I. Reduce the amount of sentence without changing its character

II. Substitute one form of punishment for other of a lighter character

III. Awarding lesser sentence

IV. A stay of execution of sentence
items.x: Reprieve = stay of execution (IV), respite = lesser sentence (III), remission = reduce amount without changing character (I), commutation = lighter form (II).

items.s: Which of the following doesn't consists in the power 'To Pardon' of President? i. Pardon ii. Commutation iii. Remission iv. Respite v. Reprieve vi. Detention vii. Continuation
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (vi vii); it is added as option 5.
Art. 72 lists pardon, commutation, remission, respite and reprieve (i-v); 'detention' and 'continuation' (vi, vii) are not part of it. None printed is correct, so 'vi vii' is added (printed key: i).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: The ____ can grant a pardon to or reduce the sentence of a convicted person for one time, particularly in cases involving punishment of death.
items.x: Under Art. 72 the President can pardon, commute or remit sentences, including a death sentence; the PM, CJI and VP have no such power.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: To which Bill of the Parliament, assent was not granted by President A P J Abdul Kalam?
items.x: President Kalam returned the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Amendment Bill, 2006 (the 'Office of Profit Bill') in May 2006; Parliament re-passed it and he then had to assent.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: Under which circumstances of the following the Indian Constitution does provides for the promulgation of an ordinance?
o: When either Speaker of Lok Sabha or Chairman of Rajya Sabha is satisfied that discussion on a pending Bill is not possible due to circumstances prevailing in the House
When the President comes to the conclusion that Parliament is not likely to pass a Bill pending before it before prorogation of Parliament
If at any time, except when both Houses of Parliament are in session, the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action
If the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action and no ordinance has been promulgated in the previous six months
items.x: Art. 123: the President may promulgate an ordinance 'if at any time, except when both Houses of Parliament are in session, the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action'; the other options are not in the Article.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screening T
items.s: Which of the following bills was returned by President K.R. Narayanan?

items.x:
Most books and keys: the Bill on pension to MPs. Strictly: that Bill (Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Amendment) Bill, 1991) was vetoed by R. Venkataraman, not K.R. Narayanan, who returned Cabinet advice on President's Rule (UP 1997, Bihar 1998) (Laxmikanth ch.18).
Exam keys give the MPs' pension Bill. Of the options, the Postal Bill was Zail Singh's pocket veto (1986); the MPs' pension Bill is the only one tied to a President's veto.

The Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes
items.x: The GNCTD (Amendment) Ordinance of 19 May 2023 nullified the SC Constitution Bench ruling of 11 May 2023 giving Delhi's elected government control over services; it became the GNCTD (Amendment) Act, 2023.

items.x: The Vice-President is elected by PR-STV (Art. 66), like the President, Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council members; Lok Sabha, Assembly members and the Speaker are not.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

No specific ground is required for removal of vice president

Only after seeking opinion of Solicitor General
Only after seeking opinion of Attorney General
items.x: The proviso to Art. 74(1) (44th Amendment) lets the President require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once, at his own discretion – no opinion of the SC, AG or SG is needed; he is bound by the advice tendered after reconsideration.

items.src: APPSC Junior Steno's in AP Vaidhya Vidhana Parishad 2012

items.x:

The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members of both Houses of Parliament (Art. 66) – the closest option; not by one House or by the people.

items.s: Vice-President of India is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of the members of
items.x: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of the members of both Houses of Parliament – Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Art. 66).

items.x: The Vice-President is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament (Art. 66) – not by the people or the LS alone.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-

12% of the number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the number of members of the Lok Sabha
20% of the number of members of the Lok Sabha

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-

o: For a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office
For a term of six years from the date on which he enters upon his office
For a term of five years from the date of election
For a term of six years from the date of election
items.x: Art. 67: the Vice-President holds office for five years from the date on which he enters upon his office (not from the date of election; six years is the Rajya Sabha member's term).

items.x: The Vice-President holds office for five years from the date he enters office (Art. 67).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017

Emergency powers that can be used at his own discretion
Power to veto Supreme Court decisions

All members (elected and nominated) of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated (Art. 66). 'Elected members' only is wrong, and State Assemblies have no role (they vote only for the President).

items.s: Civil Aviation Minister of India is
items.x:

Ajit Singh (RLD) was Civil Aviation Minister from 18 Dec 2011 to May 2014, so in 2012 the answer was Ajit Singh (now K. Ram Mohan Naidu, since June 2024).

items.x: The 44th Amendment lets the President return ministerial advice once for reconsideration; the advice binds after that.

items.s:
With reference to Union Government, consider the following statements:

b. The Union Cabinet Secretariat operates under the direction of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

items.x: Art. 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, not to Parliament as a whole or the Rajya Sabha.

To provide representation to the aged and wise
To protect the interests of States
