items.s: The house which is presided over by a non-member of the house
items.x: The Rajya Sabha is presided over by the Vice-President, its ex-officio Chairman, who is not a member of the House; the Speaker, Council Chairman and Assembly Speaker are members of their Houses.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: From the given below, under which Article of the Constitution, the Council of State (Rajya Sabha) has a Chairman and Deputy Chairman
items.x: Art. 89 – the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman and the RS elects a Deputy Chairman; Arts. 108 and 109 are joint sitting and Money Bill procedure, Art. 91 is the Deputy Chairman acting as Chairman.

items.s: Which of the following statements is true about the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
o: He is a member of the Upper House
He is elected by the Rajya Sabha
He is elected by both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
He is appointed by the President of India
items.x: The RS Chairman is the Vice-President, elected by an electoral college of members of both Houses (Art. 66); he is not a member of the RS and is not appointed by the President.

items.s: Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the speaker of
items.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Speaker of the 4th Lok Sabha (1967-69) and again of the 6th (1977), resigning each time.

items.s: First time in the history of the Upper House, four women members were nominated to the panel of Vice Chair Persons. Who was not in the list?
items.x: In July 2023 the RS Chairman nominated P.T. Usha, S. Phangnon Konyak, Fauzia Khan and Sulata Deo to the panel of Vice-Chairpersons – Priyanka Chaturvedi was not among them.

items.s: What is the quorum for Lok Sabha meetings?
items.x: The quorum of either House is one-tenth of its total membership (Art. 100(3)), which for the Lok Sabha is about 55 members.

items.s: The time gap between two sessions of Parliament is not more than:
items.x: Art. 85: not more than six months may pass between two sessions of Parliament (Art. 174 has the same rule for State Legislatures).

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: The time period between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next session shall be less than?
items.x: Art. 85(1): six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next.

items.s: What is the constitutional quorum for a House of Parliament?
items.x: Under Article 100, the quorum of either House is one-tenth of its total membership.

items.s:
Assertion (A): The gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months.
Reason (R): Article 85 implies that Parliament must have at least two sessions in a year.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: Both are true: Article 85 bars a gap of more than six months between sessions, and so Parliament must meet at least twice a year. R is a consequence of A, not its explanation.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: Who moves the Bills initiated by Government in the Lok Sabha?
items.x: A Government Bill is introduced and piloted by the minister in charge of the subject. The Speaker presides, and the Leader of the House manages business but does not move every Bill.

items.s: The differences between the two houses of parliament are resolved through
o: A joint session of the two houses
A joint committee of the two houses specially constituted for this purpose
A committee under the leadership of Minister for parliamentary Affairs
items.x: A deadlock between the Houses on an ordinary (or financial) Bill is resolved by a joint sitting under Art. 108, presided over by the Speaker.

items.s: How many readings would a Bill go through in a House of the Parliament before it becomes an Act?
items.x: A Bill passes through three readings in each House (introduction/first reading, second reading with clause-by-clause consideration, third reading) before it goes to the other House and the President.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Service
items.s: How many readings would a Bill go through in a House of the Parliament before it becomes an Act?
items.x: A Bill passes through three readings in each House (first, second and third reading) before it becomes an Act on the President's assent.

items.src: APPSC Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Serv
items.s: In case of deadlock between the two houses of Parliament with regard to a bill, who summons the joint sitting?
items.x: Under Art. 108 the President summons the joint sitting of the two Houses to resolve a deadlock over a Bill (other than a Money or Constitution Amendment Bill); the Speaker only presides.

items.s: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statements is not correct?
o: A bill shall be deemed to be Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of money out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
items.x: Art. 110(1) covers the custody of the CFI or Contingency Fund and appropriation out of the CFI; 'appropriation out of the Contingency Fund' is not a Money Bill matter, so (c) is not correct (UPSC key c).

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: An Act is a
items.x: An Act is a law (statute) passed by the legislature; a Bill becomes an Act after it is passed and receives assent.

items.s: With reference to the Indian Parliament, which one of the following is not correct?
o: The Appropriation Bill must be passed by both Houses of Parliament before it can be enacted into law.
No money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under the appropriation made
Finance Bill is required for proposing new taxes but no another Bill/Act is required for making changes in
No Money Bill can be introduced except on the recommendation of the President.
items.x: (c) is not correct: changes in the rates of existing taxes also need a Finance Bill/Act (no tax without authority of law, Art. 265). The Appropriation Bill is deemed passed by both Houses even if the RS only recommends, and (b), (d) are correct. (Some keys give (a).)

items.s: By which Bill the Government propose collection of revenues for a year?
items.x: The Finance Bill gives effect to the Budget's tax proposals, through which the Government collects revenue for the year.

items.s: Which rule of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure provides for the presentation of the budget to the Lok Sabha in two or more parts?
items.x: Rule 213 of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure allows the Budget to be presented in two or more parts, each part being dealt with as if it were the Budget. Rule 204 fixes the day of presentation and Rule 205 bars discussion on that day.

items.s: Which of the following proposals is related to the Union Budget?
items.x: Cut motions are moved on demands for grants in the Union Budget (policy cut, economy cut, token cut). Censure, calling attention and adjournment motions are not tied to the Budget.

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: Which article of the Constitution mandates presentation of Budget before the parliament?
items.x: Article 112 requires the President to lay the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) before both Houses; Art. 151 = CAG reports, Art. 111 = assent to Bills, Art. 152 = definition of State.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
items.s:
DIRECTIONS: The following question consists of two statements -
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R). Answer the question by selecting the appropriate option given below:
Assertion (A): Money from the Contingency Fund of India can be withdrawn without prior approval from Parliament.
Reason (R): The Contingency Fund of India is an imprest fund at the disposal of the President for meeting unforeseen expenditures.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are false.
items.x: Both true and R explains A: the Contingency Fund of India (Art. 267) is an imprest at the President's disposal, so advances are made from it without prior Parliamentary approval, to be authorised later.

items.s: What is it called when all remaining demands are put to vote without discussion on the last allotted day?
items.x: The guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote without discussion on the last day allotted.

items.s: To what amount does a policy cut motion reduce a demand for grant?
items.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 to show disapproval of the policy; a token cut reduces it by Rs 100.

items.s: On which date was the first Union Budget of independent India presented?
items.x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.

items.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Vote on Account?
items.x: Article 116 provides for the Vote on Account, a grant in advance for part of the year until the Budget is passed.

items.s: Which body prepares the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) of the Union?
o: Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
items.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112).

items.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Cut motion)
A. Policy cut
B. Economy cut
C. Token cut
List-II (Reduction of the demand)
1. By Rs 100
2. To Re 1
3. By a specified amount
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1, an economy cut by a specified amount and a token cut by Rs 100.

items.s: Which of the following pairs of cut motions is correctly matched?
o: Policy cut – Reduction of the demand by Rs 100
Token cut – Reduction of the demand to Re 1
Economy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
Policy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
items.x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1 and a token cut by Rs 100.

items.s: By how much does a token cut motion reduce a demand for grant?
items.x: A token cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 to air a specific grievance; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1.

items.s: How many members are there in the 'Committee of Privileges' of the Lok Sabha?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (15); it is added as option 5.
The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker (the Rajya Sabha committee has 10). None of 10, 12, 14 or 16 is right.

items.s: For which committee of the Parliament, the Comptroller and Auditor General renders his services?
items.x: The CAG acts as the friend, philosopher and guide of the Public Accounts Committee and helps it examine his audit reports.

items.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
items.s: The Public Accounts Committee became a parliamentary committee in India in which year?
items.x: The PAC was first set up in 1921 under the GoI Act, 1919, and became a parliamentary committee under the Speaker in 1950.

items.s: Which Parliamentary Committee in India is normally Chaired by a prominent member of the Opposition?
items.x: Since 1967, by convention, the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been a member of the Opposition.

items.src: APPSC NTR Health University Jr. Assistant 2012
items.s: The oldest Financial Committee of Indian Parliament is
items.x: The Public Accounts Committee (1921) is the oldest financial committee. The Estimates Committee took its present form in 1950 and the COPU dates from 1964.

items.s: Which of the following is Financial Committee of Parliament?
items.x: The financial committees are the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings. Privileges and Government Assurances are not financial committees.

items.s: The Comptroller and Auditor-General is intimately connected with the .... of Parliament.
items.x: The CAG's audit reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee, which the CAG assists.

items.s:
Which of the following committees do not have members of the Rajya Sabha as members?

A. Public Accounts Committee

B. Estimates Committee

C. Committee on Public Undertakings
items.x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. The PAC and COPU each have 15 LS and 7 RS members.

items.s: The important permanent financial committees set up by the Parliament to exercise effective control over general and financial administration of the country are Public Accounts Committee, Esti mates Committee, Departmental Committees and
o: Committee on Finances of State Government
items.x: The financial committees are the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings.

items.s: Committee on Public undertakings is a:
items.x: The Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) is a parliamentary financial committee of 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS).

items.s: Which pair is incorrect regarding the appointment of Chairpersons of Parliamentary committees constituted by the Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha for the year 2024-25?
o: Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and
Committee on Welfare of Other Backward Classes –
items.x: For 2024-25 Baijayant Panda chairs the Committee on Public Undertakings, not the Estimates Committee, which Sanjay Jaiswal heads. K.C. Venugopal heads the PAC.

items.s:
Which of the following are Financial Committees of Indian Parliament
(A) Estimates Committee
(B) Public Accounts Committee
(C) Committee on Public Undertakings
(D) Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowance for Members of Parliament
Select the correct answer using code given below:
Codes:
items.x: The financial committees are the Estimates Committee, the PAC and the COPU. The Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs is not one.

items.s: Which is largest committee of the Indian Parliament?
items.x: With 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, the Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee.

items.s: The reason for the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament being headed by a member of the opposition party in the Lok Sabha is
items.x: The PAC has been chaired by an Opposition member since 1967 by convention, not by a rule or an order.

items.s: The name of the committee set up by the Rajya Sabha in 1992 to prescribe a code of conduct for the proper behaviour of its members during the meetings of the House was
items.x: The body that prescribes and enforces a code of conduct for members is the Ethics Committee, constituted in the Rajya Sabha on 4 March 1997 after the idea was mooted in the early 1990s. The stem's '1992' is loose.

items.s: How many members are from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha respectively in the Parliamentary Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
items.x: The Committee on the Welfare of SCs and STs has 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: How many members are from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha respectively in the Parliamentary Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
items.x: The Committee on the Welfare of SCs and STs has 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes of the Parliament of India:
1. Although members of this Committee are elected from both Houses of Parliament, the Chairperson of this Committee is appointed by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. Twenty members are elected by the Rajya Sabha and ten members by the Lok Sabha.
3. No Minister, except for the Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, is eligible to be a member of this Committee. Indian Polity: Organs of the State PMF IAS IP – 54
4. Members are elected for a fixed term of two years from the date they enter their office. Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
o: There is only one correct statement.
There is only one correct statement, that is statement 2.
items.x: All four statements are false. The Speaker appoints the chair; the LS elects 20 and the RS 10; no minister may be a member; the term does not exceed one year.

items.s: The Joint Parliamentary Committee set up for probing the 2G spectrum issue, consists of
o: 15 members from each of the two Houses
20 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha
18 members from Lok Sabha and 12 members from
16 members from Lok Sabha and 14 members from
items.x: The 2G spectrum JPC (2011, chairman P.C. Chacko) had 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: The Consultative Committee of Members of Parliament for Railway Zones is constituted by which of the following?
items.x: Consultative committees, including the informal consultative committees of MPs for Railway Zones, are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

items.s: Which of the following is a Parliamentary Committee relating to delegation of power to make rules and regulations to the Executive?
items.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks whether the executive's delegated rules and regulations stay within the powers conferred by Parliament.

items.s: Public Accounts Committee 2. Estimate Committee 3. Committee on Public Undertakings Select the correct answer from the code given below :
items.x: The PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are all financial committees.

items.s: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is the
items.x:
Most keys: Leader of the Opposition. Strictly: a member of the Opposition chosen by the Speaker (since 1967), not necessarily the LoP (Laxmikanth ch.24).
By convention since 1967 the PAC Chairman is from the Opposition, appointed by the Speaker – commonly keyed as 'Leader of the Opposition'.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economics & Statistical Servi
items.s: One of the following Committees is not Joint Parliamentary Committee for Public Sector Institution
items.x: The Estimates Committee has only Lok Sabha members, so it is not a joint committee; the PAC and the Committee on Public Undertakings are joint (the other options are loosely worded).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: When was the Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha constituted?
items.x: The Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha was constituted by the Chairman on 4 March 1997; it began functioning in May 1997.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Accounts Committee?
o: A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
It has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
Its members are elected annually by PR-STV.
Its Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
items.x: Ministers cannot be members of the Public Accounts Committee.

items.s: On whose recommendation was the Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) created?
items.x: COPU came from the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation; John Mathai's recommendation gave the Estimates Committee its present form in 1950.

items.s: In which year was the Public Accounts Committee first set up?
items.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919; it examines the CAG's audit reports.

items.s: Which committee is described as the “Continuous economy committee”?
items.x: The Estimates Committee is known as the “Continuous economy committee.”

items.s: Which parliamentary committee has 30 members drawn from the Lok Sabha only and is the largest parliamentary committee?
items.x: The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee, with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. The PAC and Public Undertakings Committee have 22 members each.

items.s: Since 1967, the Chairman of which committee has been appointed from the Opposition?
items.x: The Speaker has appointed the PAC Chairman from the Opposition since 1967; the Estimates Committee Chairman comes from the ruling party.

items.s: For what term are members of the three Financial Committees of Parliament elected?
items.x: Members of the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees are elected by PR-STV for one year.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Estimates Committee – examination of budget estimates
Public Accounts Committee – scrutiny of public-sector undertaking accounts and commercial soundness
Estimates Committee – suggesting economy in administration
Committee on Public Undertakings – scrutiny of PSU accounts
items.x: The PAC scrutinises appropriation accounts and wasteful expenditure; PSU accounts are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings.

items.s: What is the status of the recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee?
o: binding once approved by the Speaker
items.x: PAC recommendations are not binding; the PAC checks spending within the scope of the demand and examines execution, not policy.

items.s: How many members does the Public Accounts Committee have?
items.x: The PAC has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha; 30 from the Lok Sabha only is the Estimates Committee.

items.s: On whose recommendation did the Estimates Committee take its present form in 1950?
items.x: The Estimates Committee dates from 1921 and took its present form in 1950 on John Mathai's recommendation; Krishna Menon is linked to COPU.

items.s: Who headed the Public Accounts Committee of the 18th Lok Sabha?
items.x: K.C. Venugopal heads the PAC of the 18th Lok Sabha (also for 2026–27).

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of Parliament?
o: Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs
items.x: The Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs is not a financial committee; the PAC, Estimates and COPU are.

items.s: To which House does the Public Accounts Committee submit its report?
o: Both Houses in a joint sitting
Neither House; it reports to the CAG
items.x: The PAC reports to the Lok Sabha through the Speaker; a copy is laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: How many members does the Committee on Public Undertakings have?
items.x: Like the PAC, the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: From which party is the Chairman of the Estimates Committee usually appointed?
o: Any party in the Rajya Sabha
items.x: The Estimates Committee chair comes from the ruling party, whereas the PAC chair has come from the Opposition since 1967.

items.s: Of which committee is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha the ex-officio Chairperson?
items.x: The Speaker is ex-officio Chairperson of the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees.

items.s: How many members does the Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges have?
items.x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha committee has 10.

items.s: What is a committee on a Bill made up of members of both Houses called?
items.x: A Joint Committee has members of both Houses and is formed on a motion; a Select Committee has members of one House only.

items.s: Which parliamentary committee regulates the timetable of the House's business?
items.x: The Business Advisory Committee sets the timetable; the Rules Committee proposes rule changes and the Assurances Committee tracks Ministers' promises.

items.s: How many members does the Committee on Subordinate Legislation have in each House?
items.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation has 15 members in each House, and Ministers cannot sit on it.

items.s: Which of the following statements regarding the 2G Spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee is incorrect?
o: It consisted of 15 Lok Sabha members and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
It was chaired by P.C. Chacko.
It included 20 Lok Sabha members and 10 Rajya Sabha members.
items.x: Option B is incorrect: the 2G JPC, chaired by P.C. Chacko, had 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. The 15 + 7 split belongs to the PAC.

items.s: Who appoints the Chairpersons of Department-related Standing Committees?
o: The Prime Minister for Lok Sabha committees and the Vice-President for Rajya Sabha committees
The respective ministers heading the departments concerned
The Speaker for Lok Sabha committees and the Chairman for Rajya Sabha committees
items.x: The Speaker appoints the Chairpersons of Lok Sabha DRSCs, while the Chairman appoints the Chairpersons of Rajya Sabha DRSCs.

items.s: Ministers are barred from the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Petitions mainly because these committees:
o: consist only of Rajya Sabha members
meet only when Parliament is not in session
items.x: These committees, along with COPU and the Subordinate Legislation Committee, scrutinise the government, so Ministers are kept out.

items.s: In which year were Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs) set up?
items.x: DRSCs were set up in 1993; there are 24 (16 Lok Sabha and 8 Rajya Sabha), each with 31 members and a quorum of 11.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ad hoc committees of Parliament?
o: Inquiry committees may be set up by a motion or by the Speaker or Chairman.
The Committee on MPLADS is an example of an inquiry committee.
They continue permanently after completing their assigned task.
Select and Joint Committees on Bills are ad hoc committees.
items.x: Ad hoc committees end when their assigned task is completed.

items.s: How are committees such as the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings described?
items.x: These committees, along with the Department-related Standing Committees, are described as watchdogs over the executive.

items.s: Which parliamentary committee is described as the 'Ombudsman' of Parliament, examining petitions on bills and on matters of general public interest?
items.x: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions on bills and matters of public interest and is called Parliament's 'Ombudsman'. The Committee on Government Assurances tracks ministers' promises, the Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks the exercise of delegated rule-making powers, and the Committee of Privileges examines breaches of privilege.

items.s: Who among the following cannot be a member of the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs?
o: A member of the ruling party
items.x: No minister can be a member of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

items.s: In which year was the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee first constituted as an ad hoc committee?
items.x: It was first set up as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000 and made permanent in 2015.

items.s: In which year was the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee made a permanent committee?
items.x: The Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015; it cannot take up matters pending in court.

items.s: Which of the following statements about the Committee on Petitions is incorrect?
o: The Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions has 15 members.
Ministers may be elected or nominated as members of the Committee on Petitions.
It examines petitions and representations submitted to the House.
The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions has 10 members.
items.x: Option B is incorrect: Ministers cannot be members of the Petitions Committee. It has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: Who constitutes Consultative Committees of MPs for particular ministries?
items.x: Consultative Committees are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.

items.s: What does the Committee on Papers Laid on the Table primarily check?
o: The estimates contain alternative taxation policies
Public sector undertakings follow commercial principles
Papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, comply with the relevant requirements
items.x: The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table checks papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, for compliance.

items.s: How many Department-related Standing Committees are there?
items.x: There are 24 DRSCs, 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha, each with 31 members.

items.s: Each Department-related Standing Committee has how many members?
items.x: Each DRSC has 31 members, 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, with a quorum of 11.

items.s: Which committee examines whether Ministers' promises in the House are implemented?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
items.x: The Committee on Government Assurances watches Ministers' promises till they are implemented.

items.s: In which year was the Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee constituted?
items.x: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee was set up on 4 March 1997; the Lok Sabha had an ad hoc one in 2000, made permanent in 2015.

items.s: How many members does the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have?
items.x: The Committee has 30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
1. It has 20 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. A Minister can be a member of this Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: It has 30 members (20 LS + 10 RS) and no Minister can be a member; its chair is appointed by the Speaker.

items.s: In which year was the Committee on Empowerment of Women, with members from both Houses, set up?
items.x: The Committee on Empowerment of Women was set up for both Houses on 29 April 1997.

items.s: What is a parliamentary committee on a Bill made up of members of one House only called?
items.x: A Select Committee has members of one House; a Joint Committee has members of both Houses.

items.s: How many of the 24 Department-related Standing Committees function under the Lok Sabha?
items.x: Of the 24 DRSCs, 16 are under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.

items.s: Who was the chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the 2G spectrum issue (2011)?
items.x: The 30-member 2G JPC (20 LS + 10 RS) was chaired by P.C. Chacko.

items.s: To which body was the FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 sent in August 2026?
o: A Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
items.x: The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

items.s: How many members does the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions have?
items.x: The Committee on Petitions has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.

items.x: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (anti-defection, Tenth Schedule) first brought the term 'political party' into the Constitution.

items.x: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) banning floor-crossing by legislators. The RP Act, NSA and MISA do not. Moved to the anti-defection row.

items.x: The Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985) deals with disqualification on grounds of defection – the anti-defection law; J&K's status was under Art. 370.

items.s: The most important factor responsible for the decline of Parliament is
o: The growth of the Committee System
items.x: The paper treats the growth of delegated legislation as the main cause of Parliament's decline: the executive makes most detailed law under delegated powers. The committee system strengthens Parliament.

items.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, what proportion of Bills were referred to parliamentary committees?
items.x: Only 16% of Bills in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees; the corresponding figure for the 15th Lok Sabha was 71%.

items.s: What share of Bills was referred to parliamentary committees in the 15th Lok Sabha?
items.x: 71% of Bills went to committees in the 15th Lok Sabha, against only 16% in the 17th.

items.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, for about what share of its scheduled time did Question Hour function?
items.x: In the 17th Lok Sabha, Question Hour ran for only about 60% of its time.

items.s:
Two statements are given below, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as
Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In a parliamentary form of government it is not the lower house which controls the executive but the executive which controls the house.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is constituted from within the legislature.
Choose the correct answer from among the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: In the parliamentary form the executive is collectively responsible to and controlled by the lower house (Art. 75(3)), so A as a statement of the system is false; R is true – the Council of Ministers is drawn from the legislature.

items.s: What is a system with a few members and under the control of a group called?
items.x: Rule by a few members under the control of a group is oligarchy, which this option calls "minority system of governance". Gerontocracy is rule by the old, and anarchy is the absence of government.

items.s: When the same person is appointed as a Governor of two or more States, the emoluments and allowances payable to the Governor shall be –
o: As expressed wish of the Governor
As decided by the Home Ministry
It shall be allocated among the States in such
items.x: Art. 158(3A): when one person is Governor of two or more States, his emoluments are allocated among the States in such proportion as the President by order determines.

items.s: The term of office of a Governor of a State is
items.x: A Governor holds office for five years (Art. 156), subject to the President's pleasure.

items.s: The Governor of a State in India is responsible to the
items.x: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156(1)) and is thus answerable to him, not to the State Legislature or Council of Ministers.

items.s: The Governor is impeached through
items.x: The Constitution provides no impeachment for a Governor; he holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156). Only the President is impeached (Art. 61).

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: What Constitutional Amendment Act allows the same person to be appointed as Governor of two or more States?
items.x: The 7th Amendment Act, 1956 added the proviso to Art. 153 so that the same person can be Governor of two or more States.

items.s:
Two statements are given below; one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as
Reason (R):
Assertion (A): One person cannot be appointed as Governor for more than one State in India
Reason (R): Article 153 of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Governor for each State.
Choose the correct answer from among the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: The 7th Amendment (1956) allows one person to be Governor of two or more States, so A is false; Article 153 does say there shall be a Governor for each State, so R is true.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
items.s: What is "Composite floor test" in case of voting in a State Assembly?
o: Voting in the Assembly as directed by the Speaker when there is more than one person staking claim to form government and majority is not clear.
Voting in the Assembly as directed by the Governor when there is more than one person staking claim to form Government and majority is not clear.
Voting in the Assembly to approve different bills at one time.
Voting in the Assembly where in Legislators from Government and opposition sit in a mingled fashion and vote in pairs.
items.x: A composite floor test is held when more than one person stakes claim to form the government and the majority is unclear; the Governor calls the Assembly to decide by vote who has the majority (as in Jagdambika Pal, 1998).

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Panchayat Secretary Grade-VI Digi
items.s: Governor of a State can be removed by
o: The Union Government at the request of the Chief Minister
items.x: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156) and can be removed by the President; there is no impeachment by the State Legislature.

items.s: The Article of the Constitution that discusses removal of the Governor is:
items.x: Article 156 deals with the Governor's term of office and removal at the pleasure of the President. Art. 155 is appointment, 157 qualifications, 158 conditions of office.

items.s: The normal term of a state Governor's office is
o: Dependent on the tenure of the state legislators.
items.x: A Governor holds office for five years from the date he enters upon it (Art. 156), though he serves during the President's pleasure; the term is not tied to the legislature.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: At which place was the 50th Governors Conference held in November 2019?
items.x: The 50th Conference of Governors was held at Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, on 23-24 November 2019.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assts. in Inter Board (APPSC Key) 2012

items.x: The Constitution sets no limit on the number of terms: a person may be appointed Governor any number of times (Art. 155-156).

items.s: A person may be appointed as a Governor for
items.x: There is no constitutional bar on reappointment, so a person may be appointed Governor for any number of terms.

items.s: Smt. Draupadi Murmu was worked as Governor of which State?
items.x: Droupadi Murmu was Governor of Jharkhand (2015-2021), its first woman Governor, before becoming President in 2022.

items.x:
Bandaru Dattatreya's term ended in July 2025 — now Prof. Ashim Kumar Ghosh is Governor of Haryana (since 21 July 2025) (lokbhavan.haryana.gov.in, search result)
Bandaru Dattatreya was Governor of Haryana (July 2021 – July 2025), so he was the answer in 2022 (now Prof. Ashim Kumar Ghosh, since 21 July 2025).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
items.s: In relation to council of ministers of a state, choose the wrong statement out of the following?
o: A council of ministers need not advise the Governor on all matters
Even after the dissolution of Legislature, council of ministers exists to advise the Governor
Even after the resignation of the chief minister, council of ministers exists to advise the Governor
Even after the imposition of the President Rule in state under Article 356 also council of ministers exist to advise the Governor
items.x: Wrong statement: under President's Rule the State Council of Ministers is dismissed, so none exists to advise the Governor. The Council continues (as caretaker) after dissolution or the CM's resignation, and need not advise on discretionary matters.

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Village Agriculture Assistant 202
items.s: The salaries and allowances of the members of the Council of Ministers in a State are determined by
o: The Governor in consultation with the President
items.x: Art. 164(5): salaries and allowances of State Ministers are determined by the State Legislature by law – not the Governor, Parliament or the President.

items.s: Who appoints the Chief Minister of a State?
o: The Governor in consultation with the Speaker
items.x: Art. 164(1): the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor – not the Speaker or the President, and no consultation with the Speaker is required.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State cannot exceed ___ of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
items.x: Art. 164(1A) (91st Amendment, 2003): Ministers including the CM cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Assembly (minimum 12).

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: ___ provides that in the States of Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha there shall be a Minister in charge of tribal welfare who may, in addition, be in charge of the welfare of the Scheduled Castes and backward classes or any other work.
items.x: The proviso to Art. 164(1) requires a Minister for tribal welfare in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha (Bihar dropped by the 94th Amendment, 2006).

P. Balaraju was AP's Minister for Tribal Welfare in the Kiran Kumar Reddy ministry (c. 2010-14), when this question was set.

items.s:
Select the Constitutional Duties of the Chief Minister from the following by using the code given below:
1. The Chief Minister communicates to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers related to the administration of the affairs of the state.
2. The Chief Minister communicates to the Governor the proposals for legislation.
3. The Chief Minister participates in the meetings of National Development Council.
4. The Chief Minister submits for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which decision has been taken by a Minister but which has not been considered by the council if the Governor requires.
Code:
items.x: Art. 167 duties: communicate Cabinet decisions and proposals for legislation to the Governor (1, 2) and, if the Governor requires, submit a Minister's decision to the Council (4). NDC participation (3) is not a constitutional duty.

items.s: Which one of the following statements about the Chief Minister is not correct ?
o: He is normally selected by the Governor
He is formally appointed by the Governor
He is chosen by the members of the majority party in
His continuance in office depends upon many factors
items.x: Not correct: the CM is not 'selected' by the Governor – he is chosen by the majority party in the Assembly and only formally appointed by the Governor (Art. 164(1)).

items.s:
In the following questions, there are two statements. One is labelled as
Assertion (A) and other is labelled as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : The courts are barred from enquiring into the advice rendered by the ministers to the Governor.
Reason (R) : There is no provision in the Indian Constitution for the system of legal responsibility of the ministers in the States. In the context of the above two statements which of the following is correct?
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
items.x:
Official key: (a). Strictly, A rests on Art. 163(3) itself; Laxmikanth lists it alongside R ('Moreover…') under 'No Legal Responsibility', so some books give (b).
Both true: Art. 163(3) bars courts from enquiring into ministers' advice, and the Constitution has no system of legal responsibility of ministers (no countersignature). The official key treats R as explaining A.

items.s: Who sets the ceiling on the number of ministers in the Council of Ministers in a State?
items.x: The ceiling is set by the Constitution itself – Art. 164(1A) (91st Amendment, 2003): 15% of the Assembly, minimum 12.

items.s: Ministers in a state get salaries as determined by
items.x: Art. 164(5): salaries of State Ministers are determined by the State Legislature by law.

items.s: Who is the Presiding Officer of the meeting of the Council of Ministers in a state?
items.x: The Chief Minister presides over meetings of the State Council of Ministers (Cabinet); the Governor does not attend them.

items.s: Who from the following acted as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh for the shortest period of time?
items.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was Chief Minister for only about a month (16 Aug – 16 Sep 1984) after toppling NTR, the shortest term among these.

items.s: Who among the following has served as a very short-term Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: N. Bhaskara Rao held office for about a month in 1984 (16 Aug – 16 Sep). Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy served about seven months in 1982; NTR and Chenna Reddy had long terms.

items.s: Who has the record of being the Chief Minister in India for the longest term?
items.x: Pawan Kumar Chamling (Sikkim, 1994-2019, about 24 years 5 months) holds the record as the longest-serving Chief Minister; Naveen Patnaik (2000-2024) ended just short of it, and Jyoti Basu served about 23 years.

items.s: Who of the following Chief Ministers resigned on October 19, 2001 after failing to ensure his/her election to the State Assembly within the mandatory period of 6 months as per the Constitution?
items.x: P. Shanmugam, Chief Minister of Pondicherry, was not an MLA and resigned in Oct 2001 after failing to get elected within six months (Art. 164(4) principle); N. Rangasamy succeeded him on 27 Oct 2001. Jayalalitha quit in Sept 2001 after the Supreme Court annulled her appointment.

items.s: In 2013, which Indian State Chief Minister was conferred the Lifetime Achievement for peace Award by the United Nations-Affiliated International Association of Educators of World peace?
items.x: In early 2013 the UN-affiliated IAEWP chose Arunachal Pradesh CM Nabam Tuki for its peace award.

items.s: Who was the longest serving Chief Minister in India?
items.x:
Pawan Kumar Chamling (Sikkim, 1994-2019) passed Jyoti Basu in 2018 and Naveen Patnaik (2000-2024) also passed him in 2023 — now Pawan Kumar Chamling is the longest-serving CM (morungexpress.com, search result)
Jyoti Basu (West Bengal, 1977-2000, about 23 years) was the longest-serving CM when this was asked in 2009 (now Pawan Kumar Chamling of Sikkim, 24 years 165 days, who passed Basu in 2018).

items.s: The 22nd Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh
items.x:
Most keys: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy. Strictly the count depends on the method: by tenures from Prakasam (1953) YSR is 21st and K. Rosaiah 22nd; Wikipedia numbers terms only up to 16 (Wikipedia list).
Printed key kept: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy (2004-09, re-sworn May 2009). Numbering of AP Chief Ministers varies (by person YSR is the 14th since 1956; by tenures from 1953 Rosaiah comes 22nd).

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: As of December 2019, who is the Education Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x:
Education Minister in Dec 2019 = Audimulapu Suresh — now Nara Lokesh (HRD/Education, since June 2024) (general knowledge, not checked)
In December 2019 Audimulapu Suresh was AP's Education Minister; Anil Kumar handled irrigation, Mekapati Goutham Reddy industries and Buggana Rajendranath finance (now Nara Lokesh holds Education/HRD, since June 2024).

items.s: Under the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a State Council of Ministers including the CM cannot exceed what share of the Assembly's total strength?
items.x: The ceiling is 15% of the Legislative Assembly's total strength, with a minimum of 12 (Art. 164(1A)).

items.s: The reported 2026 proposal for automatic removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Minister or a Minister concerns detention for
o: 30 consecutive days on charges carrying five or more years of imprisonment
60 consecutive days on charges carrying ten or more years of imprisonment
items.x: The 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill proposes automatic removal after detention for 30 consecutive days on charges carrying a possible sentence of five or more years.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Council of Ministers?
o: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister
A non-member may be a Minister but must become an MLA or MLC within six months
The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, normally the Assembly majority leader
Article 164 deals with the State Council of Ministers
items.x: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

items.s: If a no-confidence motion is passed in the State Legislative Assembly, who must resign?
o: The entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister
items.x: The State ministry is collectively responsible to the Assembly (Art. 164(2)), so a passed no-confidence motion forces the whole ministry, CM included, to resign.

items.s: Which of the following is a constitutional duty of the Chief Minister under Article 167?
o: Reserving Bills for the consideration of the President
Communicating Cabinet decisions to the Governor
items.x: Under Article 167, the Chief Minister must communicate the decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and furnish information the Governor seeks.

items.s: In which of the following groups of States is the appointment of a Minister for Tribal Welfare mandatory?
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
items.x: A Minister for Tribal Welfare is mandatory in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Bihar was removed from the list by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006.

items.s: A second chamber in the State Legislature can be created through
o: An Act of Parliament on the basis of a resolution made by the State Assembly
Order of a Governor with the consent of the President
items.x: Under Article 169 Parliament may create (or abolish) a Legislative Council by law if the State Assembly passes a resolution by special majority; it is not a constitutional amendment.

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Engineering Assistant / Ward Amen

Chairman was elected before appointed day
The Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of the United State

items.s: The Union Government is considering appointing a person as a judge in the Supreme Court. Who, in the President's opinion, is a distinguished jurist. What further qualifications are required for such an appointment?
o: Must have served as a High Court judge for at least five years
Must have been an advocate in a High Court for at least ten years
Being a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion is sufficient
items.x: Art. 124(3): a citizen who is a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President is qualified on that ground alone; 5 years as an HC judge or 10 years as an HC advocate are alternative, not extra, qualifications.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Which of the following is not a qualification prescribed for appointment as Judge of Supreme Court?

Atleast 10 years practice as advocate of High Court
A distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President
Atleast 10 years practice as advocate of Supreme Court

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017
items.s: Which one of the following is the qualification for appointment as the judge of the supreme court?

Must have practiced before Supreme Court for a period of not less than 10 years

o: The judiciary strictly interprets laws without interfering in legislative or executive actions.

items.s: Which of the following is not part of recommendations of Rajmannar Committee?
o: No decision of national importance or which may affect one or more states should be taken by the Union government except after consultation with the Inter state council
Every bill of national importance or which may affect one or more states should before its introduction in parliament be referred to the Inter state council.
Article 356 should be used only in the event of complete break down of law and order in a state.
Committee recommended vesting of residuary power of legislation and taxation in the state legislature
items.x:
Laxmikanth: Rajamannar wanted Arts 356, 357 and 365 omitted, so option C is the odd one out. Some guides (gktoday.in) list 'use Art. 356 only in a complete breakdown of law and order' as its recommendation – on that reading every printed option is a recommendation. All sources agree it recommended residuary powers for the States (the printed key).
The Rajamannar Committee (TN, 1969-71) wanted an Inter-State Council set up at once, with Bills and decisions of national importance referred to it, and residuary powers of legislation and taxation vested in the States. On President's Rule Laxmikanth records that it wanted Arts 356, 357 and 365 totally omitted – so 'use Art. 356 only in complete breakdown' is not its recommendation (that line is close to Sarkaria's 'sparingly, as a last resort'). The printed key (residuary powers to States) was in fact one of its recommendations.

items.x: Only B: the President appoints the Finance Commission chairman and members; A is wrong – FC recommendations are advisory and not binding on the government.

items.s: The Finance Commission may deal with which of the following matters?
o: Any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound public finance
Resolution of legal disputes between the Centre and States
Distribution between the State and local bodies only
Constitution of the State Finance Commission every five years
items.x: Besides sharing taxes and grants, the Finance Commission handles any other matter the President refers to it in the interest of sound finance. It does not settle legal disputes.

items.s: How often is the Union Finance Commission constituted by the President of India?
o: Only once during the President's term
Every five years or earlier as deemed necessary
Every ten years or earlier as decided by Parliament
items.x: The President sets up a Finance Commission every five years, or earlier if needed. The interval is not rigidly fixed.

items.x: Central tax devolution goes to the States; Panchayats get Central assistance through Finance Commission grants routed through the State.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?

Recommending the allocation of the States' share among the States
Recommending principles for grants-in-aid out of the Consolidated Fund of India
Resolving Centre-State legal disputes under Article 131
items.x: Article 131 disputes go to the Supreme Court; the other three are Finance Commission functions.

d. Dependency on external fund is minimal

items.x: FICCI was formed in 1927 (G.D. Birla, Purushottamdas Thakurdas). Moved to pressure groups.

items.s: Conflict is a modified form of this
items.x: In sociology conflict is treated as an intensified, personal form of competition (Park and Burgess); cooperation is its opposite and 'struggle' is not the textbook term.

items.s: Who among the following coined the concept of 'Primordial primary' group?
items.x: Edward Shils (1957) introduced 'primordial' ties and groups for the blood bonds of the family; the 'primary group' itself is C.H. Cooley's term ('C.H. wage' is a misprint), and George Homans worked on small-group exchange, not primordial groups.

items.s:
Consider the following theories:

A. The theory of positivism proposed by Comte

B. Theory of division of labor proposed by Durkheim

C. Spencer's theory of emotional similarity
Which is the correct historical timeline for the above theories ?
items.x: Comte's positivism (Course of Positive Philosophy, 1830-42) came first, then Spencer's evolutionary theory (1850s-60s), then Durkheim's Division of Labour (1893): A, C, B.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test General Stud
items.s:
Two statements labelled as
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) are given. Consider both the statements carefully and select your answer on the basis of the given options.
Assertion (A): Contemporary Indian literature reflects the complexities of societal shifts and cultural dynamics in the India.
Reason (R): Through themes of identity, gender, and social critique, Indian authors engage with the evolving fabric of Indian society, blending tradition with modernity in their literary expressions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false and R is true.
A is true and R is false.
items.x: Contemporary Indian literature reflects social and cultural change (A), and it does so precisely through themes of identity, gender and social critique blending tradition and modernity (R), so R explains A.

items.s: What is the habitual way of functioning of a community or society?
items.x: A community's habitual, prescribed way of acting is a ritual. Oath, value and statute are not habitual practices. Moved to the basic concepts row.

items.s: 'Society is a web of social relations' said?
items.x: MacIver (with Page) defined society as 'a web of social relationships'. Moved to the basic concepts row.

items.x: Culture is the man-made part of the environment, built over and above nature, so it is 'superior to nature'. Moved to the basic concepts row.

items.s: Which of the following is not a means of informal control?
items.x: The police is an agency of formal control (law, coercion); family, community and social media (gossip, ridicule) are informal controls.

items.s:
Consider the following statements on the 'social capital'

A. Interconnected network of relationships between individuals and groups

B. Trust levels in the networks or ties

C. Amount of financial investment made by the individuals to the common pool

D. Resources or benefits gained by virtue of social ties and social participation
Which of the above statements are related to the 'three dimensions of social capital'?
items.x: Social capital has structural (networks of relationships), relational (trust) and resource (benefits from ties and participation) dimensions; individual financial investment is economic, not social, capital.

items.s: Which of the following is an example of anticipatory socialization ?
o: Parents to socialize their unmarried daughters to make proper adjustments to their husbands' families in post-marriage life.
A housewife teaching her maids how to do household chores.
To train soldiers to fight the enemy.
A manager to participate in a training program to improve his communication skills.
items.x: Anticipatory socialisation is learning the norms of a group or role one expects to join – e.g. preparing daughters for life in their husbands' families.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Family, School, Club, Gymnasium, Sports and games etc, belongs to which group?
items.x: In the textbook classification by duration, groups like family, school, club and sports teams are permanent groups, as against temporary groups like a crowd or audience.

items.s: Which of the following is an example of a community ?
items.x: No key can be settled: in MacIver's sociology a club and a religious establishment are associations (organised for specific interests), not communities, so the printed key 'a club related to sports' contradicts the textbook distinction; family and kinship groups are treated as both community and association by different authors, so the question has no single defensible answer.

items.s: When a group of people gets excited and engages in or prepares to engage in violent action, what is the group called?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mob); it is added as option 5.
An excited crowd that engages in or prepares for violent action is a mob. A crowd is any temporary gathering, a gang is a small organised group and an aggregation is a mere collection, so no printed option fits.

items.s: Which of the following religions does not have a specific text (scripture)?
items.x: Hinduism has no single founding scripture (many texts: Vedas, Upanishads, Gita); Judaism has the Torah, Christianity the Bible, Islam the Quran. Moved to Indian society.

items.s: Which of the following is not a secondary group characteristic?
items.x: Membership of secondary groups is voluntary, so compulsory membership is not their characteristic.

items.s:
Consider the following features

A. Network of social relations

B. Population density

C. Membership by birth

D. Integral culture
What are the main characteristics of society?
items.x: Society is a network of social relations with membership by birth and an integral culture. Population density is a demographic feature, not a defining trait of society, so A, C and D.

items.s: The process of socialization is
o: Begins at a very young age and ends in adolescence
Contributes to the learning of an individual's disciplined lifestyle
Society helps to reproduce itself socially and biologically.
For children it helps in finding good relationships.
items.x: Socialisation is the lifelong process through which society reproduces itself socially and culturally; it does not end in adolescence.

items.s: Why is language important to human society?
o: It easily fulfills man's need for expression
Adi Aatavika created man as a supreme being
items.x: Language is a social product whose chief importance to society is that it makes communication and so social relations possible. It is not merely a human invention or a vehicle for individual expression, and the 'Adi Aatavika' option is a myth, not a reason.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who has coined the term, 'Operant Conditioning'?
items.x: B.F. Skinner coined 'operant conditioning' (learning through reinforcement). Pavlov is linked with classical conditioning, Thorndike with trial and error, Bandura with social learning.

items.s:
Which of the following are characteristics associated with a primary group?

A. Small size

B. Self-interest

C. Comparison in background

D. Common interests
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
items.x: A primary group (Cooley) is small, has similarity of background and shared common interests, with intimate face-to-face ties. Self-interest marks secondary groups and associations, not primary groups.

items.s: A group of people organized for a particular need is called
items.x: A group deliberately organised to meet a particular need or purpose is an association or formal organisation, so "organization" is correct. A community is a group of people sharing a common life in a locality, not one formed for a particular need (printed key: community).

items.s: The group, ever more conscious of its unity is made
o: When its members have common interests
When its members live relatively isolated
When it is at breaking point
items.x: A group becomes most conscious of its unity when another group threatens it, as external threat strengthens in-group solidarity (sociology).

items.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a secondary group?
items.x: Secondary groups are relatively large, formal and impersonal; physical proximity (face-to-face contact) is the classic condition of a primary group, so it is not a feature of a secondary group. Largeness in size IS a feature, so the printed key is wrong (permanency and compulsory membership are also weak features of secondary groups, but physical proximity is the textbook contrast).

items.s: Duties in Modern Family
items.x: Many traditional duties of the family (education, care, production) have moved to schools, the state and markets, so the functions of the modern family are decreasing. Off-topic, moved to book 2 row 106.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: "Socialisation is a process by which the individual is adapted to his social environment", the statement is given by:
items.x: 'Socialisation is a process by which the individual is adapted to his social environment' is James Drever's definition (A Dictionary of Psychology). Moved to the family and socialisation row.

items.s: Which of the following is not a basis for family classification?
items.x: Families are classified by inheritance, residence, authority, descent, marriage and structure – not by religion. Off-topic (society), moved.

items.s: The term 'Unstable Family' was first used by
items.x: Frederic Le Play classified families into patriarchal, stem and unstable types; the 'unstable family' is his term.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a family activity in an industrial society?
o: Imparting social values and culture to children
items.x: In an industrial society production moves out of the home into factories, so the family is no longer a production unit; it still socialises, educates and consumes.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: The process of personality development is completed in how many Stages according to Erikson.
items.x: Erik Erikson's psychosocial theory has eight stages, from trust vs mistrust (infancy) to integrity vs despair (old age).

items.s: The statuses of husbands and wives can be said in this way?
items.x: The statuses of husband and wife are functional (complementary) statuses, each defined by the role it plays in the family.

items.s: 'Marriage is the only rite performed by women, so it is said that marriage is necessary for them'. This statement is given by?
items.x: K.M. Kapadia (Marriage and Family in India) wrote that marriage was the only sacrament (samskara) for a woman, hence obligatory for her.

items.s: Menarikam marriage will happen to whom?
o: Children of siblings of the same sex
items.x: Menarikam (Telugu) is marriage with the mother's brother's daughter, a cross-cousin, i.e. children of opposite-sex siblings; parallel cousins (same-sex siblings' children) cannot marry.

items.s: Muhammadan marriage is a
items.x: Muslim marriage (nikah) is a civil contract – an agreement – not a sacrament as Hindu marriage traditionally is.

items.s: The religion which permitted widow marriage was:
items.x: Islam has always permitted widow remarriage; Hindu widow remarriage was legalised only in 1856. Moved to the marriage row.

items.s: Marriage according to traditional Hindu belief is:
items.x: In traditional Hindu belief marriage is a sacrament – a holy, indissoluble bond – not a contract. (Off-topic: moved to the marriage row.)

items.s: Levirate is practiced in which societies?
items.x: Levirate - a widow marrying her dead husband's brother - keeps the widow, her children and property within the husband's lineage, so it belongs to patriarchal (patrilineal) societies. (Moved to the marriage row of Society.)

items.s: "Mutha" is one form of marriage, which can be observed in
items.x: Muta (Mutah) is the temporary contract marriage recognised among (Shia) Muslims.

items.s: Iravati Karve's study of kinship organisation in India compared __ cultural zones.
items.x: Irawati Karve (Kinship Organization in India, 1953) compared kinship in four cultural zones: northern, central, southern and eastern.

items.s: Which sociologist made a comparative analysis of kinship arrangements in four cultural zones of India?
items.x: Irawati Karve's Kinship Organization in India (1953) compared kinship in four cultural zones (north, centre, south, east). Ghurye wrote on caste and race; Mandelbaum and I.P. Desai are distractors (printed key: G.S. Ghurye).

items.s: Author of the book 'Kinship Organization in India'
items.x: Kinship Organization in India (1953) is by Irawati Karve; T.N. Madan wrote Family and Kinship (Kashmiri Pandits), D.N. Majumdar on races and tribes.

items.s: What is a group of relatives who are all consanguineous relatives called?
items.x: A group of kin all related by blood (consanguineous) is a cognatic (cognate) group: cognates are blood relatives through both lines, agnates only through males, uterine kin only through females. 'Homogeneous group' is not a kinship term (printed key: Homogeneous group, probably a mistranslation).

items.s: Which of the following genealogical types is found among the Yakos of Nigeria?
items.x: The Yakö of Nigeria (Daryll Forde) have double (dual) descent: patrilineal clans for land and matrilineal clans for movable property.

items.s: Which of the following Muslim communities is matrilineal?
items.x: Of the printed options the Navayats of the Konkan–Kanara coast follow matrilineal descent (D'Souza 1955); Memons and Bohras are patrilineal. Option 1 is garbled ('Figure of Sri Lanka', probably the Moors of Sri Lanka, also matrilineal), so the key is uncertain.

items.s: What is the tracing of all genealogies for one purpose in the male line and for another in the female line?
items.x: Tracing descent through the male line for some purposes and the female line for others is double (dual) descent, which option 2 describes. 'Dual female pedigree' covers only one line, and monogamy is a marriage form, not descent.

items.s: ____ enunciated seven cultural traits of caste.
items.x: J.H. Hutton (Caste in India, 1946) listed the cultural traits of caste (endogamy, commensal and food restrictions, hereditary occupation, pollution etc.); printed key kept. Ghurye gave six features; Dumont stressed hierarchy and purity-pollution.

items.s: Who states that the Varna Model has produced a wrong and distorted image of caste?
items.x: M.N. Srinivas, in 'Varna and Caste' (1962), wrote that 'the varna model has produced a wrong and distorted image of caste', since the real unit is the local jati, not the four varnas.

items.s: Who holds the view that caste is a broad kinship group?
items.x: Irawati Karve (Hindu Society: An Interpretation, 1961) saw the jati as an extended kin group: endogamous, limited to a linguistic region and usually with a hereditary occupation. Ghurye stressed six structural features and Risley race (printed key: G.S. Ghurye).

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary /
items.s: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Caste System in Ancient India ?
o: There was a proliferation of castes due to growth in guilds.
The caste system became more complex with the influx of foreigners.
The caste system became more complex when tribal regions were brought under cultivation.
The caste system led to perfect social stability in ancient India.
items.x: Guild growth, foreign influx and the absorption of tribal regions multiplied castes and made the system more complex; caste never produced 'perfect social stability', so D is the wrong statement.

items.s: The mutual dependence of castes is known as this.
items.x: The hereditary interdependence of castes – service castes (kamin) serving landholding patrons (jajman) – is the jajmani system; 'mutual unity' is not a sociological term.

items.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of caste?
items.x: Caste features are endogamy ('inter-marriage' = antar-vivaha, marriage within), hereditary occupation and commensal (meal) rules; complexion is not a feature of caste. Off-topic (society), moved.

items.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
items.s: The tribal unrest which led to the demand for separate and autonomous states for protecting tribals' unique cultural identity and other systems.
items.x: Of the options, only the Gondwana movement is a tribal demand for a separate, autonomous state (for the Gonds of central India, raised since 1956). Naxalbari was a peasant uprising, and the Chota Nagpur and Munda Sardar risings were colonial-era agrarian revolts.

items.s: A person belonging to the Dalit caste abstains from eating meat and adopts ritualistic worship. Which of the following best describes this behavior?
items.x: Adopting the customs, diet and rituals of higher castes to rise in status is Sanskritisation (M.N. Srinivas); acculturation, enculturation and socialisation are wider processes.

items.s:
Examine the following statements. Modernization brings the prevalence of modern cultural influences. Over...

A. Changes traditions by banning tribalism

B. Enforcing legal rules by changing traditions

C. Changing traditions by raising incomes.

D. By strengthening the power of the government it changes traditions
Which of these statements is correct ?
items.x: The statements are garbled; the printed key (B, C, D: law, rising incomes and a stronger state change traditions) is kept. 'Banning tribalism' is not a mechanism of modernisation.

items.s: Which of the following is not a change-promoting movement?
items.x: Literacy, women's liberation and Dalit movements seek social change; an anti-reservation movement resists change (status-quo).

items.s: What is a radical cultural movement arising when there is evolution called?
items.x:
Printed keys split: transformational (this copy) vs millenarian (the 1996 copy); the stem is a garbled translation and the original key could not be found.
Garbled stem: a movement promising radical cultural change in times of extreme upheaval is usually called a millenarian movement; the two printings of this question carry different keys (transformational / millenarian).

items.s: What is the movement that occurs when there is extreme cultural evolution called?
items.x:
Printed keys split: millenarian (this copy) vs transformational (the 1999 copy); stem garbled, original key not found.
A movement arising in conditions of extreme cultural change and promising a radically new order is usually called a millenarian movement.

items.x: Sanskritisation (term coined by M.N. Srinivas) is the process by which a lower caste adopts the customs, rituals and lifestyle of higher castes to rise in the caste hierarchy, i.e. a process of upward social mobility.

items.s: Among the following what are the proposed three stages of socio-cultural evolution by L.H. Morgan?
items.x: In Ancient Society (1877) L.H. Morgan gave three stages of social evolution: savagery, barbarism and civilisation ('wild, barbaric and civilised'). The other options are not Morgan's scheme.

items.s: Social stratification is about
items.x: Social stratification is about both hierarchy (ranking) and difference (Dipankar Gupta's distinction), so 'hierarchy and difference'.

items.s: According to the available studies, which is the most influential factor of social transformation among Dalits?

items.s: What kind of word is 'status'?
items.x: Garbled stem/options: 'status' is a relational term (a position defined in relation to other positions), so the printed 'Taluk [term] of relations' is kept; it is not a moral, personal or ideal term.

items.s: Regarding schedule Caste and schedule tribe reservation choose the correct answer
o: Reservation on the basis of domicile is not impermissible in terms of clause of Article 15 of the Constitution of India
Children born to inter caste Marriage of which either father or mother belongs to SC/ST category can claim reservation benefits unconditionally
