items.s: The central tendency that can be located easily by the inspection and can be used by common people also is
items.x: The mode – the most frequent value – can be located just by inspecting the data and is easily understood by common people; mean and median need calculation or ordering, and probability is not an average.

items.s: If probability of shooter A hitting the target is 0.6 and shooter B hitting the target is 0.8, what is the probability that when both try simultaneously, the target is not hit?
items.x: The target is missed only if both miss: (1-0.6) × (1-0.8) = 0.4 × 0.2 = 0.08.

items.s: The major reason why many economists expected a sharp depression immediately following World War II was the:
o: Sharp increase in government taxes to quell inflationary pressures
Lack of consumer goods to satisfy the intense consumer demand
General reluctance of individuals and business firms to utilize their liquid assets
Sharp reduction in government purchases of goods and services
items.x: Economists feared a post-war slump because war spending, the government's huge purchases, would be cut sharply at demobilisation. In fact pent-up consumer demand prevented it.

items.s: Sampling distribution is used in inference analysis. Sampling distribution is defined as a distribution of
items.x: A sampling distribution is the distribution of a sample statistic (such as the sample mean) over all possible samples, not of the raw observations or the population parameters.

items.s: Which of the following is not a feature of a developing economy?
items.x: Developing economies have a LOW rate of capital formation; unemployment, fast population growth and poverty are their features.

items.s: Which one of the following is not a feature of a developing economy?
items.x: A low, not high, rate of capital formation marks a developing economy; the other three are its features.

items.s: At the saturation point of commodity the MU is
items.x: At the saturation point total utility is at its maximum, so marginal utility is zero; beyond it MU turns negative.

items.s: Goods for which demand directly (positively) related to income are called
items.x: Normal goods are those whose demand rises with income; for inferior goods demand falls as income rises; substitutes and complements are defined by cross-price links.

items.s: The cost that a firm incurs in purchasing or hiring any factor of production is referred to as
items.x: Payments for purchased or hired factors are explicit (accounting) costs; implicit costs are the imputed value of the firm's own factors.

items.s: Prices based on the imputed values of costs and benefits are called
items.x: Shadow (accounting) prices are imputed values of costs and benefits used where market prices do not reflect true social values.

items.s: The prices that provide sound basis for allocation decisions in public sector are
items.x: Accounting (shadow) prices, reflecting true social opportunity costs, are the sound basis for public-sector allocation and project appraisal (Tinbergen); market prices are distorted by taxes, subsidies and controls, so they cannot be the answer.

items.s: According to the Law of Diminishing Returns, in a production function, when more and more units of the variable factor are used, holding the quantities of a fixed factor constant, a point is reached beyond which
items.x: The law of diminishing returns states that beyond a point the marginal product of the variable factor falls when a fixed factor is held constant.

items.s: A consumer who is below the personal budget line (rather than on it)
o: Is not spending all personal income
May or may not be spending all personal income
items.x: A consumption point below (inside) the budget line costs less than income, so the consumer is not spending all income.

items.s: Quasi-rent is
o: Equal to the firm's total profit
Greater than the firm's total profits
Smaller than the firm's total profits
items.x: Short-run quasi-rent = total revenue − total variable cost = total fixed cost + profit, so it exceeds total profit by the fixed cost.

items.s: Total business saving is composed of
o: Undistributed corporate profits and corporate profit taxes
Undistributed corporate profits and capital consumption allowances
items.x: Gross business saving = undistributed (retained) corporate profits + capital consumption allowances (depreciation); dividends and corporate taxes leave the firm.

items.s: If we have constant returns to scale and we increase the quantity of labour used per unit of time by 10% but keep the amount of capital constant, output will
items.x: Constant returns to scale need all inputs raised by 10%; raising only labour by 10% with capital fixed meets diminishing returns, so output rises by less than 10%.

items.s: If factor prices and factor quantities move in the same direction, we have
items.x: If factor prices rise as the industry uses more factors (prices and quantities move together), the industry's costs rise as it expands: an increasing cost industry.

items.s: Gross domestic savings as per cent of GDP at current market prices in 2000-2001 was
items.x: The Economic Survey 2001-02 put gross domestic saving at 23.4% of GDP at current market prices in 2000-01 (later revised).

items.s: Which of the following is not an assumption of linear programming?
items.x: Linear programming assumes linearity: constant prices and fixed input coefficients, i.e. constant returns to scale; increasing returns violate linearity.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Which of the following cannot be treated as cash
items.x: Cash covers notes, coins and bank balances (and cash equivalents); long-term investments are not cash.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: Which of the following is an example of fixed cost for a farm?
items.x: Fixed costs do not vary with output – land rent, depreciation, interest on fixed capital; seeds, fertiliser and labour are variable costs.

items.s: In an economy of two individuals (A and B) and two commodities (X and Y), general equilibrium of production and exchange occurs when
o: MRSxy for A and B = Px/Py
items.x: General equilibrium of production and exchange needs MRT_xy = (MRS_xy)A = (MRS_xy)B – the production frontier's slope equal to both consumers' rates of substitution.

items.src: AP Forest Beat Officers Screening Test 2019
items.s: How the slope of demand curve exists?
items.x: The typical demand curve slopes downward and is drawn convex to the origin.

items.s: In terms of the IS-LM model, an easy money policy would:
o: Shift the I = S curve to the right
Shift the I = S curve to the left
Cause the L = M curve to rotate upward because income would increase and thus increase the transactions demand for money
Cause the L = M curve to rotate downward and thus increase income as the interest rate falls
items.x: An easy money policy shifts the LM curve right/down: the interest rate falls and income rises; the IS (I = S) curve does not move.

items.s: If a straight-line demand curve is tangent to a curvilinear demand curve, the elasticity of the two demand curves at the point of tangency is
o: Can be the same or different
It depends on the point of tangency
items.x: At the point of tangency the two curves have the same slope and the same price-quantity point, so their elasticities are the same.

items.s: All the following curves are U-shaped except
items.x: Average fixed cost falls continuously (a rectangular hyperbola); AVC, AC and MC are U-shaped.

items.s: What does monopolistic competition have in common with monopoly?
o: The ability to collude with respect to price
items.x: Both monopolistic competition and monopoly face a downward-sloping demand curve; mutual interdependence belongs to oligopoly.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: A perfect market is characterized by
items.at: Large number of buyers and sellers
items.x: Perfect competition has a large number of buyers and sellers, a homogeneous product and free entry and exit.

items.s: The locus of general equilibrium points of exchange in a two-individual, two-commodity economy is called
items.x: In the Edgeworth box the locus of tangencies of the two consumers' indifference curves, the exchange equilibria, is the consumption contract curve.

items.s: The locus of Pareto optimality in production and consumption is given by
items.x: The grand utility-possibility curve is the envelope of utility-possibility curves and gives Pareto optimality in production and consumption together.

items.s: An ethical or value judgment must be made in order to derive
items.x: Choosing among Pareto-optimal points needs a value judgement, which the social welfare function supplies; the other curves are positive constructs.

items.s: Economics as the study of relationship between unlimited wants and scarce resources, according to
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Lionel Robbins); it is added as option 5.
The scarcity definition – economics studies the relation between unlimited ends and scarce means – is Lionel Robbins' (1932). Keynes, Marx, Weber and Adam Smith (wealth definition) did not give it.

items.s: Which of the following will cause the I = S curve to shift outward to the right?
o: An increase in saving at all income levels
An increase in taxes at all income levels
Technological change that increases investment at all interest rates
items.x: The IS curve shifts to the right when autonomous spending rises at every interest rate, e.g. technological change that raises investment; higher saving, higher taxes or lower government purchases shift it left.

items.s: When the industry is in long-run equilibrium, the monopolistic competitor will produce at the lowest point on its LAC curve
items.x: In long-run equilibrium the monopolistically competitive firm's demand curve is tangent to LAC on its falling part, so it never produces at the lowest point of LAC (excess capacity).

items.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature of Indian Economy?
items.x: Indian economy is marked by high population growth, disguised unemployment and low literacy; it has a LOW rate of capital formation, so 'high rate of capital accumulation' is not a feature.

items.s: If the LAC curve falls as output expands, this is due to
items.x: The LAC curve falls as output expands because of economies of scale; diminishing returns shape the short-run curve and diseconomies make LAC rise. Off-topic (microeconomics), moved.

items.s: If the MU of the last unit of X consumed is twice the MU of the last unit of Y consumed, the consumer is in equilibrium only if
o: The price of X is twice the price of Y
The price of X is equal to the price of Y
The price of X is one half of the price of Y
The price of X is square of the price of Y
items.x: Equilibrium needs MUx/Px = MUy/Py; if MUx = 2 MUy then Px must be twice Py. Off-topic (microeconomics), moved.

items.s: Zero price elasticity of demand means
o: whatever the change in price, there is absolutely no change in demand.
for a small change in price, there is a small change in demand.
for a small change in price, there is a large change in demand.
for a large change in price, there is a small change in demand.
items.x: Zero price elasticity means perfectly inelastic demand: quantity demanded does not change whatever the price change.

items.s: Games in which the gains of one player equal the losses of the other are called
items.x: Games in which one player's gain equals the other's loss are zero-sum games; non-zero-sum games and the prisoner's dilemma allow joint gains or losses. Economic concept, moved to row 0.

items.s: If a population follows normal distribution then the sampling distribution from it follows
items.x: If the population is normal, the sampling distribution of the sample mean is also normal (for any sample size). Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.s: The theoretical distribution used for testing whether a population follows a specific theoretical distribution or not:
items.x: Whether data fit a specified theoretical distribution is tested with the chi-square goodness-of-fit test; Z, t and F test means and variances. Printed key (Z) was wrong. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.s: Adjusted R², wherein the adjustment is for
o: Units of measurement of dependent variable
items.x: Adjusted R² adjusts R² for degrees of freedom (number of regressors relative to sample size). Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.s: The strategy of maximizing the minimum gain is called
items.x: Maximin is the strategy of choosing the action whose minimum (worst-case) gain is the largest; minimax minimises the maximum loss.

items.s: Shadow price refers to
o: The change in the value of the constraint per unit change in the objective function
The change in the value of the objective function per unit change in any one of the constraints
The change in the value of the primal solution per unit change in the dual solution
Change in the value of input prices
items.x: In linear programming the shadow price of a constraint is the change in the optimal value of the objective function per unit change in that constraint (its right-hand side). (Moved to the economy basics row.)

items.s: The welfare economic analysis developed by Pareto relates to the production function and
items.x: Pareto's welfare analysis rests on the production function and utility: a state is Pareto-optimal when no one's utility can be raised without lowering another's. (Moved to the economy basics row.)

items.s: When a perfectly competitive industry is taken over by a monopoly, some consumer surplus is transferred to the monopolist in the form of
items.x: When a monopoly takes over a competitive industry, part of the consumer surplus becomes the monopolist's economic (supernormal) profit; the rest is lost as deadweight loss. Microeconomics question, moved.

items.s: The marginal value product of labour (or value of the marginal product of labour) equals:
o: The marginal product of labour times price
The marginal product of labour divided by price
The marginal product of labour plus price
items.x: The value of the marginal product of labour = marginal physical product × output price. Microeconomics question, moved.

items.s: The concept of consumer surplus is useful in which policy ?
items.x: Consumer surplus is used in tax policy (who bears a tax and the welfare loss from it), price discrimination and cost-benefit analysis. Microeconomics question, moved.

items.s: A businessman's opportunity cost of using his own funds to undertake an investment is the:
o: Cost of purchasing the machines and other things necessary to undertake the investment
Interest income he could receive if he loaned out the funds that would be required to make the investment
Operating cost of machines needed for the investment
Cost of determining the rate of return of the investment opportunity
items.x: The opportunity cost of using his own funds is the interest he gives up by not lending them out. Microeconomics question, moved.

items.s: In long-run equilibrium, the pure monopolist (as opposed to the perfectly competitive firm) can make pure profits because of
items.x: A pure monopolist keeps pure (supernormal) profits in the long run because entry is blocked by barriers; in perfect competition free entry wipes such profits out. High prices or advertising alone do not sustain them.

items.s:
Consider the following statements
Other things remaining unchanged, market demand for a good might increase if

1. Price of its substitute increases

2. Price of its complement increases

3. The good is an inferior good and income of the consumers increases

4. Its price falls
Which of the above statements are correct?
items.x: Demand rises if the price of a substitute rises (1); a fall in the good's own price raises the quantity demanded (4, the official key counts it). A complement's price rise, or higher income for an inferior good, lowers demand. (Official UPSC key: 1 and 4 only.)

items.s: In drawing a farmer's supply curve for a commodity, all but which one of the following are kept constant?
o: Features of nature such as climate and weather conditions
The price of the commodity under consideration
items.x: A supply curve plots quantity against the commodity's own price, so that price varies; technology, input prices and nature are held constant. (Moved: no microeconomics row in this book; filed with basic economics, row 0.)

items.s: If the amount of a commodity purchased remains unchanged when the price of another commodity changes, the cross elasticity of demand between them is
items.x: If the quantity bought of one good does not change when another good's price changes, cross elasticity is zero – the goods are unrelated. (Moved: no microeconomics row in this book; filed with basic economics, row 0.)

items.s: According to the theory of contestable markets, perfect competition can occur
o: Only if there are a large number of firms in the industry
If entry into the industry is absolutely free and exit from the industry is entirely costless
Only in the absence of government regulation
Only in the presence of foreign competition
items.x: In a contestable market, free entry and costless exit make even a few firms behave competitively. Microeconomics question, moved.

items.s: Each seller determines his price on the assumption that his rival will keep his price constant, under
items.x: In Bertrand's duopoly model each seller sets price assuming the rival keeps his price constant; Cournot assumes the rival's quantity constant.

items.s: With reference to the Cournot model, determine which of the following statements is false
o: The duopolists do not recognize their interdependence
Each duopolist assumes the other will keep its quantity constant
Each duopolist assumes the other will keep its price constant
items.x: Cournot duopolists assume the rival keeps its output (quantity) constant – the 'price constant' statement is false; that is the Bertrand/Edgeworth assumption.

items.s: With reference to the Edgeworth model, determine which of the following statements is correct
o: Each duopolist assumes the other keeps its price constant
Each duopolist assumes the other keeps its quantity constant
items.x: Edgeworth's model, like Bertrand's, assumes each duopolist expects the rival to keep its price constant; the solution oscillates and the duopolists do not recognise interdependence.

items.s: The elasticity of substitution between two inputs in CES production function
items.x: The CES production function has a constant elasticity of substitution (σ = 1/(1+ρ)), hence its name.

items.s: When the total product remains constant, the marginal product will be :
items.x: When total product is constant (at its maximum), the marginal product is zero.

items.s: From a class of 10 students, wherein male and female are in equal numbers, what is the probability of picking six female students?
items.x: Only 5 of the 10 students are girls, so picking six girls is impossible – probability zero. Mental-ability item, moved.

items.s: Difference of mode and mean is equal to?
items.x: From Karl Pearson's empirical relation Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, we get Mean − Mode = 3(Mean − Median), so the difference of mode and mean equals 3(mean − median).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Mean, Mode and Median are called ____.
items.x: Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency: each gives a single typical value of a distribution.

items.src: APPSC Group-II Screening Test General Studies & Mental Abili
items.s: For a moderately skewed distribution, what is the empirical relationship between Mean, Median and Mode?
items.x: For a moderately skewed distribution, Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, which rearranges to Mean − Mode = 3(Mean − Median).

items.s: The empirical relationship among mean, median and mode is:
items.x: From Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean: Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean), which is option 4. Option 3 (Mode − Median = 2(Median − Mean)) is the same identity rearranged, so it is also true; options 1 and 2 are false.

items.x: Behavioural economics applies psychological insights into human behaviour to explain economic decisions (Kahneman, Thaler).

items.s:

items.s: GDP according to income method is measured through
o: Domestic factor incomes plus Net Income from aboard
Domestic factor incomes minus Transfer payments
items.x:
Printed key and old notes: domestic factor incomes minus transfer payments. Strictly: GDP by the income method = sum of domestic factor incomes; transfers are simply excluded (NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics ch.2).
Under the income method GDP (domestic product) is the sum of factor incomes earned within the domestic territory (wages, rent, interest, profit, mixed income), with depreciation added for the gross figure; adding NFIA gives a national, not domestic, aggregate. Transfer payments are never part of factor incomes, so 'minus transfer payments' is not a step of the method.

items.s: Which one of the following is India's first city to have its logo?

items.s: Under Prime Ministers Integrated Urban Poverty Eradication Programme (PMIUPEP) those urban areas were included which had a population
items.x:

PMIUPEP (November 1995) covered the 345 Class II urban agglomerations with a population between 50,000 and 1 lakh (1991 Census); the printed key's '60,000 to 1 lakh' is a misprint of that range. (Off-topic: moved to urban programmes.)

items.s: The focus of Saakshar Bharat Programme is on :

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x: The first age scale of intelligence was the Binet-Simon scale (1905/1908). Terman's Stanford-Binet revision came in 1916; Spearman gave the two-factor theory.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x: Montessori's sensorial method trains the senses with concrete didactic material, so it is classed with (sense) realism. (Moved to education.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x: In naturalism the child learns from nature and experience, and the teacher only observes, so the teacher's role is smallest. (Moved to education.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x: Sri Aurobindo's contribution is integral education; basic education is Gandhi's and 'man-making' education Vivekananda's. (Moved to education.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x: Delhi University started correspondence courses (School of Correspondence Courses) in 1962, the first distance education in India; IGNOU came in 1985.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

o: Discipline should emphasis on factors external to the individual
Discipline is necessary only for idealists
Punishment is important to impose discipline
items.x: The idealistic view holds that true discipline is self-discipline coming from within the learner; external control and punishment belong to the repressionist view.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A

items.x: Union Budget 2012-13 raised the education allocation by about 18% to Rs 61,427 crore (school education Rs 45,969 crore, higher education Rs 15,458 crore). Rs 58,427 crore is wrong. (Moved to the human-capital row.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Micro teaching is which type of training?
items.x: Micro-teaching (Stanford, 1963) is a skill-based teacher-training technique: one teaching skill is practised in a short, scaled-down lesson with feedback. It is not content-, need- or time-based.

items.s: The activities like sorting of similarities and differences helps to improve the skills in which developmental area?
items.x: Sorting by similarities and differences (classification) builds thinking skills – cognitive development (Piaget), not social, language or physical development.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2

promoting the education and health of adolescent girls
providing affordable and quality education to the citizens for free

items.x: An epidiascope projects images of opaque and transparent material onto a screen; a globe, diorama and blackboard are non-projected aids.

items.x: DPEP (District Primary Education Programme, 1994) targeted the primary stage (classes I-V); 'elementary' also covers upper primary, which DPEP reached only in some districts.

items.s: 'Destiny of India is being shaped in her classrooms'; This is stated in
items.x: 'The destiny of India is now being shaped in her classrooms' opens the Kothari Education Commission (1964-66) report.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: Which state government launched a scheme called 'Paray Shikshalaya' in February 2022 to provide elementary education for students of classes 1 to 5?
items.x: West Bengal launched 'Paray Shikshalaya' (neighbourhood open-air schools) on 7 February 2022 for classes 1 to 5 (later 6-7 too) while schools stayed closed after COVID.

items.s: Which of the following examinations does the National Institute of Open Schooling conduct?
items.x: NIOS conducts Secondary and Senior Secondary examinations through open schooling.

items.x: HEFA = Higher Education Financing Agency (2017, Canara Bank + MoE joint venture) that funds infrastructure in IITs, NITs and other central institutions; the 'Himalayan' expansions are invented.

items.x: IIT Kharagpur (1951, at Hijli) was the first IIT; Bombay (1958), Madras (1959) and Kanpur (1959) came later.

items.x: In the 'National Ranking' (NIRF) 2020 overall list IISc Bangalore was second, after IIT Madras.

items.s: During mapping of words, children may make opposite error, by defining the word too narrowly and this is referred as :
items.x: Defining a word too narrowly (e.g. 'dog' only for the family pet) is under-extension; over-extension is the opposite error of using a word too broadly (all four-legged animals 'dog'), so the printed key was wrong. Child psychology, not ICT.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: A good test should possesses?
items.x: A good test must have all three: validity (measures what it claims), reliability (consistent results) and objectivity (scoring free of examiner bias).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: The following is a measure of reliability obtained by administering the same test twice over a period of time to a group of individuals.
items.x: Test-retest reliability = giving the same test to the same group twice over a time gap and correlating the scores; parallel forms use two equivalent tests, split-half divides one test.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2013, operates under which of the following ministries?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.x: RUSA (2013), the centrally sponsored scheme for state higher education, runs under the Ministry of Education (then MHRD).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Which was the first group of intelligence test?
items.x: The Army Alpha test (USA, 1917) was the first group intelligence test, made to screen army recruits; Stanford-Binet is an individual test and the Army General Classification Test came later (1940s).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: World of Learning includes information about
items.at: Universities, Colleges, Libraries, Museums, Archives, Research Institutes and Learned societies
items.x: The World of Learning (Europa/Routledge) is an annual directory of universities, colleges, libraries, museums, archives, research institutes and learned societies worldwide.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: When a group of people learn something and change their behavior and attitude as a result then we can say that this group has which type of learning?
items.x: Printed key: when a group learns and its behaviour and attitudes change as a result, the learning is called assimilated learning (educational psychology item, off this topic).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: "We forget something not by disuse but by other learning". Which of the following theory convey this meaning?
items.x: Guthrie's contiguity theory holds that forgetting comes not from disuse but from interference by new learning (new responses replace old ones).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Which one is the highest order of learning?
items.x: In Gagne's hierarchy of learning, problem-solving is the highest type; signal (conditioned-reflex) and stimulus-response learning are the lowest, with chaining in between.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: According to Psychologists, what is 'plateau' in learning process?
o: An indication of fatigue and boredom to give a gap in our trail for learning
The final stage of learning indicating the further attempts will lead to frustration
A Stage when the learner is consolidating his previous learning and preparing for further learning
A stage at which an individual faces some difficulty in progressing further
items.x: A plateau is a period of no visible progress in the learning curve; psychologists explain it as a stage when the learner consolidates earlier learning and prepares for further gains – not the final stage.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Teachers typically administer the following test for reading and math skills and using that results try to provide remedial instruction or place students within appropriately leveled classes.
items.x: A diagnostic test finds a pupil's specific weaknesses so that remedial teaching or level placement can follow; achievement tests measure what was learnt.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Which of the following was used by Bandura for his experiment on 'Social Learning Theory'?
items.x: Albert Bandura used the Bobo doll experiment (1961) to show children learn aggression by observing models (social learning theory). Rats, pigeons and dogs belong to Skinner, Pavlov and others. (Off-topic: psychology.)

items.s:
Which of the following statements is correct about 'shanghai technique'?

I. Shanghai Technique is to shape lesson so that it concentrates on a single concept.

II. UK has experimentally adopted this system.

III. It involves interactive teaching to an all-ability group in classroom.

IV. Subject covered in depth. Class does not move on till every student has performed well with the lesson.
items.x: The Shanghai (maths mastery) technique teaches one concept per lesson to the whole mixed-ability class interactively and does not move on until all have mastered it; the UK piloted it, so all statements are correct.

items.s: Emotional intelligence is―
o: The ability to score high in IQ tests
The ability to monitor one's own and others ' feelings and one's thinking and actions
The ability to avoid emotional responses in decision-making
The ability to manipulate others ' emotions
items.x: Emotional intelligence is the ability to perceive and monitor one's own and others' feelings and to use that to guide thinking and action. It is not IQ, avoiding emotions or manipulating others.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: The biggest reality according to pragmatism is?
items.x: Pragmatism (James, Dewey) holds that reality is not fixed but is constant change and progress, judged by practical consequences. So progress and change is the printed answer.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Counseling based on learning theories and principles is known as
items.x: Behaviour therapy applies the principles of learning theory (conditioning) to change behaviour. Play therapy, eclectic therapy and shock therapy are not based on learning theory. (Off-topic: psychology.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: What are Motives?
items.x: Motives are not seen directly. They are inferred from behaviour. (Off-topic: psychology.)

items.s: The recent statement made by the Indian Prime Minister that the Higher Education in India can be developed through adopting approach of:
o: Earmarking 60% of the national income for higher education
items.x: The Prime Minister's statement was that higher education can be expanded through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) approach, which combines government support with private investment. Outright privatisation, relying on foreign providers, and spending 60% of national income on higher education (an impossible share) were not the approach suggested.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: The report 'Learning Without Burden' is associated with:

items.x: IISc Bangalore was placed second in the National Ranking Index-2020.

items.x: The Expenditure Reforms Commission (2000-01) recommended phased decontrol of the fertiliser (urea) industry, to be complete by 1 April 2006; Government accepted it in the 2001-02 Budget.

items.s: Which one of the following best describes the main objective of 'Seed Village Concept'?
o: Encouraging the farmers to use their own farm seeds
Involving the farmers for training in quality seed
Earmarking some villages exclusively for the
Identifying the entrepreneurs in villages and providing
items.x: The seed village concept trains a group of farmers in quality seed production so they supply seed to themselves and neighbouring villages at the right time and affordable cost.

items.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
items.s: Development and spread of high-yielding varieties of rice and wheat suited to local ecologies was central to which of the following in India?
items.x: HYV seeds of wheat and rice, suited to local conditions, with fertiliser and irrigation, were the core of the Green Revolution; Grey, Silver and White refer to fertilisers, eggs and milk.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: How did the Green Revolution impact socio-economic disparities in rural India?
o: Reduced income inequality across all regions
Led to uniform economic growth in all rural areas
Increased disparities between large and small farmers due to differential access to technology
Fostered equal distribution of agricultural resources
items.x: The Green Revolution widened disparities between large and small farmers, who had unequal access to the new technology and credit.

items.s: Select the correct Colour-Commodity option related to Rainbow Revolution (food area)
items.x: Silver Revolution stands for eggs/poultry, so Silver - Eggs is right; Yellow is oilseeds (not fruits), Golden is horticulture/honey (not oilseeds) and Grey (not Brown) is fertilisers.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: The 'Yellow Revolution' in India is associated with:
o: increase in the production of oil seeds
increase in the production of fish and marine products
items.x: The Yellow Revolution relates to oilseeds (Technology Mission on Oilseeds, 1986); horticulture is Golden and fish Blue.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: The Green Revolution was introduced in which Five-Year Plan?
items.x:
Official key / most books: 3rd Plan. Strictly, the HYV programme began in kharif 1966, during the Annual Plans (Plan holiday 1966-69) just after the Third Plan (1961-66) (Rocket Indian Economy: 1966-67).
The new agricultural strategy (HYV seeds) behind the Green Revolution was introduced in the Third Five-Year Plan (1965), and showed results in the Annual Plans 1966-69.

items.s: Green revolution is also called as (one of the following):
items.x: The Green Revolution is also called the seed-fertiliser-water technology (HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, irrigation). Off-topic here; moved to Indian economy (agriculture).

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: 'Black Revolution' in India refers to increase in
items.x: The Black Revolution refers to petroleum/crude oil production. Eggs = Silver Revolution, oilseeds = Yellow Revolution.

items.x: The Green Revolution – Krishonnati Yojana (umbrella scheme, 2016-17) brought 11 agricultural schemes together.

items.x: Unviable farming, ineffective MSP and rural indebtedness cause agrarian distress; favourable terms of trade would help farmers, so they are not a cause.

items.x: The Bhu Seva (Bhudhaar) pilot began on 11 April 2018 in Jaggaiahpeta mandal and Vuyyuru of Krishna district (announced by Deputy CM K.E. Krishnamurthy); CM Chandrababu Naidu launched it statewide on 20 Nov 2018.

items.x: Punjab pioneered contract farming in India (PepsiCo tomato project, late 1980s).

items.x: NSSO rounds show the share of households reporting seasonal or chronic hunger (not getting two square meals) has fallen steadily since the 1980s - it has decreased. (Moved to the food-security row.)

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)

In urban India, malnutrition is not a problem
Compared to rural areas, higher percentage of population in Urban India suffer from malnutrition
Malnutrition levels are equal both in urban and Rural India

items.x: Semen is collected from cocks by abdominal massage, called 'milking'; candling checks eggs, brooding rears chicks.

items.x: Sheep and goats are commonly identified by ear tags (also ear notching); hot-iron branding is used for cattle.

items.x:
India was 3rd (after China and the USA) when older keys were set — now 2nd in world egg production (DAHD BAHS 2024)
India is now the 2nd largest egg producer in the world after China (142.77 billion eggs, 2023-24); older books and keys gave 3rd (after China and the USA).

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: How much concentrate mixture is given for every one litre of cow milk over and above the maintenance
items.x: Feeding standard: a dairy cow gets about 0.4 kg of concentrate per litre of milk (1 kg per 2.5 litres) over maintenance; a buffalo about 0.5 kg per litre.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Ideal market weight of pigs at slaughter
items.x: Pigs are marketed at about 80-90 kg live weight (6-8 months), the weight at which feed efficiency and carcass quality are best.

items.s: In which of the following years, the National Food Processing Policy was formulated?
items.x: The draft National Food Processing Policy came in 2005 (with the Vision, Strategy and Action Plan for food processing); 2002-2004 are wrong. Agro-processing item, moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Feeding of excess proteins to Ruminants causes
items.x: Excess protein in a ruminant's diet is broken down to ammonia in the rumen, raising its pH and causing alkaline indigestion. Acid indigestion follows excess grain (carbohydrate).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'Gram Samridhi Yojana'.

a. Gram Samridhi Yojana, is a Rs. 3,000 crore scheme funded by the World Bank and the Government of India, to strengthen the unorganised food processing sector concentrated in rural areas.

b. World Bank will be giving Rs. 1,000 crore, Rs. 1,500 crore will be borne by the Centre while state governments will put in Rs. 500 crore.

c. The scheme will be run in Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Punjab for a 5-year period.
Which of the above statement is incorrect?
items.x: As keyed, statement b on the funding split of the Gram Samridhi Yojana is the incorrect one.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: After Reorganization, the "Vijaya" milk brand belongs to?
items.x: After bifurcation both States' dairy federations use the 'Vijaya' brand (Telangana as 'Vijaya Telangana') and the ownership is still disputed, so neither 'Telangana' nor 'AP' alone is right. Off-topic (dairy), moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Turning of the eggs should be done during the incubation period in chicken
items.x: Eggs are turned from day 1 to day 18 of the 21-day chicken incubation; turning stops in the last three days (hatching period).

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The most widely used extender for frozen semen is
items.x: Tris (tris-egg yolk-citrate-glycerol) is the most widely used extender for frozen bull semen.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: India is ranked first in milk production in the world in 2015-16 with the production accounting for following percentage of world production?
items.x: In 2015-16 India produced about 155.5 million tonnes of milk, roughly 18.5% of world production, and ranked first. 50% and 30% are far too high.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which of the following is NOT considered an Indian Major Carp?
items.x: The Indian major carps are rohu, catla and mrigal. Tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus) is an exotic African cichlid. (Off-topic: fisheries.)

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The percentage of CO2 in an egg incubator for achieving optimum hatchability
items.x: Optimum hatchability needs CO2 kept low, about 0.3-0.5% in the incubator; higher levels cut hatchability.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The primary purpose of vaccinating animals is
items.x: Vaccination of animals primarily prevents infectious diseases; it does not treat animals or prevent non-infectious diseases.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: What is the moisture percent present in hay
items.x: Well-cured hay keeps about 15-18% moisture. Wetter hay moulds. (Off-topic: animal husbandry.)

items.s: Kanva-2, S-36, S-14 and S-54 are hybrid varieties of
items.x: Kanva-2, S-36, S-54 and similar are high-yielding mulberry varieties bred for sericulture (CSRTI Mysore). (Off-topic: sericulture.)

items.s: Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme for genetic upgradation of Bovines in the country is being implemented under which scheme?
items.x: The Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme for genetic upgradation of bovines is implemented under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The vaccine strain not used for vaccinating broilers is
items.x: R2B (Mukteswar) is a mesogenic Newcastle disease strain used only as a booster in older layer birds, not in broilers; LaSota and IBD vaccines are used in broilers.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The type of vaccine commonly used for control of foot and mouth disease is
items.x: Foot-and-mouth disease is controlled with inactivated (killed) vaccines in India.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following vaccine needs to be handled carefully to avoid infection to vaccinator
items.x: Brucella vaccine (live S19 strain) can infect humans, so vaccinators must handle it carefully.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives of the Government of India's funded Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Provide subsidy to farmers for the purchase of cattle feeds
items.x: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (launched 2014) aims to raise bovine productivity and milk production and to conserve and develop indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds. Giving farmers a subsidy to buy cattle feed is not one of its objectives.

items.s: Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has declared 2002-03 as the
items.x: APPSC key: CII declared 2002-03 the Year of Merger and Acquisition (not verified).

items.s: The predominant type of organisation in Indian industry is
items.x: By number of units, proprietorship is the predominant form of organisation (about 96% of unincorporated non-farm enterprises, NSS 73rd round); co-operatives are a small share. Joint-stock companies lead only by output and capital.

items.s: What is the most remarkable aspect of Indian industry since Independence?
items.x: The most remarkable feature of Indian industry since Independence is its diversification – from a narrow consumer-goods base to a wide range of capital and basic goods. (Printed: no key.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following Public Sector Company is the most profitable company for the financial year 2016-17 in India?
items.x: In 2016-17 Indian Oil Corporation overtook ONGC as the most profitable public sector company.

items.s: “Promotion and development of Micro and Small Enterprises by supporting them in marketing of products produced and services rendered by them”, comes under which policy of Government of India?
o: Public Procurement (Preference to make in India) Policy
items.x: Support to MSEs in marketing their goods and services through government purchase falls under the public procurement policy; among the options that is the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) policy – UDAY, Skill India and Mission Indradhanush are unrelated.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: The abbreviation SSI means:
items.x: SSI stands for Small Scale Industries (now part of MSMEs).

items.s: Meera Seth Committee related to
items.x: The Meera Seth Committee (1996) reviewed the development of handlooms.

items.s: In July 2022, the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with which of the following banks for providing loans to the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in 39 industrial parks in the first phase and other MSMEs in the next phase?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
items.x: In July 2022 APIIC signed an MoU with Punjab National Bank to finance MSMEs in 39 industrial parks (SIDBI's APIIC MoU came later, in 2023).

items.s: The Indian City in which the first plastic park is located
items.x:
Most keys: Chennai (Thiruvallur park). Strictly: Odisha's Paradip park is usually called the first to start work (drishtiias.com 'Plastic Parks in India').
Kept at Chennai: Tamil Nadu's plastic park at Thiruvallur (Chennai region) is among the first parks under the Chemicals Ministry's scheme, and no other option has one. Odisha (Paradip, Jagatsinghpur) is often called the first State to start work on a plastic park.

items.s: The absence of barriers to entry in monopolistic competition means that in the long run firms
o: Quit the market for lack of profit
items.x: With free entry, new firms enter until profits are competed away, so in the long run firms under monopolistic competition earn zero economic (only normal) profit, not supernormal profit or losses.

items.s: Which of the following most closely approximates our definition of oligopoly?
o: The barber shops in a city
The petrol stations in a city
items.x: A few big firms dominating the cigarette industry are an oligopoly; barber shops, petrol stations and paddy farmers are closer to competitive markets.

items.s:
Assertion (A): Many industries in India have obtained ISO 9001 and ISO 9002 certification in the recent past.
Reason (R) : There has been considerable liberalization in the licensing policy of the Government of India.
Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct expla-
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Many Indian firms have ISO 9001/9002 certification (A) and licensing was liberalised in 1991 (R), but certification follows quality standards, not licensing – both true, R not the explanation. (Moved to the licensing row.)

items.s: The Lerner index equals
items.x: The Lerner index of market power = (P - MC)/P, ranging from 0 (perfect competition) towards 1. (Off-topic: moved to the competition row.)

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: The Committee that recommended the policy of disinvestment is
items.x: The Rangarajan Committee (1993) recommended the disinvestment policy for PSUs (up to 49%, 74% in some); Chelliah = tax, Lakdawala = poverty estimation.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.s: In 1991-92, against the target to mobilise Rs.2,500 crore through disinvestment of Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs), the Government of India was able to mobilise what amount of the following, which was more than the target?
items.x: In 1991-92 disinvestment raised about Rs 3,038 crore (option Rs 3,040 crore) against a target of Rs 2,500 crore. Disinvestment item, moved.

items.s: Ease of Doing Business ranking for the States in India is released by :
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal
items.x: State Ease of Doing Business rankings (Business Reform Action Plan) are released by DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

items.s: According to the International Trade Administration (ITA), India emerged as the ____ largest manufacturer of mobile handsets in the world in 2021.
items.x: India became the second-largest manufacturer of mobile handsets in the world after China, as noted by the US International Trade Administration for 2021.

items.s: Which country is the second largest producer of mobile phones in the world?
items.x: India is the world's second-largest producer of mobile phones after China; Taiwan, Malaysia and Singapore are not.

items.src: Technical Assistant (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistant in AP
items.s: Stand-Up India Scheme relates to encouraging
o: Sports persons to participate at international level
items.x: Stand-Up India (2016) gives bank loans of Rs 10 lakh-1 crore to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs for greenfield units.

items.s: In India, Special Economic Zone policy was announced in :
items.x: The SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000; the SEZ Act followed in 2005. SEZ topic, moved to row 68.

items.x: The SEZ policy was first introduced in 2000 (1 April 2000); 2005 is the SEZ Act. Moved to row 68.

items.s: Special Economic Zone Act was passed by the Parliament, in the year :
items.x: Parliament passed the SEZ Act in 2005; it came into force with the Rules on 10 February 2006. Moved to row 68.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh

items.s: What is the number of notified Special Economic Zones in the state of Andhra Pradesh till July 2023?
items.x:
Most keys: 32. Strictly: 30 SEZs were notified in AP as of 30 Nov 2023 (Lok Sabha reply, 13 Dec 2023; search result); 32 is the formal-approvals figure.
Printed key kept (32). The Lok Sabha reply of 13 Dec 2023 lists 30 notified SEZs (25 operational) in AP as of 30 Nov 2023; 32 matches the formal-approvals count.

items.s: The aggregate investment in Indian Special Economic Zones (SEZs) till end September 2011 amounted to
items.x: Total investment in SEZs till 30 Sept 2011 was about Rs 2,77,259 crore, i.e. Rs 2.77 lakh crore. SEZ item, moved.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Types of Investment Models?
items.x: Investment models are public, private and public-private partnership; 'non-foreign investment model' is not a recognised model.

items.s: Infrastructure investment requirement during 12th Five Year Plan, projected by the Planning Commission, is
items.x:
Most keys: Rs 45 lakh crore (Approach Paper, US$ 1 trillion). Strictly: the final 12th Plan document projected about Rs 55.7 lakh crore (general knowledge, not checked).
The 12th Plan approach paper put infrastructure investment at about Rs 45 lakh crore (US$ 1 trillion), the keyed figure; the final Plan document raised it to about Rs 55.7 lakh crore.

items.s:
With reference to 'National Investment and Infrastructure Fund', which of the following statements is/are correct?

2. It has a corpus of ₹4,00,000 crore at present.

items.x: Both are wrong: NIIF is a government-anchored fund under the Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance), not a NITI Aayog organ, and its planned corpus was ₹40,000 crore, not ₹4 lakh crore.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab

items.x:

Goyal's targets kept shifting – full electrification by 2022 (2018 plans), then within four years (2019), and 'electric by 2024, net-zero by 2030' – the option keyed is 2024 (now over 99% of the broad-gauge network is electrified).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: The New Centrally Sponsored Umbrella Program for the holistic high way development is?
items.x: Bharatmala Pariyojana (2017) is the umbrella programme for holistic highway development (economic corridors, border and coastal roads).

newer metros have opened since 2017 (e.g. Kanpur, Agra, Bhopal, Indore) — Lucknow is no longer the latest (general knowledge, not checked)
At the time of the exam (2017) Lucknow Metro was the latest to open; several metros have opened since.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St

items.x: Gujarat (2015) became the first State to launch an Agro-Solar Policy letting farmers generate and sell solar power.

items.s: Which kind of power accounts for the largest share of power generation in India?
items.x: Thermal (mainly coal) power gives the largest share of India's electricity generation – far ahead of hydro, nuclear and solar.

items.x: As keyed, AP's RDSS plan aimed to save about ₹2,000 crore in transmission and distribution losses.

items.x: Anantapur (Ananthapuramu): in 2025 Tata Power Renewable (after its March 2025 MoU with NREDCAP) tied up with Suzlon for a 700 MW, Rs 6,000 crore wind project there; Anantapur is AP's main wind belt, not Guntur, Visakhapatnam or Krishna.

items.x: The printed key is Andhra Pradesh, which was yet to take over 100% of its DISCOMs' debt under UDAY at that time. The notes do not cover it.

items.s: Liberalization of Indian economy since 1990 has resulted in
o: The transformation of patterns of domestic and foreign investment
increased international cooperation in science and technology
rapid expansion of domestic and foreign trade
rapid increase in international investment in infrastructure

items.x: The 1991 BoP crisis forced immediate stabilisation – devaluation of the rupee (July 1991) and fiscal correction; deregulation, financial-sector and PSU reforms were the longer structural-adjustment measures.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St

items.x:

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: The most important legacy of the Rajiv Gandhi government in India was the background research on ____, which was carried out within the Prime Minister's Office, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and the Ministry of Finance.
items.x: Rajiv Gandhi's government began the background work on economic liberalisation (deregulation, tech missions) that shaped the 1991 reforms.

items.x: CII proposed a 10-point agenda for economic revival (June 2012 and again in August-September 2013).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer & Analyst Grade-II (A
items.s:
Identify the option that arranges the following major policy moves by the Union Government in chronological order of their announcement.

1. Expansion of PLI (Production-Linked Incentive) Scheme - A move to extend incentives to more sectors, boosting domestic manufacturing and exports

2. Introduction of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Framework - A policy aimed at enhancing digital governance and promoting seamless digital transactions

3. National Logistics Policy 2.0 - An updated policy designed to improve supply chain efficiency and reduce logistics costs

4. FDI Policy Reforms 2024 - Amendments to foreign direct investment (FDI) rules to attract more global investments into key sectors
items.x:
The stem's 'National Logistics Policy 2.0' is not a recognised policy name; the key assumes it means the National Logistics Policy 2022. Strictly the question is loosely framed.
Taking 'National Logistics Policy 2.0' as the National Logistics Policy of September 2022: PLI expansion (Nov 2020) → logistics policy (2022) → DPI framework (G20, 2023) → FDI reforms (2024), i.e. 1-3-2-4. Moved to row 72 (reform record since 2014).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries, AP Fisheries Service
items.s: Out of the following, which could be considered as a labour sector reform?
o: Giving free hands to Trade unions
Allowing sick industry to close after paying ex-gratia to workers
Not allowing any industry to close
items.x: An exit policy – letting sick units close after paying workers – is a labour-market reform; encouraging informality or banning closures is not.

items.s: India's share in total world exports
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1.66); it is added as option 5.
India's share of world merchandise exports was about 1.5-1.7% around the exam (WTO: 1.48% in 2010, 1.66% in 2011; Economic Survey 2012-13: 1.7% in 2011); 1.44, 1.88, 2.44 and 2.88 all miss it. Moved to trade.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT an export from India?
items.x: India consumes almost all its milk at home, so milk and milk products were not a significant export, while manufactured goods, handicrafts, textiles and gems were major exports.

items.src: APSLPRB SI Final Written Exam Paper-IV 2023
items.s: After 2002, India registered a foreign trade surplus during
items.x: In June 2020 India recorded a merchandise trade surplus, its first in about 18 years, as imports collapsed during the lockdown.

items.s: What is the experience of the Indian Economy related to International Trade?
items.x: India's imports have persistently exceeded its exports, so its experience is a trade deficit; balance of trade and BoP equilibrium are not outcomes but concepts.

items.s: Which country accounts for the largest share of Indian exports?
items.x: The USA is the largest destination of Indian exports (then and now); the UAE is second, the UK and Australia smaller.

items.s:
With reference to trade, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It represents demand and supply both.
2. It deals with only the demand side.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Code :
items.x: Trade is exchange between buyers and sellers, so it involves both demand and supply; it does not deal with demand alone.

items.s:
Read the following statements about Supply Chain Resilience Initiative (SCRI) :
1. In the context of International trade, supply chain resilience is an approach that helps a country to ensure uninterrupted supply of import in an uexpected situation.
2. This is an initiative of five countries, India is one of them.
Choose the correct code :
items.x: SCRI aims at resilient supply chains for uninterrupted supply (1 true); it was launched by three countries – India, Japan and Australia – not five (2 false). (Moved to the trade row.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains P
items.s: Which of the following is not a standard measure to ascertain degree of openness of an economy?
o: Extent of dominance of PSUs in commercial activities
items.x: Openness is measured by openness to trade and to foreign capital (and state dominance in commerce); the level of online trade is not a standard measure. (Moved to the trade row.)

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: In the early 1960s, at a time when most distinguished development economists were talking about the virtues of import substitution, it was ____ who has pointed out, through a detailed empirical analysis, that trade would be an important factor for the development of a less developed country such as India.
items.x: Manmohan Singh's Oxford thesis (published 1964 as 'India's Export Trends and Prospects for Self-Sustained Growth') argued that trade was important for India's development, against the import-substitution consensus.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries, AP Fisheries Service
items.s: As per recent data published by Government of India for 2015, exports of textiles and apparels constitute approximately how much percentage of the total commodity exports of India in value terms?
items.x: Printed key kept: textiles and apparel were about 15% of India's merchandise exports in 2015 (about 13-15% in DGCI&S data); not verified.

items.s: In which one of the following commodities was India's percentage share in the world market in the year 2004 the largest ?
items.x: In 2004 India's share of world exports was rice 18.0%, iron ore 17.8%, tea 10.3% and woven cotton fabrics 3.0%, so rice was the largest. Off-topic (trade).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv

o: As a measure of retaliation against USA
To check import of fungus infected commodities
items.x: The 10% import duty on wheat and tur (pigeon pea) in 2017 was imposed to check falling domestic prices after bumper harvests and cheap imports, protecting farmers.

items.s:
Consider the following actions which the Government can take:

A. Devaluing the domestic currency

B. Reduction in the export subsidy

C. Adopting suitable policies which attract greater FDI and more funds from FIIs
Which of the above action/actions can help in reducing the current account deficit?
items.x: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer, and FDI/FII-friendly policies bring in funds (UPSC key d); cutting export subsidies would hurt exports. Off-topic (BoP), moved.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St

items.x: Of the options only 'foreign currency reserves' relates to the balance of payments – the BoP is the record of a country's external transactions, and its overall balance shows up as a change in forex reserves; CRR, SLR and demonetisation are domestic monetary terms.

items.src: Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, As

items.x: The Budget 2017-18 highlights put India's foreign exchange reserves at US$ 361 billion as on 20 January 2017.

items.x: NRIs send the largest foreign exchange to India as remittances (India is the world's top remittance recipient), ahead of MNCs, foreign banks or tourists.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

items.x: The United States holds the world's largest official gold reserves (about 8,133 tonnes) per the World Gold Council – far ahead of others; India, Japan and the UAE hold much less.

items.s: Which of the following statements is not true in the context of foreign exchange reserves of India?
o: Gold and Foreign currency assets present with
It is maintained by the Reserve Bank of India
Special Drawing Rights are not included in this
Current state of Foreign exchange is satisfactory in
items.x: India's forex reserves include foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position, held by the RBI – so 'SDRs are not included' is the untrue statement.

items.s: According to the Reserve Bank of India, what was the total values of the foreign exchange reserves of India in 2018-19?
items.x: According to the RBI, India's foreign exchange reserves at end-March 2019 (2018-19) were US$ 412,871 million.

items.s: What place does India occupy among the world's largest possessors of International (Forex) Reserves?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (4th); it is added as option 5.
the key was 6th — now 4th, with $785.71 bn on 15 Sep 2026, after China, Japan and Switzerland (app notes 3:76 sub 10, Carpediem CA)
India's place among forex reserve holders has changed over time (6th was the key when asked; now 4th): with $785.71 bn on 15 Sep 2026 India became 4th, after China, Japan and Switzerland, overtaking Russia.

items.s: When a country devalues its currency, its effect would be :
o: imports become cheaper and exports become costly
imports become costly and exports become cheaper
both imports and exports become cheaper
both import and exports become costly
items.x: Devaluation makes imports costly and exports cheaper abroad; the first option reverses the effect. Exchange-rate topic, moved to row 76.

items.s: The outcome of devaluation of currency is :
o: Increase in imports and exports in the country
Decrease in imports and exports in the country
Increase of exports and decrease of imports in the
Increase of imports and decrease of exports in the
items.x: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer, so exports rise and imports fall. Moved to row 76.

items.s: The major aim of devaluation is to
items.x: The main aim of devaluation is to encourage exports by making them cheaper abroad; imports become dearer. Moved to row 76.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P

items.x: The rupee symbol (₹), designed by D. Udaya Kumar, was approved by the Union Cabinet on 15 July 2010. Currency question, moved.

items.x: The WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) was held in Abu Dhabi, UAE, in February 2024. Moved to row 77.

items.x: India signed the CEPA with Japan on 16 February 2011. Moved to row 78.

items.x: India signed the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement with Malaysia on 18 February 2011 (Putrajaya). Moved to row 78.

items.x: On 13 January 2002 Japan and Singapore signed the Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement, Japan's (and Asia's) first bilateral FTA; China and Bangladesh signed no FTA in 2002. Moved to row 78.

items.x: Israel signed an FTA with the UAE on 31 May 2022, its first with an Arab country. Moved to row 78.

items.x: India signed the Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) with Australia (in force 29 December 2022); with the UAE it is a CEPA. Moved to row 78.

items.src: APPSC AP Municipal Junior Accounts Officers 2012

items.s: A Multinational is:
o: a company operating in several countries
a company having shareholders from more than one country
a company which does charitable work in poor countries
a company that operates only in those countries that do not have import restrictions
items.x: A multinational company is one that operates (owns production or service facilities) in several countries; shareholders' nationality or charity work do not define it.

items.s:
With reference to foreign-owned e-commerce firms operating in India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. They can sell their own goods in addition to offering their platforms as market-places.

B. The degree to which they can own big sellers on their platforms is limited.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x:
Most keys (Vajiram & Ravi, official-key reports): B only. Some keys (Testbook, GetMarks): neither A nor B, holding that no ownership limit applies.
Foreign-owned e-commerce firms may only run marketplaces – no inventory model – so they cannot sell their own goods (A wrong). Since 2018, a vendor with over 25% of the platform's sales counts as controlled, limiting how far they can own big sellers (B correct).

items.s: The small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) was set up in the year

items.x: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935, so its 85th foundation day fell on 1 April 2020.

items.x: In August 2021 Das said the RBI could begin its first digital-currency trials by December 2021 (the e₹ pilots finally began in November–December 2022). RBI/currency question, moved.

items.x: M1 (narrow money) = currency with the public + demand (checkable) deposits + other deposits with the RBI; gold, credit cards and MMMFs are not part of it. (Moved to the money supply row.)

items.x: Money should be generally acceptable, legal tender and portable; a fall in its purchasing power (as in inflation) is not a desirable attribute.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M

items.s: The demand for money will fall if:
items.x: Higher real interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding money, so money demand falls; higher real GDP or prices raise it, and expected deflation makes people hold more money.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016

items.x: The ₹1,000, ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 notes were demonetised on 16 January 1978 under the High Denomination Bank Notes (Demonetisation) Act, 1978 (PM Morarji Desai). (Moved to the money-supply row.)

In 2011 ICICI Bank was India's largest private bank by assets (now HDFC Bank, especially after its 2023 merger with HDFC Ltd).

items.x:

items.x: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to cover the 149.6 million km to the Earth, so 8 minutes.
