items.x: The question contrasts Earth's fluid (outer) core with the Moon's core, which books describe as solid; the Moon has in fact a small solid inner core with a fluid outer layer (NASA 2011). Off-topic (solar system), moved.

items.s:
Arrange the following planets in order of their nearness to the Sun

I. Mars
II. Mercury
III. Venus
IV. Earth
items.x: Order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars = II, III, IV, I. Off-topic (solar system), moved.

items.s:
Match the following.
List-I:
a. Titan
b. Ganymede
c. Phobos
d. Triton
List-II: i. Jupiter ii. Mars iii. Neptune iv. Saturn
The correct answer is:
items.x: Titan orbits Saturn, Ganymede Jupiter, Phobos Mars and Triton Neptune. Moved.

items.src: Assistant Director of Fisheries in AP Fisheries Service 2017
items.s: With which material the inter galactic space is filled up?
items.x: Intergalactic space is almost a perfect vacuum (a few atoms per cubic metre); air, oxygen, nitrogen, CO2 and ozone exist only in planetary atmospheres. No printed key; off-topic (universe), moved.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Which of the following continents witnessed total solar eclipse in August, 2017?
items.x: The total solar eclipse of 21 August 2017 crossed the USA coast to coast, i.e. North America. Moved to the solar-system row.

items.s: The bright outer layer of the Sun is known as :
items.x: The photosphere is the Sun's bright visible 'surface', emitting most of its light; ionosphere and mesosphere are layers of Earth's atmosphere and sunspots are dark patches on the photosphere.

items.s: In the universe, what are pulsars?
o: Radio waves emitted by a star
items.x: Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars that emit beams of radiation seen as regular pulses.

items.s: Highly dense stars are called –
items.x: Neutron stars – collapsed cores of massive stars – are the densest stars known; a supernova is an explosion and asteroids are not stars.

items.s:
Consider the following pairs : Objects in space Description
1. Cepheids : Giant clouds of dust and gas in space
2. Nebulae : Stars which brighten and dim periodically
3. Pulsars : Neutron stars that are formed when massive stars run out of fuel and collapse
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
items.x: Only pair 3 is right: pulsars are neutron stars formed when massive stars collapse. Cepheids are stars that brighten and dim periodically, and nebulae are clouds of dust and gas – pairs 1 and 2 are swapped.

items.s: In January 2023, scientists at NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) announced the discovery of a planet named ____, slightly smaller in size than the earth, orbiting within the habitable zone of its star.
items.x: In January 2023 NASA's TESS mission announced TOI 700 e, slightly smaller than Earth, in the habitable zone of TOI 700 (TOI 700 d was found in 2020).

items.s: Which one of the following is a spacecraft?
items.x: Cassini (NASA–ESA, Saturn, RTG-powered) was a spacecraft; Apophis is an asteroid, Spitzer a space telescope and TecSAR an Israeli radar satellite.

items.s: The basic fuel for the thermo-nuclear reactions going on within the sun is
items.x: Hydrogen is the basic fuel of the Sun's thermonuclear (fusion) reactions, fusing into helium.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: What is the significance of graphic representation?
o: They make comparison of variables easy
Complete accuracy is not possible on a graph
Only a few characteristics can be depicted on a graph
items.x: Graphs and diagrams make comparison of variables easy at a glance; inaccuracy and the few traits shown are limitations, not the significance. Off-topic statistics, moved.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
items.s: If a ship is approaching the shore from the deep sea, which portion of the ship would be first seen by a person standing on the seashore?
items.x: Because the Earth's surface is curved, the top of the ship – the mast – is seen first and the hull last.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: The area represented by contours whose values decrease towards the centre (1300, 1280, 1260 from outer to inner) is a ____
items.x: Closed contours whose values fall towards the centre show a depression (hollow); rising values would show a hill. Off-topic (maps/contours), moved.

items.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
A. Longitude
B. Pole
C. Prime latitude
D. Axis
List-II:
I. Straight line
II. Circle
III. Semi circle
IV. Dot
items.x: A longitude (meridian) is a semicircle, a pole a dot, the prime latitude (Equator) a circle and the axis a straight line. Moved to latitudes/longitudes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: A level surface is a surface ____ to the ____ of the earth
items.x: In surveying, a level surface is a curved surface parallel to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth (every point normal to the plumb line). Off-topic (geodesy/surveying), moved to Earth – shape and geoid.

items.s: A person stood alone in a desert on a dark night and wanted to reach his village which was situated 5 km east of the point where he was standing. He had no instruments to find the direction, but he located the polestar. The most convenient way now to reach his village is to walk in the:
o: direction keeping the polestar to his left
direction keeping the polestar to his right
items.x: The Pole Star marks north; facing east, north lies on your left, so he should walk keeping the Pole Star to his left.

items.s: The shape of the Earth's orbit is
items.x: Earth's orbit is an ellipse so close to a circle that it is only a slightly 'scaled' oval; 'elongated oval' exaggerates it and 'circular' ignores the small eccentricity (0.017).

items.src: Technical Assistant (Hydrology) & Laboratory Assistant in AP
items.s: The Indian City which experiences longest period of sunlight during summer is
items.x: Srinagar, the northernmost of these cities, has the longest summer day because day length in summer increases with latitude.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Isogonic lines pass through points of ____
items.x: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination; isoclinic lines join points of equal dip.

items.s:
Match the following
List-I:
(A) Shale
(B) Limestone
(C) Coal
(D) Sandstone
List-II: (i) Quartzite (ii) Diamond (iii) Slate (iv) Marble
items.x: Shale → slate, limestone → marble, coal → diamond (the textbook pairing; strictly graphite), sandstone → quartzite. Moved to rocks.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Two statements are given labelled as
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
Select the correct option based on the given statements.
Assertion (A): Felsic rocks contain relatively high amounts of iron, magnesium, and calcium.
Reason (R): Olivine and Pyroxene are dark in colour.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
items.x: A is false: felsic rocks are rich in silica, feldspar and aluminium, while mafic rocks are rich in iron and magnesium. R is true: olivine and pyroxene are dark. Moved to Geography.

items.s: What is mountain building by folding and faulting due to horizontal (tangential) forces called?
items.x: Orogenic movements act through horizontal forces and build mountains such as the Himalayas.

items.s: Which forces mainly cause epeirogenic movements?
items.x: Epeirogenic movements are vertical and uplift or warp continents and plateaus.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about diastrophism:
1. Orogenic movements uplift or warp whole continents and plateaus.
2. Sudden movements such as earthquakes and volcanoes are treated separately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Uplift or warping of continents is epeirogenic, not orogenic; sudden movements are treated separately.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of folds with increasing pressure:
1. A symmetrical fold comes before an asymmetrical fold.
2. A nappe forms before a recumbent fold.
3. A recumbent fold forms after an asymmetrical fold.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: The order is symmetrical, asymmetrical, recumbent and finally nappe, so a nappe forms after (not before) a recumbent fold.

items.s: In plate-tectonic terms, what are the Eastern Ghats?
o: Old, highly eroded, discontinuous hills of the stable Gondwana shield
Block mountains of recently uplifted nappes
Young fold mountains formed by recent continental collision
Volcanic hills formed along a rift
items.x: The Eastern Ghats are old, highly eroded and discontinuous hills of the stable Gondwana shield, not young fold mountains.

items.s: What are an up-arched fold and a down-troughed fold respectively called?
items.x: An anticline is an up-arched fold, while a syncline is a down-troughed fold. Horst and graben are fault blocks, not folds.

items.s: Which one of the following is an old fold mountain range?
items.x: The Aravallis are old, worn-down fold mountains and are among the oldest mountain systems in India.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Alps – Young fold mountains of Europe
Appalachians – Old fold mountains of North America
Urals – Old fold mountains along the Europe–Asia divide
Rockies – Old fold mountains of North America
items.x: The Rockies are young fold mountains of North America; the Appalachians are the old ones.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Himalayas?
o: Their formation began about 70 million years ago and continues at present
They were formed from sediments of the Tethys Sea
Their uplift is associated with the Eocene, Miocene and Pliocene epochs
The Siwaliks are the oldest Himalayan range
items.x: The Siwaliks are the youngest Himalayan range, not the oldest.

items.s: With rising pressure, which fold forms next after an asymmetrical fold?
items.x: The sequence is symmetrical, asymmetrical, overfold, recumbent and nappe.

items.s: Which one of the following is NOT an old fold mountain?
items.x: The Rockies are young (Tertiary/Alpine) fold mountains; the Aravallis, Appalachians and Urals are old, worn-down folds.

items.s: Which is the youngest Himalayan range, with simple Jura-type folds?
items.x: The Siwaliks are the youngest Himalayan range and show simple Jura-type folds.

items.s: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is bounded by which of the following fault systems?
o: Two thrust faults on both sides
A normal fault in the north and the Himalayan Frontal Fault in the south
The Himalayan Frontal Fault in the north and a normal fault in the south
Two strike-slip faults in the north and south
items.x: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is bounded by the Himalayan Frontal Fault to the north and a normal fault to the south.

items.s: Which of the following is an example of a block mountain in India?
items.x: The Satpura is a block mountain, flanked by the rift valleys of the Narmada and Tapi.

items.s: The Himalayan MCT, MBT and HFF are examples of which one of the following?
items.x: The Himalayan Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault are examples of thrust faults.

items.s: What is a low-angle reverse fault called?
items.x: A thrust fault is a low-angle reverse fault; in a normal fault the hanging wall moves down and a strike-slip fault moves horizontally.

items.s: Which lake lies at the southern end of the East African Rift?
items.x: The East African Rift holds a series of mostly freshwater lakes with Lake Malawi at its southern end; Lake Victoria lies between the two branches and is not a rift lake.

items.s: In the Vosges–Rhine example, what is the Rhine Valley?
items.x: The Rhine Valley is a graben (sunken block); the Vosges are horsts, i.e. block mountains.

items.s: The Satpura is a block mountain lying between the rift valleys of which rivers?
items.x: The Satpura is a block mountain between the rift valleys of the Narmada and Tapi.

items.s: What are horsts also known as?
items.x: A horst is an uplifted block between faults, so it forms a block mountain; a sunken block (graben) forms a rift valley.

items.s: Which of the following lakes is NOT a rift lake of the East African Rift?
items.x: Lake Victoria lies in a shallow basin between the rift arms, so it is not a rift lake; Lake Malawi lies at the rift's southern end.

items.s: Which force produces a normal fault?
items.x: A normal fault forms under tension, with the hanging wall moving down; reverse and thrust faults form under compression.

items.s: In a reverse fault, which force acts and how does the hanging wall move?
items.x: A reverse fault forms under compression and its hanging wall moves up; a normal fault forms under tension.

items.s:
Following are the intrusive landforms of volcanic activity and their characteristic features:

I. Batholiths: Huge mass of igneous rocks, usually granite at the deeper layers of the crust.

II. Phacoliths: Large igneous mounds with a dome-shaped upper surface.

III. Dykes: Wall-like structures developed by solidifying almost perpendicular to the ground.

IV. Sills: The near horizontal bodies of intrusive igneous rocks.
Which of the above are correctly matched?
items.x: A large dome-shaped mound is a laccolith; a phacolith is a wavy, lens-shaped mass at the base of synclines or top of anticlines, so II is wrong. Moved.

items.s: Barren island is located in-
items.x: Barren Island, India's only active volcano, lies in the Andaman Sea, Bay of Bengal, ~135 km NE of Port Blair. Moved.

items.s:
With reference to 'Indonesia', which of the following statements is / are correct?
(1) It comprises of over 15,000 islands.
(2) It has over 150 active volcanoes.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Code:
items.x: Indonesia has about 17,000 islands but roughly 127–130 active volcanoes, fewer than 150, so only statement 1 is correct. Moved.

items.s: The most active Volcano is –
items.x: Kilauea (Hawaii) is commonly cited as the world's most active volcano; Vesuvius and Fuji are dormant-to-active, Cotopaxi less frequent. Moved.

items.s: Which gas is present in the greatest proportion among the principal gases released by volcanoes?
items.x: Volcanic gases consist mostly of water vapour, followed by carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and hydrogen sulphide.

items.s: Composite or stratovolcanoes constitute approximately what share of the Earth's volcanoes?
items.x: Composite volcanoes, with viscous lava, steep cones and explosive eruptions, make up approximately 60% of Earth's volcanoes.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mauna Loa — caldera formed by explosive collapse
Mount Aso — one of the world's largest calderas
Etna — complex volcano with several overlapping vents only
Dukono — shield volcano with gentle basaltic slopes
items.x: Mount Aso is one of the world's largest calderas. Mauna Loa is a shield volcano, while Dukono is listed as a complex volcano.

items.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a complex or compound volcano?
items.x: Taal in the Philippines is a complex or compound volcano. Dukono is in Indonesia, while Mount Aso is a caldera in Japan.

items.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Strombolian and Vulcanian eruptions?
o: Vulcanian eruptions consist only of gentle lava flows.
Strombolian eruptions are frequent and mild, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.
Strombolian eruptions are always more explosive than Vulcanian eruptions.
Both terms refer exclusively to dormant volcanoes.
items.x: Strombolian eruptions involve frequent, mild bursts of bombs and ash, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.

items.s: In which country is Mount Aso, among the world's largest calderas, located?
items.x: Mount Aso in Japan is a caldera, among the world's largest.

items.s: Which one of the following is an extrusive volcanic landform?
items.x: Lava plateaus, cinder and composite cones, craters, calderas and lava flows are extrusive volcanic landforms. Batholiths, lopoliths and phacoliths are intrusive forms.

items.s: What is a vertical wall of igneous rock cutting across the rock beds called?
items.x: A dyke is a vertical wall cutting across beds; a sill is a horizontal sheet parallel to the beds. Dykes fed the Deccan Traps.

items.s: What is a large, often dome-shaped mass of granite occurring at great depth and exposed after denudation called?
items.x: A batholith is a huge mass of granite emplaced at depth. It may become exposed after denudation removes the overlying rocks.

items.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lopolith — wavy mass in a folded structure
Phacolith — wavy mass at the base of a syncline or top of an anticline
Laccolith — vertical wall cutting across rock beds
items.x: A phacolith is a wavy intrusive mass occurring at the base of a syncline or the top of an anticline. A lopolith is saucer-shaped, a laccolith is dome-shaped with a flat base, and a dyke is a vertical wall.

items.s: What is a dome-shaped intrusive body with a flat base, fed by a pipe from below, called?
items.x: Domes with a flat base are laccoliths; a phacolith is a wavy mass, so calling phacoliths large domed mounds is wrong.

items.s: With which hotspot are the Deccan Traps, the fissure basalts of the end-Cretaceous, linked?
items.x: The Deccan Traps formed about 65 million years ago from the Reunion hotspot.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Barren Island – Only active volcano of India
items.x: Narcondam is dormant, not extinct; Dhinodhar in Kutch is the extinct one.

items.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Mount Etna is correct?
o: It is Europe's largest and most active volcano, rises to about 3,300 m and became a UNESCO site in 2013.
It is Africa's highest peak and has been dormant since 1707.
It is the world's highest active volcano at 6,893 m.
It is an extinct volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79.
items.x: Etna is Europe's largest and most active volcano, is approximately 3,300 m high and has been a UNESCO site since 2013.

items.s: White Island (Whakaari), a volcano that erupted in December 2019, is located in which country?
items.x: White Island (Whakaari) is in New Zealand and erupted in December 2019. Indonesia has Krakatoa and Dukono, Japan has Fujiyama and Mount Aso, and the Philippines has Taal and Mayon.

items.s: Which volcano is associated with the burial of Pompeii in AD 79?
items.x: Mount Vesuvius is an active volcano in Italy and buried Pompeii in AD 79.

items.s: Which is the world's highest active volcano?
items.x: Ojos del Salado in Chile (6,893 m) is the world's highest active volcano; Mauna Loa is the largest.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about Fujiyama:
1. It is a dormant volcano.
2. Its last eruption was in 1707.
3. It is Europe's largest and most active volcano.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Fujiyama in Japan is dormant and last erupted in 1707; Europe's largest and most active volcano is Etna.

items.s: What is the status of Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak?
items.x: Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) in Tanzania is dormant, unlike the active Italian volcanoes.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mauna Loa – Lighthouse of the Mediterranean
Mount St. Helens – Fujiyama of America
items.x: Mount St. Helens is the 'Fujiyama of America'; Stromboli is the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean and Mauna Loa means 'Long Mountain'.

items.s: In which country is the Mayon volcano, a symmetrical composite cone, located?
items.x: Mayon in the Philippines is a symmetrical composite cone on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

items.s: In which year did the Krakatoa volcano of Indonesia erupt, causing great tsunamis?
items.x: Krakatoa, between Java and Sumatra, erupted in 1883 and caused tsunamis.

items.s: The scientist who conducted comprehensive research on the earthquakes that occurred in Himalayan mountains prior to 1890s was
items.x: R.D. Oldham of the Geological Survey of India studied the Himalayan/Assam earthquakes (report on the great 1897 Assam earthquake) and later identified the Earth's core from seismic waves. Moved to Earthquakes.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s:
Which of the following Statements is most appropriate?

I. Earthquakes do not kill people

II. It is badly designed buildings that kill people
o: Statement I is True and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Both Statements are true and Statement II is the reason behind Statement I
items.x: Both are true and II explains I: earthquakes themselves rarely kill; most deaths come from the collapse of badly designed, non-engineered buildings – hence earthquake-resistant codes.

items.src: APPSC Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Serv
items.s: Which of the following is likely to kill more people?
items.x: Earthquakes kill mainly through the collapse of badly designed buildings; hazards in empty deserts, the deep sea or deep forests kill few. Off-topic (earthquake risk), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: Out of the following, which major disaster struck India in the year 2001?
items.x: The Bhuj (Gujarat) earthquake struck on 26 January 2001; Kedarnath was 2013, Kumbakonam fire 2004 and the tsunami December 2004. Moved to row 10.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-I Screening Test 2017
items.s: The ground shaking during an earthquake would be higher in
o: Shaking does not vary with soil type
items.x: Soft, loose soils amplify seismic waves and shake more (and may liquefy), while hard rock shakes least.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: The movement of earthy materials from higher region to lower region due to gravitational pull is called
items.x: The downslope movement of earth material under gravity is mass movement; its sudden form is a landslide. Off-topic (mass wasting), moved.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: What is measured in cubic/sec?
items.x: Cubic metres (or feet) per second – cumecs/cusecs – measure discharge, the rate of water flow in a river or canal. Off-topic (river discharge), moved.

items.s: Drumlins are found in?
items.x: Drumlins are inverted-boat-shaped mounds of glacial till, so they are found in glaciated areas such as Himalayan glaciers, not oceans, deserts or deltas.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: Over which of the following regions is the major ozone hole of the Earth?
items.x: The ozone hole forms over Antarctica every southern spring, when polar stratospheric clouds help chlorine destroy ozone; the Arctic loss is much smaller. Moved to the atmosphere row.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The largest ozone hole is observed over
items.x: The largest (seasonal) ozone hole lies over Antarctica, not over Africa, Australia or India. Moved to the atmosphere row.

items.s: In absorption of insolation, the most significant part is played by
items.x: Of the options, carbon dioxide (with water vapour, not offered) absorbs the most insolation over a broad band; ozone absorbs only a small share (UV), and oxygen and haze little. Moved to insolation and heat budget.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statement-I: The atmosphere is heated more by incoming solar radiation than by terrestrial radiation.
2. Statement II: Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are good absorbers of longwave radiation. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
items.x: Statement I is wrong: the atmosphere is mostly transparent to incoming short-wave radiation and is heated mainly by terrestrial (long-wave) radiation. Statement II is right: CO2 and other GHGs absorb long-wave radiation. Moved to heat budget.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: In which of the following places, boiling point of water would be higher compared to others?
items.x: Water boils at a higher temperature where air pressure is higher, that is, at the lowest altitude. Visakhapatnam is a sea-level port, Kolleru is a low inland delta lake, and Tirumala and Nanda Devi are high up. The intended answer is the sea-level city, Visakhapatnam (no official key found; Kolleru is also near sea level).

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: In normal atmosphere, at which temperature, evaporation of water takes place?
items.x: Evaporation goes on at all temperatures (from the surface of a liquid); 100°C is the boiling point. Belongs to row 17 (evaporation), moved.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Which cloud type produces rainstorms?
items.x: Cumulonimbus clouds, tall and dense, bring thunderstorms and heavy rain.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, Technical Asst. (Hydrog
items.s:
Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
(i) Cyclone Idai : 2019
(ii) Cyclone Ockhi : 2017
(iii) Cyclone Phailin : 2013
(iv) Cyclone Gonu : 2008
items.x: Cyclone Gonu struck Oman in June 2007, not 2008; Idai (2019), Ockhi (2017) and Phailin (2013) are correctly dated. Moved.

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Super cyclone in Odisha occurred in the year
items.x: The Odisha super cyclone struck in October 1999 (about 10,000 deaths). Moved to row 19.

items.s: The 'Bhola' natural disaster that struck the Indian subcontinent in 1970 was a
items.x: The Bhola disaster of 1970 was a cyclone that struck East Pakistan (Bangladesh). Moved to row 19.

items.s: The term 'Cyclone' is derived from a ____.
items.x: 'Cyclone' comes from the Greek 'kyklos' (coil of a snake), coined by Henry Piddington. A geography question, moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: Which of the following states of United States of America was worst affected by Hurricane Harvey recently?
items.x: Hurricane Harvey (August 2017) caused catastrophic flooding in Texas, especially Houston.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
items.s: Out of the given below, what is the name of the Hurricane that recently caused severe destruction in Caribbean Islands and USA?
items.x: Hurricane Irma (September 2017) devastated the Caribbean islands and Florida. (Cyclones; moved to book 4.)

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: The average life cycle of a cyclone as generally seen is
items.x: A tropical cyclone typically lasts about a week (roughly 6 days) from formation to dissipation; hours, weeks or months are wrong.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following would not cause major influence on the climate of a place?
items.x: Longitude affects local time, not climate; latitude, altitude and distance from the sea do.

items.s: Zulu tribes are found in - - C)
items.x: The Zulu are a Bantu people of South Africa, mainly in KwaZulu-Natal, known for the military organisation of Shaka Zulu. They are not native to Kenya, Nigeria or Congo.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: A scrub forest found in California, along the Mediterranean Sea, and along the southern coast of Australia, where the annual rainfall ranges from 65 cm to 75 cm and the majority of the rain falls in the winter falls in ____ Biome
items.x: Chaparral is the Mediterranean scrub biome of California, the Mediterranean coast and southern Australia, with mostly winter rain.

items.s: The symbols used in the Indian Daily weather report were approved in 1998 by
items.x: The printed key is the International Meteorological Organisation, the only meteorological body among the options. (The IMO became the WMO in 1950-51, so the stated 1998 date is doubtful.)

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s:
Which of the following elements are involved in determining past climate change events?

1. Tree rings

2. Ice cores from the cryosphere

3. Coral reefs
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
items.x: Tree rings, ice cores and coral growth bands are all proxy records of past climate. Moved to row 21 (climate change evidence).

items.src: Assistant Director in AP Economics and Statistics 2017
items.s: With global warming, the following would not increase in India?
items.x: Global warming melts glaciers, so glacier area shrinks; precipitation extremes, sea-level (thermal expansion) and floods increase.

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
items.s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A: Global warming is a gradual increase in the average temperature of the earth's lower atmosphere as a result of the increase in greenhouse gases since the Industrial Revolution.
R: During the past century, the atmospheric temperature has risen and fallen alternately by 1.1°F (0.6°C) and sea level has risen several inches.
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: A is true. R is false as worded: temperature rose (about 0.6 °C) over the past century rather than 'rising and falling alternately'.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: The largest part of our hydrosphere is:
items.x: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, about a third of the Earth's surface, so it is the largest part of the hydrosphere.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Freshwater content on the earth's surface is about
items.x: Fresh water is only about 2.5% of Earth's water; the oceans hold about 97%. Moved to row 23 (distribution of Earth's water).

items.s: What does the name 'El Nino' mean?
items.x: El Nino means 'the Christ child'; it is a warm current off Peru that recurs on average every 2–7 years.

items.s: At what sea-surface temperature anomaly in the central Pacific is a 'Super El Nino' identified?
items.x: A Super El Nino is associated with a sea-surface temperature anomaly above +2.0°C in the central Pacific.

items.s: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich tracked which phenomenon regarded as an early signal of El Nino?
o: An eastward Kelvin wave carrying warm water along the equatorial Pacific
A southward-moving polar air mass over the Pacific
A westward cold-water surge across the Indian Ocean
A stationary cold eddy in the North Atlantic
items.x: The satellite tracked an eastward Kelvin wave, meaning warm water moving east along the equatorial Pacific, an early El Nino signal.

items.s: How do the trade winds behave during La Nina?
items.x: Trade winds are stronger than usual during La Nina, with strong eastern Pacific upwelling and usually good rain over India.

items.s: What is the usual effect of El Nino on the Indian summer monsoon?
o: Brings the monsoon early with normal rainfall
Has no relationship with the monsoon
items.x: El Nino is generally associated with a delayed and weakened Indian monsoon and a higher risk of deficient rainfall.

items.s: Between which two places is the pressure difference measured by the Southern Oscillation Index?
items.x: The SOI is Tahiti minus Darwin; a sustained negative SOI indicates El Nino.

items.s: In May 2026, the IMD warned that a developing super El Nino could have what effect on the 2026 South-West Monsoon?
o: It could strengthen it throughout India.
It could reverse it into a winter monsoon.
It would have no possible effect.
items.x: The IMD warned that a developing super El Nino could weaken the 2026 South-West Monsoon.

items.s: According to the IMD criterion, El Nino is identified when the central equatorial Pacific is at least:
o: 0.2°C warmer than average for three consecutive months
2.0°C warmer than average for one season
1.0°C warmer than average for ten consecutive months
0.5°C warmer than average for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods
items.x: The stated IMD criterion is a warming of at least 0.5°C above average for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods in the central equatorial Pacific.

items.s: Who described the Southern Oscillation in 1920?
items.x: Sir Gilbert Walker described the Southern Oscillation in 1920.

items.s: What does the Southern Oscillation represent in ENSO?
items.x: El Nino and La Nina are the oceanic side of ENSO, while the Southern Oscillation is the atmospheric pressure side.

items.s: How often does El Nino recur on average?
items.x: El Nino recurs on average every 2–7 years, not every year.

items.s: What does a negative Southern Oscillation Index (Tahiti minus Darwin) indicate?
items.x: Negative SOI goes with El Nino; positive SOI with La Nina.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about El Nino?
o: It weakens or reverses the trade winds.
It delays and weakens the Indian monsoon.
It is a storm that forms over the Pacific.
items.x: El Nino is a climate pattern, not a storm; the other statements are correct.

items.s: In a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, the western Indian Ocean is:
o: Warmer, and the eastern part cooler
Cooler, and the eastern part warmer
Cooler, along with the eastern part
Warmer, along with the eastern part
items.x: In a positive IOD the west is warmer and the east cooler; the monsoon usually strengthens.

items.s: A negative Indian Ocean Dipole usually brings the Indian monsoon:
items.x: A negative IOD (west cooler, east warmer) usually means weaker rain; a positive IOD strengthens the monsoon and can offset El Nino.

items.s: Which phase of the Indian Ocean Dipole can offset the effect of El Nino on the Indian monsoon?
items.x: A positive IOD (warmer western Indian Ocean) usually strengthens the monsoon and can offset El Nino.

items.s:
Which of the following have coral reefs?

I. Andaman and Nicobar Islands

II. Gulf of Kachchh

III. Gulf of Mannar

IV. Sunderbans
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: Coral reefs occur in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Gulf of Kachchh and Gulf of Mannar; the Sundarbans are a muddy mangrove delta without reefs. Moved to coral reefs (row 26).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Which of the following is a real fish?
items.x: The sea horse (Hippocampus) is a true bony fish (Osteichthyes); sea cow and sea lion are mammals, and starfish, jellyfish and cuttlefish are not fish. Moved to marine organisms (row 26).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following is true about phytoplankton?
o: Phytoplankton flowers are blue in colour
items.x: Many phytoplankton are salt tolerant, living in the sea. They are microscopic (not tall), have no flowers and lack vascular tissue.

items.s: Of what are coral reefs mainly built?
items.x: Coral reefs are built of calcium carbonate secreted by coral polyps.

items.s: What are the algae that live together with coral polyps called?
items.x: Coral polyps live with algae called zooxanthellae.

items.s: What is a reef lying farther from the shore, with a deep lagoon or channel between it and the land, called?
items.x: A barrier reef lies farther out with a deep lagoon between it and land; a fringing reef lies close to the shore.

items.s: Which Indian reef region is the least diverse, owing to turbidity?
items.x: The Gulf of Kachchh reefs are the least diverse because of turbidity; Andaman and Nicobar reefs are the most extensive.

items.s: Who gave the subsidence theory of coral reef formation (fringing to barrier to atoll)?
items.x: Darwin's subsidence theory (1842) says fringing reefs become barrier reefs and then atolls as the land sinks.

items.s: Which of the following pairs (Indian coral region – feature) is correctly matched?
o: Gulf of Kachchh – Most extensive reefs
Andaman and Nicobar – Least diverse reefs
items.x: Lakshadweep has atolls; Andaman and Nicobar reefs are the most extensive, Gulf of Kachchh the least diverse, and Palk Bay has fringing reefs.

items.s: Which region of India has the most extensive and richest coral reefs?
items.x: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have India's most extensive and richest reefs; the Gulf of Kachchh reefs are the least diverse.

items.s: Which of the following conditions is NOT favourable for the growth of coral reefs?
items.x: Corals need warm, shallow, clear, sunlit, saline water free of silt; silt blocks light and smothers polyps.

items.s: Which type of coral reef is found in Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar?
items.x: Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar have fringing reefs; Lakshadweep has atolls.

items.s:
Construction of water shed structures at right places can be the mitigation action for which of the following disasters?
(i) Tornadoes (ii) Fire (iii) Drought (iv) Flood
items.x: Watershed structures (check dams, percolation tanks) store runoff for dry spells and slow floods, so they mitigate drought and flood – not tornadoes or fire. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Which technique is used for flood forecasting?
items.x: Flood forecasting uses GIS, radar and remote sensing; Richter measures earthquakes, Pascal is a pressure unit and MRI is medical imaging. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Asst. B.C. Welfare Officers, Royalty Inspector
items.s: In which year did the 'Boxing Day Tsunami' take place?
items.x: The Indian Ocean "Boxing Day" tsunami struck on 26 December 2004.

items.s: Which of the following state was not affected by the Tsunami that occurred in 2004?
items.x: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami struck Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and the A&N Islands; Odisha's coast was not affected.

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Which State is the most affected in India during the massive Tsunami that occurred in the year 2004?
items.x: Tamil Nadu was the worst-affected Indian State in the December 2004 tsunami (Nagapattinam the worst district); Odisha, Goa and Karnataka were hardly affected.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which of the following in not a reason for drought?
items.x: Low rainfall, groundwater depletion and rising temperatures cause drought. High soil salt concentration is a consequence of poor drainage and irrigation, not a cause of drought.

items.s: Which type of houses are constructed by people in Assam close to river embankments?
items.x: In flood-prone Assam houses near river embankments are raised on bamboo stilts so floodwater passes beneath. Off-topic (floods/settlements), moved.

items.s: Which of the following Indian states is vulnerable to Tsunamis?
items.x: Andhra Pradesh, with a long east coast facing the Bay of Bengal, is tsunami-prone (2004 tsunami); the others are landlocked.

items.s: In a Tsunami, the first wave
o: None of the given answers is correct
items.x: Tsunamis come as a series of waves; the first wave may not be the largest, so people must not return after it.

items.s: If a quake hits Los Angeles, from there a Tsunami can reach Tokyo in a time
o: Less than a Jet plane would take to travel the same distance
Less than a Bullet Train would take to travel the same distance
items.x: Deep-ocean tsunamis travel at about jet-airliner speed (~500 mph), so one could cross from Los Angeles to Tokyo in roughly 10 hours, about a flight's time and far faster than 36-48 hours. Printed key 'less than a jet plane'. Off-topic, moved to hydrological disasters.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: Which of the following Indian states is most vulnerable to tsunamis?
items.x: Among these, Tamil Nadu, on the east coast facing the Bay of Bengal-Andaman subduction zone, is most exposed to tsunamis (2004); Rajasthan and Punjab are landlocked.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: In August 2025, which Indian State faced severe monsoon floods with 21 deaths and large scale evacuations?
items.x: In mid-August 2025 Maharashtra (Mumbai, Thane, Palghar, Nanded and other districts) was hit by heavy monsoon rain and flash floods; the State emergency operation centre put the toll at about 21 deaths over three days, with hundreds to thousands evacuated. Gujarat, Assam and Odisha did not have this event.

items.s: Geological Survey of India forecasts:
items.x: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency that forecasts landslides; avalanches are DGRE's work, heat/cold waves IMD's and floods CWC's. Agency question, moved to row 28.

items.src: APPSC 2021 Mains Junior Assistant Cum Computer Assistant In
items.s: Which of the following ministries constituted a Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) for Landslide Mitigation and Management in India on the initiative of NDMA and as per recommendations of NDMA Guidelines on Management of Landslide and Snow Avalanches (2009)?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
items.x: The Ministry of Mines, the nodal ministry for landslides, set up the TAC for landslide mitigation – not Home Affairs, Housing or Earth Sciences. Moved to row 28.

items.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
items.s: Which of the following pair is INCORRECTLY matched with respect to the disaster wise nodal agencies for forecast?
o: Avalanches – Snow and Avalanche Study Establishment
items.x: Flood forecasting is done by the Central Water Commission, not IMD; avalanches (SASE/DGRE), landslides (GSI) and cyclones (IMD) are correctly paired. Moved to row 28.

items.s: In case of which disaster, the country was totally unprepared for starting relief operations?
items.x: The Bhuj earthquake (2001) found India unprepared and led to the shift of disaster management to the MHA and to the DM Act 2005. Chennai and Kedarnath came later, when NDRF and the DM Act already existed. Moved to row 28.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following is the first State in India that has developed an Early Warning Dissemination System (EWDS) in the entire coastal area in the case of natural calamities?
items.x: Odisha was the first state to install an Early Warning Dissemination System (sirens on 122 towers) along its entire 480 km coastline (launched 2018, under NCRMP). Moved to the DM framework row.

items.s: Which one of these is man-made disaster?
items.x: NDMA groups biological disasters with chemical, industrial, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) disasters, i.e. human-made; urban floods, heat waves and tsunamis are natural hazards (urban floods are worsened, not caused, by people). No printed key.

items.s: Which of the following would not likely be a disaster?
o: Cyclone without loss of human life
Cyclone without human or economic loss
Low pressure trough causing rains but no wind
items.x:
Printed key: low-pressure trough with rain but no wind. Strictly, a cyclone that causes no human or economic loss is also only a hazard, not a disaster (DM Act 2005 s.2(d)).
A low-pressure trough giving rain without wind is an ordinary weather event, not a disaster (printed key). A cyclone causing some human or economic loss is a disaster.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, Technical Asst. (Hydrog
items.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE regarding GIS?
(i) GIS stands for Geological Information System
(ii) GIS deals with spatial data.
(iii) GIS is a tool in disaster management.
items.x: GIS stands for Geographic (not Geological) Information System; it handles spatial data and is a disaster-management tool. Moved.

items.s:
Which of these statements are CORRECT about GIS technology?

I. GIS technology helps identify disasters before they occur, using forecasts or risk zone maps

II. Remote sensing and GIS technology for Disaster Management create an emergency database for people in need of all assistance in the event of a disaster.

III. The GIS Technology is combined with Global Positioning System (GPS), which will help to receive / update the help from disaster rescue teams

IV. Remote Sensing and GIS technology have strong essence to provide the solution to all natural disasters.
items.x: GIS helps map risk zones before disasters, builds emergency databases and works with GPS for rescue, but it cannot 'solve all natural disasters', so IV is wrong. Moved.

items.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
items.s:
Which statements are accurate regarding the use of technology in disaster mitigation and preparedness?
I. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) aid in mapping disaster-prone areas and vulnerable populations.
II. Early warning systems rely solely on traditional communication methods.
III. Remote sensing technology can provide real-time data during disaster events.
IV. social media and mobile apps are increasingly used for disaster alerts and communication.
items.x: GIS mapping, real-time remote sensing and mobile/social-media alerts are used in disaster management, so I, III and IV are correct; early warning does not rely solely on traditional methods. Moved.

items.s:
Match the following.

A. Long Range Climate Modeling - i. Landslide

B. Measuring Strain Accumulation - ii. Earthquake

C. Monitoring Rainfall and Slope Stability - iii. Volcano

D. Emission Monitoring, Thermal Alerts - iv. Cyclone
items.x: Long-range climate modelling serves cyclone forecasting, strain accumulation (GPS/geodesy) earthquakes, rainfall and slope monitoring landslides, and gas-emission and thermal alerts volcanoes. No printed key; keyed from the hazard-monitoring methods.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s:
Which of the following can be employed in 'disaster mapping'
(i) Remote Sensing
(ii) GIS
(iii) Satellite data
items.x: Remote sensing, GIS and satellite data are all used in disaster mapping.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
items.s: Out of 36 states and union territories in India, how many are disaster prone?
items.x: NDMA describes 27 of India's 36 States and UTs as disaster prone. (Disaster management; moved to the Disaster Management row.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer & Analyst Grade-II (A
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of a comprehensive vulnerability profile?
items.x: A vulnerability profile records exposure – location and housing structures, emergency shelters, hazardous materials; tourist attractions are not part of it.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: India is unanimously chosen as the ____ of Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) for the fiscal year 2020.
items.x: India was unanimously chosen co-chair of the Consultative Group of the World Bank's Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) for fiscal year 2020.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Management of a nuclear disaster requires a?
items.x: A nuclear (radiological) emergency needs a top-down, centrally commanded response – specialised agencies (AERB, DAE, NDMA) direct evacuation and decontamination.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: What is the best shape of a house in cyclone resistant architecture?
items.x: Compact symmetric plans resist cyclonic wind best; of the options a square plan is best (NIDM), better than rectangle, L or U shapes, which create wind pockets.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Hydrologist and other posts 2017
items.s: Who has to respond first to a disaster?
items.x: The local community is the first responder to any disaster – it acts before State, Central or Red Cross help arrives; community-based disaster management rests on this.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
items.s: Which of the following organisations is NOT a part of the National Disaster Management Plan for animals?
items.x: The NDMA's plan for animals was prepared with the NIDM, World Animal Protection and Policy Perspectives Foundation; Amnesty International, a human-rights NGO, is not part of it. A disaster-management question, moved.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P. Sainik Welfare Sub Service 2
items.s: In the advanced triage system involving colour-coding scheme, the red tag is used to label which of the following categories of people
o: Those who will need medical care at some point, after more critical injuries have been taken care of
Those whose injuries are so extensive that they will not be able to survive given the care that is available
Those with minor injuries, do not require doctor
Those who cannot survive without immediate treatment but have a chance of survival
items.x: In colour-coded (START) triage, red = immediate: those who cannot survive without immediate treatment but can survive with it; yellow = delayed, green = minor, black = expectant/dead.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017 (07-0
items.s: Risk from a disaster can be reduced by
o: Training community members in necessary measures to be taken
Training pets to indicate onset of disaster
items.x: Disaster risk is reduced most by preparing the community: training community members in the measures to take. Fire alarms cover one hazard only, and pets or prayers do not reduce risk. (Not history; moved out.)

items.s: The statement 'There is no such thing as natural disaster, only natural hazards', is
items.x: True: a hazard (flood, earthquake) becomes a disaster only when it hits a vulnerable population, so disasters are a product of human exposure and vulnerability, not of nature alone.

items.s: Out of the given below, which of the following would be more useful when a super cyclone hits a district?
items.x: A super cyclone knocks out landlines and mobile towers; a satellite phone works without ground infrastructure, so it is most useful.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Out of the ones given below, which is Not an essential element for a rescue operation immediately after a disaster like Tsunami or Earthquake?
items.x: Immediately after a tsunami or earthquake a rescue needs manpower, equipment and a method; money is not an essential element of the rescue itself (official key). (Moved to disaster management.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: How many States have joined the pan-India Emergency Helpline No. 112?
items.x:
20 States/UTs had joined 112 by April 2019 — now the 112/ERSS number covers all States and UTs (general knowledge, not checked)
When the Home Ministry's ERSS rolled out the single emergency number 112, 20 States/UTs had joined by April 2019 (now all States/UTs).

items.s: Which of the following suffers more human loss due to disasters compared to others?
o: A highly populous country irrespective of development
Any disaster prone country would suffer loss
items.x: Human loss from disasters is highest in a populous underdeveloped country: high exposure combined with weak housing, warning systems and response capacity. Development, not population alone, decides vulnerability.

items.s: Which Indian state is the most vulnerable to natural disasters as per the National Disaster Risk Index?
items.x: The draft National Disaster Risk Index (MHA with UNDP) ranked Maharashtra the most vulnerable State, followed by West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan; Delhi topped the UTs.

items.s: Which of the following States is more prone to chemical disasters compared to others given below?
items.x: Maharashtra, with the largest concentration of chemical and petrochemical industries (Mumbai–Thane, Raigad), is the most prone to chemical disasters of these States.

items.s: Which of the following is not a vulnerability factor for occurrence of a disaster?
items.x: Disaster vulnerability rises with poverty, population growth and hazardous location; religion is not a vulnerability factor. Off-topic (disaster management), moved.

items.s: One of the key advantages of using GIS-based tools for the risk decision-making process is the possibility to use ____ analysis by varying parameters and generating alternative scenarios in a spatial context.
items.x: GIS-based decision support lets planners run 'what-if' analyses by varying parameters and generating alternative scenarios in a spatial context; 'what-is' is not the term and sensitivity analysis only tests one parameter's effect.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: Out of the following, which is not a man-made disaster?
o: Stubble burning by farmers in Punjab
Cutting of trees for Podu cultivation by Tribals
Cutting of forests for Red Sanders
items.x: All four are human-caused, but the key treats tribal podu as a traditional livelihood rather than a man-made disaster.

items.s: Where is the 10th Battalion of NDRF located in Andhra Pradesh?
items.x:
the battalion moved to its own campus — now at Kondapavuluru, Gannavaram mandal, Krishna district (inaugurated 2025; web search summary)
The 10th Bn NDRF was first stationed on the Acharya Nagarjuna University campus, Guntur district (2011).

items.s: The production of cultured pearl is an important cottage industry of :
items.x: Cultured (Akoya) pearl production, pioneered by Kokichi Mikimoto, is an important cottage industry of Japan. Moved to Geography (marine resources).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: Which country recently banned mining of metals?
items.x: El Salvador became the first country to ban metal mining (law passed 29 March 2017), to protect its water. Off-topic (mineral resources), moved to row 30.

items.s:
Match the following:
List-I

a. Tendu leaves

b. Shellac

c. Keera-jari herb

d. Khus-Khus grass
List-II
i. Energy Booster
ii. Cooling screens
iii. Bangle making
iv. Beedi making
items.x: Tendu leaves wrap beedis, shellac (lac) makes bangles, keera-jari (Yarsagumba) is an energy booster and khus grass makes cooling screens. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
items.s:
Which of the following statements accurately describe natural resources in the Indian subcontinent?

I. The Indian subcontinent is rich in mineral resources, including coal, iron ore, and bauxite.

II. The Himalayan region is abundant in hydropower potential due to its numerous rivers and water bodies.

III. The subcontinent lacks fertile land and suitable conditions for agricultural production.

IV. The Thar Desert in northwest India is a major source of freshwater resources.
items.x: India is rich in coal, iron ore and bauxite and the Himalaya have large hydropower potential; it does not lack fertile land, and the Thar is not a major freshwater source. Moved to resources.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What is the term for the ratio between the mid diameter and the diameter at breast height?
items.x: Form quotient is the ratio of the diameter at mid-height (or a fixed height) to the diameter at breast height; form factors are volume ratios. Off-topic (forest mensuration).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic used in field identification of timbers?
items.x: Timbers are identified in the field by physical features such as colour, lustre, hardness, odour, grain and texture; chemical composition needs laboratory analysis, so it is not a field character.

items.src: Assistant Director in AP Economics and Statistics 2017
items.s: What is the name of underground water tanks in Bikaner area of Rajasthan to store rain water till the next season?
items.x: Tankas (taankas) are the underground rain-water tanks of the Bikaner–Thar region; kuls are Himalayan channels and baolis stepwells.

items.src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
items.s: Which is a special type of well used by Kurumba Tribe of Wayanad to conserve water?
items.x: Panam keni is the wooden-cylinder well of the Kurumba tribe of Wayanad, Kerala. Baoli and kunda are stepwells/tanks of the north-west and taanka is a Thar cistern.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following need not be a characteristic of a "resource"?
o: None of the given answers is correct
items.x: A resource must have utility and value (and be accessible/acceptable); a large quantity is not a necessary characteristic. Resources topic, moved to Geography.

items.s: What is the name of traditional rainwater harvesting technique practiced in Thar desert?
items.x: Taanka is the underground tank for harvesting rainwater in the Thar desert (Rajasthan); bawadi is a stepwell and bandhi a bund.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The percentage of agricultural land is very high in all the following states except
items.x: Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh are plains States with a very high share of agricultural land. Hilly Sikkim has very little, so it is the exception.

items.src: APPSC Group-I Paper-I Screening Test General Studies & Menta
items.s: Karaganda basin is famous for
items.x: Karaganda basin in Kazakhstan is a major coal basin. Off-topic (world mineral resources).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: The minimum amount of water per person per day as recommended by UNO for drinking, washing, cooking and maintaining proper hygiene is?
items.x: UN/WHO put the basic need at 50–100 litres per person per day; 50 litres is the minimum figure.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: What is the name of the large area of land submerged in sea near Newzealand, for which recognition as a new continent is sought by some scientists?
items.x: Zealandia (Te Riu-a-Maui) is the largely submerged landmass around New Zealand proposed as a continent (2017). Off-topic, moved.

items.s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? Country Capital
items.x: Maldives' capital is Male; Malabo is the capital of Equatorial Guinea. Guinea-Bissau – Bissau, Taiwan – Taipei and Nicaragua – Managua are correct. (Options print only the countries.)

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: Majority of the deserts of the World lie between the following latitudes?
o: 0 to 15 degree north and south latitudes
There is no relation between latitude and location of desert
15 to 30 degree north and south latitudes
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (15 to 30 degree north and south latitudes); it is added as option 5.
Most of the world's hot deserts lie between about 15° and 30° N and S, on the western margins of continents under the subtropical high-pressure belts and trade winds. The 0–15° belt is the wet equatorial zone, and deserts clearly follow latitude, so none of the printed options is right.

items.s: The term Levant often heard in the news roughly corresponds to which of the following regions?
o: Region along the eastern Mediterranean shores
Region along North African shores stretching from Egypt to Morocco
Region along Persian Gulf and Horn of Africa
The entire coastal areas of Mediterranean Sea
items.x: The Levant is the region along the eastern Mediterranean shores – Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Jordan. Moved to regions in news.

items.s: Which pair is incorrect?
items.x: 'Hermit Kingdom' was Korea (Joseon), not Japan; Egypt is the Gift of the Nile, Palestine the Holy Land and Canada the 'Land of Lilies' in GK lists. Moved to nicknames.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: In which of the following countries, India has two important Arctic research stations: Himadri and IndARC?
items.x: Himadri (2008) at Ny-Ålesund and the IndARC underwater observatory in Kongsfjorden are both in Svalbard, Norway. Moved to polar regions.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: In which country is the 'Knuckles range' located?
items.x: The Knuckles mountain range is in central Sri Lanka (Matale–Kandy), a UNESCO World Heritage area.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Strait of Hormuz:

2. It connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

Which of the above statements are correct?
items.x: About 20%, not 10%, of global oil trade passes through Hormuz, which lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about Bab-el-Mandeb:
1. It connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
2. It is a gateway to the Suez Canal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Bab-el-Mandeb joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, which puts it on the route to the Suez Canal.

items.x: The Strait of Malacca, between Malaysia and Sumatra, is the busiest commercial strait.

items.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

items.x: About 20% (not 10%) of global oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.x: The Mozambique Channel lies between Mozambique and Madagascar and is a shipping route.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rivers that cross a line of latitude twice?

The Congo crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.

items.s: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Siachen glacier?
o: It is the largest glacier in India
It has a length of 75.6 km
It is the third longest glacier in the Karakoram
It is the second-longest glacier in the world's non-polar areas
items.x: Siachen (about 76 km; 75.6 km in many books) is India's largest glacier, the longest in the Karakoram and the second-longest in the world's non-polar areas (after Fedchenko). So 'third longest in the Karakoram' is NOT true.

items.s: The longitudinal valleys lying between Himachal and Shivaliks are called
items.x: Duns (e.g. Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun) are longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and the Shiwaliks. Bhabar, Terai and Bhangar are belts of the Northern Plains.

items.s:
Select the option that is correct regarding the correctness of the following two statements labelled
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A : Two of the highest peaks of Himalayas, Mt. Everest (in Nepal) and Kanchenjunga are not very far from the plains.
R : In the east, the Himalayas rise almost abruptly from the plains of West Bengal and Assam.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Both true and R explains A: in the east the Himalayas rise abruptly from the plains of West Bengal and Assam, so peaks like Everest and Kanchenjunga lie close to the plains.

items.s: Pindari Glacier is situated in which of the following states?
items.x: Pindari Glacier is in the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Pindar river, a tributary of the Alaknanda.

items.x: Shipki La, Nathu La and Lipulekh are the official trade routes; Bomdila is the gateway to Tawang.

o: Lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces belonging to the Tertiary system
Floodplain deposits renewed annually by the Ganga
Coral reefs formed along the western coast
Young volcanic cones of the Trans-Himalaya
items.x: Karewas, also called Vudr, are lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces in the Kashmir Valley and form part of the Tertiary system. They are famous for saffron cultivation.

items.x: The Punjab Himalaya extends between the Indus and Sutlej. Kumaon lies between Sutlej and Kali, Nepal between Kali and Tista, and Assam between Tista and Dihang.

items.x: Nathu La is in Sikkim and forms part of the India–Tibet trade route; it is also one of the highest motorable passes.

items.x: The BRO is building a 120 km road to Lipulekh; Shipki La was opened to Indian tourists for border tourism.

items.s: Between which points does the Himalayan mountain system extend?
items.x: The Himalayas extend for about 2,414 kilometres from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namche Barwa in the east.

items.x: The Lahaul Valley is in Himachal Pradesh, not Assam.

items.x: From north to south the zones are the Indus-Tsangpo Suture, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault.

items.x: Patli Dun is in Uttarakhand. Dehradun (the largest dun) is in Uttarakhand, not Arunachal Pradesh, and Nalagarh Dun is in Himachal Pradesh, not Sikkim; duns lie between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks, so none is in Assam.

items.s: Which is the largest dun of the Himalayas?
items.x: Dehra Dun is the largest dun; Nalagarh Dun is in Himachal Pradesh.

items.s: The Sutlej enters India through which pass?
items.x: The Sutlej enters India at Shipki La in Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh.

items.s: In which State is the Zemu Glacier located?
items.x: Zemu Glacier is in Sikkim; Gangotri is in Uttarakhand and Siachen in Ladakh.

items.s: What are the longitudinal valleys of the Shiwaliks called?
items.x: The Shiwaliks, the youngest and narrowest range, have longitudinal valleys called duns.

items.s: Which is the largest glacier of India?
items.x: Siachen in the Karakoram (Ladakh) is the largest and longest glacier in India.

items.x: The Great (Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra) Plains are built by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and their tributaries. Moved to the northern-plains row.

B. khadar
