items.x:
the April 2022 district reorganisation moved Doravarisatram mandal out of Nellore – now Nelapattu is in Tirupati district (general knowledge, not checked).
Nelapattu bird sanctuary (Doravarisatram mandal) was in Nellore district (now Tirupati district).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: In Andhra Pradesh which district of the following is not having 'Mica' deposits?
items.x: Mica in AP occurs in the Nellore belt (1st in production) and in Krishna/NTR and West Godavari; Chittoor is the district without mica deposits in the key.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh are rich in Gold resources?
items.x: Gold occurs in Chittoor, Kurnool, Kadapa and Anantapur districts of AP (e.g. Ramagiri in Anantapur, Chigargunta in Chittoor). Off-topic (AP minerals), moved.

items.s: Sirasanambedu, Kovanur and Suramala are iron ore mines located in the ____ district of Andhra Pradesh.
items.x:
APPSC key: Chittoor. Strictly the IBM mining plan registers the Sirasanambedu iron-ore mine under Nellore district (not an option), so the location is uncertain (IBM mine code 30APR15003).
The APPSC key places the Sirasanambedu, Kovanur and Suramala iron-ore mines in Chittoor district (the old Chittoor–Nellore border belt of the south).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: Which of the following was the highest produced mineral (in terms of quantity) in Andhra Pradesh during 2023-24?
items.x: By quantity limestone is AP's largest mineral output (Kurnool, Kadapa, Guntur), far ahead of iron ore, gold or vermiculite.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Andhra Pradesh contributes significantly to which minerals production in India?
items.x: Andhra Pradesh holds a large share of India's bauxite (about 17.7% of resources; with Odisha over 90% of metallurgical-grade ore), the mineral the key names.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Single largest deposits of Barytes in this place of Y.S.R. Kadapa district
items.x: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa district holds India's single largest barytes deposit; AP has about 92–93% of India's barytes.

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh is known for its copper mines?
items.x: Guntur district has the Agnigundala–Bondalamottu copper (lead, zinc, silver) deposits.

items.src: APPSC Group-I Preliminary Paper-I General Studies 2023
items.s: Andhra Pradesh is the sole producer of
items.x: Andhra Pradesh (Mangampet, Kadapa) is in effect the sole producer of barytes (about 92% of resources; APMDC alone gave 90% of output). Apatite output in India has been nil since 2016-17, iron ore and granite come from many States.

items.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT for the mineral Asbestos?

I. Asbestos is known for its heat resistance capacity

II. Andhra Pradesh is the leading producer of Asbestos in India
items.x:
Key: Only II. Strictly Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa chrysotile) was India's only asbestos-producing State until 2013-14, so II was true then; no production since 2014-15 (IMYB 2022 Asbestos; Lok Sabha reply cited in web search).
The key marks only II incorrect: asbestos resists heat (I true), but India now has no asbestos production and Rajasthan holds most resources.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Works), APRO, ASO, HO and
items.s: Andhra Pradesh is the sole producer of which of the following minerals in India?
items.x:
Key: apatite. Strictly IMYB reports India's apatite production as nil since 2016-17, and AP's true sole-producer mineral is barytes (IMYB Apatite & Rock Phosphate reviews, web search).
The key is apatite: AP (Kasipatnam, Visakhapatnam) ranks first in apatite and was its producer; calcite, bauxite and dolomite come from several States.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P. Sainik Welfare Sub Service 2
items.s: The Tummalapalle Mine located in Andhra Pradesh is a
items.x: Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) is a uranium mine run by UCIL.

items.s: Andhra Pradesh has largest deposits of which of the following mineral?
items.x:
No printed key. Two options fit: AP has ~96% of chrysotile asbestos (IMYB 2022) and also the largest uranium resources (1,44,541 t U3O8 in a 2017 government table, web search); chrysotile is keyed as the near-monopoly.
Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa) holds about 96% of India's chrysotile asbestos resources (7.98 of 8.32 lakh t). It also leads in uranium (Tummalapalle), but not in iron ore or marble.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(A) Engineering Assistant
items.s: Andhra Pradesh stands first in the country in the production of
items.x: AP ranks first in barytes (Mangampet) and is a leading limestone State (Kurnool); manganese, coal, copper and aluminium are led by other States.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: As per an Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research press release of March 2017, Andhra Pradesh has nearly 1.22 lakh tonnes of Uranium oxide, which is equal to nearly ______ tonnes of Uranium metal.
items.x: U3O8 is about 84.8% uranium by mass (714/842), so 1.22 lakh t of oxide ≈ 1.04 lakh t of uranium metal.

items.s: As per the reports of National Geophysical Research Institute in 2023, which district of Andhra Pradesh has the large deposit of 15 rare earth elements?
items.x: NGRI (2023) reported 15 rare earth elements in Anantapur district.

items.s:
Match the minerals in column A with their respective districts in column
B.
Column A (Minerals):

1. Mica

2. Coal

3. Bauxite

4. Manganese
Column B (Districts with the highest abundance):

A. West Godavari
B. East Godavari

C. Nellore

D. Srikakulam
items.x: Mica is in Nellore, coal in West Godavari (Chintalapudi), bauxite in the Eastern Ghats of East Godavari/Visakhapatnam, and manganese in Srikakulam: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D.

items.s:
Match the minerals with the districts of Andhra Pradesh in which they are found.
Minerals:
I. Bauxite
II. Manganese
III. Lead-Zinc
Districts:
a. Vishakhapatnam & East Godavari
b. Guntur & Kadapa
c. Srikakulam & Vizianagaram
items.x: Bauxite – Visakhapatnam & East Godavari; Manganese – Srikakulam & Vizianagaram; Lead-Zinc – Guntur (Agnigundala) & Kadapa: I-a, II-c, III-b.

items.s: What was the total estimated coal reserve (in million tonnes) in Andhra Pradesh as of 1st April 2022, as per the Coal Inventory published by GSI?
items.x: GSI's inventory put Andhra Pradesh's coal resources at about 4,142 million tonnes on 1 April 2022 (921 proved, 2,443 indicated, 778 inferred). (Moved to 4:53.)

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: The Andhra Pradesh Government launched the 'Manufactured Sand Policy' in the year.
items.x: AP's New Sand Policy-2016 (G.O.Ms.No.19, 15 January 2016) encouraged manufactured (crushed-stone) sand as an alternative to river sand, so 2016. (Off-topic: AP minerals.)

items.s: For deposits of which mineral are Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli and Paderu in Andhra Pradesh known?
items.x: These Eastern Ghats agency areas hold bauxite; mining clashes with PVTG rights and Eastern Ghats ecology.

items.s: The chromite deposits of the Kondapalli Hills are associated with which district of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Chromite occurs in the Kondapalli Hills of Krishna district in Andhra Pradesh.

items.s: Until 1929, which district was the world's top producer of manganese?
items.x: Visakhapatnam district was the world's top manganese producer until 1929.

items.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with respect to gold mining in Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Ramagiri is located in Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh. Jonnagiri is in Kurnool, while Hutti and Kolar are in Karnataka.

items.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the predominant type of iron ore is which one of the following?
items.x: Most of Andhra Pradesh's iron ore is haematite, and Anantapur ranks first in the State for iron ore. Magnetite has the most iron, but it is not AP's main ore; limonite and siderite are lower grades.

items.s: For deposits of which mineral is Thummalapalli in YSR Kadapa district known?
items.x: Thummalapalli in YSR Kadapa is associated with uranium; Agnigundala and Bondalamottu in Guntur have copper, zinc and silver.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It was renamed from the Jonnagiri Gold Mine
It is an underground mine operated under a ten-year lease
It belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt
It is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district
items.x: Swarnagiri is an open-pit mine with a 30-year lease, not an underground mine on a ten-year lease.

items.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Mica production and reserves are highest in erstwhile Nellore.
Vermiculite production and reserves are highest at Kasipatnam in Visakhapatnam.
Limestone production and reserves are highest in Kadapa.
Asbestos production and reserves are highest in Kadapa.
items.x: Option C is incorrect: Kurnool leads in limestone; Kadapa leads in asbestos. The mica and vermiculite facts are right.

items.s: At which place do apatite reserves and production rank first?
items.x: Kasipatnam in Visakhapatnam district leads in apatite (and vermiculite) reserves and production. Bethamcherla is a limestone centre.

items.s: Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla in Kurnool district are major centres of which mineral?
items.x: Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla are the main limestone centres; barytes is linked to the Kadapa rocks.

items.s: By what name is Andhra Pradesh often called because of its rich and varied mineral deposits?
items.x: AP is nicknamed 'Ratna Garbha' (womb of gems) for its mineral wealth. 'Annapurna' and 'Dhanya Kosh' describe granary roles, and Swarna Bhoomi is not the stated nickname.

items.s: Pulivendula in Andhra Pradesh is known for deposits of which mineral?
items.x: Pulivendula in Kadapa district has asbestos; Kadapa ranks first in AP for asbestos.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the minerals of Andhra Pradesh:
1. NGRI reported 15 rare earth elements in Anantapur district in 2023.
2. Andhra Pradesh is the sole producer of apatite in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: NGRI found 15 rare earth elements in Anantapur (2023), and Kasipatnam makes AP India's sole apatite producer.

items.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh ranks first in iron ore?
items.x: Iron ore in AP is mainly haematite, and Anantapur district ranks first.

items.s: Of which mineral does Andhra Pradesh hold India's largest reserve?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Barytes); it is added as option 5.
Andhra Pradesh does not hold India's largest bauxite reserve – Odisha does (about 50%; AP about 12–18%). AP's largest-reserve mineral is barytes (about 92–93% of India's resources, Mangampet); AP has no major coal, copper or chromite reserves.

items.s: Which is India's first private gold mine since Independence, working from June 2026?
items.x: The Swarnagiri (Jonnagiri) mine in Tuggali, Kurnool, run by Geomysore, is the first private gold mine since Independence.

items.s: Agnigundala and Bondalamottu in Andhra Pradesh are known for deposits of which minerals?
items.x: Agnigundala and Bondalamottu (Guntur) have copper, zinc and silver deposits.

items.s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh are the Agnigundala base-metal deposits located?
items.x: Agnigundala and Bondalamottu lie in Guntur district.

items.s: The Boksampalli blocks, to be auctioned in 2026 for gold and platinum group elements, are in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: The Boksampalli gold and PGE blocks lie in Anantapur district.

items.x: Singapore is among the most densely populated countries yet ranks high on environmental quality and quality of life. Off-topic here; moved to world population.

items.s: How much percentage of land of the World is occupied by 70 percent population of the World (who are not very rich) (choose nearest figure)?

Printed key: sugar (books long gave Brazil as top sugar producer). As printed, 'ninth in crude steel' is plainly false – India is 2nd (PMF H&E Geography 05 p.26).
India is the world's 2nd-largest crude steel producer, so 'ninth' is the incorrect statement; India is the largest producer of jute and jaggery and was the largest sugar producer in 2021-22, so the sugar statement is defensible.

items.x: Bhilai is primarily an iron and steel centre; Jamnagar, Vadodara and Haldia are the petrochemical centres.

items.x: VISL Bhadravati (1923, Mysore State) used charcoal and was the only plant outside the coal area.

items.x: Bokaro (1964, USSR help) was the fourth public-sector steel plant after Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur.

items.x: Coastal plants use imported coking coal, mainly from Australia.

(II) In 1973, the various privately owned coal mines at Raniganj were nationalised.

(III) National Coal Development Corporation Ltd. (NCDC) was set up in 1956.
items.x: (I) is wrong – SCCL is a Government of Telangana–Government of India company sharing equity 51:49, not Assam 45:55. (II) is right – non-coking coal mines incl. Raniganj were nationalised in 1973. (III) is right – NCDC was set up in 1956. So II and III.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: The New Silk Route connects the countries
items.x: The 'New Silk Road' freight rail runs from Chongqing (China) to Duisburg (Germany), so it is answered as China and Germany.

items.s: The New silk Route connects the countries
items.x: As in the twin question, the New Silk Route (Chongqing-Duisburg) links China and Germany; the other options are wrong.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Material learnt without any understanding and reproduced is?
items.x: Material learnt without understanding and reproduced mechanically is rote memory.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Carroll's model includes six elements with ...... output variable(s), ...... input variable(s) and ...... intermediate variable(s) in that order.
items.x: The printed key gives Carroll's model of school learning as 1 output, 1 input and 4 intermediate variables.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who criticized the subject centered traditional curriculum?
items.x:
Printed key: Alfred North Whitehead. Many pedagogy books instead link John Dewey with the criticism of the subject-centred traditional curriculum (child-centred / activity curriculum).
A.N. Whitehead ('The Aims of Education') attacked 'inert ideas' and the fatal disconnection of subjects in the traditional curriculum; the printed key is Whitehead.

items.s: For which branch of science U.N. has designated the year 2011 ?
items.x: The UN declared 2011 the International Year of Chemistry (also of Forests); 2009 was Astronomy, 2010 Biodiversity, 2005 Physics.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who developed 'Personalized Programme of Instruction'?
items.x: Fred S. Keller developed the Personalized System (Programme) of Instruction, the 'Keller Plan' (1968).

items.s: Which organization is responsible for maintaining the International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) located at Devasthal Observatory?
o: Aryabhata Research Institute of Observational Sciences
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
items.x: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope at Devasthal (Nainital) is maintained by ARIES (Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences), a DST institute.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: According to Freud, during which period super ego is developed?
items.x:
Printed key / many guides: Latency period. Strictly: Freud has the superego form at the end of the phallic stage, when the Oedipus complex is resolved (Britannica).
Printed key: latency period, as many teacher-education guides state that the superego develops/consolidates in latency. Freud himself placed the formation of the superego at the resolution of the Oedipus complex at the end of the phallic stage (about age 5-6). Off-topic here; moved to psychology.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Flander classified the classroom behaviour of the teacher and pupils into how many categories.
items.x: Flanders' Interaction Analysis Categories (FIAC) sort classroom verbal behaviour into 10 categories (7 teacher talk, 2 pupil talk, 1 silence/confusion). (Pedagogy; moved to row 0.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: An optical projector capable of giving images of both opaque and transparent objects is said to be?
items.x: An epidiascope projects both opaque objects (episcope) and transparencies (diascope); a slide projector shows only transparencies and an opaque projector only opaque objects. (Teaching aids; moved to row 0.)

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: A researcher measured height of class Xth students. The measurement of height is on
items.x: Height has a true zero and equal intervals, so it is measured on a ratio scale.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
items.x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: What is the scientific name of Ashwagandha?
items.x: Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
items.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
items.x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Goiter is characterized by:
items.x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
items.x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
items.x: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules into seeds.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Viscosity is measured in:
items.x: Viscosity is measured in poise (CGS unit); the SI unit is the pascal-second (1 Pa·s = 10 poise).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answer from the given options.
Column I (Phylum):

A. Ctenophora

B. Porifera

C. Coelenterata (Cnidaria)

D. Echinodermata
Column II (Distinctive features):

1. Choanocytes

2. Bioluminescence

3. Water vascular system

4. Polyp and Medusa
items.x: Ctenophores show bioluminescence, sponges (Porifera) have choanocytes, Cnidaria have polyp and medusa forms, and echinoderms have a water vascular system: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3. (Biology, filed under polity by mistake.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
items.x: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
items.x: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
items.x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Sun drying is a method of:
items.x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: In periodic table helium is placed at
items.x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
items.s: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
items.x: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

items.s: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
items.x: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

items.s: Inflammable air is:
items.x: Henry Cavendish (1766) called hydrogen 'inflammable air' because it burns; the name 'hydrogen' was given later by Lavoisier.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
items.x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: In Pavlovian conditioning paradigm as developed originally which of the following was used as independent variable?
items.x: In Pavlov's original paradigm the experimenter varied the number of pairings of the conditioned stimulus (bell) with the unconditioned stimulus (food) – the independent variable; response magnitude and latency were the measured (dependent) variables.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
items.x: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Which of the following is a noble gas?
items.x: Helium is a noble (inert) gas of Group 18; hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are reactive.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
items.s: It would be less safe to fill a gas balloon with the following gas:
items.x: Hydrogen is lighter than air but highly inflammable, so it is the least safe gas for a balloon; helium is inert and safe.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
items.s: 'Volume of a given mass of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature'. This statement is associated with:
items.x: Boyle's Law: at constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's Law relates volume and temperature.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
items.x: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Ignoring friction of air, if one brick and one feather are released to ground from top of a building, which one reaches ground first?
items.x: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g whatever their mass, so the brick and the feather reach the ground together (Galileo; shown on the Moon by Apollo 15).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: Which liquid would boil last?
items.x: Mercury boils at about 357°C, far above water (100°C), benzene (80°C) and ethyl alcohol (78°C), so it boils last.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of friction?
o: Applying brakes to stop a moving car
Revolution of the planets around the sun
items.x: Planets revolve round the Sun because of gravity in near-vacuum space, so there is no friction; brakes, striking a match and walking all depend on friction.

items.s: A Ball thrown outside from an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth will –
o: Revolve around the Earth in the same orbit with the
items.x: A ball released from an orbiting satellite already has the satellite's orbital speed, so it keeps falling round the Earth in the same orbit, like the satellite itself.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: The test in which the scorer is asked to rank samples in a decreasing or increasing order of same characteristics is:
items.x: In a ranking test (sensory evaluation) the judge arranges samples in increasing or decreasing order of one characteristic, such as sweetness.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-1 (Physicists):
A. WK Roentgen
B. Victor Francis Hess
C. Ernest Orlando Lawrence
D. CH Townes
List-2 (Major contribution/discovery):
1. Cosmic radiation
2. Maser
3. X-rays
4. Cyclotron
items.x: Roentgen discovered X-rays, Hess cosmic radiation, Lawrence invented the cyclotron and Townes the maser, so A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2. Off-topic science, moved.

items.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: If egg shell is carefully dissolved in acid and then immersed in salt water, then the shell?
items.x: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate shell, leaving the semi-permeable membrane; in strong salt water (hypertonic) water leaves the egg by osmosis, so it shrinks. Off-topic science, moved.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Rectifiers convert ____.
items.x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Saponification is the reaction between
o: A fat and a strong acid
A fat and a strong base
items.x: Saponification is the hydrolysis of a fat (or oil) with a strong base such as NaOH, giving soap and glycerol. An acid-base reaction is neutralisation.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Saurology is the
items.x: Saurology (herpetology of lizards) is the study of lizards.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who among of the following is not an exponent of Humanistic Realism?
items.x: Humanistic realism is a 16th-century Renaissance school whose exponents were Erasmus, Rabelais and Milton; Aristotle is an ancient Greek philosopher, not one of its exponents. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who opined, "The world is continuously evolving towards greater degree of perfection that is God." It is the opinion of
items.x: The idea that the world is continuously evolving towards a greater perfection that is God (the Divine) is Sri Aurobindo's theory of spiritual evolution. Aristotle (the printed key) spoke of an unmoved mover, not of the world evolving into God; Plato and Russell do not hold this view. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: New ideas (Eureka) suddenly come in the minds of the creative children in which of the following stage?
items.x: In Wallas's stages of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) the sudden 'Eureka' insight comes at illumination. Off-subject (educational psychology).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
items.s: Which of the following forces is responsible for all the nucleons to be concentrated in the nucleus?
items.x: The strong nuclear force, short-range and far stronger than electrostatic repulsion, binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Off-subject (physics).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The most malleable metal is
items.x: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: The magnitude of root pressure would be minimum during
items.x: Root pressure is lowest in summer, when heavy transpiration pulls water up and the positive root pressure largely disappears. It is highest in the rainy season, when absorption is high and transpiration low, so Rainy season was wrong.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: A metric chain of 20 metre length consists of ____ links.
items.x: A 20 m metric chain has 100 links of 0.2 m (20 cm) each.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: The permissible percentage overload on DG sets for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation is
items.x: Prime-rated diesel generator sets are allowed a 10% overload for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation. Off-topic (electrical engineering).

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Temperature and time used to sterilise glassware in hot air oven
items.x: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is
items.x: The exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex, always add up to 360°. Off-topic (mathematics).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
items.s: What happens if you plug in a heater device rated for 110 V, 50 Hz in a household AC electric supply plug in India?
o: It burns out within minutes or even in seconds
Its heat supply would be poorer than its rated value.
You cannot use such a device in an Indian Plug
items.x: On India's 230 V supply a 110 V heater draws about (230/110)² ≈ 4 times its rated power, so its element burns out quickly. Off-topic (physics).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
items.x: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: In which of the following season human beings require food with more fat content
items.x: In winter the body needs more energy to keep warm, so fat-rich (energy-dense) food is needed most then. Off-topic (nutrition).

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
items.x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
items.x: No standard source (ICMR-NIN RDA) gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement; deficiency signs such as night blindness peak in the hot pre-harvest season, while the printed key says winter. Left unkeyed. Off-topic (nutrition).

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: Carbohydrates are organic compounds with the basic structure:
items.x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is a diuretic
items.x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
items.x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: Which is the most abundant element by mass in human body?
items.x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: When an iron nail gets rusted, its weight?
o: Increase or decrease depends on temperature and pressure
items.x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide; the iron combines with oxygen and water, so the weight increases. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.s: Which metal has the maximum use as pure metal?
items.x: Aluminium is keyed: light, abundant and corrosion-resistant, it is used very widely in nearly pure form (foils, cans, sheets, conductors); silver is scarce and iron is used mostly as steel. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
items.s: Which of the following is an inorganic lubricant?
items.x: Graphite is an inorganic layered form of carbon used as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: A soap molecule has two ends, one of which is an ionic end and the other is a carbonic chain end. Which part of the soap molecule interacts with oily dirt to enable cleansing?
o: The end that is closer to the oil molecule
items.x: The hydrocarbon (carbon-chain) tail dissolves in oil and grips the dirt, while the ionic end faces water, forming micelles. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: Which of the following features is NOT common in Chordates and non-chordates?
items.x: Printed key: bilateral symmetry – all chordates are bilaterally symmetrical, but many non-chordates (cnidarians, adult echinoderms) are radial, so it is not common to both groups. Off-topic (zoology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: If a piece of wood and a piece of iron are placed in a fridge and taken out after 15 minutes, which one would feel more cold on touching?
items.x: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster and feels colder, though both are at the same temperature. Wood is a poor conductor.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Commonly used absorbable suture material is
items.x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
items.s: Skull of mammals is
items.x: Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'pi' (π)

a. Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.

b. Pi is a rational number
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
items.x: Only a is correct: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is irrational (Aryabhata's 3.1416 is only an approximation), so statement b is false.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Why alum is used in the process of purifying drinking water?
items.x: Alum (potash alum) supplies Al3+ ions that neutralise the charge on suspended clay particles so they coagulate and settle. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: What is a change of position?
items.x:
Most keys: Motion. Strictly: the change in position (a vector) is displacement (NCERT Class 9 ch. 8).
In school physics, motion is the change of position of a body with time, which is the key the paper gives. Strictly, the size and direction of the change in position is displacement, and distance is the path length.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving at a constant velocity will continue moving at a constant velocity, unless it is acted on by an unbalanced force". This law is called as ____.
items.x: Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The second law gives F = ma, the third deals with action and reaction, and there is no fourth law.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Under what conditions the resistivity of the material does not change?
o: When the shape of the resistor is changed
When both the material and temperature are changed
items.x: Resistivity is a property of the material and its temperature, so it does not change when only the shape (length or area) of the resistor changes; resistance would change, resistivity would not.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
items.x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: Which type of sound waves can propagate in solids?
items.x: Solids can carry both longitudinal and transverse mechanical waves (like seismic P- and S-waves); fluids carry only longitudinal waves. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
items.s: A louder sound is produced by a wave that has a greater
items.x: Loudness depends on amplitude – a larger amplitude gives a louder sound; frequency decides pitch. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
items.s:
Identify the correct pair(s) from the given pairs with respect to minerals and their function and choose the correct option.

I. Zinc - For insulin production

II. Phosphorus - Development of strong bones and teeth

III. Fluoride - Makes enamel of teeth hard and prevents dental caries
items.x: Zinc is needed for insulin synthesis and storage, phosphorus (with calcium) builds bones and teeth, and fluoride hardens tooth enamel and prevents caries – all three pairs are correct. Off-topic (nutrition), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s:
Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules which include carbohydrates. Match the following Group of Carbohydrates with their examples.
Group of Carbohydrates:
I. Monosaccharides
II. Oligosaccharides
III. Polysaccharides
Examples:
a. Cellulose
b. Ribose
c. Maltose
items.x: Ribose – monosaccharide, maltose – oligosaccharide (disaccharide), cellulose – polysaccharide. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s:
Which of the following are correct with reference to proteins?
i. They are made up of nucleotides.
ii. They are linear chains of amino acids.
iii. They are heteropolymer.
iv. They are homopolymer.
items.x: Proteins are linear chains of amino acids and are heteropolymers (20 kinds of amino acids); nucleotides make nucleic acids. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.s:
Match the phylum in column A with their features in column B.
Column A (Phylum):

I. Porifera

II. Cnidaria

III. Arthropoda
Column B (Features):

a. Presence of Ostia and Osculum

b. Available in two forms- Polyp and Medusa

c. Have jointed appendages.
items.x: Porifera – ostia and osculum, Cnidaria – polyp and medusa forms, Arthropoda – jointed appendages. Off-topic, moved.

items.x: Stomata – tiny pores on leaves, guard cells – open and close them, chloroplasts – contain chlorophyll, enzymes – biocatalysts. Off-topic, moved.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: What is the resting rate heart for a normal person?
items.x: A normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (American Heart Association); about 72 is the textbook average.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: If Kilo is Thousand, then Deka is
items.x: Deka (deca) is the SI prefix for ten (10^1); kilo = 10^3, hecto = 10^2.

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to sporopollenin?
i. The exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin so that pollen grains can be preserved as fossils.
ii. It cannot withstand high temperatures.
iii. It is one of the most resistant organic materials.
iv. Enzymes can degrade it.
items.x: Sporopollenin forms the exine; it is one of the most resistant organic materials, withstands high temperatures and strong acids and alkalis, and no enzyme is known to degrade it – so only i and iii. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s:
Match the given component of living tissues with the percentage of the total cellular mass.
Component:
I. Lipids
II. Proteins
III. Carbohydrates
IV. Nucleic acids
Percentage of the total cellular mass:
a. 5-7%
b. 10-15%
c. 3%
d. 2%
items.x: In a cell, proteins are 10–15%, nucleic acids 5–7%, carbohydrates 3% and lipids 2% of the mass (water 70–90%). Moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: Which of the following is incorrect about the ultrasonic waves?
o: These waves are can be used for imaging
It cannot be heard by normal human ears
The speed of ultrasonic waves is more in denser media
The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
items.x: Ultrasonic waves are mechanical sound waves and cannot travel through vacuum; they are inaudible, used for imaging and travel faster in denser media. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s:
Match the following from table A to Table B - Use of Salts
Table A:
I. Sodium Carbonate
II. Sodium Benzoate
III. Calcium Carbonate
IV. Calcium Phosphate
Table B:
1. Extraction of Metals
2. As Washing Soda, Manufacturing of Glass
3. As a Fertilizers
4. As a Food preservative for Pickles
items.x: Sodium carbonate is washing soda used in glass-making, sodium benzoate is a food preservative, calcium carbonate is a flux in metal extraction and calcium phosphate is a fertiliser. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s:

items.x: Butyric acid is in rancid butter, malic acid ('Maleic' in the stem) in apples, stearic acid in fats and oxalic acid in wood sorrel. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
items.s: The caramelization reactions require intense heat about
items.x: Caramelisation of sucrose needs about 170 °C (it begins near 160 °C); 100 °C only boils water and 200-240 °C burns the sugar.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Out of the below, what is the example of a chemical reaction?
items.x: Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide), so it is a chemical change; freezing, glowing of a lamp filament and dissolving salt are physical changes. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
items.s: Oxidation process means
items.x: In chemistry oxidation is the loss of electrons (reduction = gain of electrons). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s: Which of these is the change of gaseous state directly to solid state without going through liquid state?
items.x: The change of a gas directly into a solid is deposition (desublimation); sublimation is the reverse, solid to gas. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called.
items.x: Deposition of calcium and other minerals that turns cartilage into bone is ossification. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which type of chemical process is tarnishing of silver?
items.x: Tarnishing of silver (black silver sulphide from H2S in air) is a form of corrosion. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which reaction demonstrate the chemical property of alcohols as reducing agent?
o: Reaction with sodium to release hydrogen
items.x: Alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes or ketones, so they act as reducing agents (they are themselves oxidised); esterification, reaction with sodium and dehydration are not redox reactions of this kind. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: If two papers are kept very close to each other and wind is blown in between them, they would
items.x: Air blown between the sheets moves fast and its pressure drops (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher outside pressure pushes the papers together. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which among the following is appropriate Phrasal verb for 'Loiter Aimlessly'?
items.x: 'Hang out' means to spend time idly or loiter; hold up = delay, keep on = continue, lay off = dismiss. Off-topic (English), moved.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: Which gas is evolved when an acid reacts with a metal?
items.x: A metal reacting with an acid gives a salt and hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2). Off-topic (general science), moved.

items.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
items.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT for the processes involved in photosynthesis?

I. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll

II. Oxidation of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates
items.x: Photosynthesis begins with absorption of light by chlorophyll (I correct); carbon dioxide is reduced, not oxidised, to carbohydrate (II wrong) → Only I. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: Apart from Sun light and Carbon Dioxide, the source for production of Oxygen through photosynthesis in plants is?
items.x: Plants split water in photosynthesis (photolysis); the oxygen released comes from water, not from CO2, air, chlorophyll or glucose. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
items.x: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Formation of Carbon dioxide gas from Carbon and Oxygen is a/an?
items.x: Burning carbon in oxygen to CO2 gives out heat – an exothermic (combination) reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
o: To absorb water from the soil
To take in carbon dioxide and release helium
To transport vitamins through the stem
items.x: Photosynthesis lets green plants make their own food (glucose) from CO2 and water using sunlight; it releases oxygen, not helium. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Name the factor that does not require for photosynthesis
items.x: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, water and carbon dioxide (and chlorophyll); oxygen is a product, not a requirement. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Aerobic respiration process requires
items.x: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose using oxygen (giving CO2, water, energy). Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour it
items.x: An opaque object looks the colour of the light it reflects; the other colours are absorbed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: The production of tears when dust particles hit the human eye; is an example of which of the following?
items.x: Tears flushing dust from the eye are part of the body's first-line (innate) defence – immunity; they contain lysozyme. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What is a characteristic feature of a first-degree burn?
o: Minor epithelial damage, presence of redness
Partial thickness burn and scalds, may be painful
items.x: A first-degree (superficial) burn damages only the epidermis, with redness and pain; partial-thickness is second degree and full-thickness/necrosis third degree. Off-topic (first aid), moved.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Which one of the following is pure water?
items.x: Rain water is the purest natural water (natural distillation); well, river and sea water carry dissolved salts.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
items.x: Anemophily is pollination by wind; hydrophily is by water, entomophily by insects and ornithophily by birds.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s: Who among the following determined the charge of electrons as 1.5924 x 10^-19 C?
items.x: Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909-13) measured the electron's charge, about 1.59 x 10^-19 C in his 1913 result (now 1.602 x 10^-19 C).

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: Which of the following principles is used in the process of cooling air in air-conditioners?
items.x: Air-conditioners cool a room by circulating air: cooled air sinks and warm air rises to the unit – a convection current. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: When a semiconductor is heated, its resistance would
o: Resistance has no relation with temperature
items.x: A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient: heating frees more charge carriers, so its resistance decreases (a metal's would increase). Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
items.s: A person wonders how is it possible for insects to walk on water, human beings can't do it. In order to answer this question, we will have to refer to the concept of:
items.x: Surface tension – the cohesive 'skin' of the water surface – supports light insects such as water striders. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
items.x: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of substance by 1°C is called
items.x: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C is its specific heat. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Why a glass bottle full of water breaks, if kept in a fridge?
o: The pressure in the fridge would be very high
When water solidifies, it expands in volume
items.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice exerts pressure that cracks the glass bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: The electrical resistance of the insulators is
items.x: An ideal insulator offers (practically) infinitely high resistance to current, hence 'infinitely high' rather than merely 'high'. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which instrument is used to measure speed?
items.x: A tachometer measures speed (rotational speed of an engine, rpm); an ammeter measures current, a venturimeter flow rate. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APSLPRB SI Paper-IV Final Written Exam 2017
items.s: The instrument used to measure high temperatures
items.x: A pyrometer measures very high temperatures (furnaces) from emitted radiation; a pedometer counts steps. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: If Mental Age of a Child is 6 and Physical Age is 10, the IQ of the child is?
items.x: IQ = mental age ÷ chronological age × 100 = 6 ÷ 10 × 100 = 60. Off-topic (psychology / mental ability), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: A projector for images of both opaque objects and transparencies is called an ______.
items.x: An epidiascope projects images of both opaque objects and transparencies (episcope + diascope); an anemometer measures wind speed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Which of the following substances is invariably formed, whenever an acid combines with a base?
items.x: An acid and a base always react to form a salt (and water). Off-topic science PYQ, moved.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The Volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain of freezing
items.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: If a person goes down into a deep mine, his weight?
o: Depends on location of the mine
items.x: g falls with depth below the surface, so a person's weight decreases slightly in a deep mine. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: A hydrometer is used to measure?
items.x: A hydrometer measures the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids; humidity is measured by a hygrometer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: When an air bubble at the bottom of a lake rises to the top, it will
o: Flattens into a dish like shape
items.x: Water pressure falls as the bubble rises, so the trapped air expands and the bubble grows (Boyle's law). Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain on freezing
items.x: Water expands on freezing; the ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Wood neither gaining or losing moisture content is called:
items.x: Wood that neither gains nor loses moisture is at its equilibrium moisture content (in balance with the surrounding humidity); the fibre saturation point is the stage when cell walls are saturated but cell cavities empty. No printed key. Off-topic (wood science), moved.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: What happens to the weight of Iron when it rusts?
items.x: Rust is iron combined with oxygen and water (hydrated iron oxide), so the rusted iron weighs more. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.s: Super cooling stands for cooling of a liquid
items.x: Supercooling is cooling a liquid below its freezing point without it solidifying. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Out of the following, which would not indicate occurence of a chemical reaction?
items.x: Evaporation is only a change of state (physical change); gas evolution, colour change and heat absorption can signal a chemical reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: After taking out from the fridge, compared to an apple, water melon would retain the coolness for more time because?
o: It is bigger in size and hene more volume
It contains more water which has higher specific heat
It is more green in colour which does reflects atmospheric heat
It has thicker skin which would not allow penetration of heat
items.x: Watermelon contains more water, which has a high specific heat, so it takes longer to warm up. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: What happens when salt is added to boiling water?
o: The water will boil more and temperature of the water would fall
The Water will stop boiling and the temperature of the water would fall
The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
The water will boil more and the temperature of the water would rise
items.x: Salt raises the boiling point, so the water stops boiling for a moment and its temperature rises to the new, higher boiling point before it boils again. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: An 'aerosol' is a fine dispersion of
o: Tiny droplets of liquid in the air
Chalk and sand particles in water
items.x: An aerosol is a fine dispersion of liquid droplets (or solid particles) in air/gas, e.g. fog, mist, sprays. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: Ice skating demonstrates that when ice is under pressure, its melting point
o: Melting point has no relation with pressure
items.x: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice (regelation); the skate's pressure melts a thin water layer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: What is the result when we add salt in water?
o: The boiling point decreases and freezing point increases.
The boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.
Both the boiling point and the freezing point increase.
Both the boiling point and freezing point decrease.
items.x: A dissolved salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: 'Latent learning' is a concept enunciated by whom?
items.x: 'Latent learning' – learning that shows only when there is a reason to use it – was put forward by Edward Tolman (rats in mazes, cognitive maps). Off-topic (psychology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
items.s: Mothballs work on the principle of
items.x: Naphthalene mothballs pass straight from solid to vapour – sublimation. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: The lower limit of the aperture of a pinhole camera is set by?
items.x: Making a pinhole too small spreads the image by diffraction, which sets its lower limit. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: What is the cause of dispersion of light through a prism?
items.x: A prism disperses white light because each colour is refracted by a different amount. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Twinkling of stars is due to?
items.x: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction by turbulent air layers of changing density. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: The sun is seen little before it rises and for a short while after it sets. This is because of
o: apparent shift in the direction of sun
items.x: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon, so the Sun is seen about 2 minutes before sunrise and after sunset. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s:
Consider the following statements

I. The sky appears blue because of scattering.

II. The main cause of seven colors of the rainbow is scattering of light.

III. At the time of sunrise, the sun appears red, due to scattering of light.
Choose the correct statement/s from the given options
items.x: The blue sky and the red rising Sun are due to scattering (I, III true); the rainbow's colours come from dispersion, not scattering (II false). Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: When the sun is near the horizon during the morning or evening, it appears reddish. The phenomenon that is responsible for this observation is
items.x: Near the horizon sunlight crosses more air, blue is scattered away and the Sun looks red – scattering. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: When light passes from one medium to another, this phenomenon of change in its direction is called …… .
items.x: Change of direction of light passing from one medium to another is refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: Bending of light rays in denser medium is termed as
items.x: Bending of light on entering a denser medium is refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.s: Why does water tank appear shallower when viewed from the top?
items.x: Light from the tank bottom bends away from the normal on leaving water, so the bottom looks raised – refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
items.x: Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer. Off-topic (biology/health), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which part of Garlic plant is used?
items.x: The edible part of garlic is the bulb made of cloves (modified leaves). Off-topic (botany), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
items.s: When there is a short circuit what happens to the current in the circuit?
items.x: In a short circuit resistance falls almost to zero, so the current increases heavily. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: When you are facing the periodic table, on which side of the table the non-metals are present?
o: On the right-hand side of the periodic table
In the middle column of the periodic table
On the left-hand side of the periodic table
In the bottom most row of the periodic table
items.x: In the modern periodic table metals lie on the left, metalloids along a zigzag line and non-metals on the right-hand side.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Most of the artificial food colouring agents are derived from
items.x: Most synthetic food colours (tartrazine, sunset yellow) are coal-tar (petroleum-derived) dyes. Flowers, fruits and lichens give natural colours.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: The function of the capacitor across the supply to the fluorescent tube is primarily to
items.x: The capacitor across the supply of a fluorescent tube corrects the lagging power factor caused by the choke.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: ______ is an instrument for measuring the distance travelled by a vehicle.
items.x: An odometer measures the distance travelled by a vehicle (a speedometer measures speed).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: In nominal scaling, if the observations in a group are not much different from each other but they can be ranked according to some criteria then they are said to be measured on:
items.x: Data that can be ranked but not measured in equal units are on an ordinal scale; nominal only names categories, interval and ratio need equal units. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: Microsecond = x seconds; What is 'x'?
items.x: One microsecond = 10^-6 second (one millionth of a second).

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: Out of the following, which type of graph is best suited for representing the outgo of a rupee in Budget?
items.x: The outgo of each rupee of the Budget is a share of a whole (paise per rupee), which a pie chart shows best; bar and line graphs compare amounts or trends and a histogram shows frequency. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: During winter in cold countries, the following is mixed to melt the ice on the roads?
items.x: Salt (rock salt) spread on roads lowers the freezing point of water and melts ice. Off-topic (everyday chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: The Least Count of a measuring instrument is the
items.at: Smallest change in the measured quantity that can be resolved
items.x: The least count is the smallest value (smallest change in the measured quantity) that an instrument can resolve, e.g. 1 mm for a metre scale.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: The triple point of pure water is at
items.x: The triple point of pure water – where ice, liquid water and vapour coexist in equilibrium – is 0.01 °C (273.16 K) at about 611.657 Pa. (Off-topic physics; moved.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Which of the following chemicals is generally used for purifying muddy water?
items.x: Alum (potash alum) coagulates suspended clay so it settles, purifying muddy water. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Which of the following is a mixture?
items.x: Sea water is a mixture of water and many dissolved salts in no fixed ratio; table salt, sugar and lime are compounds. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: When ice is melting its temperature would?
items.x: While ice melts, the heat supplied goes into latent heat of fusion, so its temperature stays constant at 0°C. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: Which of the following is used in glass industry?
items.x: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) is a main raw material of glass. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is antidote for cyanide poisoning
items.x: Sodium thiosulphate is an antidote for cyanide poisoning (it turns cyanide into less toxic thiocyanate). Off-topic (chemistry/medicine), moved.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Percentage of sodium chloride present in normal saline is
items.x: Normal saline is 0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride, isotonic with blood. Off-topic (science), moved; the question had no printed key.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Fill in the blanks: Gunpowder, also known as black powder is made of Sulphur (S), Charcoal (C), and ______.
items.x: Gunpowder (black powder) is sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate (saltpetre). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: Out of the following, which compound has highest solubility in Water?
items.x: Glucose dissolves about 90 g per 100 mL water at 25°C, far more than table salt (~36 g), ammonium chloride (~38 g) or alum (~14 g). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
items.s: In case of heat stroke, the body temperature?
items.x: In heat stroke the body's cooling fails and core temperature rises quickly (above 40°C). Off-topic (health), moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: An electric fuse is used to prevent?
items.x: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when an excessive (heavy) current flows, protecting appliances. Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about Galvanometer?

1. It is a device used to detect electric current in a circuit.

2. It shows the direction of current flows in the circuit.

3. The accuracy of the galvanometer is more as compared to the ammeter.

4. The Galvanometer is mostly used in bridge for knowing the zero current.
items.x: A galvanometer detects current and its direction and serves as the null detector in bridges (1, 2, 4); it is more sensitive but not more accurate than an ammeter (3 wrong). Off-topic (physics), moved.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: The weight of a brain of a normal human adult is about
items.x: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3-1.4 kg, i.e. about 3 pounds.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Who developed regression analysis?
items.x: Francis Galton introduced regression (regression toward the mean, 1880s); Karl Pearson developed correlation and Spearman rank correlation. (Moved: general science.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the excretory system in humans?
items.x: Nissl's granules are in the cell body of a neuron (nervous system), not the excretory system; the glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron. Off-topic (human biology), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: An abnormal cavity containing pus is called as
items.x: An abscess is a localised cavity filled with pus; a hematoma is collected blood, a cyst a fluid sac, a tumour a mass of cells. Off-topic (health), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s: Who among the following wrote 'De Magnete' in the 1600s, which gave the first rational explanation of the compass needle's mysterious ability to point north-south?
items.x: William Gilbert's De Magnete (1600) first explained the compass by treating the Earth as a giant magnet. Off-topic (physics), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: If Limestone (Calcium Carbonate) kept in a test tube is heated with a spirit lamp and a burning match stick is kept near the mouth of the test tube
o: The stick will glow with higher brightness
The stick will glow with same brightness
items.x: Heating limestone (CaCO3) decomposes it into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide; CO2 does not support burning, so the flame goes out. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
items.s: What happens when calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water?
o: Calcium Hypochlorite is produced and a large amount of heat is released
Calcium Oxyacid is produced and a precipitate is formed that settle down in the test-tube
Calcium Carbonate is produced and hydrogen gas is released
Calcium Hydroxide is produced and a large amount of heat is released
items.x: Calcium oxide (quicklime) reacts vigorously with water to form calcium hydroxide (slaked lime), releasing a lot of heat. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Tooth enamel is made up of which of the following?
items.x: Tooth enamel, the hardest substance in the body, is made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite). Off-topic (biology), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Which one of the following are richest sources of calcium:
items.x: Ragi (finger millet), amaranth and milk are among the richest common sources of calcium. Off-topic (nutrition), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
items.x: Displacement is the shortest straight-line path between the initial and final positions; distance is the actual path length. Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
items.x: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so the current rises very sharply (which blows the fuse). Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: When any one experiences acidity problem, he may get immediate relief by taking a glass of water in which, a tea spoon of the following substance is dissolved?
items.x: Acidity is neutralised by a weak base such as baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) or an antacid dissolved in water; a strong base would harm the body.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: When a synchronous motor is running at synchronous speed, the damper winding produces
items.x: At synchronous speed there is no relative motion between the rotor and the rotating field, so no current is induced in the damper winding and it produces no torque.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct with respect to definition of anatomy and physiology?

I. Physiology focuses on the physical arrangement of parts in the body.

II. Anatomy studies the inner functioning of cells, tissues and organs.
o: Only statement I is not correct
Only statement II is not correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Both statements I and II are correct
items.x: Both statements swap the definitions: anatomy studies the structure (physical arrangement) of body parts, physiology studies how cells, tissues and organs function – so both are not correct.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: How much heat is required to increase the temperature of 1 gram kerosene by 1 degree centigrade?
items.x: The specific heat of kerosene is about 2.1 J/g°C, i.e. about 0.5 cal per gram per °C (water = 1 cal). A physics question, moved.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: What is the approximate value of 1 calorie in Joules?
items.x: 1 calorie = 4.186 J, i.e. about 4.2 J (Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat). A physics question, moved.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: Which liquid is represented by the Volume-Temperature Curve? (The curve shows volume falling from 0°C to a minimum at 4°C and rising again up to 10°C.)
items.x: Water contracts from 0°C to 4°C (maximum density) and expands above it – the anomalous expansion of water.
