items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s: Which of the following is a procedure used to save an abscessed tooth in which the pulp chamber is cleaned out, disinfected, and filled with a permanent filling?
items.x: Root canal therapy cleans, disinfects and fills the pulp chamber of an abscessed tooth; gum grafts and gingivoplasty treat gums. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as _____ to give saturated hydrocarbons.
items.x: Hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons uses a nickel (or Pd/Pt) catalyst. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Grass appears green because
items.x: Grass looks green because chlorophyll reflects green light and absorbs the rest. Off-topic (physics/biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Pick up the correct pair among the following.
items.x: In chain surveying a ranging rod is set up to mark the position of stations and to range (align) survey lines; it does not measure distance or angles.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human female reproductive system?
items.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the MALE reproductive system; fimbriae (of the fallopian tube), cervix and endometrium (uterine lining) are female parts.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Plants that complete their life cycle within one season are called
items.x: Plants that complete their life cycle in one season are annuals, also called seasonal plants; biennials take two seasons/years and perennials live many years.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
items.s: Which of the following is responsible for slowing down a moving object?
items.x: Friction is the force that opposes motion and slows a moving object.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
items.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the male reproductive system; ovary, uterus and fallopian tube are female organs. (Biology; moved.)

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory?
items.x: John Dalton put forward his atomic theory in the early 1800s and published it in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' (1808), the year usually asked.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of gravity?
o: Revolution of planets around the sun
A rock rolling down a hill
Formation of tides in the ocean
items.x: Writing with a pencil works by friction, not gravity; planetary revolution, a rock rolling downhill and tides are effects of gravity.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: The following is generally used in bone healing in humans?
items.x: Cissus quadrangularis (hadjod, 'bone-setter') is the herb traditionally used for bone healing; garlic, black pepper and onion are not.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: The purpose of child lock feature in a car/vehicle is to:
o: automatic closing of the door by the driver
items.x: A child lock disables the inside handle of a rear door so it cannot be opened from inside; it can still be opened from outside.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I - Table-II

A. Lipase -
1. Breaks lactose

B. Amylase -
2. Breaks fat

C. Trypsin -
3. Breaks starch

D. Lactase -
4. Breaks Protein
items.x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
items.s: Which plants are called naked-seeded plants?
items.x: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines, cycas) bear naked seeds not enclosed in a fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits. (Moved to general science.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
items.x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, so the seeds and progeny are weaker; cross-pollination gives vigour and new varieties. (Moved to general science.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: The synthesis of Urea occurs in:
items.x: Urea is made in the liver through the ornithine (urea) cycle and excreted by the kidneys.

items.s: The first synthetically prepared organic compound was
items.x: Friedrich Wohler synthesised urea from inorganic ammonium cyanate in 1828, the first organic compound made in a laboratory.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: A boat filled with heavy stones is in a lake. If the stones are thrown into the lake, the level of water with respect to the boat would?
items.x: A floating boat displaces water equal to the stones' weight; sunk, the stones displace only their volume, so the lake level falls (and the lighter boat rides higher).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: In humans, Milk Teeth generally fall off at what age?
items.x:
Most books and keys: between 6 and 8 years. Strictly: shedding starts at about 6 and is complete by about 12 (incisors 6-8, canines and molars 9-12) (AAP healthychildren.org; Wikipedia 'Deciduous teeth').
Milk (deciduous) teeth begin to fall at about 6 years, and the incisors are shed by about 6-8 years, so most keys give 6-8. Shedding of canines and molars continues until about 12, which is why 10-12 is only the end of the process.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: The study of grasses is known as:
items.x: Agrostology is the study of grasses; agronomy is crop science and anthology a collection of writings.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Which of the following is an example of colloid?
items.x: Milk is the classic colloid (an emulsion of fat in water); sugar solution is a true solution and muddy water a suspension. (Water-in-oil is also an emulsion, but milk is the textbook answer.)

items.s:
A company marketing food products advertise that its items do not contain trans-fats. What does this campaign signify to the customers?

A. The food products are not made out of hydrogenated oils.

B. The food products are not made out of animal fats/oils.

C. The oils used are not likely to damage the cardiovascular health of the consumers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: 'No trans-fats' means no partially hydrogenated oils (A) and so less harm to heart health (C); animal fats may still be used (small natural trans fats aside), so B does not follow.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The classical example for closed wound is
items.x: A contusion (bruise) is the classic closed wound, with the skin unbroken; lacerated, penetrating and incised wounds are open.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: The beak of an insect eating bird would be?
items.x: Insect-eating birds have long, sharp/pointed beaks to pick insects (woodpecker, kingfisher-type); short strong beaks crack seeds. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s: Which is the correct statement about a genetic code?
o: UAC, UAG, and UGA are stop codons.
Initiation codon AUG codes for arginine.
items.x: The genetic code is a triplet (codon of three bases) and nearly universal; stop codons are UAA, UAG, UGA (not UAC); AUG codes for methionine. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: The strike plate of a match box is made up of
items.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

items.s: The strike plate of a match box is is made up of
items.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which of the following is NOT the advantage of dumpy level over the wye level?
o: Simpler construction with fewer movable parts
Adjustment tested with greater rapidity and ease
items.x: The dumpy level's advantages are simpler construction, fewer adjustments and longer-lasting adjustments; quick and easy testing of adjustments is the advantage of the wye level.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
items.x: Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: What is the principle of working of transformer?
items.x: A transformer works on mutual induction: a changing current in the primary coil induces an emf in the secondary coil.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: The pH value of Curd as compared to that of Milk would be?
items.x: Curd contains lactic acid formed by bacteria from lactose, so it is more acidic than milk and its pH is lower (about 4-4.5 against 6.5-6.7).

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: In a healthy adult, what is the approximate percentage of white blood cells in total blood volume?
items.x: White blood cells (with platelets) form well under 1% of blood volume (the thin buffy coat), so 'one percent' is the nearest figure.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: For a transformer operating at constant load current, maximum efficiency will occur at
items.x: At constant load current the copper loss is fixed, so output and efficiency are highest at unity power factor. Off-topic here (electrical engineering).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: ATP molecule releases about how much energy?
items.x: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP releases about 30.5 kJ/mol (7.3 kcal/mol) under standard conditions.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Normally how many number of Autosomes will be present in human beings?
items.x: Human cells have 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs (44) of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: In the fluorescent tube circuit the function of the choke is primarily to
items.at: Initiate the arc and stabilize it
items.x: The choke (ballast) gives a high-voltage kick to strike the arc in the tube and then limits the current to keep it stable.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
items.x: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the pharynx to the stomach; the duodenum and jejunum are parts of the small intestine and the pylorus is the stomach's outlet.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is used in titration
items.x: A burette delivers measured volumes of titrant in a titration; a pipette transfers a fixed volume.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
items.s: Which cranial nerve in humans is the largest and has both, sensory and motor functions?
items.x: The trigeminal (5th) nerve is the largest cranial nerve and has both sensory and motor fibres.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: The structural carbohydrates of vegetables and fruits are
items.x: Cellulose is the structural carbohydrate of plant cell walls in fruits and vegetables.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
items.s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
items.x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is not a solid form of medicine
items.x: Syrup is a liquid dosage form; tablets, capsules and boluses are solid.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Genes controlling the body characteristics are found in
items.x: Genes for body characters are carried by both sperms and eggs, which each pass one set of chromosomes.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: Which of the following coloured lights has the highest wavelength?
items.x: Red light has the longest wavelength of visible light (about 620–750 nm); yellow, green and blue are progressively shorter.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The thermite process is used to weld railway tracks; it involves a reaction between
items.x: The thermite reaction is between iron oxide and aluminium; aluminium reduces the oxide and the molten iron produced welds rail joints.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: Which of the following nuts has the highest potassium content per equal weight?
items.x: Per 100 g, almonds (about 730 mg) have more potassium than peanuts (~705 mg), cashews (~660 mg) and walnuts (~440 mg).

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What is the term for water contained within the cell wall of wood?
items.x: Water held within the cell walls of wood is bound (hygroscopic) water; free water fills the cell cavities. Wood-science texts call it bound water.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: What happens when a dry litmus paper is exposed to Anhydrous hydrochloric acid vapor?
o: Colour changes from blue to red
items.x: Dry HCl gas does not ionise without water, so dry litmus paper shows no colour change.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: The Elements of Group IA are called:
items.x: Group IA (Group 1) elements – lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium – are the alkali metals. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Galvanization is a method of protecting iron from corrosion by coating the iron with a thin layer of which of the following element?
items.x: Galvanisation coats iron with a thin layer of zinc. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s: In Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides on treatment with-metal in dry ethereal (free from moisture) solution give higher alkanes.
items.x: The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether to give higher alkanes. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: In Chlorophyll, the central metal ion is?
items.x: Magnesium is the central metal ion of chlorophyll. Off-topic (biology).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which metal coating is used in Galvanization process to protect Steel and Iron from rusting?
items.x: Galvanisation coats steel and iron with zinc to stop rusting. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Which of the following metal is the best conductor of electricity?
items.x: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, ahead of copper and aluminium. Off-topic (physics).

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: Which of the following is a toxic material found in automotive batteries?
items.x: Lead in lead-acid automotive batteries is the toxic material. Off-topic (pollution / chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: A solution reacts with crushed-egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains
items.x: Hydrochloric acid reacts with egg shells (calcium carbonate) to release CO2, which turns lime water milky. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following metals can be easily cut with a knife?
items.x: Potassium, a soft alkali metal, can be cut with a knife; lead, aluminium and selenium cannot be cut easily. Off-topic (chemistry).

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: Which of the following chromosomes is/are the sex chromosomes?
items.x: Humans have two sex chromosomes, X and Y (XX female, XY male); Z belongs to the ZW system of birds.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: If an object is thrown upwards, what will be its velocity, when it reaches its maximum height (neglect the air resistance)?
items.x: At the maximum height the vertical velocity of a body thrown upwards becomes zero (it then falls back).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
items.x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: The head of a matchstick is generally made of
items.x:
Most books and keys: phosphorus. Strictly, a safety-match head is mainly potassium chlorate with antimony trisulphide; the red phosphorus is on the striking strip (only old 'strike-anywhere' heads carried phosphorus sesquisulphide) (general knowledge, not checked).
Exam keys answer phosphorus for the match head; see the dispute for what a safety-match head is actually made of.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
items.x: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the alveoli, across their thin walls into the capillaries. Off-topic (biology), moved.

items.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
items.s: In vulcanization of natural rubber, the following is used?
items.x: Vulcanisation heats rubber with sulphur to make it strong and elastic (Goodyear, 1839).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which of the following seeds have wings that help in seed dispersal?
items.x: Drumstick (Moringa) and maple seeds are winged and dispersed by wind; Xanthium and Urena have hooks, castor and balsam burst open.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: Which of the following contains high caffeine content per equal weight?
items.x: By equal dry weight, tea leaves contain more caffeine (about 3-4%) than coffee beans (about 1-2%), though a brewed cup of coffee has more; chocolate has far less.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The longest fibre on the cell body of a neuron is called:
items.x: The axon is the single long fibre that carries impulses away from the neuron's cell body; dendrites are short and branched.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Which of the following substances can be used as an acid-base indicator?
items.x: Turmeric turns reddish-brown in bases and back to yellow in acids, so it works as a natural acid-base indicator; tamarind, sugar and salt do not change colour.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The eyes of the potato tuber are
items.x: The 'eyes' of a potato tuber are axillary buds (in the axils of scale leaves), proving the tuber is a stem.

items.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: The fibre length of cotton is 1-5 cm
Recommended dose of fertilizer (kg/ha) for Pusa
Edible part of apple is mesocarp
items.x: The edible part of an apple is the fleshy thalamus (receptacle), not the mesocarp, so 4 is wrong; cotton fibre of about 1-5 cm and boron as a micronutrient are correct.

items.s: Which dog-breed and region-of-origin pair is NOT correctly matched?
items.x: The Chihuahua comes from Mexico, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, not China.

items.s: What is the immediate first aid that can be administered to a victim of burns?
o: Wetting the burnt part in cold water
Removing stuck cloth on the burnt part
items.x: Immediate first aid for a burn is to cool the part in cool or cold running water. Stuck cloth must not be pulled off, butter or ointment should not be applied, and water should not be poured with force.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Which of the following materials is not commonly used as sound-proof material?
items.x: Rockwool, wood and (double/laminated) glass are used for sound insulation; plain iron sheets reflect and transmit sound and are not a sound-proofing material.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
items.s: Which of the following can be prepared using Methyl Alcohol?
items.x: Perspex is PMMA, whose monomer methyl methacrylate is made by esterifying methacrylic acid with methanol (methyl alcohol); neoprene comes from chloroprene and Bakelite from phenol and formaldehyde.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: What is the full form of ATP?
items.x: ATP is Adenosine Triphosphate: adenosine (adenine + ribose) with three phosphate groups, the cell's energy currency. 'Adenine' alone lacks the ribose, and 'protease' is an enzyme class.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: The sweetest sugar is
items.x: Fructose (fruit sugar, levulose) is the sweetest natural sugar, about 1.7 times as sweet as sucrose.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Honey is sweeter than cane sugar or corn syrup. Which one of the following carbon sugars is responsible for this?
items.x:
Levulose (option 2) is the same sugar as fructose, so both options are chemically right; keyed 'Fructose' as the standard name.
Honey is sweeter than cane sugar mainly because of fructose, the sweetest sugar. Levulose is only another name for fructose; dextrose (glucose) and sucrose are less sweet.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: What is the minimum distance required to hear an echo?
items.x: An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later; with sound at about 344 m/s the reflector must be at least 344 x 0.1 / 2 = 17.2 m away.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following forms of sugar is the main constituent of sugar cane juice?
items.x: Sugarcane juice is mainly sucrose (cane sugar), a disaccharide of glucose and fructose. Glucose, fructose and dextrose are only minor components.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: Stainless steel pans are sometimes provided with copper bottom because?
o: Copper is not a harmful metal
Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
Oil stains on Copper are easier to clean
items.x: Copper conducts heat much better than steel, so a copper bottom spreads heat quickly and evenly.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Maximum permissible earth resistance at large power stations is
items.x: Large power stations need earth resistance of no more than about 0.5 ohm (major substations 1 ohm, small substations 2 ohm).

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: What is the function of "stomata" in plants?
items.x: Stomata are leaf pores for gas exchange (CO2 in, O2 and water vapour out); xylem transports water.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Which device is used to measure current in a circuit?
items.x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: After eating which of the following items, a person is likely feel more thirsty?
items.x: Salted chips add sodium, raising the salt concentration of body fluids and triggering thirst; the other foods have little salt.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which type of snake bite leads to neuroparalytic symptoms?
items.x: Krait (and cobra) venom is neurotoxic and causes neuroparalysis; Russell's and saw-scaled viper venom is mainly haemotoxic, and pythons are non-venomous.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human respiratory system?
items.x: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves (nervous system); trachea, bronchi and larynx are parts of the respiratory tract.

items.s:
Read the following statements about the impact of Science and Technology on the Environment and Society:

A. Technology misuse and its wrong implementation leads to the occurrence of environmental pollution

B. Scientists have proposed technology as a medium through which the environment can be sincerely helped if directed positively
Identify the INCORRECT statement/statements
items.x: Both statements are true (misused technology pollutes; well-directed technology can help the environment), so neither is incorrect.

items.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the impact of science and technology on society?
o: Science and technology have eliminated poverty and inequality worldwide
Advances in science and technology have led to significant improvements in healthcare and increased life expectancy
Science and technology have completely eliminated the risk of natural disasters
The development of science and technology has had no impact on economic growth and productivity
items.x: Science and technology have improved healthcare and life expectancy; the other options are absolute claims that are false.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: How many classes of levers are there with reference to simple machines?
items.x: Levers are of three classes (fulcrum, load or effort in the middle). Physics of simple machines, not ICT.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
items.s: Number of Incisors, Canines, Premolars and Molars in humans is respectively
items.x: Human adult dentition (32 teeth) = 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, 12 molars (dental formula 2123 per half-jaw).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
o: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
items.x: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
items.x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

items.s: Which of the following are parts of the excretory system?
items.x: Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron in the kidney; colon, rectum, appendix and ileum belong to the digestive system.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: Which of following is NOT a part of the human excretory system?
items.x: Alveoli are air sacs of the lungs (respiratory system); nephrons, Bowman's capsule and ureters belong to the excretory system.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Steridian is unit of?
items.x: The steradian is the SI unit of solid angle; the radian measures a plane angle.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Which of the following types of matter is in ionic state?
items.x: Plasma is ionised gas, i.e. matter in the ionic state, as in the Sun and lightning. Solids, liquids and ordinary gases are made of neutral atoms or molecules.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: How many moles of Oxygen are required for combustion of one mole of Propane?
items.x: C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, so one mole of propane needs 5 moles of oxygen.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: A spectral line is emitted when an electron
o: jumps from lower orbit to higher orbit
jumps from higher orbit to lower orbit
items.x: A spectral (emission) line is emitted when an electron jumps from a higher orbit (energy level) to a lower one, giving out a photon. Jumping up absorbs energy.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: A salient pole synchronous motor is running at no load. Its field current is switched off. The motor will
items.at: Continue to run at synchronous speed
items.x: A salient-pole motor at no load keeps running at synchronous speed even with its field switched off, because the reluctance torque of the salient poles holds it in step.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
items.s: Which of the following is a voluntary muscle that you can control consciously?
items.x: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary; smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following inputs is required for photosynthesis to occur?
items.x: Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll, light, CO2 and water; oxygen and glucose are its products.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: What is the density of water?
items.x: Pure water has a density of about 1 g/cm3 (1,000 kg/m3), highest at 4 °C.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Designed power factor of a DG set is generally at:
items.x: DG (diesel generator) sets are rated at a power factor of 0.8 lagging, so their kVA rating is 1.25 times the kW rating.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Curd should not be kept in
items.x: Curd is acidic and reacts with brass (copper-zinc), forming toxic salts, so it should not be kept in brass vessels; glass, steel and earthen pots are safe.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which of the following mechanisms help prevent cavitation in the xylem?
o: Negative pressure inside the vessels and the pores
End walls of the vessels and the pores
items.x: The end walls of xylem vessels and their pit pores (pit membranes) stop air bubbles spreading, preventing cavitation from blocking the whole water column.

items.s: The pitch of the voice of the women is in general –
o: marginally lower than that of men
much lower than that of men
the same as that of men
items.x: Women's vocal cords are shorter and thinner and vibrate faster, so their voice pitch (frequency) is generally higher than men's.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: The capsules that contain medicines taken by us are normally made of
items.x: Medicine capsule shells are normally made of gelatin (from collagen), which dissolves in the stomach.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is used to control Mange
items.x: Sulphur ointment (sulphur, often with lime) is the classic remedy for mange, a mite infestation of animal skin.

items.s:
Assertion (A) : A man standing on a completely frictionless surface can propel himself by whistling.
Reason (R) : If no external force acts on a system, its momentum cannot change.
Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x:
Printed key: (b) both true, R not the explanation. Many solvers argue (a), since conservation of momentum (R) explains the recoil, and some call A practically false (general knowledge, not checked).
Both statements are true, and the printed key takes R as not the correct explanation of A. Blowing air out while whistling pushes the man the opposite way (third law), while R is the general conservation of momentum.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: What is known as the 'energy molecule' in the living World?
items.x: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. TNT is an explosive, ADP is its spent form and DNA is the genetic material.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: What is range of the pH value of the human blood?
items.x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, pH 7.35-7.45.

items.s:
The efforts to detect the existence of Higgs boson particle have become frequent news in the recent past. What is/are the importance/importances of discovering this particle?

a. It will enable us to understand as to why elementary particles have mass

b. It will enable us in the near future to develop the technology of transferring matter from one point to another without traversing the physical space between them

c. It will enable us to create better fuels for nuclear fission
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: The Higgs boson explains why elementary particles have mass (Higgs mechanism, confirmed at CERN 2012). It has nothing to do with teleporting matter or with fission fuels, so only statement a is right.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
items.x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
items.s: Which of the following is the controlling centre of a cell?
items.x: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and directs its activities, so it is the control centre of the cell. Chloroplasts make food, mitochondria release energy and the nucleolus only makes ribosomes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which organelle is called power house of the cell?
items.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell: they release energy as ATP by cellular respiration.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following part of a cell is called power house of energy?
items.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; the nucleus controls the cell and vacuoles store substances.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which Tissue helps in the transport of water in plants?
items.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from roots upward; phloem carries food.

items.s:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
Inventor : Invention

A. Christopher Cockerell : Hovercraft

B. David Bushnell : Submarine

C. J.C. Perrier : Steamship
Select the correct answer by using the code given below:
items.x: All pairs match: Christopher Cockerell – hovercraft; David Bushnell – submarine (Turtle, 1775); J.C. Périer – steamship (1775).

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Hyper Natrimia is excess presence in blood of?
items.x: Hypernatraemia means too much sodium in the blood (natrium = sodium).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: Which of the following are the main constituents of Dettol, a commonly used antiseptic in homes?
items.x: Dettol's main constituents are chloroxylenol and alpha-terpineol (with pine oil); it has no iodine.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: No-load current in a transformer
items.at: Lags behind the voltage by about 75°
items.x: At no load a transformer draws mainly magnetising current, so the power factor is very low (about 0.1-0.2) and the current lags the applied voltage by roughly 75-85°. Standard objective keys give about 75°.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which cells control the opening and closing of stomata?
items.x: Two kidney-shaped guard cells around each stoma swell or shrink and so open or close the pore; xylem and phloem conduct water and food.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: The gap between two neurons is called a
items.x: The junction between two neurons is a synapse; dendrites and axons are parts of a neuron, and an impulse is the signal it carries.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which plant is traditionally known as an antidote for snake bites?
items.x: Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha) is the traditional snake-bite remedy; neem, teak and sal are not.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: An example of a phosphoenol pyruvate carboxyl kinase (PEP-CK) type of C4 photosynthesis
items.x: Panicum (e.g. Panicum maximum) is the classic PEP-CK type C4 plant; sugarcane and maize are NADP-ME type, Amaranthus NAD-ME type.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the plant kingdom?
items.x: Annelids (earthworms, leeches) are animals; algae, pteridophytes and angiosperms belong to the plant kingdom.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
items.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant through evaporation at the root surface.

II. Transpiration is the main driver of water movement in the root nodules.

III. Transpiration is caused by the evaporation of water at the leaf-atmosphere interface; it creates negative pressure (tension) at the leaf surface.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
items.x: Only III is correct: transpiration is evaporation at the leaf-air interface creating tension that pulls water up; it is not loss at the root surface, and it does not drive water in root nodules.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
items.x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following plant tissues contains starch grains and is known as the starch sheath?
items.x: The endodermis of dicot stems stores starch grains and is called the starch sheath.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: Which element is common to all acids?
items.x: All acids contain hydrogen, which they release as H+ ions in water.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: What is the meaning of pH?
o: To measure the pressure of liquid
To measure the density of a solution
To measure the pressure of a blood
items.x: pH = 'potential of hydrogen' (power of hydrogen), a measure of hydrogen-ion concentration.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which of the following is not necessary for combustion to occur?
items.x: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and the ignition temperature (the fire triangle); water is not needed.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: An organic compound must contain?
items.x: An organic compound must contain carbon.

items.s: Ammonia is a compound of
o: Nitrogen and sodium hydroxide APPSC PYQS "
items.x: Ammonia (NH3) = one nitrogen + three hydrogen atoms.

items.s: Which of the following elements does not contain neutrons?
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
items.x: Protium (ordinary hydrogen, 1H1) has no neutron; oxygen and nitrogen nuclei contain neutrons.

items.s: Approximately how many different chemical elements exist on the Earth?
items.x: 118 elements are known and about 94 occur naturally on Earth, so 'about 100' is nearest; 200–300 elements do not exist.

items.s: Which of the following is the most common element in the Universe?
items.x: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Universe (about 3/4 of matter); oxygen leads in the Earth's crust.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: An iron nail dipped into Copper sulphate solution turns into the following colour?
items.x: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate; the nail gets a reddish-brown copper coating (solution turns pale green).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: Into which colour will the yellow silver bromide turn when exposed to sunlight?
items.x: Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to grey silver metal (photolytic reaction).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The catalyst used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils is
items.x: Finely divided nickel is the catalyst for hydrogenating vegetable oils into vanaspati.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron fillings?
o: Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced
Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced
Iron salt and water are produced
items.x: Iron reacts with dilute HCl to give iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: How much water a dripping tap is likely to waste in a year (choose nearest figure)
items.x: A tap dripping once a second wastes on the order of 1,000+ litres a year, so 1,200 litres is nearest.

items.s: Which of the following has 1 as its atomic number?
items.x: Hydrogen has one proton, so its atomic number is 1; ammonia is a compound.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: The bright colour of fire crackers containing Magnesium is due to?
items.x: The dazzling white light of magnesium in crackers comes from burning, i.e. oxidation of magnesium to MgO. Reduction and 'explosion of metal' are wrong; 'redox' is too general.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which of the following happens during the electro refining of copper?
o: Pure copper from anode deposits at the cathode
Pure copper from anode deposits in the electrolytic solution
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the anode
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the cathode
items.x: In electrolytic refining the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the solution deposits at the cathode. Copper does not pass directly from anode to cathode, and nothing deposits at the anode.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: What is the primary function of calcium in plants?
items.x: Calcium (as calcium pectate of the middle lamella) is needed for cell wall formation and development. ATP synthesis and electron transport rely on phosphorus, iron and magnesium.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
items.x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Rancidity is a/an
items.x: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: For the examination of skin scrapings which of the following is required
items.x: Skin scrapings are cleared with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH mount) so that fungal elements and mites can be seen. Heparin is an anticoagulant, and HCl and dichromate are not used for this.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
items.s: If mitochondria is removed from a living cell?
o: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
Cell fluid would not be transported
items.x: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, so removing them stops the cell's energy metabolism. Reproduction and transport would only fail as a later result.

items.s: The colour given by excess Lithium in Lithium Chloride solid is:
items.x: Excess lithium makes LiCl crystals pink. The colour comes from F-centres, electrons trapped at anion vacancies (NCERT Class XII, Solid State). Excess potassium in KCl gives violet, and excess sodium in NaCl gives yellow.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: Splitting of white light into seven colors on passing through the glass prism is called
items.x: Splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is dispersion, because different wavelengths refract by different amounts.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: At what time respiration takes place in plants?
o: There is no need for respiration in plants
items.x: Plants respire all the time, day and night; only photosynthesis needs light. So respiration is a continuous process.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: Which one of the following is an animal belonging to the Marsupial category?
items.x: The koala is a marsupial of Australia that carries its young in a pouch. Rabbit, porcupine and squirrel are placental mammals.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
items.x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: The occurrence of differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species is called
items.x: Differences in characters among individuals of the same species are called variation. Inheritance is passing on traits, evolution the long-term change and adaptation a fit to the habitat.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: In which of the following species is axile placentation commonly observed?
items.x: Hibiscus (family Malvaceae, e.g. China rose, roselle) has axile placentation, ovules on a central axis of a multi-chambered ovary. Legumes such as Delonix show marginal placentation.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: Fermentation of Yeast is an example of?
items.x: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and CO2 without oxygen, so fermentation is anaerobic respiration.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: The limit of growth is fixed by which of the following factor?
items.x: The limit of growth is fixed by internal (genetic, hormonal) factors of the organism; nutrition and exercise only help reach it.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The patterns of arrangement of leaves on the stem are called
items.x: The arrangement of leaves on the stem is phyllotaxy. Venation is the vein pattern, aestivation the arrangement of floral parts in a bud and placentation of ovules.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
items.x: Insects such as the grasshopper breathe through a network of tracheae opening at spiracles; gills and lungs belong to other animals.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: What is the primary function of the human digestive system?
o: To break down food and absorb nutrients
To provide Oxygen to the body
items.x: The digestive system breaks food down into simple absorbable molecules and absorbs the nutrients; temperature control, blood circulation and oxygen supply belong to other systems.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
Identify the correct pairs of organic chemical reactions and their mechanisms.

1. Gatterman-Koch Reaction - The formation of cyclopropanes from alkenes using methylene carbene.

2. Friedel-Crafts Acylation Reaction - The conversion of carboxylic acids into esters using acids and alcohols.

3. Etard Reaction - The direct oxidation of an aromatic or heterocyclic bound methyl group with an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.

4. Stephen Reaction - The conversion of nitriles to aldehydes in the presence of hydrochloric acid, using tin chloride.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
items.x: Etard reaction oxidises an aromatic methyl group to an aldehyde with chromyl chloride, and Stephen reaction reduces nitriles to aldehydes with SnCl2/HCl, so 3 and 4 are right. Gattermann-Koch is formylation of benzene (CO + HCl), not cyclopropanation, and Friedel-Crafts acylation adds an acyl group to an aromatic ring, not esterification.

items.s: Pollination by birds is called
items.x: Pollination by birds is ornithophily. Anemophily is by wind, entomophily by insects and autogamy is self-pollination.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: Which of the elements is used as fungicide?
items.x: Sulphur (wettable or dusting sulphur, lime-sulphur) is a widely used fungicide; calcium, phosphorus and carbon are not used as fungicides.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following ions is essential for the opening and closing of stomata in plants?
items.x: Potassium ions moving into and out of guard cells open and close the stomata. Carbon, iron and sulphur have no such role.

items.src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
items.s: Which of the following chemical compound added to bread was banned in India
items.x: FSSAI removed potassium bromate from the list of permitted additives in 2016 after CSE found it in bread (possible carcinogen). Gluconate, sulphate and oxalate were not the banned bread additive.

items.s: Essential element of alkaloids is:
items.x: Alkaloids (nicotine, morphine, quinine, caffeine) are plant compounds containing basic nitrogen atoms, so nitrogen is the essential element.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: Sweating is an
o: Difficult to state, which type of process it is
items.x: Sweat cools the body because its evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, so sweating is an endothermic process.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Respiration is an
items.x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Lycopene is a pigment present in:
items.x: Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment of tomato (also watermelon).

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: The reaction of sodium Hydroxide with Hydrochloric acid leading to formation of salt and water is a?
items.x: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is a neutralisation, a double displacement reaction (ions exchange partners).

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is a/an?
items.x: Composting is microbial oxidation of organic matter and releases heat (compost heaps warm up), so it is exothermic.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: In the Haber's process, X moles of nitrogen react with Y moles of hydrogen to form Z moles of ammonia. What are the values of X, Y and Z?
items.x: Haber process: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, so X = 1, Y = 3, Z = 2.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: An electric bulb is rated 11 W. What does W signify here?
o: Amount of electricity consumed in a day
items.x: The watt is the unit of power, i.e. energy consumed per unit time (1 W = 1 J/s); an 11 W bulb uses 11 joules each second. It does not measure light output or daily consumption.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: In which of the following arthropods is the first pair of legs on the cranial segment modified into pincer-like forcipules?
items.x: Centipedes (Chilopoda) have their first pair of trunk legs modified into poison claws called forcipules. Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment and no forcipules; cicadas and wasps are insects.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: What is the primary purpose of a Wasp's sting?
o: To defend themselves or their colony
items.x:
Most books and keys: defence of self and colony. Strictly: in solitary wasps the sting is used mainly to paralyse prey (Britannica, "wasp").
Wasps chiefly use the sting (a modified ovipositor) to defend themselves and the colony. Solitary wasps also use it to paralyse prey, but stinging plays no part in pollination or marking territory.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: What is the function of Xylem in a plant?
o: Transport of food from leaves to rest of the plant
Transport of water from roots to leaves
items.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Phloem carries food from the leaves to the rest of the plant, and cambium makes new wood layers.

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
items.s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are grouped under Thallophyta.
R: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara lack roots, stem, leaves, and vascular system.
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are algae, grouped under Thallophyta because the plant body is an undifferentiated thallus with no roots, stem, leaves or vascular tissue. R states that defining feature, so it correctly explains A.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
items.x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots through stems to leaves. Phloem carries food; cambium and cortex do not conduct water.

items.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
items.s: In a plant transports food from the leaves to the rest of the plant through a process known as translocation.
items.x: Phloem moves food (sugars) from the leaves to the rest of the plant; this is translocation. Xylem and tracheids carry water, and meristem is growing tissue.

items.s: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
o: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
items.x: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Which of the below is a physical change?
items.x: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change: no new substance forms and evaporation recovers the salt. Burning wax or wood and curdling milk make new substances, so they are chemical changes.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Why chameleon changes its colours?
o: To tune its colour with temperature of the day
The colours automatically change on their own
items.x:
Most books and keys: to protect itself from predators (camouflage). Strictly: chameleons change colour mainly for social signalling and thermoregulation (Stuart-Fox & Moussalli 2008, PLoS Biology).
Most books say chameleons change colour mainly to camouflage themselves against predators. Strictly, colour change serves mainly social signalling and temperature control.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: According to Sach's, the body of the vascular plant is composed of the following three tissue systems
o: Dermal tissue system, vascular tissue system and fundamental tissue system
items.x: Julius Sachs grouped plant tissues into three systems: dermal (epidermal), vascular (fundamental conducting) and fundamental (ground) tissue systems. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissue types, not Sachs' tissue systems.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following parts of the stem consists of xylem and phloem together?
items.x: A vascular bundle contains xylem and phloem together. The cortex, endodermis and pith are ground-tissue regions without both conducting tissues.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
items.s: Name the non-metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature.
items.x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature. Mercury is liquid but a metal; silicon and lithium are solids.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
items.s: Which of the following is a non-metal that remains liquid at room temperature?
items.x: Bromine is the non-metal that is liquid at room temperature. Helium and chlorine are gases.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: If a chain is too long, the corrections to the measured distances will be ____
items.x: A chain that is too long measures fewer chain lengths than the true distance, so the correction is positive (added).

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following can be used as Tear Gas?
items.x: Tear gas CN is alpha- (omega-) chloroacetophenone, i.e. 2-chloro-1-phenylethanone. Plain acetophenone is not a lachrymator.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
items.x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: What should be the size of the burner of the gas stove to save the consumption of LPG?
o: Size of the burner does not matter
items.x: A small burner saves LPG because its flame stays under the vessel's base. A large flame spills heat around the sides. (Off-topic: energy saving in daily life.)

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which among the following does not contain crop
items.x: The emu, a flightless ratite, has no crop. Turkey, duck and quail store food in a crop. (Off-topic: zoology.)

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of class Amphibia?
items.x: Clarias is a catfish (class Pisces), not an amphibian. Bufo (toad), Rana (frog) and Hyla (tree frog) are amphibians. (Off-topic: zoology.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which among the following is actually not a tree?
items.x: The banana is a giant herb: its 'trunk' is a pseudostem of leaf sheaths, not wood. Neem, peepal and banyan are true trees. (Off-topic: botany.)

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
items.s: Which of the following seeds can benifit a patient of diabetes mellitus?
items.x: Fenugreek (methi) seeds are rich in soluble fibre and help lower blood sugar, so they benefit diabetics. (Biology item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s:
Which of the following statements is correct about Angiosperms?

A. Seeds naked (not enclosed in ovary)

B. Xylem vessels usually absent

C. Bears flowers where reproductive spores (gametes) develop
items.x: Angiosperms bear flowers, have seeds enclosed in an ovary (fruit) and usually have xylem vessels. Naked seeds and absent vessels describe gymnosperms, so only C is correct. (Biology item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The seeds of the following plants are often called 'dust seeds'
items.x: Orchids produce minute, endosperm-less 'dust seeds' dispersed by wind. Lodoicea (double coconut) has the largest seed. (Botany item, moved.)

items.s: Microscope was invented by
items.x:
Official key / most books: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. Strictly: the compound microscope is credited to Zacharias Janssen (c. 1590); Leeuwenhoek perfected the simple microscope (general knowledge, not checked).
The usual key credits the microscope to Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, who built powerful single-lens microscopes (1670s). (Science item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: If a balloon filled with air is immersed in hot water, its volume would
items.x: Air expands when heated (Charles's law), so a balloon in hot water swells and its volume increases. (Off-topic: physics.)

items.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
items.s: Which of the following characteristics of a sound wave depends only on the source of sound and not on the medium through which it travels?
items.x: Frequency is set by the vibrating source and stays the same in any medium. Speed and wavelength change with the medium. (Off-topic: physics of sound.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Which blood vessels have the smallest diameter?
items.x: Capillaries are the narrowest blood vessels (about 5–10 micrometres), one cell thick. (Off-topic: biology.)

items.s: Which of the following noble gases is NOT present in the air?
items.x:
Most books: all noble gases except radon occur in air. Strictly, radon is present in trace amounts near the ground (decay of radium in soil).
Argon, neon and helium are constituents of air. Radon is radioactive and short-lived, so it is taken as the noble gas not present in air. (Off-topic: chemistry.)

items.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
items.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
a. Mycology
b. Palynology
c. Oncology
d. Paleontology
List-II: i. study of pollen grains ii. study of treatment of tumours iii. study of fossils of animals and plants iv. study of fungi
items.x: Mycology is the study of fungi, palynology of pollen, oncology of tumours and palaeontology of fossils, so (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

items.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
items.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Plant):
a. Potato
b. Carrot
c. Apple
d. Cabbage
List-II (Edible Part): i. Swollen thalamus ii. Vegetative bud iii. Modified root iv. Modified stem
items.x: The potato is a modified stem (tuber), the carrot a modified root, the apple a swollen thalamus (false fruit) and the cabbage a vegetative bud.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Which of the elements found in human body has functional requirement?
items.x:
Official key: Arsenic. Strictly: arsenic's essentiality in humans is unproven (it is a toxic element); none of the options is an established essential element.
Among the options only arsenic is treated as a (possibly essential) ultra-trace element with a functional role; titanium, caesium and aluminium have no known requirement.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Name the homologous series with an -OH functional group.
items.x: Alcohols form the homologous series with the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group. Hydroxide is the OH- ion of bases, not a functional group.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: When an alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 170°C, it undergoes dehydration. What is the major product formed?
items.x: Heating an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 at about 170°C removes water (dehydration) and gives an alkene, e.g. ethanol → ethene.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: Dry ice is used for packing Covid-19 vaccines for transportation. What is dry ice?
items.x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide (sublimes at -78.5°C), used to keep vaccines cold.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: What is the process of extracting metals from their ores called?
items.x: Smelting is extracting a metal from its ore by reduction at high temperature in the fused state; refining purifies the metal and mining removes the ore.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Identify the functional group responsible for the characteristic smell of fruits.
items.x: Esters (RCOOR') give the characteristic fruity smell of fruits and are used in perfumes and flavouring; aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are not the answer.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s:
C2H5OH + alkaline KMnO4 + Heat → X
X + C2H5OH (acid) → Y
What are the products X and Y, respectively?
items.x: Alkaline KMnO4 oxidises ethanol to ethanoic (acetic) acid (X); the acid reacts with ethanol in acid medium to form an ester, ethyl acetate (Y).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which of the following reactions does not occur in a blast furnace during the extraction of iron?
items.x: In the blast furnace, coke burns to CO, limestone decomposes to CaO + CO2 and CO reduces Fe2O3 to iron; decomposition of FeSO4 does not occur there.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Which part of the eye gives it a distinctive colour?
items.x: The iris is the pigmented muscular ring around the pupil and gives the eye its colour. The cornea is transparent, the pupil is an opening and the retina lies at the back.

items.s: What term describes the phenomenon in which a single species evolves into several different forms to exploit different ecological niches?
items.x:
Printed key: Adaptation (adaptive radiation). Strictly the phenomenon is adaptive radiation, a form of divergent evolution, so 'Divergence' is also defensible (general knowledge, not checked).
A single species evolving into many forms that exploit different niches is adaptive radiation (Darwin's finches), which the key reads as 'adaptation'. Strictly, adaptive radiation is a case of divergent evolution; convergence is the opposite process.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: Which of the following is incorrect about acids?
o: Aqueous solutions of acids are electrolytes
Acids can change the colour of certain acid-base indicators
Acids do not react with active metals
items.x: Acids do react with active metals (e.g. zinc, iron) to give hydrogen gas, so that statement is incorrect. Aqueous acids conduct electricity, taste sour and change indicator colours.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: What is the range of mercury thermometer in Fahrenheit?
items.x:
Printed answer: -35 to 673 °F. Strictly mercury freezes at -38.8 °C (-37.9 °F) and boils at 356.7 °C (674 °F) (general knowledge, not checked).
A mercury thermometer works between mercury's freezing and boiling points, about -38 °C to 357 °C, i.e. roughly -37 °F to 674 °F; the printed answer gives the commonly quoted -35 to 673 °F.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: What is the colour of litmus solution when it is neither acidic or basic?
items.x: Litmus solution is purple in a neutral solution; it turns red in acid and blue in base.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about chemicals and their popular names?

A. The chemical name of 'Alum' is Potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate.

B. The chemical name of 'Aspirin' is Acetyl salicylic acid.

C. The chemical name of 'Chalk' is Hypochlorus acid.
items.x: Alum (potash alum) is potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate, KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, and aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, so A and B are correct; chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO3), not hypochlorous acid.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: Out of the following, which is a product of the first stage of oxidation of Glucose?
items.x: The first stage of glucose oxidation is glycolysis, which splits glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate) in the cytoplasm; CO2, and ethanol (in fermentation) come later, and ATP is a by-product, not the product of glucose breakdown.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men
items.s: The human saliva has an average pH of____.
items.x: Human saliva is slightly acidic to near-neutral, pH about 6.2-7.6 with an average of about 6.7 (salivary amylase works best near this); 5.5 is the enamel-dissolving critical pH, and 7.8 and 9.1 are too alkaline.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Tobacco plant contains the following alkaloid?
items.x: Nicotine is the alkaloid of the tobacco plant; morphine comes from the opium poppy and reserpine from Rauwolfia, and resin is not an alkaloid. (Off-topic: general science.)

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: What happens to the colour of litmus paper when you put a drop of acid on it?
o: Blue Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to blue
Green Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to green
items.x: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following is not a primary colour?
items.x: Red, green and blue are the additive primary colours of light, so yellow is not one. (Moved to 5:1.)

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: What is the colour of Chlorophyll a?
items.x: Chlorophyll a is blue-green, while chlorophyll b is yellow-green. (Moved to 5:1.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: What is the role of Barium Nitrate (Ba(NO3)2) in fireworks and fountains?
o: It acts as a fuel for combustion.
It produces a blue color in the flames.
It is an oxidizer that produces a green color in the flames.
It produces a red color in the flames.
items.x: Barium nitrate is an oxidiser in fireworks that gives a green flame; strontium gives red and copper blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
items.s: Plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation, are called ......
items.x: Gymnosperms (gymnos = naked, sperma = seed) have ovules not enclosed in an ovary, exposed before and after fertilisation. Angiosperms enclose ovules in an ovary.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: Which of the following is an example of a Maillard reaction?
o: Burning of eyes while cutting onions
items.x: The Maillard reaction is the browning of food when sugars react with amino acids on heating - e.g. bread turning into toast; tears from onions, egg hardening (protein denaturation) and curd formation are other processes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Identify the organisms that reproduce asexually by budding.
items.x: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by budding; Amoeba and Paramecium divide by binary fission.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following digestive enzymes acts in the stomach of humans?
items.x: Pepsin acts in the stomach (protein digestion in acid medium); amylase acts in mouth and intestine, trypsin and lipase come from the pancreas.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
items.s: Which enzyme helps in the digestion of fats in the gut of humans?
items.x: Lipase digests fats (pancreas, intestine); amylase digests starch, lactase lactose, and helicase unwinds DNA.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following enzyme is elevated in Downer cow syndrome
items.x: In downer cow syndrome the recumbent cow suffers muscle damage, so serum creatine phosphokinase (CK) rises sharply; tryptophan and creatinine are not enzymes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The foods of Protozoans is digested by
items.x: Protozoa such as Amoeba digest food with enzymes inside food vacuoles; contractile vacuoles remove water.

items.s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?

a. Melamine polymer is used in the manufacture of unbreakable crockery

b. Enzymes are biocatalysts

c. DNA fingerprinting is used for identification of criminals

d. Tincture of iodine is an antiseptic
items.x: All four are correct: melamine makes unbreakable crockery, enzymes are biocatalysts, DNA fingerprinting identifies criminals and tincture of iodine is an antiseptic.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The postmortem sample collected during abortion is
items.x: After an abortion the aborted fetus (with placenta) is the key post-mortem sample for diagnosing the cause; blood, milk or serum are ante-mortem samples.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: In humans, which cells can perform anaerobic respiration during oxygen shortage?
items.x: Skeletal muscle cells respire anaerobically in oxygen shortage, producing lactic acid.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: Spirogyra is an example of:
items.x: Spirogyra is a green filamentous alga.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: No. of lobes present in left lung of cow
items.x:
Most keys: 3 lobes (apical/cranial, cardiac/middle, diaphragmatic/caudal). Strictly in current veterinary nomenclature the left lung has 2 lobes, the cranial lobe being split into two parts (general knowledge, not checked).
Classical veterinary anatomy divides the ox's left lung into three lobes (apical, cardiac, diaphragmatic); the right lung has four or five.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
items.s:
Identify the compound described below:
- It is present in crude oil and gasoline.
- It can cause Leukemia, DNA Strand Breaks, Chromosomal damage, Cancer, and harmful effects on bone marrow.
- It is known to be carcinogenic to humans.
items.x: Benzene, found in crude oil and petrol, is a known human carcinogen causing leukaemia and bone-marrow and chromosome damage.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Which part of the plant is a potato?
items.x: The potato is a tuber - a modified underground stem with eyes (buds).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
items.s: Which of the following is matched INCORRECTLY?
o: Protein - Needed for the building of antibodies and immune system cells.
Vitamin A - Helps regulate the immune system and protect the body by keeping skin and tissues in the mouth.
Vitamin C - helps the body build healthy skin.
Zinc - Helps to activate immune cells and properly regulate their function.
items.x: Protein builds antibodies; vitamin A keeps skin and the linings of mouth, gut and airways healthy; vitamin C helps build skin (collagen) and antibodies; the printed key marks the zinc statement as the mismatch.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following is present in plant cells but not cells of animals?
items.x: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack; both have vacuoles, plasma membrane and Golgi.

items.s:
Assertion (A): The amount of DNA present in somatic cell depends on the phase of the cell cycle.
Reason (R): Telophase and G1 phase nuclei contain only half (as 2c) the amount of DNA found in the prophase; G2 phase and metaphase cells represent 4c.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is not correct explanation for (A).
(A) is correct and (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct and (R) is correct
items.x: DNA content changes over the cell cycle: G1 and telophase nuclei are 2C, G2/prophase/metaphase 4C after S-phase replication - so R correctly explains A.

items.s: Mycology is the study of
items.x: Mycology is the study of fungi; entomology = insects, limnology = fresh waters, volcanology = volcanoes.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: During the period of intense body exercise, which of the following increases in the blood of person?
items.x: During intense exercise muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up in the blood; oxygen and glucose fall.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: Which of the following enzymes found in saliva is responsible for digestion?
items.x: Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin), which digests starch; pepsin acts in the stomach, trypsin from the pancreas.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: Of the following bacteria, ____ causes pneumonia.
