items.x: Haemophilus influenzae causes pneumonia (as does Streptococcus pneumoniae); S. thermophilus and Lactobacillus are curd/yoghurt bacteria and E. coli is a gut bacterium.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is not used in lactic acidosis in cattle
items.x: Rumen lactic acidosis is treated with alkalising agents - sodium bicarbonate, magnesium hydroxide, Ringer's lactate fluids; vinegar (acetic acid) is used for urea/ammonia poisoning, not acidosis.

items.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
items.x: Orange - citric, tomato - oxalic, tamarind - tartaric: I-c, II-a, III-b.

items.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
items.s:
Match the following items with the acids found in them.
Natural source:

I. Orange

II. Tamarind

III. Tomato
Acid:

a. Tartaric Acid

b. Oxalic Acid

c. Citric Acid
items.x: Orange - citric (c), tamarind - tartaric (a), tomato - oxalic (b): I-c, II-a, III-b (options 2 and 4 are printed identically).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: How many square metres make one acre of area?
items.x: One acre = 4,046.86 square metres (about 0.4047 hectare); one hectare = 10,000 sq m. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Atoms are composed of
items.x: An atom is a small nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The smallest ketone has ____ carbon atom/s.
items.x: The smallest ketone is acetone (propanone, CH3COCH3) with 3 carbon atoms, since the C=O must be bonded to two carbons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which of the following could be the molecular formula of an alcohol?
items.x: C2H6O is ethanol (C2H5OH), a saturated alcohol CnH2n+2O; C2H4O is acetaldehyde, C3H6O acetone or propanal, and CH2O formaldehyde. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s: Which of the following is a homopolymer?
items.x: Cellulose is a homopolymer of beta-glucose only; proteins and collagen are built from many different amino acids, and agarose has alternating galactose units (agarobiose). (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: The most abundant organic compound in world is?
items.x: Cellulose, the main component of plant cell walls, is the most abundant organic compound on Earth. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.s: The ATP production through respiration is called
items.x: ATP made in respiration via the electron transport chain is oxidative phosphorylation; photophosphorylation is ATP formation in photosynthesis. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General

items.x: The photocopier drum is coated with photoconductive selenium (or amorphous silicon/organic photoconductor) that holds charge in the dark and loses it when lit.

items.s: Holography is a technique which is now extensively used by:
items.x:
Printed/book key: Navigators. Strictly: holography is used widely by museum authorities (3D recording/display of artefacts) and in security; no source found stating 'navigators' (web search).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: In a mammal, what is the ratio of the number of chromosomes in a somatic cell to that in a gamete?
items.x: Somatic cells are diploid (2n, 46 in humans) and gametes haploid (n, 23), so the ratio is 2:1.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
items.x: Mitochondria - powerhouse, ATP (3); ribosomes - protein synthesis (1); cell membrane - regulates passage (4); nucleus - control centre with genetic material (2).

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Amoeba is reproduced by fission.
2.
Reason (R): All unicellular organisms are reproduced by asexual methods.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Amoeba reproduces by binary fission (A true), but not all unicellular organisms are only asexual - Chlamydomonas, Paramecium (conjugation) and yeast show sexual reproduction (R false).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: The traits of Kalikak family of USA were studied by whom?
items.x: Henry H. Goddard studied the Kallikak family (1912) to argue that 'feeble-mindedness' was inherited; Galton studied hereditary genius.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who is not a behaviorist from the following?
items.x: Kurt Lewin was a Gestalt/field-theory psychologist, not a behaviourist; Pavlov, Watson and Skinner are behaviourists.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Which of the following is a plant hormone?
items.x: Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division and delay ageing. Insulin, thyroxin and oestrogen are animal hormones. (Off-topic: plant physiology.)

items.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: Which enzyme is found in tears?
items.x: Tears contain lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme that breaks down bacterial cell walls. Ptyalin is in saliva, pepsin in the stomach, and sebum is skin oil. (Off-topic: human physiology.)

items.s:
Arrange the following events of "biogeny theory" in a sequence.

a. Formation of coacervates

b. Aerobic organisms came to existence

c. Heterotropic organisms began to form

d. Mycoplasmas are first formed cells
items.x: In the biogeny sequence, coacervates formed first, then the first cells (mycoplasma-like), then heterotrophs, and aerobic organisms came last: a, d, c, b. (Off-topic: origin of life.)

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Pneumatic bones are commonly present in
items.x: Birds have pneumatic (air-filled) bones that lighten the skeleton for flight; cattle, horses and pigs have solid marrow-filled bones.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The venom of Russell's Viper primarily affects the
items.x: Russell's viper venom is haemotoxic: it disrupts blood clotting (consumption coagulopathy, bleeding). Cobra and krait venoms are the neurotoxic ones.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which body fluid plays an important role in transporting digested fats in humans?
items.x: Digested fats are absorbed into the lacteals (lymph vessels) of the villi and carried by lymph, not directly by blood.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: What is the main function of the kidneys in the human body?
o: To filter waste products and excess of water from the blood
Help the body to absorb nutrients from the food
To pump the blood throughout the body
items.x: The kidneys filter waste products and excess water from the blood and form urine; digestion, absorption and pumping are other organs' jobs.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following is the longest part of the alimentary canal?
items.x: The small intestine (about 6-7 m) is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Paste consisting of the drug mixed with either honey/jaggery and administered orally in large animals is called
items.x: An electuary is a drug mixed into a paste with honey, jaggery or treacle and given by mouth (smeared on the tongue). A bolus is a large pill, a drench a liquid dose, a pessary a vaginal insert.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Fat in the food eaten by us is completely digested in?
items.x: Fats are completely digested in the small intestine by bile (emulsification) and pancreatic and intestinal lipase.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Which of the following plants eats mosquitoes?
items.x: The pitcher plant is insectivorous – its pitcher traps and digests insects such as mosquitoes. Cinchona gives quinine; lemon grass only repels.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: The digestive fluid bile is produced by which organ of the human body?
items.x: Bile is produced by the liver and only stored in the gall bladder.

items.x: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine.

items.x: Starch in milk turns blue with iodine solution – the iodine test.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
items.x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

items.s: If all the alveoli in a human lung are separated and spread, they will occupy the size of a typical?
items.x: The roughly 300-500 million alveoli have a surface area of about 70 m² – about a tennis court.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P

items.x: Gastric glands of the stomach wall release HCl.

items.x: Leucocytes are white blood cells – colourless because they lack haemoglobin.

items.x: Melanocytes are the cells that make melanin pigment in the iris.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M

items.x: Red blood cells are formed in the red bone marrow.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The drug Rauwolfia, is obtained from ______ of Sarpgandha.
items.x: The drug from Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina), used for blood pressure, comes from its roots. (Off-topic: medicinal plants.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which type of fungi is most notorious for causing dry rot in wood?
items.x:
Most keys: 'Dry rot fungus'. Strictly, the dry rot fungus Serpula lacrymans is itself a brown-rot fungus (general knowledge, not checked).
The fungus notorious for dry rot of timber is the dry rot fungus (Serpula lacrymans), keyed as option 3; it decays wood as a brown rot. (Off-topic: wood decay.)

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: Out of the below, which food is richer in Zinc?
items.x:
Printed key: chicken (animal foods give well-absorbed zinc). Strictly, per 100 g almonds and dry legumes hold about as much or more zinc than chicken (general knowledge, not checked).
Animal foods such as chicken give well-absorbed zinc, so the printed key is chicken; green leafy vegetables are poor zinc sources. (Off-topic: nutrition.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Which drugs are used to lower the body temperature?
items.x: Antipyretics (e.g. paracetamol) lower raised body temperature; analgesics relieve pain.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What substance is added to water to dissolve shellac and create a water-based varnish?
items.x: Shellac dissolves in water when borax (an alkali) is added, giving a water-based shellac varnish; spirit (alcohol) gives the ordinary spirit varnish, not a water-based one.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which group of elements generally form coloured compounds?
items.x: Transition (d-block) metals form coloured compounds because of d-d electron transitions in partly filled d orbitals; alkali-metal and non-metal compounds are mostly colourless.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The artery used for recording pulse in dog is
items.x: In dogs the pulse is recorded from the femoral artery on the inner thigh.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Site of recording pulse in dogs
items.x: The pulse of a dog is taken at the femoral artery (inner thigh); the coccygeal artery is used in cattle and the jugular is a vein.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: Which of the following carries Carbon dioxide rich blood from heart to lungs in humans?
items.x: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated (CO2-rich) blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The largest artery in the human body
items.x: The aorta, leaving the left ventricle, is the largest artery of the body.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: A blood vessel which pumps the blood from the heart to the entire body
items.x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the body (the aorta from the left ventricle); veins return it and capillaries exchange materials.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing cast iron cookware from rusting?
items.x: Seasoning (coating with fat or oil and heating) forms a protective layer that keeps cast iron from rusting; soap and abrasives strip that layer.

items.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023

Organ:

II. Liver

III. Heart
Arteries which supply blood:

b. Hepatic arteries

c. Coronary arteries
items.x: Renal arteries supply the kidney, hepatic arteries the liver and coronary arteries the heart: I-a, II-b, III-c.

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: Which of the following is an emulsion?
items.x: Butter is an emulsion (water droplets dispersed in fat); vinegar, sugar solution and honey are solutions.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Development of off odour in fats & oils when they are stored for a longer duration is known as
items.x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

items.s: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?
items.x: Viruses are acellular and have no metabolic enzymes of their own; lichens, bacteria and algae are cellular organisms with enzymes.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: What is the name of the process through which unicellular organisms eat food?
items.x: Unicellular organisms like Amoeba engulf food by phagocytosis; pinocytosis is the intake of fluid droplets.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Sulphur is used in vulcanization. This process is mainly associated with
items.x: Vulcanisation is heating natural rubber with sulphur, which cross-links it and makes it harder, stronger and more elastic and wear-resistant (tyres, footwear). Steel, glass and cement making do not use it.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Alimentary canal runs from mouth to?
items.x: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, rectum, anus).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s:
Read the following statements in respect to difference between 'Poisonous and Venomous animals':

a. If you bite it and you die, it's Poisonous. If it bites and you die, it's Venomous.

b. If you bite it and you die, it's Venomous. If it bites and you die, it's Poisonous.
Which of the above statements is/ are correct?
items.x: Poisonous animals harm you when you bite or eat them (toxin passively delivered); venomous animals inject venom by biting or stinging. So only statement a is correct.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
items.s: Which of the following systems of the human body is responsible when a person sneezes?
items.x: Sneezing is a reflex of the respiratory system: irritants in the nasal lining trigger a forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth. It is controlled by the medulla, but the system involved is respiratory, not immune (printed key: immune system).

items.s: Anorexia and bulimia are types of ____ disorders.
items.x: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa are eating disorders (self-starvation; binge eating with purging).

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Primary methods to prevent food spoilage do NOT include:
items.x: Food spoilage is prevented by refrigeration, drying, salting, canning and preservatives; exposure to air, moisture and microbes causes spoilage, so it is not a method.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: A cardiac portion, a fundic region and a pyloric portion are parts of which of the following organs/body parts?
items.x: The stomach has a cardiac part (near the oesophagus), a fundic region and a pyloric part (opening into the duodenum).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s:
In the context of human physiology, match the blood components with their respective names.
Blood components:
1. Erythrocytes
2. Leukocytes
3. Thrombocytes
Names:
A. White blood cells
B. Platelets
C. Red blood cells
items.x: Erythrocytes are red blood cells, leukocytes white blood cells and thrombocytes platelets: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s: Anorexia nervosa is a ....disorder.
items.x: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder (self-starvation from fear of weight gain).

items.src: Pollution Control Board Steno Typist, Junior Assistant 2017
items.s: Who invented Television?
items.x: John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television in 1926. Fleming discovered penicillin and Watt improved the steam engine.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The ignition temperatures of four substances P, Q, R and S are 95°C, 98°C, 105°C and 108°C, respectively. Which substance/s will catch fire when they are exposed to a temperature of 100°C?
items.x: A substance catches fire only when its temperature reaches its ignition temperature. At 100°C, P (95°C) and Q (98°C) are above their ignition temperatures and burn; R (105°C) and S (108°C) stay below theirs, so only P and Q catch fire.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a region of the human stomach?
items.x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Which blood group is known as the universal recipient?
items.x: Group AB is the universal recipient: its plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it can receive red cells of any ABO group. O is the universal donor (its red cells carry no A or B antigen).

items.s: All of the following are tests for brain, spinal cord, and nerve disorders, EXCEPT ______
items.x: Bronchoscopy examines the airways and lungs, not the nervous system. Myelography (spinal cord imaging), electroencephalography (EEG – brain's electrical activity) and echoencephalography (ultrasound of the brain) are nervous-system tests.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting
items.x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions – heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing, salivation, swallowing and vomiting. The cerebrum handles voluntary action and thought, the cerebellum balance, and the diencephalon (hypothalamus) temperature, hunger and thirst.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Which part of the brain controls the process of Breathing?
items.x: Breathing is controlled by the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata (with the pons). The cerebellum controls balance, the hypothalamus temperature/hunger, the cerebrum voluntary actions.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which of the following instruments is NOT used for setting out gradient?
items.x: The prismatic compass measures bearings (horizontal directions), not gradients. The clinometer measures slopes and the Ceylon ghat tracer locates points on a given gradient (hill-road surveys); the dumpy level gives levels from which gradients are set out.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The complete male flower of the following plant is transported to the female flower for pollination
items.x: In Vallisneria the male flowers break off and float up to the water surface, where water currents carry them to the female flowers raised on long stalks, so the whole male flower travels. In Zostera (a seagrass) only long pollen grains are released and carried under water; Nymphaea (water lily) is insect-pollinated.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: Which of the following has a open circulatory system?
items.x: The cockroach, an insect (arthropod), has an open circulatory system: haemolymph is pumped into open sinuses (haemocoel) and bathes the organs. Fish, snakes and earthworms have closed circulatory systems with blood kept inside vessels.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Tracheal respiration occurs in which of the following organisms?
items.x: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Identify the organisms that undergo cutaneous respiration.
items.x: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The National Tree of India is
items.x: India's national tree is the Indian banyan, Ficus benghalensis. Ficus religiosa is the peepal (sacred fig), Ficus elastica the rubber fig and Ficus racemosa the cluster fig (gular).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: What is the main function of worker bees in a hive?
items.x: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
items.x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Why are roughages important in our food?
o: They help in expel of undigested food
items.x: Roughage (dietary fibre) is indigestible plant carbohydrate: it gives no energy or nutrients but adds bulk and helps the body get rid of undigested food (prevents constipation). Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats, body building from proteins, and vitamins from food itself – not from roughage.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Which university has been ranked as world's most innovative university by Reuters news agency in 2018?
items.x: Reuters' 2018 ranking of the world's most innovative universities placed Stanford University first, ahead of MIT and Harvard.

items.s: The first woman appointed as the Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
items.x: Dr N. Kalaiselvi (2022) is the first woman Director General of CSIR.

items.s: Identify a mismatch among the following pairs :

items.x: CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute is in Lucknow. (CSIR lab item, moved.)

items.x: The Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR, a DST institute) is at Jakkur, Bengaluru. (Moved to 5:4.)

items.s: The 90th Indian Science Congress was held in the first week of January, 2003 at Bangalore. Who of the following was/were the organiser(s) of the Congress?
items.x: The 90th Indian Science Congress (3-7 Jan 2003, Bangalore) was hosted jointly by ISRO and Bangalore University.

items.s: Which among the following institutions hosted the 106th Indian Science Congress in 2018?
items.x:
Printed key: Central University of Manipur (the 2018 session, 105th). Strictly the 106th session was at Lovely Professional University, Jalandhar, in January 2019 (Wikipedia ISCA sessions table).
The 2018 session (the 105th, March 2018) was hosted by Manipur University, Imphal, the key here; the 106th was at Lovely Professional University, Jalandhar, in January 2019.

items.s:
Which of the following is correct about Accelerate Vigyan Scheme of Government of India?

I. It is run by Department of Science and Technology, Govt of India

II. Its target Audience are Students from the Universities/Institutes/Recognised colleges
items.x: Accelerate Vigyan is a scheme of SERB, the statutory board under DST, for research internships and workshops for students of universities, institutes and colleges, so both statements are accepted.

items.s: The Ministry of Science and Technology has recently launched a new programme called "SATYAM". Its main object is to
o: protect the intellectual property rights in India.
strengthen research in the areas of yoga and meditation.
conduct lie detector tests in all the courts in India.
link ancient wisdom to modern knowledge.
items.x: SATYAM (Science and Technology of Yoga and Meditation, DST, 2015) funds research on yoga and meditation.

items.s: Which Indian city hosted the "India International Science Festival 2021", a flagship event that aims to promote scientific temper and foster research and innovation in the country?
items.x: The India International Science Festival (IISF) 2021, the 7th edition, was held at Panaji, Goa (10-13 Dec 2021), organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and Vijnana Bharati.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan launched on 9th July 2015 by
items.x: The Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, the MHRD programme to make school children curious about science and maths, was launched by Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on 9 July 2015 at Vigyan Bhawan.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
As of 31st December 2024, which of the following statements is/are correct about PARAM Rudra Supercomputers under NSM?
Statement A: 33 supercomputers with 32 Petaflops capacity have been deployed in IISc, IITs, C-DAC and Tier-II and Tier-III institutions.
Statement B: These supercomputers support 10,000+ researchers, including 1,700+ PhD scholars from 200+ institutions.
Statement C: NSM provides Tier-II and Tier-III city researchers' access to advanced supercomputing facilities.
o: Only Statements A and B are correct
Only Statements B and C are correct
All Statements A, B and C are correct
items.x: All three are correct: by 31 Dec 2024 NSM had deployed 33 supercomputers (32 Petaflops) at IISc, IITs, C-DAC and Tier-II/III institutions, used by 10,000+ researchers incl. 1,700+ PhD scholars from 200+ institutions; PARAM Rudra systems (Sept 2024) extend access to Tier-II/III cities.

items.s: The only manned submersible vehicle that can reach any region of Oceans, "DSV Limiting Factor", will be carried by the following research vessel
items.x: DSV Limiting Factor was carried by the support ship DSSV Pressure Drop ('Prizer drop' is a misprint) in the Five Deeps Expedition.

items.s: The Sagar Kanya is the name of
o: The Oceanographic research vessel India has bought
A ship employed by the Coast guards
A new high yielding variety of wheat
items.x: ORV Sagar Kanya is the oceanographic research vessel India bought from West Germany (commissioned 1983). (Off-topic: ocean research.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: The Concept of "PURA" was the brain child of?
items.x: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) was the idea of Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, launched as a scheme in 2004.

items.s: Recently, scientists of which organization named a bacteria after Dr APJ Abdul Kalam?
items.x: In 2017 NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory named a bacterium found on the International Space Station Solibacillus kalamii after Dr APJ Abdul Kalam.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: In which place, recently Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Abdul Kalam Memorial?
items.x: PM Modi inaugurated the Dr APJ Abdul Kalam National Memorial at Pei Karumbu, Rameswaram (Kalam's birthplace), on 27 July 2017.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Abdul Kalam served as the ____ President of India from 2002 to 2007.
items.x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam was the 11th President of India (2002-2007), succeeding K.R. Narayanan.

o: Design and synthesis of Molecular machines
items.x: The 2016 Chemistry Nobel (Sauvage, Stoddart, Feringa) was for the design and synthesis of molecular machines. Quasicrystals = 2011, DNA repair = 2015, super-resolved fluorescence microscopy = 2014. (Moved to row 11.)

items.x: Digitisation converts text, images, sound or video from analogue form into digital (computer-readable) form.

items.x: Integrated circuits are made on silicon chips (a semiconductor). Off-topic (computers), moved.

o: Information about the tool of research

items.s: Among the following groups, which group is most reliable for primary source of information? (Information Sources)
items.x: Primary sources of information are original records such as patents, standards, theses and journal articles.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Encapsulation is a term associated with:
items.x: Encapsulation is a digital-preservation strategy: an object is packaged with its metadata and the information needed to render it later. (ICT item; moved.)

items.x: A personal computer is a microcomputer (built around a microprocessor). (Computer topic; moved.)

items.x: Magnetic tape is a plastic ribbon, typically half an inch wide, coated on one side with magnetisable iron oxide.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: Which feature of Microsoft Word is used to generate bulk letters?
items.x: Mail Merge in MS Word produces bulk personalised letters from one template and a data list. Templates only give a layout, and Envelopes prints single envelopes.

items.s: Which of the following keys must be used in order to quit from Gateway of Tally?
items.x: In Tally, Ctrl + Q quits from the Gateway of Tally (or the current screen).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Abstract which not only describes the content of the work but also evaluates the work and its presentation is called
items.x: A critical abstract summarises a work and also evaluates it and its presentation. An informative or indicative abstract only describes the content.

items.s: Resolution of screen is
o: Number of horizontal and vertical pixels displayed on the screen
Number of pixels in the diagonal length of displayed on the screen
Number of colours displayed on the screen
Density and thickness of display screen
items.x: Screen resolution is the number of horizontal and vertical pixels displayed (e.g. 1920 x 1080). It is not the colour count or the diagonal pixel count.

items.s: The headquarters of Microsoft are located in which state of USA?
items.x: Microsoft's headquarters is in Redmond, Washington state, USA.

items.s: Choose the correct statement which defines a motion path in MS PowerPoint :
o: This allows the display of the Slide show
A way of moving item like Picture on a slide
A way of advancing the slides
Display of the pictures without any effect
items.x: A motion path in PowerPoint is an animation that moves an item, such as a picture, along a set path on a slide.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Core in computers means
items.x: A core is an individual processing unit within a CPU chip (a processor), as in dual-core or quad-core.

items.s: Choose the incorrect short-cut key combinations of Tally ERP9 in the given below:
items.x: Unscorable: in Tally ERP 9 all four are valid - Alt+2 duplicates a voucher, Alt+A adds, Alt+I inserts, and Alt+D deletes a voucher, master or (in Company Alteration) a company - so no combination is incorrect.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: What are Transitions in Powerpoint Presentation?
items.x: Slide transitions are the visual effects used when one slide gives way to (introduces) the next; animations act on objects within a slide. Off-topic, moved to software.

items.s: What is the definition of USB in computer terms?
items.x: USB = Universal Serial Bus, the standard port and cable for connecting peripherals. Off-topic, moved to hardware.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(B) VRO/Village Surveyor
items.s: Drawings created with commercial software are typically saved as
items.x: Drawings made with CAD/commercial software are saved as electronic files. Off-topic, moved to software.

items.s: To move to the bottom of a document, press
items.x: Ctrl + End moves to the bottom (end) of the document; the End key alone only moves to the end of the current line. Off-topic, moved to software.

items.s: The first computer fabricated in India by Electronic Corporation of India
items.x: Siddhartha was the first computer (microcomputer) made by the Electronics Corporation of India (ECIL). Off-topic, moved to hardware.

items.s: SQL stands for
items.x: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, used to manage relational databases. Off-topic here; moved to software.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: Which system allows multiple users to access a single computer system?
items.x: A time-shared system lets many users use one computer at the same time by giving each a short time slice; cluster and grid systems join many computers.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: Which Command is used to modify the structure of the database?
items.x: ALTER (a DDL command) changes the structure of a table; UPDATE changes the data, REVOKE removes privileges.

items.s: A DVD is an example of
items.x: A DVD is an optical disc read by a laser; it is not a hard disc or a solid-state device.

items.s: Process of inserting an element in an array is called.....
items.x: Adding an element to the top of a stack-style array is called push; pop removes it. Create and Evaluate are not insertion operations.

items.s: The icon with a minus sign (-) in Windows is used to
o: Move the window to the required place
items.x: The minus (–) button on a window's title bar minimises the window.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Which of the following statements is not valid about operator overloading?
o: Only existing operators can be overloaded
Overloaded operator must have at least one operand of its class type
The overloaded operators follow the syntax rules of the original operator
items.x: All three statements are true rules of C++ operator overloading (only existing operators, at least one class-type operand, original syntax kept), so 'None of the above' is the answer.

items.s: A function inside another function in excel is called
items.x: A function used inside another function in Excel is a nested function, e.g. =ROUND(SUM(A1:A5),0). Round and Sum are single functions.

items.s: Database is
o: A collection of information that can only be retrieved
An organized collection of data that can be manipulated or retrieved
A collection of only numeric data that can be manipulated and retrieved
A backup storage where data can be saved
items.x: A database is an organised collection of data that can be stored, manipulated and retrieved; it is not read-only, not limited to numbers and not merely a backup store. (ICT item, moved.)

items.s: MS - Excel is a good application for What IF analysis. Which of the following tool help for this?
items.x: Goal Seek is MS-Excel's What-If Analysis tool that finds the input needed to reach a target result (the other What-If tools are Scenario Manager and Data Table). Off-topic ICT question.

items.s: In MS-Access, Lookup wizard is used to:
items.x: In MS-Access the Lookup Wizard makes a field that picks its value from another table (or a value list).

items.s: In computers, what does Yosemite, Mavericks, Mountain Lion, Lion, Snow Leopard, Leopard, Tiger, Panther, Jaguar, Puma and Cheetah stand for?
items.x: Cheetah, Puma, Jaguar, Panther, Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Lion, Mountain Lion, Mavericks and Yosemite are successive versions of Apple's Mac OS X. (Computer item, moved.)

items.s: When you start typing the same value as of some cells on same column, Excel automatically shows that text. This feature is known as :
items.x: AutoComplete in Excel suggests the rest of an entry when you start typing text already present in that column. AutoFill extends series, AutoCorrect fixes typos.

items.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
items.s: What is Cardinality?
o: Number of entities in a entity set.
Number of times an entity set participates in a relationship set.
Number of attributes of an entity.
Number of Unique keys of an entity set.
items.x: In ER modelling, cardinality is the number of times an entity of an entity set participates in a relationship set (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many). The number of entities in a set or of attributes is something else.

items.s: An RDBMS consists of
items.x: An RDBMS stores data as a collection of related tables (relations) made of records and fields. (Moved to 5:12.)

items.s: All the slides of MS PowerPoint presentation can be viewed in a single screen by using __.
items.x: Slide Sorter view shows all slides as thumbnails on one screen; Slide Show runs them one at a time and Master view edits the template. (Computers; moved to row 12.)

items.s: The first in the world, the Wi-Fi banking branch network was started by
o: State Bank of India and Windsor
items.x: Yes Bank, with Intel, launched the world's first Wi-Fi banking branch network.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: What is a homepage?
items.x: A homepage is the main or introductory page of a website, from which its other pages are linked.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Solr is related to
items.x: Apache Solr is an open-source enterprise search platform (built on Lucene) used for full-text indexing and searching, e.g. in library discovery systems.

items.s: LAN stands for
items.x: LAN = Local Area Network, a network within a building or campus. Off-topic, moved to networks.

items.s: What is the full form of IP?
items.x: IP stands for Internet Protocol, the addressing and routing protocol of the internet. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

items.s: I.R.C. stands for :
items.x: IRC stands for Internet Relay Chat, an application-layer protocol for real-time text chat. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

items.s: Which of the following best describes a private, company wide network, closed to public access?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Intranet); it is added as option 6.
A private, company-wide network closed to public access is an intranet. The printed options repeat 'Internet' (option b is evidently a misprint of 'Intranet'); a VPN is a secure tunnel over a public network, cloud computing is remote services, and an extranet opens part of the network to outsiders.

items.s: Speed of internet is measured in
items.x: Internet speed is a data rate, measured in bits per second (Mbps, Gbps); GHz is frequency, GB is storage and dpi is print/scan resolution. Off-topic here; moved to networks.

items.s: The search engine "Bing" is created and operated by
items.x: Bing is the search engine of Microsoft.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: An online search in which all aspects of the records in natural language may be used as sought terms is known as ____.
items.x: Free-text searching lets every word in the records, in natural language, be used as a search term (unlike controlled-vocabulary searching).

items.s: Who is called the father of e-Mail?
items.x: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network e-mail on ARPANET in 1971 and chose the @ sign, so he is called the father of e-mail.

items.s: HTTP refers to
items.x: HTTP = HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol of the World Wide Web.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
items.s: What does PPTP stand for?
items.x: PPTP = Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, a VPN protocol.

items.s: To reload a webpage, press the ____ button.
items.x: A web page is reloaded with the browser's Reload (Refresh) button, shortcut F5 or Ctrl+R. Ctrl alone does nothing. (Off-topic: ICT.)

items.s: The PTT (Push-To-Talk) services, a mix of Internet Telephone and Wireless Walkie-Talkie, was announced by Tata Teleservices for its mobile telephone customers on May 27, 2004 - a unique technology which is available only in three other countries in the world. Identify the one which does not have this technology.
items.x: Per the key, Malaysia did not yet have Push-to-Talk in 2004, while the USA (Nextel), Japan and Australia did. Tata Teleservices launched India's first PTT service (Qualcomm BREWChat, Kyocera KX440) on 27-28 May 2004.

items.s: What is 'Tangi' app launched by Google?
items.x: Tangi (Google Area 120, Jan 2020) is a short-video app for how-to videos on arts, crafts, cooking and style, not a dance portal, messenger or OS.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: Which song video became the first on You Tube platform to cross the 'billion views' mark?
items.x: PSY's 'Gangnam Style' became the first YouTube video to cross one billion views (December 2012).

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics), Technical Assistant
items.s: What is the name of the smart Phone application for android operating system developed by UC Berkeley University to detect earthquakes?
items.x: MyShake, from UC Berkeley's Seismological Laboratory, uses smartphone sensors to detect earthquakes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: A sign is anything which produces ______
items.x: In semiotics a sign is anything that produces meanings (signifier + signified, Saussure); semiotics is the study of signs.

items.s: Who was the first commercial Mobile service provider in India?
items.x: India's first commercial mobile service was Modi Telstra's MobileNet in Kolkata: the first call on 31 July 1995 (Jyoti Basu to Sukh Ram); BSNL's CellOne came only in 2002.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: TV Channels dedicated to the subjects of home, garden and family:
items.x: Channels on home, garden and family (e.g. TLC, HGTV, Food) are lifestyle channels. Off-topic, moved to digital media.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Method of assessing information needs of user community is known as
items.x: In library and information science, the methods of assessing a user community's information needs are called user studies. Off-topic, moved to media/information services.

items.s: 'Audio conferencing' is
items.x: Audio conferencing is a live voice call among two or more parties, so it is two-sided verbal communication; there are no visual or non-verbal cues. Off-topic here; moved to ICT in day-to-day life.

items.s: J.L. Baird discovered
items.x: John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television (1926). Dynamite = Nobel, radioactivity = Becquerel, radio = Marconi. Off-topic here; moved to ICT/digital media.

items.s: The media which has been playing an important role in the knowledge empowerment of people in the country is
items.x: Printed key: television, credited with the widest audio-visual reach for mass awareness and knowledge empowerment. Off-topic here; moved to digital media.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: ____ is a structured sequence of events in time.
items.x: A narrative is a structured sequence of events in time (a story told in order). Off-topic here; moved to digital media terms.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of mass communication?
items.x: Mass communication is impersonal, reaches a large and scattered audience and passes through gatekeepers, but its feedback is delayed and indirect, so instant feedback is not one of its characteristics. Off-topic here; moved to media.

items.s: Which of the following companies launched the Audible Suno app in India in December 2019?
items.x: Amazon launched Audible Suno, a free audio-entertainment app, in India in December 2019.

items.s: Country with biggest internet population is:
items.x: China has the world's largest internet-user population, ahead of India and the USA.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Expansion of SMS
items.x: SMS stands for Short Message Service, the text-messaging service of mobile networks.

items.s: In which country was the world's first face recognition ATM developed?
items.x: The world's first face-recognition ATM was developed in China (2015, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua Unisplendour).

items.s: The 5th World Information Technology Forum was held during 17-18 April 2012 at
items.x: WITFOR 2012 (5th World IT Forum, IFIP) was held in New Delhi, 16–18 April 2012.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie

items.x: Founding years: LinkedIn 2002 (launched 2003), Facebook 2004, YouTube 2005, Twitter 2006.

items.s: Which of the following cities has India's first 'Techno Park'?
items.x: Technopark, Thiruvananthapuram (1990) was India's first technology park. Gurgaon, Pune and Bangalore came later.

items.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
items.s: Which of the following organisations primarily collaborated with IIT Madras to develop the IRIS chip?
items.x: IRIS (Indigenous RISC-V Controller for Space), a SHAKTI-based chip, was developed by IIT Madras with ISRO (2025).

items.s: Which state government has launched India's first State Robotics Framework in May, 2023?
items.x: Telangana launched India's first State Robotics Framework on 9 May 2023 at T-Hub, Hyderabad.

items.s:
Which of the following indigenously developed technologies were launched at the 11th Traffic Expo and Smart Mobility Conference in October 2023?

I. CMOS Sensor based Camera for Industrial Application

II. Thermal Sensor Camera for Intelligent Transportation System

III. Online Sucro Crystal Imaging System
items.x: All three – iViS (CMOS-sensor industrial camera), TvITS (thermal-sensor ITS camera) and OSIS (Online Sucro Crystal Imaging System) – were launched by MeitY at the 11th Traffic Expo, Oct 2023.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which type of concrete paint among the following is used for areas with high chemical exposure?
items.x: Epoxy coatings resist chemicals and are used on concrete floors with high chemical exposure; acrylic latex paints are not chemical-resistant.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: What is a Bit coin?
o: Copper coin used as currency for payments on dark web
A form of digital currency created and held electronically
items.x: Bitcoin is a decentralised digital (crypto) currency created and held electronically on a blockchain. Off-topic here; moved to blockchain and cryptocurrency.

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
items.s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A: 5G services were launched in India on 1st October 2022
R: Keeping in view India's specific requirements and to take lead in 5G deployment, Department of Telecommunications (DOT) approved financial grant for multi institute collaborative project to set up Indigenous 5G Test Bed at five locations
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: 5G was launched by the PM on 1 October 2022 (India Mobile Congress), and DoT funded the Rs 224-crore indigenous 5G Test Bed (approved March 2018, eight institutes, test beds at five locations: CEWiT/IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Kanpur, IISc). Both are true, but the test bed does not explain the launch date.

items.s: The largest Telecom operator in India is
items.x:
BSNL was the largest operator in 2003 — now Reliance Jio is the largest by subscribers (general knowledge, TRAI data)
In 2003 BSNL was India's largest telecom operator.

items.src: General Studies & Mental Ability (paper title page missing i
items.s: With which of the following country India has recently signed Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation in the field of Information and Communications Technology for cooperation in the areas of telecom security and 5G technologies?
items.x: In October 2020 the Union Cabinet approved a Memorandum of Cooperation with Japan on ICT covering 5G, telecom security and submarine cables.

items.s: In fibre optic communication the source of Light used is:
items.x:
LEDs are also used as sources for short multimode links; the usual key is the semiconductor laser.
Long-distance optical fibre links use semiconductor lasers (laser diodes), which give narrow, coherent, high-speed light. LEDs serve only short, low-speed links, and a CFL is never used.

items.s:
Match the following
List-I -
List-II

a. Radio Broadcasting - i. LF Band

b. Marine and Navigational aids - ii. HF Band

c. T.V. Broadcasting - iii. SHF Band

d. Satellite Communication - iv. VHF Band

items.x: Radio broadcasting (short wave) uses the HF band, marine navigational aids the LF band, TV broadcasting VHF and satellite communication SHF.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022

items.x: The Hyderabad Declaration was adopted at the 22nd National Conference on e-Governance (Hyderabad, October 2019).

items.x: ITIR = Information Technology Investment Region: the 2008 policy resolution (Ministry of Communications and IT) for large delineated regions (about 40 sq km) for IT, ITES and electronic hardware units, e.g. Bengaluru, Hyderabad. It is not 'International' or 'Industrial'.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M

items.x: Union Tribal Affairs Minister Arjun Munda launched the e-governance initiatives for ST welfare schemes (scholarship portals, DBT tracking).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: What is the name of the web portal launched by Survey of India on the 250th Anniversary?
items.x: Survey of India launched the 'Nakshe' web portal (free downloadable topographic maps) on its 250th anniversary in 2017. Off-topic for AP ICT, moved to e-governance portals.

items.s: Which of the following statements about the 'Amantran' portal launched by Rajnath Singh in January 2023 is INCORRECT?
o: It will be used to extend e-invitations to dignitaries/guests and for the online sale of tickets to the general public for witnessing Republic Day and Independence Day events.
It contains QR code-based authentication for enhanced security.
Passes/tickets will be delivered digitally through emails/sms.
The passes/tickets can be easily cancelled/transferred.
items.x: The Amantran portal (MoD, Jan 2023) sends e-invitations and sells Republic Day/Beating Retreat tickets with QR-code authentication and digital delivery; the 'easily cancelled/transferred' claim is the incorrect one. Moved to e-governance portals.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016

items.x: The 2015-16 National Award for e-Governance (Gold) for excellence in Government Process Re-engineering went to COSMOS (Chhattisgarh Online School Monitoring System), Balrampur; MAHA-GEOMIN won in the GIS category. Moved to e-governance programmes.

items.x: PRIASoft (Panchayati Raj Institutions Accounting Software) under e-Panchayat is the accounting software most States use for panchayat accounts.

items.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men

o: The Tele-Law program is exclusively designed for medical advice and consultation
The Tele-Law program is limited to urban areas and does not extend to rural areas
The Tele-Law program provides legal aid exclusively through physical meetings at Common Service Centres
The Tele-Law programme is an e-interface mechanism to seek legal advice and consultation at a pre-litigation stage

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: How many digits are there in the unique identification number issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India under Aadhaar?
items.x: The Aadhaar number issued by UIDAI has 12 digits. Off-topic here; moved to digital identity.

The IT and ITES sectors in India are growing due to digitalisation, cloud technologies, and high demand for IT services, but a talent gap in fields like cyber-security and data science remains. Government initiatives like 'Future Skills PRIME' aim to address this gap through upskilling programs.

Government initiatives are focused on bridging the skill gap in emerging technologies.
Cloud technologies are irrelevant to the growth of IT and ITES sectors.
IT positions are in low demand globally.
items.x: The passage says a talent gap in cyber-security and data science remains and that Future Skills PRIME is meant to close it by upskilling, so the only valid conclusion is that government initiatives aim to bridge the skill gap in emerging technologies. The other options contradict the passage (no workforce challenge, cloud irrelevant, low demand).

items.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: Which of the following companies signed agreement with AP Government to get Women and SMEs online as part of Digital AP programme?
items.x: Printed key: Google India signed an agreement with the AP government to get women and SMEs online under the Digital AP programme.

items.s: India's first Gramin Cyber Centre was launched in
items.x: India's first rural cyber centre ('Cyber Grameen Centre', Swarna Bharat Trust) opened in 2003 at Venkatachalam, Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: The data related to food items issued to students is received on the same day at Head Office in the institutions run by APSWREIS by using?
items.x: Printed key: the ANNAPURNA app, used in APSWREIS institutions so that data on food items issued to students reaches the head office the same day. (AP welfare / e-governance item, moved.)

items.s: Prana Raksha web application has been developed by the Chittoor Police. The app has been developed
o: To save the lives of road accident victims and reach out to women in distress
To control the sandalwood smugglers and arrest them
To provide guidance and protection to pilgrims who are visiting Tirumala
Any citizen can use this app for any purpose
items.x: Chittoor Police's Prana Raksha web app was built to help road-accident victims reach help quickly and to reach women in distress.

items.s: Which company took an initiative of 'News Initiative India Training Network' in five new Indian languages?
items.x: Google's News Initiative (GNI) India Training Network trains journalists in fact-checking and fighting misinformation, and was extended to more Indian languages.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Barriers which are directly connected with the sender and receiver is said to be:
items.x: Barriers arising from the sender and receiver themselves (their attitudes, emotions, perceptions) are personal barriers; organisational barriers come from structure and semantic barriers from language.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Communication is a part of ____ skills.
items.x: Communication is a soft (interpersonal) skill, like teamwork and leadership; hard skills are technical, job-specific abilities.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: What is "phishing" in cybersecurity?
o: Fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive data
items.x: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt, usually by e-mail or fake websites, to obtain sensitive data such as passwords and card details.

items.s: The meaning of data integrity compromise is
o: Data was changed without the knowledge of the owner
Data was copied without the knowledge of the owner
The owner was denied access to the data
The data was denied from backup and restore facility
items.x: An integrity compromise means data was changed without the owner's knowledge; copying is a confidentiality breach and denial of access is an availability breach.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Panchayat Secretary Gra
items.s: In computer terminology, the full form of malware is
items.x: Malware is short for malicious software. Cyber-security topic.

items.s: Computer virus is a
items.x: A computer virus is a software program that copies itself and harms files; it is not a living organism. Cyber-security topic.

items.src: Common GS for IFS, APLIS, ATT 2012
items.s: The first country to launch artificial satellite is
items.x: The USSR launched the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, on 4 October 1957.

items.s: The first country to launch artificial satellite
items.x: The USSR (Sputnik 1, 4 October 1957) was the first country to launch an artificial satellite; the USA followed with Explorer 1 in 1958.

items.s: India's first satellite 'Aryabhatta' was launched from the country of
items.x: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975 by a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket from Kapustin Yar, USSR.

items.s: The main objective of the Indian Space Research Programme is
items.x: India's space programme aims at using space technology for national socio-economic development, not defence.

items.s: With the 1980 SLV-3/Rohini launch, India became which nation in the world to launch a satellite indigenously?
items.x: SLV-3/Rohini made India the sixth such nation; Aryabhata (1975) had flown on a Soviet rocket.

items.s: By which country's rocket was Aryabhata, India's first satellite, launched in 1975?
items.x: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975 on a Soviet rocket.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which Indian city is known as Space city?
items.x: Bengaluru is called India's Space City: ISRO headquarters and the U R Rao Satellite Centre are there. Sriharikota is the launch site, Thiruvananthapuram has VSSC.

items.s: ISRO opened its 1st visitor's gallery to watch rocket launches at Andhra Pradesh's Sriharikota. Its capacity is
items.x: ISRO's first launch-view gallery at Sriharikota (Satish Dhawan Space Centre), opened in 2019, can seat 5,000 people.

items.s: Sriharikota range, which is India's satellite launch centre, is located in which state?
items.x: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota is in Tirupati (formerly Nellore) district, Andhra Pradesh. Thumba is in Kerala, and Kulasekarapattinam (new SSLV port) is in Tamil Nadu.

items.src: TSPSC Assistant Veterinary Surgeon in Animal Husbandry Depar
items.s: In which state did the ISRO establish the first titanium plant in the country?
items.x: India's first titanium sponge plant, set up with ISRO's VSSC, is at KMML, Chavara in Kerala.

items.s:
PSLV type satellite launching vehicle is used to launch:

A. Remote sensing satellites

B. Interstellar probes

C. Communication satellites

D. Navigation satellites
Choose the correct answer:
items.x: PSLV has launched remote-sensing (IRS), communication (GSAT-12, CMS-01) and navigation (IRNSS) satellites and the interplanetary Chandrayaan-1 and Mars Orbiter. Only option b contains A, C and D, so 'interstellar' is read loosely as interplanetary.

items.s:
Assertion (A) : ISRO launched a communication satellite named GSAT-31 in February 2019, successfully.
Reason (R) : GSAT-31 will provide DTH television services, connectivity to VSATs for ATM, stock exchange, e-governance applications etc.
Choose the correct answer :
o: A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.x: GSAT-31, ISRO's communication satellite, was launched on 6 Feb 2019 from Kourou by Ariane-5, and it supports DTH, VSAT links for ATMs, stock exchanges and e-governance. Both are true, but the services do not explain the launch.

items.s: DTH television stands for:
items.x: DTH = Direct To Home: TV signals from geostationary satellites go straight to small home dishes.

items.s:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding GSLV-II

a. It was launched from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota

b. It was launched from Kourou launch base French Guiana

c. Launch vehicle was Delta-IV

d. Launch vehicle was Ariane-5
items.x: The stem is garbled: it evidently means GSAT-11, launched on 5 Dec 2018 from Kourou, French Guiana, on Ariane-5 (b and d). A GSLV itself flies from Sriharikota, and Delta-IV is an American rocket.

items.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of India's advanced satellite INSAT-4A:

A. INSAT-4A was launched in December, 2005 from New Mexico.

B. The European commercial launch service provider Ariane space was associated with the launch of INSAT-4A.

C. Tata-Sky-a digital cable service provider is associated with DTH television broadcasting services from INSAT-4A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.x: INSAT-4A was launched in December 2005 from Kourou, French Guiana (not New Mexico) on an Arianespace Ariane-5 (B), and Tata Sky's DTH service uses it (C). So B and C.

items.s: The orbit of INSAT - 1B is said to be :
items.x: INSAT-1B, like all INSAT satellites, is in a geostationary orbit.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:

A. ISRO recently developed Satellite G-Sat for SAARC Countries

B. G-Sat is communication-cum-meteorology satellite which has been launched by ISRO

C. All the SAARC Countries signed for launching G-Sat satellite
items.x: GSAT-9, the South Asia Satellite, was built by ISRO for SAARC nations (A) as a communication satellite also used for disaster and weather information (B). Pakistan did not join, so C is false.

items.s:
Consider the following:

a. Satellites move around the earth with the same speed as the Earth spins

b. Satellites cover every part of earth except poles and surrounding areas which are out of their range
o: Both a and b are true
Neither a nor b is true
items.x:
No printed key. If the stem means geostationary satellites only, both a and b would be true (option c).
Taken generally, neither holds: only geostationary satellites keep pace with the Earth's spin, and polar-orbiting satellites do cover the poles.

items.s: The period of revolution of geostationary satellite is:
items.x: A geostationary satellite completes one revolution in about 24 hours (one sidereal day), matching Earth's rotation.

items.s: By which launch vehicle was GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Indian Navy's communication satellite, launched in 2013?
items.x: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2013.

items.s: By which launch vehicle was APPLE (1981), India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, launched?
items.x: APPLE was launched in 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou. SLV-3 launched Rohini (1980); the Space Shuttle Challenger carried INSAT-1B (1983); the Vostok launcher carried IRS-1A (1988).

items.s: By which launch vehicle was INSAT-1B (1983), with which the INSAT system was commissioned, launched?
items.x: INSAT-1B went up on the US Space Shuttle Challenger; Ariane-1 carried APPLE (1981).

items.s: INSAT supports which search-and-rescue programme?
items.x: Besides telecom, TV, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education, INSAT supports COSPAS-SARSAT search and rescue.

items.s: Which satellite was GSAT-30 (January 2020) launched to replace?
items.x: GSAT-30, a C/Ku communication satellite on Ariane-5, replaces INSAT-4A.

items.s: INSAT services are carried in which frequency bands?
items.x: INSAT uses the C, Ku, Ka and S bands; L5 and S are NavIC bands.

items.s: Which launch vehicle launched INSAT-4CR (2007), the heaviest satellite launched from India in its day?
items.x: INSAT-4CR (2,130 kg) was launched by GSLV-F04.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: What is the reason for failure in the launch of IRNSS-1H satellite of ISRO?
o: The heat shield did not separate
The rocket ran of fuel before the launch
items.x: IRNSS-1H on PSLV-C39 (31 Aug 2017) failed because the heat shield (payload fairing) did not separate, so the satellite stayed trapped inside.

items.s: ScatSat is for
items.x: SCATSAT-1 (2016) carries a Ku-band scatterometer measuring ocean-surface winds, so it is for weather monitoring and cyclone forecasting, not communication or education.

items.s: ____ is a satellite that provides weather forecasting, cyclone prediction and tracking services to India.
items.x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer gives ocean wind data for weather forecasting and cyclone prediction and tracking. GSAT-31 and GSAT-7A are communication satellites, and Cartosat-2C does mapping.

items.s: ____ is a collaboration between five federal agencies that are major users and producers of satellite land remote sensing data.
items.x: JACIE (Joint Agency Commercial Imagery Evaluation) is a collaboration of US agencies (NASA, NOAA, NGA, USGS, USDA) that use and produce satellite land remote-sensing data; the other options are Indian institutes.

items.s: For the purpose of effective utilization of remote sensing and GIS technology, a web geo-portal has been developed by National Informatics Centre (NIC), initially for the use of National Capital Region (NCR). What is this geo-portal called as?
items.x: PARIMAN (Portal for Analytical Regional Information and Mapping of NCR) is the NIC-developed web geo-portal of the NCR Planning Board, launched in 2021 and opened to the public in July 2022.

items.s: Which Indian satellite was launched on 27th November, 2019 by ISRO from the Sriharikota centre for the purpose of geographical research and studies?
items.x: Cartosat-3, a high-resolution earth-imaging satellite, was launched on PSLV-C47 from Sriharikota on 27 November 2019.

items.src: Technical Assistant (Geo Physics), Technical Asst in AP Mini
items.s: Which satellite was launched by ISRO into space on 07-12-2016
items.x: Resourcesat-2A was launched on PSLV-C36 on 7 December 2016 for resource monitoring.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II Ward Planning and Regula
items.s: Which among the following is not an Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System?
items.x:
Printed key: AstroSat. Strictly: NavIC (navigation) is not an IRS satellite either, so two options fit.
AstroSat is a space observatory, not an IRS (remote sensing) satellite; ResourceSat and OceanSat are IRS satellites.

items.s: The term LIDAR stands for?
o: Low Income and Drought Affected Regions
Licensed Development Agency of the Region
items.x: LIDAR = Light Detection and Ranging: a remote-sensing method that uses laser pulses to measure distances and make 3-D maps.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:
The satellite Oceansat-2 launched by India helps in

A. estimating the water vapour content in the atmosphere

B. predicting the onset of monsoons

C. monitoring the pollution of coastal waters
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Oceansat-2 (2009) carries an ocean colour monitor and scatterometer: water vapour/winds, monsoon onset and coastal pollution – all three (UPSC 2010).

items.s:
Consider the following in view of PSLV-C53 :

A. It was launched from the second launch pad of Satish Dhawan Space Centre on June 30, 2022.

B. It is the dedicated commercial mission of Antrix Corporation.

C. The launch vehicle carried three satellites from Singapore, namely DS-EO, NeuSAR, Scoob-1.
Choose the correct answer :
items.x: A and C are right: PSLV-C53 flew from the second launch pad on 30 June 2022 carrying Singapore's DS-EO, NeuSAR and SCOOB-I. B is wrong: it was NSIL's (not Antrix's) second dedicated commercial mission.

items.s:
With reference to 'Astrosat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. Other than USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space

B. Astrosat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: Neither is correct. Japan and the European Space Agency (and others) had launched space observatories before ASTROSAT (2015), and ASTROSAT weighs 1,513 kg and orbits at about 650 km, not 2,000 kg at 1,650 km.

items.s: Cabinet, in the year 2008, closed Chandrayaan II moon mission costing:
items.x: In September 2008 the Union Cabinet approved Chandrayaan-II, then planned as an Indo-Russian mission, at a cost of Rs 425 crore (Rs 293.5 crore foreign exchange).

items.s: Which of the following mission was launched by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on July 14, 2023?
items.x: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 by LVM3-M4 from Sriharikota and landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
items.s: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to launch first solar mission in 2019-2020. What is it called?
items.x: Aditya-L1, India's first solar mission (space-based solar observatory), was planned for 2019-20 and finally launched on PSLV-C57 on 2 September 2023 to the Sun-Earth L1 point.

items.s:
What is true about Chandrayan-3 mission of India?

I. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) had launched the GLVM 3 rocket from the second launchpad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on July 15, 2022.

II. Chandrayaan-3's lander module on August 23, 2023, made a soft landing on the surface of the Moon.
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
items.x: Only II is true: the lander soft-landed on 23 August 2023. Statement I is wrong: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3-M4 on 14 July 2023, not 15 July 2022.

items.s:
Identify the statements which are true about Chandrayaan-1

A. Launch Vehicle: PSLV-XL C11

B. Mission Design and Management: Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO)

C. Launch Site: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Thiruvananthapuram (Thumba)

D. Launch Date: 22 October 2008
items.x: A, B and D are true: PSLV-C11 (XL), ISRO, 22 October 2008. C is wrong: it was launched from Sriharikota, not Thumba (TERLS launches only sounding rockets).

items.s:
Match the following.
Country:
I. Russia
II. USA
III. India
Lunar Missions:
1. Chandrayaan-3
2. Luna-25
3. Artemis-II
items.x: Russia – Luna-25, USA – Artemis-II, India – Chandrayaan-3: I-2, II-3, III-1.

items.s: Chandrayan-I Antenna's weight is
items.x: The 32 m deep-space antenna at Byalalu (IDSN), built for Chandrayaan-1, weighs about 300 tonnes.

items.s: What is the full form of MOXIE, 2020?
o: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
Mars Orbital In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
Mars Orbital In-Situ Resource Utilization Exploration
Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Exploration
items.x: MOXIE on NASA's Perseverance rover (2020) is the Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment. It made oxygen from Martian CO2. (Space item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: What is dark matter primarily made of, according to current scientific understanding?
items.x: Current understanding holds that dark matter is mostly non-baryonic, with WIMPs the leading candidate; neutrinos are too light and it does not emit electromagnetic radiation.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Name the Soviet Union suborbital flight carrying two dogs Dezik and Tsygan.
items.at: An R-1V rocket flight of 22 July 1951 (first animals recovered alive from a suborbital flight)
items.x: Dezik and Tsygan flew on a Soviet R-1 (R-1V) suborbital rocket on 22 July 1951 and were recovered alive. The printed answer 'Robotics spacecraft' names no flight.

items.s:
Match the nomenclature used for space travellers in different countries/continent

A. Russia
B. USA
C. China
D. Germany
i. Astronaut ii. Taikonaut iii. Spationaut iv. Cosmonaut
items.x:
Official key: Germany – Spationaut. Strictly: 'spationaut' is the French term; Germany uses astronaut.
Russia uses cosmonaut, the USA astronaut and China taikonaut; spationaut (France) is left for Germany, so option 2 is the only possible match.

items.s: Who has launched a solar calculator app that can calculate the benefits of installing solar panels in different regions of the country?
items.x: ISRO (Space Applications Centre) released a solar calculator app that uses satellite data to estimate solar-panel benefits across India.

items.s: As per satellite images released by the National Remote Sensing Centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation, Joshimath in Uttarakhand sank at a pace of ____ cm in 12 days between December 2022 and January 2023.
items.x: NRSC Cartosat-2S images showed Joshimath sank 5.4 cm in 12 days (27 Dec 2022 - 8 Jan 2023), against about 9 cm over April-November 2022.

items.s:
This question consists of two statements -
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R). Answer the question selecting the appropriate option given below:
Assertion (A): GIS technology has been vital for emergency preparedness through planning & execution.
Reason (R): GIS technology has improved certain extended limits like environmental understanding, strategic decision making monitoring of climate change impact, and ascertaining future risks.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are false
items.x: GIS helps emergency preparedness because it maps risk, monitors climate impacts and supports strategic decisions, so R explains A. (Off-topic: GIS application.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to telehealth?
o: Cell phones, mobile devices and PCs are helping connect patients with their practitioners
Doctor on Demand and Now Clinic are mobile apps for telehealth
Health insurance industry's major players offer some form of telehealth in their health coverage
Telehealth option is available only in the developed countries
items.x: Telehealth is used worldwide, including in India (e.g. eSanjeevani), so 'available only in developed countries' is the incorrect statement.

items.s: Akash missile is developed and produced by
items.x: Akash, the medium-range SAM of the IGMDP, was developed by DRDO and is produced by Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL, Hyderabad), with BEL for the radars.

items.s:
Which of the following are related to Agni-V missile?

A. Intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM)

B. Solid fuelled ballistic missile

C. Four stage missile

D. Air to surface launchable missile
Choose the correct answer:
items.x: Agni-V is a solid-fuelled surface-to-surface ballistic missile of 5,000 km+ (often called ICBM), so A and B; it has three stages (not four) and is not air-launched.

items.s: AGNI-V Missile was launched on
items.x: Agni-V was first test-fired on 19 April 2012 from Wheeler (Abdul Kalam) Island, Odisha.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III ANM/Ward Health Secreta
items.s: Recently Mission Shakti was conducted. Which of the following Organisations conducted the test?
items.x: Mission Shakti, India's first anti-satellite test (27 March 2019), was conducted by DRDO, destroying Microsat-R at about 300 km. ISRO only built the target satellite; DRDL is a DRDO lab, not the organisation.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: What is the name of the Medium Range Surface to Air Missile jointly developed by India and Israel?
items.x: Barak-8 (MRSAM) is the medium-range surface-to-air missile developed jointly by DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries. BrahMos is India-Russia, Pinaka a rocket launcher.

items.s:
India successfully conducted maiden flight-test of Phase-II ballistic missile defence interceptor AD-1 missile off Odisha Coast in November 2022.
Which of the following statements is/are correct in this context?

I. This test was conducted by DRDO

II. This test was conducted at the APJ Abdul Kalam Island
items.x: The Phase-II BMD interceptor AD-1 had its maiden flight test on 2 November 2022, conducted by DRDO from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha, so both statements are correct.

items.s: India is the ____ nation in the world to have a nuclear powered attack submarine.
items.x: With INS Chakra (leased Akula-II, 2012) India became the sixth nation to operate a nuclear-powered submarine, after the US, Russia, the UK, France and China.

items.src: Technical Assistants (Hydrology) in Ground Water Sub-Service
items.s: Which was the third country in the world to hold S-400 missiles after Russia and Belarus?
items.x: China was the first foreign buyer of the Russian S-400 (contract 2014-15, deliveries from 2018); Turkey and India followed. The printed key is kept, though Belarus's own S-400 holding is poorly documented.

items.s: In the following, which is an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle used by Indian Army?
items.x: Heron is the Israeli-made medium-altitude long-endurance UAV used by the Indian Army (and IAF, Navy). Sparrow, Stork and Eagle are not Army UAVs.

items.s: 'Eye in the sky' is the name given to:
o: AWACS-Airborne Early Warning and Control System
