items.x: AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) aircraft are called the "eye in the sky" because their rotating radar watches a wide airspace. Sukhoi and MiG are fighters and Agni-III is a missile.

items.s: Choose the correct match (Army - Navy - Airforce)
o: Major-General - Rear Admiral - Air Vice Marshal
items.x: Major-General (Army) = Rear Admiral (Navy) = Air Vice Marshal (IAF). The others are mismatched: Captain = Lieutenant = Flight Lieutenant, Major = Lieutenant Commander = Squadron Leader, Colonel = Captain = Group Captain.

items.s: In August 2022 Modern equipment was supplied to Indian Army. Nipun is one of them. It is a
items.x: "Nipun", handed over to the Army in August 2022, is an indigenous anti-personnel mine (developed by ARDE/HEMRL with industry) – not a helicopter, missile or thermal imager.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Section Officer (ASO) Mains General Studies
items.s: Which of the following Water Jet Fast Attack Craft (WJFAC) ship was commissioned into Indian Navy in September, 2017?
items.x: INS Tarasa, the last of the four Car Nicobar-class follow-on Water Jet Fast Attack Craft built by GRSE Kolkata, was commissioned in September 2017 at Mumbai. Tihayu (Oct 2016), Tillanchang (Mar 2017) and Tarmugli (May 2016) came earlier.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: Name of the Water Jet Fast Attack Craft commissioned by Indian Navy in October, 2016?
items.x: INS Tihayu, a Water Jet Fast Attack Craft built by GRSE, was commissioned at Visakhapatnam in October 2016; Tarmugli was commissioned in May 2016.

items.s: India's INS Virat represented India in the International Fleet Review during 15-20 February, 2001. Britain was represented by
items.x: At India's first International Fleet Review (Mumbai, February 2001) the Royal Navy was represented by the frigate HMS Cumberland. HMAS Darwin is Australian, HMS Hermes had become India's INS Viraat, and there is no 'HMS Random'.

items.s: INS Trishul acquired by the Indian Navy in 2003 has been built by:
items.x: INS Trishul (F43) is a Talwar-class stealth frigate built in Russia (Baltic Shipyard, St Petersburg) and commissioned in 2003.

items.s: Which of the following is named 'Gajraj'?
items.x: 'Gajraj' is the IAF name of the Ilyushin IL-76 heavy transport aircraft; MiG-27 = Bahadur, Jaguar = Shamsher, Mirage 2000 = Vajra.

items.s: Which one of the following is a decommissioned aircraft carrier?
items.x: INS Viraat (ex-HMS Hermes) was an aircraft carrier decommissioned in March 2017; INS Rajput was a destroyer, INS Chakra a nuclear submarine and INS Khanderi a submarine.

items.s: When India and Russia signed an agreement in Moscow in January 2003, which of the following did Russia give free to India as a gift?
items.x: Russia offered the carrier Admiral Gorshkov (now INS Vikramaditya) free, with India paying for its refit and MiG-29Ks; the deal was signed in January 2004.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
items.s: Radar is used to
items.x: Radar (Radio Detection And Ranging) detects and tracks objects, giving their range, direction and speed – not only distance or frequency.

items.s: AWACS is an:
o: air-based long-range radar surveillance and control system for air defence
instrument to measure wind speed in snow covered regions
air to air guided 2nd generation missile for air defence
items.x: AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) is a large airborne long-range radar surveillance and control system, e.g. India's IL-76-based Phalcon.

items.s: What is the meaning of 'Sea-dog' in Navy terminology?
o: A variety of dog lives in the sea
items.x: 'Sea-dog' is navy slang for an old, experienced sailor, not a dog or a captain.

items.s: This institution has successfully tested 'Abhyas', a pilotless aircraft.
items.x: 'Abhyas', a High-speed Expendable Aerial Target (pilotless target aircraft), was developed and tested by DRDO (ADE Bengaluru).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: Dassault Aviation is a firm located in:
items.x: Dassault Aviation, maker of the Rafale and Mirage fighters, is a French firm based in Paris.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: The recently launched INS Khanderi Submarine is built in collaboration with?
items.x: INS Khanderi is the second Kalvari-class (Scorpene) submarine, built by Mazagon Dock with France's Naval Group (DCNS).

items.s: The Indian Military Academy is located at
items.x: The Indian Military Academy (1932) is at Dehradun, Uttarakhand. (Defence item, moved.)

items.s: Naval Hydrographic Office is located at
items.x: The (Naval) National Hydrographic Office of the Indian Navy is at Dehradun.

items.src: Common GS for IFS, APLIS, ATT 2012
items.s: Indian Military Academy is at
items.x: The Indian Military Academy is at Dehradun. Wellington has the Defence Services Staff College, and Khadakwasla the National Defence Academy.

items.s: On 10th January 2023, the three procurement proposals were approved by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) headed by the Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at a total cost of Rs. 4,276 crores. Which one of the following was not in the list of procurement.
o: Brahmos Launcher and Fire Control System
items.x: On 10 January 2023 the DAC approved HELINA anti-tank missiles, VSHORADS (IR homing) missile systems and BrahMos launchers with fire-control systems (Rs 4,276 crore). Advanced Heron drones were not on that list.

items.s: Aerospace industry in Hyderabad located at
items.x: Adibatla (Ranga Reddy district) hosts Hyderabad's aerospace SEZ, with Tata's aero-structure units (Tata-Sikorsky, Tata-Lockheed).

items.s: In which place the first Indian Defence Industrial Park is proposed?
items.x: India's first Defence Industrial Park was set up by KINFRA at Ottapalam (Palakkad), Kerala.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s:
A: As per India Energy Outlook 2021 published by International Energy Agency (IEA), India has been ranked the third largest primary energy consumer in the world.
R: This was because the Government of India has allowed 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) in many segments of the sector, including natural gas, petroleum products and refineries, among others.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: IEA's India Energy Outlook 2021 ranked India the third-largest primary energy consumer. 100% FDI is allowed in many energy segments, but that does not explain the consumption rank, which comes from population and growth.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: As of 01.04.2023, what were the estimated reserves of crude oil in India?
items.x: The MoSPI estimate of India's crude oil reserves is 651.77 million tonnes (shown as of 01.04.2023 in Energy Statistics 2024; the 2023 edition dates the same figure 01.04.2022). (Moved to 5:54.)

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: After reorganization, how much percentage of equity of Singareni Collieries Company Ltd is allotted to Government of AP?
items.x: Under the Twelfth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, SCCL's equity is 51% Telangana and 49% Government of India, so AP got nil.

items.s: Which coal is associated with the Godavari valley?
items.x: The Godavari valley coalfields are associated with Singareni, which is now in Telangana. The historical observation was that Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.

items.s: Which body compiles coal statistics, monitors captive coal blocks and hears objections on acquisition of coal-bearing land?
items.x: The Coal Controller's Organisation performs all three functions.

items.s: Where is India's first coal-gasification fertiliser plant planned?
items.x: The first coal-gasification fertiliser plant is planned at Talcher, Odisha; JSPL's Angul plant is the only commercial-scale gasification plant.

items.s: What is India's rank among the world's coal producers?
items.x: India is the second-largest producer (about 10%) after China (51%); its output was 1,040.08 MT in FY 2025-26.

items.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment
items.x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which enabled auction-based allocation.

items.s: In which year did commercial mining auctions for coal begin?
items.x: Commercial mining auctions for coal began in 2020.

items.s: In which year was Coal India Ltd established?
items.x: Coal India Ltd was set up in 1975, after coking coal (1971-72) and non-coking coal (1973) were nationalised.

items.s: How is the equity of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) held?
items.x: SCCL is a joint company of Telangana and the Centre: Telangana holds 51% and the Government of India 49%. Reversing the split is the usual trap. It is neither wholly State-owned nor majority Central.

items.s: What does the syngas produced by coal gasification mainly contain?
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide
items.x: Coal gasification produces syngas containing carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide.

items.s: In which year was coking coal nationalised in India?
items.x: Coking coal mines were nationalised in 1971-72 and non-coking mines in 1973; Coal India came in 1975.

items.s: Which of the following lignite field - State pairs is correctly matched?
items.x: Neyveli lignite is in Tamil Nadu and Barmer lignite is in Rajasthan.

items.s: In January 2023, The Indian Oil Corporation started the export of its special aviation fuel for small aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles (drones), AVGAS 100 LL. The first consignment was exported to which country?
items.x: IOC's first export consignment of AVGAS 100 LL (Jan 2023) went to Papua New Guinea.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: As of 31.03.2023, what was the total number of crude oil refineries in India?
items.x:
23 refineries was the count on 31.03.2023 — now 24 refineries (PPAC installed refinery capacity as on 1 April 2026)
PPAC's refinery table with capacity as on 01.04.2023 lists 23 refineries (installed capacity 253.9 MMTPA) – IOCL 9, CPCL 2, BPCL 3, NRL, ONGC Tatipaka, MRPL, HPCL 2, HMEL Bathinda, RIL 2 and Nayara Vadinar. (now 24 refineries as on 1 April 2026 – PPAC.)

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: The starting current value of a DG set should not exceed what % of full load capacity of the DG set?
items.x: The printed answer is 200%: the motor starting current drawn from a DG set should not exceed about twice its full-load current, or the voltage dips badly.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Auxiliary power consumption of a DG set at full load in its operating capacity is about
items.x: A diesel-generator set's own auxiliary consumption at full load is small, about 1-2% of its output (engineering item, not nuclear).

items.s:
Match the given thermal power plants with the state where they are situated.
Thermal power plants State

I. Barauni Thermal Power plant
a. Bihar

II. Gandhinagar Thermal Power plant
b. Gujarat

III. Kota Thermal Power plant
c. Rajasthan
items.x: Barauni – Bihar, Gandhinagar – Gujarat, Kota – Rajasthan.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Maximum permissible earth resistance for buildings is
items.x: Printed key: 8 ohms as the maximum permissible earth resistance for buildings (power stations 0.5 Ω, major substations 1 Ω). This could not be verified against IS 3043.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: The rating required for a DG set with 500 kW connected load and with diversity factor of 1.5, 80% loading and 0.8 power factor is
items.x: Maximum demand = 500 kW ÷ 1.5 = 333 kW. At 80% loading the rating = 333 ÷ 0.8 = 417 kW, and at 0.8 pf that is 417 ÷ 0.8 ≈ 520 kVA.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: Who among the following is a member of Atomic Energy Commission?
items.x: Printed key kept: Dr. P. Rama Rao (metallurgist, ex-DST Secretary) served on the Atomic Energy Commission.

items.s: India made its first atomic explosion in
items.x: India's first nuclear explosion, 'Smiling Buddha', was at Pokhran on 18 May 1974.

items.s: Kalpakkam is in the news because
o: a triple murder took place there
its atomic power plant went critical
gold was struck in the mines.
items.x: Kalpakkam was in the news in 1983-84 because its atomic power plant (Madras Atomic Power Station, unit 1) went critical in 1983.

items.s: Who is the author of 'Nuclear Reactor Time Bomb' :
items.x: 'Nuclear Reactor Time Bomb' is by the Japanese writer Takashi Hirose (2010), an anti-nuclear critic.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: As of August 2024, how many commercial nuclear power reactors are operational in India?
items.x: NPCIL ran 24 commercial power reactors in 2024; the count is still 24 operating units (8.78 GW) in September 2026.

items.s:
"Parmanu Tech 2019" conference, which was held in February 2019 in India, was organised by

a. Ministry of External Affairs

b. Ministry of Defence

c. Ministry of Science and Technology

d. Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)
Choose the correct answer :
items.x: ParmanuTech 2019 (6 Feb 2019, Pravasi Bharatiya Kendra, New Delhi) was organised by the Department of Atomic Energy in consultation with the Ministry of External Affairs, to show DAE technologies to diplomats; Defence and S&T ministries were not organisers.

items.s: Kudankulam Atomic Power Project in Tamil Nadu is being set up with the assistance of which country?
items.x: Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu) is being built with Russian VVER-1000 reactors under the 1988 India-USSR agreement.

items.s: The State which has highest Atomic Reactors in the country is
items.x:
Printed key: Tamil Nadu. Strictly: Rajasthan (Rawatbhata) has the most power reactors; among the options Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu each had about four in 2016 (general knowledge, not checked).
The printed key is Tamil Nadu: in 2016 it had Kudankulam and Madras (Kalpakkam) reactors, plus the Kalpakkam research and fast-breeder reactors. Strictly, Rajasthan (RAPS, Rawatbhata) has the most power reactors, but it is not offered.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Which of the following options is correct for the given assertion and reason?
Assertion (A): India is actively promoting the use of renewable energy sources such as wind, hydro, solar, geothermal, bio, and tidal power to supplement fossil fuel-based electricity generation.
Reason (R): Renewable energy sources are sustainable and environmentally friendly unlike non-renewable sources like coal, oil, and natural gas, which are finite and contribute to environmental pollution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
items.x: Both are true and R explains A: India pushes renewables because they are sustainable and clean, unlike finite, polluting fossil fuels. (Moved to 5:64.)

items.s: Unlike traditional asphalt, bio-asphalt is not based on fossil fuels. 2. Bio-asphalt can be made from non-renewable resources. 3. Bi-asphalt can be made from non-organic waste materials. 4. It is eco-friendly to use bio-asphalt for surfacing of the roads. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Bio-asphalt is made from renewable organic matter (vegetable oils, molasses, lignin, waste), not fossil fuels, and it is eco-friendly for road surfacing. Statement 2 (non-renewable resources) is false. Statement 3 says 'non-organic' here, but the original UPSC wording is 'organic', which is why the official key is 1, 3 and 4.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which of the following statements is not correct about 'Mangal Turbine'?
o: The turbine provides clean alternative source of energy.
It requires low water heads upto 1 meter.
Flow of wind is the source of energy for turbine.
items.x: The Mangal Turbine (Mangal Singh, Lalitpur, UP) is driven by flowing water at low heads, not by wind. It is clean and eco-friendly and lifts water for irrigation.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of bio-mass energy source?
items.x: Atomic energy comes from uranium nuclei, not from biomass. Wood and gobar gas are biomass sources, and coal is fossilised plant matter.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: What does the Waste to Energy Programme focus on?
o: Producing energy from urban, industrial and agricultural wastes/residues
Enhancing the efficiency of hydroelectric power plants
Promoting the use of natural gas for power generation
items.x: MNRE's Waste to Energy Programme supports plants that recover energy (biogas, bio-CNG, power) from urban, industrial and agricultural wastes and residues; it is not about fossil fuels, hydro efficiency or natural gas.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The main constituents of Bio-gas or Gobar gas are
items.x: Biogas is mainly methane (50-65%) with carbon dioxide (35-50%) and traces of hydrogen, nitrogen and hydrogen sulphide, so 'all of the above' is the intended answer; methane alone is only the main constituent.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Which is the major constituent of Gobar Gas?
items.x: Gobar gas (biogas) is mainly methane (50-65%), with CO2 next; ethane, butane and H2S are not the major constituent.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Leading ethanol producing country
items.x: The USA is the world's leading ethanol producer (mainly corn ethanol), ahead of Brazil (sugarcane). India is third.

items.s: India's first ever bio-fuel flight facilitated by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research flew between
items.x: India's first biofuel-powered flight (SpiceJet, August 2018, fuel from CSIR-IIP) flew from Dehradun to Delhi.

items.s:
Microbial fuel cells are considered a source of sustainable energy. Why?

A. They use living organisms as catalyst to generate electricity from certain substrates.

B. They use a variety of inorganic materials as substrates.

C. They can be installed in waste water treatment plants to cleanse water and produce electricity
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x:
UPSC/coaching key: (c) A and C only. Some books (e.g. the printed key here) give (d), since a few inorganic substrates such as sulphides can be used.
Statements A and C are correct: MFCs use living microbes as catalysts and can be fitted in waste-water plants to clean water while making electricity. Statement B is wrong as a reason because MFCs mainly run on organic substrates. (Moved to 5:67.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: The wastes discharged from a biogas plant are reused as
items.x: The slurry (digestate) left after biogas is made is a nutrient-rich organic manure, so it is reused as fertilizer for crops. It is not used as cooking fuel (the gas is), animal feed or building material.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: Which of the following is the main focus of the SATAT initiative launched by the Government of India?
items.x: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, 2018) promotes setting up compressed bio-gas (CBG) plants and selling CBG as a transport fuel; GOBARdhan builds on it. It is not a solar, EV or refinery scheme. (Moved to book 5, other renewables/biofuels.)

items.s: Which company unveiled India's first H2ICE technology for heavy duty trucks in 2023 ?
items.x: Reliance Industries, with Ashok Leyland, unveiled India's first hydrogen internal-combustion-engine (H2ICE) heavy-duty truck at India Energy Week, Bengaluru, on 6 Feb 2023.

items.s: When an environmentally sensitive person driving a car stops at a traffic light, the person would?
o: Keeps the engine on in neutral gear
Keeps the engine in gear, uses the brake and goes fast on green signal so that others would spend less fuel in waiting
Switches off the engine and turns on till green light
Does not stop at any signal because waiting and starting wastes fuel
items.x: An environmentally sensitive driver switches the engine off while waiting at a red light, saving fuel and cutting emissions; idling or never stopping is wasteful or unsafe.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: The maximum permissible percentage unbalance in phase loads on DG sets is
items.x: Load on the phases of a DG set should be balanced; the maximum permissible unbalance between phase loads is about 10% (energy-audit guidance).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Which state government has decided to launch a project 'Chullah' for smokeless kitchens?
items.x: Maharashtra announced a pilot 'Chullah-free and smoke-free Maharashtra' project in its 2019 budget for women not covered by Ujjwala or other LPG schemes. (Clean-cooking item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Forests and lakes are best classified as examples of:
items.x: Forests and lakes are natural ecosystems (terrestrial and aquatic); croplands and gardens are man-made ones.

items.s:
Match
List-I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below.
List - I (Biotic factor):

a. Humans

b. Saprotrophs

c. Reptiles

d. Camel
List - II (Characteristic feature):

I. Recycling nutrients

II. Top order heterotrophs in food chain

III. Less urinating animal

IV. Stenothermal
items.x: Humans – top-order heterotrophs, saprotrophs – recycle nutrients, reptiles – stenothermal (narrow temperature tolerance), camel – passes little urine. Off-topic, moved.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Out of the sunlight falling on leaves of green plants in the terrestrial ecosystem, how much percentage is captured by them (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: Green plants capture only about 1% of the sunlight falling on them for photosynthesis.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: What is the term used to describe dead animal matter, which may also be actively decaying?
items.x: Carrion is the dead and decaying flesh of animals (eaten by scavengers such as vultures). Curare is a plant poison, benthos are bottom organisms, chitin is a polysaccharide. Off-topic (ecology), moved to book 5.

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: The relation between bees and flowers is?
items.x: Bees get nectar and pollen while flowers get pollinated – both gain, so the relation is symbiotic (mutualism), not parasitic or predatory.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: The transition area between two biomes is known as
items.x: An ecotone is the junction or transition zone between two biomes, e.g. mangroves and estuaries.

items.s: Which of the following organisms perform waggle dance for others of their kin to indicate the direction and the distance to a source of their food?
items.x: Honeybees perform the waggle dance to show direction and distance of food (Karl von Frisch).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: What is the primary reason for bird migration?
o: Search for food and suitable breeding grounds
items.x: Birds migrate mainly in search of food and suitable breeding grounds as seasons change; escaping predators or finding nesting material are not the primary reason. (Ecology item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural resource?
items.x: Concrete is a man-made material; coal, cow dung and petrol (from crude oil) are natural resources.

items.s: In lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, ____ live together.
o: More than one of the above
items.x: A lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga (the chlorophyll-containing partner) and a fungus. (Off-topic: ecology.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: What is the role of ecological succession in an ecosystem?
o: To show the energy flow through different trophic levels
To depict the rate of biomass production
To illustrate the process of decomposition
To describe the gradual process of change in the species structure of an ecosystem
items.x: Ecological succession is the gradual change in the species structure of an ecosystem over time. It is not about energy flow, biomass production or decomposition.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What does succession describe in an ecological community?
o: The gradual change in species composition over time after a disturbance
The daily movement of organisms within an ecosystem
The complete extinction of species in an area
items.x: Succession is the gradual change in species composition over time, for example after a disturbance. It is not migration, daily movement or extinction.

items.s:
Which of the following are the consequences of deforestation?

I. It enhanced carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere

II. It causes loss of biodiversity

III. It disturbs hydrologic cycle
items.x: Deforestation raises atmospheric CO2, causes biodiversity loss and disturbs the hydrological cycle – all three.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Wasteland refers to land with what percentage of productivity?
items.x: Wasteland is commonly defined as land whose biomass/economic productivity is less than 20% of its potential (degraded land lying unused). 25-35% are not the usual threshold.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Large-scale forest die-offs take place due to the biotic agent
items.x: Large-scale forest die-offs are driven by biotic agents such as insect pests and their pathogens (bark beetles, defoliators). Age, chemicals and water deficiency are not biotic. (Off-topic: forest ecology.)

items.s: In which of the following year, the Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in India?
items.x: The Environment (Protection) Act, an umbrella law under Article 253 prompted by the Stockholm Conference and the Bhopal tragedy, was enacted in 1986.

items.s: In which year was the Environment (Protection) Act of India enacted?
items.x: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986, after the Bhopal gas tragedy, to implement the Stockholm decisions.

items.s: Which of the following Ministry in India is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the Central Government for the planning, promotion, co-ordination and overseeing the implementation of India's environmental and forestry policies and programmes?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is the nodal agency for planning, promoting, coordinating and overseeing India's environmental and forestry policies and programmes.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
items.s: First International Earth Summit was held at
items.x: The first Earth Summit (UN Conference on Environment and Development, June 1992) was held at Rio de Janeiro; it adopted the UNFCCC, CBD and Agenda 21. Paris hosted COP21 (2015), not the Earth Summit.

items.s:
Which of the following statements is correct:

(a) Renewable resources should provide a sustainable yield (the rate of harvest should not exceed the rate of regeneration).

(b) For non-renewable resources, there should be equivalent development of renewable substitutes.

(c) Waste generation should exceed the assimilative capacity of the environment.
items.x: The sustainability rules say harvest should not exceed regeneration (a) and non-renewables need renewable substitutes (b). Waste must stay WITHIN the assimilative capacity, so (c) is wrong.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
Match each strategy for sustainable development with its corresponding example of implementation.
Strategies:
A. Renewable Energy
B. Sustainable Agriculture
C. Waste Reduction
Implementation:
1. Crop Rotation
2. Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
3. Solar Power
items.x: Renewable energy – solar power; sustainable agriculture – crop rotation; waste reduction – reduce, reuse, recycle: A-3, B-1, C-2.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
items.s: Planting trees and reducing plastic use mainly support which pillar of sustainable development?
items.x: Planting trees and cutting plastic protect natural resources – the environmental pillar of sustainable development (the others are economic and social).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: Which of the following is an essential principle of sustainable development highlighted by international conventions?
o: Increasing the use of fossil fuels to boost economic growth
Prioritizing present economic needs over future environmental concerns
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions to ensure environmental sustainability
Ignoring biodiversity conservation in favor of urban expansion
items.x: Reducing GHG emissions for environmental sustainability is a principle in international conventions; the rest put growth before environment.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
items.s: Which document is credited with first defining "Sustainable Development"?
items.x: The Brundtland Report 'Our Common Future' (1987) gave the classic definition of sustainable development. Paris, Montreal and Kyoto are climate or ozone treaties.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of sustainable development?
o: Setting up of rain water harvesting systems
items.x: Unplanned waste generation wastes resources and pollutes, so it is not sustainable development. Crop rotation, solar energy and rainwater harvesting are sustainable practices. (Moved to 5:80.)

items.s: Which of the following has constructed the Sustainable Development Index for different states of India?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.x: The SDG India Index, which ranks States and UTs on sustainable development, is built by NITI Aayog (with MoSPI and the UN in India).

items.s: One of the United Nation's Millennium goals is to eradicate extreme poverty and hunger globally; today more than half of the extreme poor in the world live in
items.x: By World Bank estimates, more than half of the world's extremely poor live in Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Sustainable Development Goals apply to
items.x: The SDGs (2030 Agenda, 2015) are universal and apply to all countries, developed and developing alike, unlike the MDGs, which targeted developing countries.

items.s: Which of the following is not true about SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALs of UNO?
o: They encourage promotion of health, well being and prosperity for all
They promote sustainable cities and infrastructure.
They are legally binding on all member countries of UNO
items.x: The SDGs are a voluntary political agenda (2030 Agenda) and are not legally binding on UN members. They do promote health, innovation (Goal 9) and sustainable cities (Goal 11).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
items.s: Which one of the following is one of the 17 sustainable development goals of UNO?
o: Reduce carbon emissions by 90 percent during the period of 15 years
Reduce global warming by 3 degrees centigrade in 5 years
Replace all appliances using green house gases in 15 years
Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts
items.x: SDG 13 is 'Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts'. The other options are invented numerical targets that are not SDGs.

items.s: Which is not part of the UNO's SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALs on ecosystems?
items.x: SDG 15 (Life on Land) asks to use ecosystems sustainably, halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss; it does not ask to halt biotechnology.

items.s: What are the two least performing states in India in the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals during the year 2020-21?
items.x: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2020-21, Bihar and Jharkhand were the two lowest-scoring States.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s: Which of the following policies and practices is most effective in achieving Sustainable Development?
o: Subsidizing fossil fuel industries to ensure lower energy costs for consumers.
Implementing carbon pricing to incentivize renewable energy investments.
Encouraging the use of single-use plastics to boost economic growth.
Promoting deforestation to create more land for agricultural activities.
items.x: Carbon pricing makes polluters pay and pushes investment into renewables; fossil subsidies, single-use plastics and deforestation work against sustainable development.

items.s: What is the formula of Ozone?
items.x: Ozone is triatomic oxygen, O3; O2 is ordinary oxygen and O4/O5 are not ozone.

items.s: — is/are responsible for ozone depletion.
items.x: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine in the stratosphere that destroys ozone; H2O2, CO and SO2 are not the ozone-depleting substances.

items.s: Which of the following refrigerants is the least toxic?
items.x: CFCs (freons) are non-toxic, non-flammable refrigerants (their problem is ozone depletion); SO2, methyl chloride and ammonia are toxic.

items.s: Which of the following chemicals, also known as C8, has been banned at the 9th Stockholm Convention held in Geneva?
items.x: COP-9 of the Stockholm Convention (Geneva, 2019) listed perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA, 'C8', used in making Teflon) in Annex A for elimination, with some exemptions, along with dicofol.

items.s: Which of the following is not responsible for the increase in the biodiversity of an ecosystem?
items.x: High productivity, intermediate disturbance and greater ecosystem age all raise biodiversity. Fewer trophic levels reduce it, so that is the factor not responsible.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which of the following is not a type of biodiversity?
items.x: The three levels of biodiversity are genetic, species and ecosystem diversity; 'population biodiversity' is not a recognised type.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Biodiversity is valued for
items.x: Biodiversity preserves ecological processes, maintains hydrological cycles and supports global life-support systems, so all of the above.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains P
items.s: What is Alpha Diversity?
o: Species biodiversity between two habitats (local communities)
Species biodiversity within a habitat (local community)
items.x: Alpha diversity is species diversity within one habitat or community. Diversity between habitats is beta, and over a whole region or biome is gamma diversity.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: Out of the recognized species on earth insects constitute approximately about?
items.x: About 1 million of the roughly 1.8 million described species are insects, so insects make up about half (50%) of recognised species. NCERT says insects are over 70% of animal species, not of all species.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP BC Wel
items.s: Approximately how much percentage of world's species live in tropical rain forests?
items.x: Tropical rainforests cover under 10% of land but hold about half (often quoted 50%+) of the world's species. 20% and 30% understate it.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Cissus Quadrangularis (Nalleru) is used as medicine for
items.x: Nalleru (Cissus quadrangularis, 'bone setter') is used in traditional medicine for bone health and fracture healing.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: How many quadrats of 20 x 20 square metres can be taken from an area of 20 hectares if the sampling intensity is 1%?
items.x: 20 ha = 2,00,000 m²; 1% sampling intensity = 2,000 m² to be sampled; one 20 m × 20 m quadrat = 400 m², so 2,000 ÷ 400 = 5 quadrats. 4 would sample only 0.8% of the area.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What is the term used to refer to the population value of a characteristic?
items.x: A parameter is a numerical characteristic of the whole population (e.g. population mean μ); a statistic is the corresponding value computed from a sample, and an estimate is a statistic's value used to approximate the parameter. Probability is unrelated to this definition.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The hot spots of biodiversity are characterized by
o: Low population, low endemicity and low threat of extinction
Low population, low endemicity and higher threat of extinction
Rich population, high endemicity and low threat of extinction
Rich population, high endemicity and high threat of extinction
items.x: Biodiversity hotspots have rich species populations, high endemism and a high threat of habitat loss and extinction. (Moved to the hotspots row.)

items.s: Which of the following is NOT an extinct species?
items.x: The red panda is endangered but alive (Eastern Himalaya). The dodo, the West African black rhino (2011) and the Chinese river dolphin (baiji, functionally extinct 2006) are extinct.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Read the
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) carefully, and select the correct option.
(A): Parthenium hysterophorus are considered the second largest threat to biodiversity.
(R): Invasive species are a threat to biodiversity.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A).
items.x:
APPSC key: (A) both true, R explains A. Strictly: 'second largest threat' is said of invasive species as a group; Parthenium is only one of them.
Invasive alien species are the second-biggest cause of biodiversity loss after habitat destruction, and Parthenium (congress grass) is one of India's worst invasive weeds; so A and R are true and R explains A.

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Which organization publishes data about rare and extinct species?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
items.x: The IUCN publishes the Red List and Red Data Book on threatened, rare and extinct species. UNEP and the other options do not.

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: The 'Red Data Book' is a document established by the
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
items.x: The Red Data Book is compiled by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), which keeps the Red List of threatened species.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Which human activity affects biodiversity the most?
items.x: Deforestation destroys whole habitats, so it affects biodiversity the most; afforestation and organic farming help it. (Off-topic: biodiversity loss.)

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, Technical Asst. (Hydrog
items.s: Which of the following National Park is situated in Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
items.x: Campbell Bay NP (1992) is on Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Dachigam is in J&K, Gir in Gujarat and Guindy in Chennai.

items.s: Which of the following lakes is situated between the deltas of the Godavari and Krishna rivers?
items.x: Kolleru Lake, AP's Ramsar site, lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; Pulicat is on the AP–TN border, Wular in J&K, Vembanad in Kerala.

items.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
items.s: Which of these lakes is in Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Kolleru Lake is in Andhra Pradesh; Loktak is in Manipur, Vembanad in Kerala and Chilika in Odisha.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Select the correct match Wild Life Sanctuary areas in Andhra Pradesh
items.x: Rollapadu Wildlife (Bird) Sanctuary is in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, AP, known for the Great Indian Bustard. (AP protected-area item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: Which of the following statements regarding the India Rhino Vision (IRV) 2020 is INCORRECT?
o: Its vision was to build a wild population of 3,000 Greater One Horned Rhinos by 2020.
It was launched in partnership with WWF India and the International Rhino Foundation.
It was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
IRV achieved its target of increasing the population of Greater One Horned Rhinos in Assam to 3,000 by 2020.
items.x: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was adopted in 2005 by the Assam government (with the Bodoland Territorial Council) in partnership with WWF India and the International Rhino Foundation, not launched by MoEFCC. It aimed at 3,000 wild rhinos in 7 PAs of Assam by 2020, a target believed to have been met.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: Which of the following statements about the Wildlife (Protection) Act (WPA), 1972, is correct?
o: The Act was amended in 2010 to establish the NTCA.
The 2022 amendment to the Act reduced the number of Schedules from six to five.
The 1972 Act covers animal species, not plant species.
The WPA 1972 established the Central Zoo Authority, which regulates the management of zoos in India.
items.x: The Central Zoo Authority was created under the WPA 1972 by its 1991 amendment, so D is correct. NTCA came in 2006, not 2010. The 2022 amendment cut the schedules to four, not five. The Act also covers plants (Schedule VI, 1991). (WPA item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: Under the Vanam-Manam Programme in total how many trees are proposed to be planted?
items.x:
the drive's yearly targets changed (2 crore in 2016, 1 crore in 2017, 25 crore in 2018-19) — the 1 crore (10 million) figure is the 2017 target (Hans India, 30 Jun 2017).
For the 2017 Vanam-Manam drive the AP government targeted one crore (10 million) saplings across the State, as part of its goal of 50% green cover by 2029.

items.s:
Choose the correct option based on the statements below:
Statement I: Deforestation leads to loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services
Statement II: The government of India has established community-based forest management systems to involve local communities in the conservation and management of forest resources.
items.x: Both are true: deforestation causes loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services, and India has community-based forest management (Joint Forest Management, forest rights) to involve local communities. The printed item had no key.

items.s: The Chipko movement, began in Uttarakhand demanded
o: Local Communities should have effective control over natural resources like land, water and forests
Prohibition of liquor that spoils household economy
Stopping of economic exploitation of forests by corporates
items.x: The Chipko villagers demanded that no forest-exploitation contracts be given to outsiders and that local communities have effective control over natural resources like land, water and forests (NCERT Class XII Politics in India since Independence).

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s:
A: Global warming is a gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth's lower atmosphere.
R: Global warming is a result of the increase in greenhouse gases since the industrial revolution.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Global warming is the gradual rise in the average temperature of the lower atmosphere, and it is caused by the rise in greenhouse gases since the Industrial Revolution, so R explains A. (Moved to climate change.)

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: As per recent data, what is the average level of Carbon Dioxide in atmosphere in India (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: Atmospheric CO2 crossed 400 ppm in 2015-16 and is about 420+ ppm now, so 400 ppm is the nearest figure.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: A small change in temperature of the earth does not cause?
o: Starvation of all plants and animals
Melting of ice at the poles
Flooding in some places and drought in other places
items.x: A small rise in Earth's temperature melts polar ice, raises seas and brings floods and droughts. It would not starve all plants and animals. (Off-topic: climate change.)

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC, Tribal Welfare Officers 2017
items.s: Global warming would make the Indian Monsoon
o: It is too early to predict
items.x: Global warming is expected to make the Indian monsoon more erratic and extreme (devastating and unpredictable).

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: What is the main aim of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change?
o: To limit global temperature rise to well below 2° C
items.x: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: The Paris Climate Agreement (2015) mainly aims to
o: Limit global temperature rise to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels
Increase fossil fuel production for energy security
items.x: Paris (2015) aims to keep the temperature rise well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.

items.s:
Which is/are correct about the goal/goals of Paris Climate Agreement?

A. To hold "the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels".

B. To pursue efforts "to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels".
items.x: Both are Paris goals: well below 2°C (A) and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C (B).

items.s: In the COP 21 convention held at Paris, it was proposed to limit the level of global warming to
o: 3 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
1 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
2 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
4 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
items.x: COP21 Paris set the limit at 2°C above pre-industrial levels (well below 2°C, aiming for 1.5°C).

items.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: Which of the following was the first country to declare the climate emergency?
items.x: The UK Parliament was the first national parliament to declare a climate emergency, on 1 May 2019.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s:
A: A UN Conference on Climate Change, held in Kyoto, Japan, in 1997 called for reductions in emissions of greenhouse gases by industrialised nations.
R: Montreal Protocol banned the use of chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) compounds, as well as other ozone-depleting chemicals such as carbon tetrachloride, trichloroethane (also known as methyl chloroform), and bromine compounds are known as halons.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Both statements are true: Kyoto (1997) set emission cuts for industrialised nations, and the Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs, halons and other ozone-depleting substances. R is about ozone, not greenhouse-gas cuts, so it does not explain A. (Moved to climate initiatives.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Kyoto Protocol deals with
items.x: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) under the UNFCCC sets binding greenhouse-gas cuts for developed countries, so it deals with climate change. Ozone depletion is the Montreal Protocol; biodiversity is the CBD.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary/Mahil
items.s: The Principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities is specially focused on
items.x: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (and Respective Capabilities) is the core equity principle of the UNFCCC climate regime: developed countries take the lead in cutting emissions. India invokes it in climate talks.

items.s: Where was the 2022 United Nations Climate Change Conference, referred as COP-27 held in November, 2022?
items.x: COP27 (November 2022) was held at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. COP28 was in Dubai (UAE) and COP26 in Glasgow (UK).

items.s: 'Kyoto Protocol', which was adopted in 1997, is associated with:
items.x: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, deals with climate change: binding greenhouse-gas cuts for developed countries. It is not about noise, population or general air pollution.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: Where is the head quarters of International Solar Alliance, an Intergovernmental Organization to promote solar energy is located?
items.x: The International Solar Alliance, launched by India and France at COP21 (2015), is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana. It is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: As per recent study by researchers of University of Maryland, India's emissions of the air pollutant sulphur dioxide increased by approximately how much percent since 2007 (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: The 2017 University of Maryland-led study (Scientific Reports, with NASA OMI satellite data) found India's SO2 emissions up about 50% since 2007 while China's fell about 75%. So 50 percent, not 75 or 100.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: As per the WHO report released in May, 2016, which is the worst city in India in terms of air pollution?
items.x: The WHO's May 2016 urban air-quality database ranked Gwalior the most polluted Indian city (2nd in the world after Zabol, Iran), ahead of Allahabad, Patna and Raipur.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which of the following is the principal cause of acid rain?
items.x: Acid rain is caused mainly by high SO2 (with NOx) that forms sulphuric and nitric acids; ozone depletion, UV-B and GHGs are not its cause.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
items.s:
Which of the following is/are the methods to control air pollution?
(i) Setting up of cheaper and faster public transportation systems with better connectivity.
(ii) Devising rules to ensure pooling of private transport.
(iii) Setting up sound-proof infrastructure in the hospitals.
items.x: Cheaper, faster public transport and pooling of private vehicles cut vehicle emissions; sound-proofing hospitals addresses noise, not air pollution, so (i) and (ii).

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: According to reports of Central Pollution Control Board of India, what was the average air quality index (AQI) of Delhi in 2021?
items.x: Printed key: 144. Caution: CAQM/CPCB-based reports give Delhi's 2021 daily-average AQI as about 209 for the whole year, so the 144 figure may refer to a part of the year or a different metric. (AQI item, moved.)

items.s:
Magnetite particles, suspected to cause neurodegenerative problems are generated as environmental pollutants from which of the following?

1. Brakes of motor vehicles

2. Engines of motor vehicles

3. Microwave stoves within homes

4. Power plants

5. Telephone lines
Select the correct answer using the code given below
items.x: Magnetite comes from vehicle brakes, vehicle engines and coal-fired power plants (1, 2, 4); there is no evidence for microwave stoves or telephone lines.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: Out of the given below acids, which one is prominently found in acid rain?
items.x: SO2 from burning coal and oil forms sulphuric acid, the main acid of acid rain; NOx adds nitric acid. Hydrochloric, formic and acetic acids are minor or absent.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: According to Ministry of Environment and Forest, Government of India, between 2006 to 2015 in the lives lost due to the Air pollution, which of the following states had the highest deaths?
items.x: The MoEF reply put acute respiratory infection deaths in 2006-2015 at 35,616, with West Bengal the highest, followed by Andhra Pradesh. Off-topic (environment).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Which is a measure to control air pollution?
items.x: Switching vehicles to CNG, a cleaner fuel, cuts air pollution; deforestation, more vehicles and burning plastic all worsen it.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
items.s: Which of the following is most affected by acid rains?
items.x: Acid rain lowers the pH of poorly buffered lakes and streams, so fish (and the shrimps, snails and mussels they feed on) decline or are eliminated; its effects on birds and mammals are indirect and hard to document. Off-topic (air pollution), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
items.s: According to World Health Organization, how much percentage of the world's population was living in places where the WHO air quality guidelines levels were not met in 2019?
items.x: WHO reported (2022 database update) that 99% of the world's population in 2019 lived where its air-quality guideline levels were not met.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Acid rain occurs when precipitation becomes more acidic than usual, with a pH below 5.6.
Reason (R): Nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) are formed during high-temperature combustion reactions, which later react with water to form nitric acid (HNO3), contributing to acid rain.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
items.x: Rain with pH below 5.6 is acid rain; NOx from high-temperature combustion forms nitric acid in the air, which is one cause of acid rain, so R explains A.

items.src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
items.s: According to recent study of IIT, Mumbai what is the approximate cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015?
items.x: An IIT Bombay study put the economic cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015 at about Rs 70,000 crore. Pollution item, moved.

items.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
items.s: Which was the first State/UT to implement the Odd-Even Scheme to combat air pollution?
items.x: Delhi first ran the odd-even road-rationing scheme in January 2016 to fight air pollution. Off-topic (pollution), moved.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: Which of the following is not a way of reducing air pollution?
o: Going fast to the destination in automobile
Travelling by Bus instead of Car
Using diesel car instead of petrol car
items.x:
No printed key. Strictly, 'going fast to the destination' is not a way of reducing pollution either (fuel use rises at high speed); the diesel option is keyed as the standard textbook point.
Diesel cars emit more NOx and particulates than petrol cars, so switching to diesel does not reduce air pollution; natural gas vehicles and buses instead of cars do.

items.s: Which one of the following is known for cleaning a polluted environment?
items.x: Rain washes particles and soluble gases out of the air (wet deposition), so it cleans a polluted atmosphere. (Moved to 5:99.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: Eutrophication is a
items.at: Process of nutrient accumulation in the water bodies
items.x: Eutrophication is the enrichment of water bodies with nutrients (N, P), which causes algal blooms that deplete oxygen and kill aquatic life.

items.s: IISER Pune developed macro/microporous ionic organic framework in 2023 which can
items.x: IISER Pune (2023) made a macro/microporous ionic organic framework that rapidly traps toxic oxo-anion pollutants (e.g. chromate, arsenate) from water.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: How can improper waste management, especially biomedical and e-waste, indirectly contribute to deforestation and biodiversity loss?
o: By providing organic fertilizers that help forest regeneration
By releasing toxic substances into soil and water, damaging ecosystems and forcing land-use changes like deforestation
By reducing industrial pollution and improving ecosystem balance
By increasing green cover through waste-to-energy plants in forests
items.x: Improperly managed biomedical and e-waste releases toxic substances into soil and water, damaging ecosystems and pushing land-use change. The other options describe benefits, not harm.

items.s: As per Indian State of Forest Report (ISFR)-2015, what is the total carbon stock in forests of India?
items.x: ISFR 2015 put the carbon stock of India's forests at 7,044 million tonnes. (Moved to 5:104.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Which Agency in India ensures implementation of fire cracker safety standards?
items.x: The Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO, under DPIIT) licenses fireworks and enforces their safety standards. (Moved to 5:105.)

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
items.s: Which of the following is not a reason for increasing vulnerability to disasters?
o: Blind faith in beliefs and customs
items.x: Lack of resources, low awareness and blind faith raise vulnerability to disasters; spread of irrigation reduces drought vulnerability and is not a cause.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Hydrologist and other posts 2017
items.s: Which weapon of biological disaster was used by the European colonizers of America to wipe out native red Indians?
items.x: At Fort Pitt (1763) the British gave Native Americans 'two Blankets and an Handkerchief out of the Small Pox Hospital' – smallpox-laden cloth, so (a). Jaundice, anthrax and flu are wrong.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Land slides occur mostly in ______ areas.
items.x: Landslides occur mostly in hilly and mountainous areas with steep slopes (Himalayas, Western Ghats).

items.s: Main objective of First Aid is
o: To prevent victim's condition from worsening
items.x: First aid aims to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening and promote recovery - all the above (the three Ps).

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
items.s: The outcome of hazard mapping is
o: Segregation of different types of hazards
items.x: Hazard mapping shows where hazards occur and so identifies vulnerable areas; evacuation plans and fund allocation are later uses of the map.

items.s: Which of the following is a natural factor which makes the country prone to various forms of disasters?
items.x: Extreme weather (cyclones, floods, droughts) is a natural factor; unscientific development, population pressure and unplanned urbanisation are human-made.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
items.s: What does the colour black in triage refer to?
items.x: In START triage, black means the casualty is dead or expectant (not expected to survive), so only comfort care such as pain relief is given. Red is life-threatening, yellow serious, green minor.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer & Analyst Grade-II (A
items.s: Which of the following is the least effective way to prepare for a hurricane?
o: Leaving valuables in a low-lying area
items.x: Hurricanes (tropical cyclones) bring storm surge and flooding that hit low-lying areas first, so leaving valuables there is the least effective step - they should be moved to higher, safer places. Securing outdoor furniture, boarding up windows and a family communication plan are all standard preparedness measures.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Which of the following best describes the role of biotechnology in environmental sustainability?
o: Using genetically modified microbes and plants to reduce pollution and conserve natural resources
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides
items.x: Biotechnology serves environmental sustainability by using GM microbes and plants for bioremediation and resource saving. More agrochemicals, deforestation or extra plastics do the opposite. (Moved to 5:108.)

items.s: 'Aerial metagenomics' best refers to which one of the following situations?
o: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
Understanding the genetic makeup of avian species of a habitat
Using air-borne devices to collect blood samples from moving animals
Sending drones to inaccessible areas to collect plant and animal samples from land surfaces and water bodies
items.x: Aerial metagenomics means collecting DNA from the air of a habitat in one go and sequencing it to identify the species present. It does not need blood samples, drones or a study of birds only.

items.s:
Identify the correct statements relating to 'IndiGau'

A. Second largest cattle chip of the world

B. It is developed for the conservation of pure varieties of indigenous cattle breeds

C. India's first Cattle Genomic Chip
items.x: IndiGau (NIAB Hyderabad, Aug 2021) is India's first cattle genomic chip, made for conserving pure indigenous breeds such as Gir, Kankrej, Sahiwal and Ongole; the government called it the world's largest cattle chip, not the second largest, so A is wrong.

items.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
items.s: The Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) facility was inaugurated in which city?
items.x: The Next Generation Sequencing facility was inaugurated at CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad, by Union S&T Minister Harsh Vardhan in July 2019; it can sequence up to 30 human genomes a day.

items.src: TSPSC Tutors in Medical Education, Dental Asst Surgeon, Civi
items.s:
Consider the following in relation to a new artificial womb technology:

A. It uses ex-vivo uterine environment therapy

B. It aims to prevent the severe morbidity suffered by premature infants

C. It uses amniotic fluid bath combined with an artificial placenta

D. It has been successfully used on human bodies at the Tohoku University Hospital, Japan
Select the right answer:
items.x: EVE (ex-vivo uterine environment) therapy uses an amniotic-fluid bath with an artificial placenta to save extremely premature infants (A, B, C true); it was tested on lambs, not yet on humans, so D is false.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
items.s: Scientists of which institute have developed a simple paper kit that can test freshness of milk and tell how well it has been pasteurized?
items.x: Researchers of IIT Guwahati developed a simple paper kit that shows milk freshness and how well it was pasteurised.

items.s:
With reference to 'Optogenetics' which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Optogenetics is a relatively new field of biotechnology.

2. It gives researchers the ability to transform brain activity into light and light into brain activity.

3. It will serve as an interface through which computers can become part of our brain, and through which our art of our brains could directly interface with each other.

4. It is the practice of stimulating biased inheritance of particular genes to alter entire populations.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
items.x: Optogenetics is a new field that uses light-sensitive proteins to turn light into neural activity and to read activity as light (1, 2). Statement 4 describes a gene drive, so the printed key '1, 2 and 4' is wrong, and statement 3 is only a speculative possibility (WEF frames it as a question), so 1 and 2 only.

items.s: Though officially not recognised at first, Subash Mukhopadhyaya created India's first and world's second Test Tube baby on 3rd October, 1978. What is the name of the baby?
items.x: Kanupriya Agarwal, nicknamed Durga, born in Kolkata on 3 October 1978 through Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyay's work, was India's first (and the world's second) IVF baby, after Louise Brown (UK, July 1978).

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: In which district, A.P government is developing Bio-Technology Hub?
items.x: The printed answer is Visakhapatnam, where the AP government planned its biotechnology hub/park.

items.src: TSPSC Tutors in Medical Education, Dental Asst Surgeon, Civi
items.s: Scientists from the following organization have successfully created an implanted bio-artificial Pancreas.
items.x: IIT Guwahati researchers created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas (3D-printed, insulin-secreting) for diabetes.

items.src: TSPSC Gurukulam JL, DL, Language Pandits 2017
items.s: From whom among the following scientists have successfully created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas?
items.x: IIT Guwahati researchers created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas (3D-printed, insulin-secreting) for diabetes.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The first ever genome sequencing of the Jamun tree (Syzygium cumini) was completed by the researchers of
o: National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) New Delhi
Jawaharlal Nehru Center for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bangalore
Indian Institute of Science Educational and Research (IISER), Bhopal
items.x: Researchers at IISER Bhopal completed the first genome sequencing of the jamun tree (Syzygium cumini) in 2023.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: If progeny is produced by crossing two types of pea plants i.e. Tall and Short (Tall being the dominant trait), then in the first generation what would be the percentage of Tall plants?
items.x: Crossing a pure-breeding tall pea with a dwarf one gives an F1 in which all plants (100%) are tall, because tall is dominant (Tt); the 3:1 ratio appears only in F2.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Serum can be sterilised by
items.x: Serum is heat-sensitive, so it is sterilised by membrane filtration. Autoclaving, hot air and boiling would denature its proteins.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
items.s: In which district of Telangana did the State Government allot an area, known as Genome Valley, for biotech activities?

items.s: Select the correct statement about in vitro fertilisation (IVF).
o: In vitro fertilisation (IVF) is a type of assisted cardiac technology (ART).
In vitro fertilisation (IVF) sperm and an egg are fertilised inside the human body.
IVF is a complex process that involves retrieving eggs from ovaries and manually combining them with sperm in a lab for fertilisation.
Several days after fertilisation, the fertilised egg (now called an embryo) is placed inside the testis of the male.
items.x: IVF retrieves eggs from the ovaries and fertilises them with sperm in a laboratory, outside the body; the embryo is then transferred into the woman's uterus (not into a testis). It is an assisted reproductive technology (ART), not 'assisted cardiac technology', and fertilisation does not happen inside the body.

items.s: Why Calico Act was passed by British Government in 1721?
o: To prescribe sizes for books bound with Calico
To regulate the price of Calico Cloth
To levy import tariffs on Calico Cloth
To ban imports of printed cotton textiles
