o: He undertook a 24-hour fast at Kolkata.
He unveiled the tricolour on Red Fort.
He oversaw the procession of lakhs of people at Raisina Hill.
He addressed a massive public meeting on communal harmony at Kolkata.
items.x: On 15 August 1947 Gandhiji was in Calcutta working for communal peace and marked the day with a 24-hour fast (and spinning); he did not hoist the flag at the Red Fort.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Which of the following bank was founded by Lala Lajpat Rai at Lahore in 1894
items.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of the Punjab National Bank at Lahore (1894).

items.s:
Consider the following statements concerning the American war of Independence.

I. The Americans raised the slogan, “No taxation without representation.”

II. The American merchants resorted to boycott the British products.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: The colonists raised 'No taxation without representation' and American merchants boycotted British goods. Both are correct.

items.s: The first Emperor of France was
items.x: Napoleon Bonaparte became Emperor of the French in 1804, the first emperor of France; Charlemagne was emperor of the Romans (800), and Louis XIV a king.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: The term '3H' concept of Education was given by
items.x:
Most Indian keys: Mahatma Gandhi (Nai Talim). Strictly: the head-heart-hand idea comes from J.H. Pestalozzi (18th-19th c.), from whom Gandhi took it (general knowledge, not checked).
Indian exam keys credit the '3H' formula (Head, Heart, Hand) to Gandhi's basic education (Nai Talim), which taught the hand along with the head and heart. The formula itself goes back to the Swiss educator Pestalozzi.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant in Police Transport Organisation 2
items.s: In which country did the Industrial Revolution start first?
items.x: The Industrial Revolution began in England (Britain) in the late 18th century, then spread to France, Germany and the USA.

items.s: Who narrated Bhagavata Puranam to Parikshita Maharaja?
items.x: Sage Shuka (son of Vyasa) narrated the Bhagavata Purana to King Parikshit; Suta later retold it to Shaunaka and the sages. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.s: In Andhra Pradesh State, the 1973 land reforms Act was introduced according to the suggestions made by
items.x: The 1973 AP Act lowered ceilings and made the family the unit along the national guidelines of 1972 evolved through the Central Land Reforms Committee.

items.s:
Who started the educational reform movements among Muslims in India?

A. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan

B. Sir W. W. Hunter

C. Shah Wali Ullah

D. Zakir Hussain
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
items.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (Aligarh) and Zakir Hussain (Jamia Millia, basic education) led educational reform among Muslims; Hunter only wrote 'The Indian Musalmans' and Shah Wali Ullah was an 18th-century theologian. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.s:
Which of the following statements about the Arya Samaj which emerged in the late 19th century are correct?

I. Had a strong supporting base amongst the trading castes.

II. Introduced ‘Shuddhi’ or mass purification.

III. The moderates in the Arya Samaj were headed by Hans Raj and Lajpat Rai and set up a chain of Dayananda Anglo-Vedic Colleges.

IV. The Arya Samaj had fewer membery than the Brahmo Samaj.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: The Arya Samaj drew on the trading castes (I), started Shuddhi (II) and its College Party under Hansraj and Lajpat Rai ran the DAV colleges (III); its following was larger than the Brahmo Samaj's, so IV is wrong.

items.s: Who wrote the book-The Story of The Integration of the Indian States?
items.x: 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States' was written by V.P. Menon, Secretary of the States Department under Patel.

items.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The ‘Bombay Manifesto’ signed in 1936 openly opposed the preaching of socialist ideals.

II. It evoked support from a large section of business community from all across India.
Which of the statements given above is/are are correct?
items.x: In May 1936 twenty-one Bombay businessmen signed the 'Bombay Manifesto' openly attacking Nehru's preaching of socialism (I is right). Most of the business class did not join it, and many criticised it, so II is wrong.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: In Madras State, the Local Boards Act was passed in which of the following years?
items.x: The Madras Local Boards Act was passed in 1884 (after Ripon's 1882 resolution), creating village unions, taluk boards and district boards.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Which governor general eased the entry of British investors and traders into India without any problems?
items.x: Under Bentinck the Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's trade and let Europeans settle and buy land freely, easing the entry of British investors and traders.

items.s:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
I. Theodore Beck — Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College
II. Ilbert Bill — Ripon
III. Pherozeshah Mehta — Indian National Congress
IV. Badruddin Tyabji — Muslim League
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
items.x: Beck – MAO College, Ilbert Bill – Ripon and Pherozeshah Mehta – INC are right; Badruddin Tyabji was INC President (1887), not a Muslim League man – so I, II and III.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: Who said that 'The first principle of teaching is that nothing can be taught'?
items.x: 'The first principle of true teaching is that nothing can be taught' is Sri Aurobindo's, from A System of National Education (1910).

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Who was the author of our National Anthem?
items.x: Rabindranath Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana, the National Anthem; Bankim Chandra wrote Vande Mataram, the National Song.

items.s: In 1918 'India In Transition' was written by
items.x: 'India in Transition' (1918) was written by the Aga Khan III; M.N. Roy's book of the same name came in 1922.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: Which period was marked by the rapid growth of public opinion for Telugu identity and shift from problems of the people to a province for the people, from District Conferences to a separate Andhra Conference?
items.x: Public opinion for a Telugu province grew from the Vandemataram movement (1907) to the first Andhra Conference at Bapatla (1913), when district conferences gave way to an Andhra Conference.

items.s: Which one of the following leaders of the Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan?
items.x:
Printed key: Mahatma Gandhi. gktoday.in gives Sardar Patel, and Azad (India Wins Freedom) claimed the plan as his own; general knowledge, not checked.
The printed key holds that Gandhi was wholly in favour of the Cabinet Mission Plan, which he called the best document the British could have produced.

items.s: Who among the following were traditionalists who worked against Veeresalingam Pantulu's reforms?
items.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam led the orthodox attack on women's education and widow remarriage, and A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu also opposed Veeresalingam; Uma Ranganayakulu was his ally (Veeresalingam wrote in his Purushartha Pradayini), so options with him are wrong.

items.src: Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Servic
items.s: Out of the below, Who was the first graduate from the Calcutta University in 1858?
items.x: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (with Jadunath Bose) was among the first graduates of Calcutta University in 1858.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in A.P BC We
items.s: In known history, which is the deadliest military conflict in the world in terms of total casualties?
items.x: The Second World War (1939-45) is the deadliest conflict in recorded history, with about 70-85 million dead. The First World War killed far fewer, and the Kalinga war and the Hundred Years' War are much smaller.

items.s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
o: Bhagwati Charan Vohra : The Philosophy of Bomb
items.x: 'The Indian Sociologist' was Shyamji Krishna Varma's London journal, not Bhagat Singh's. Sanyal wrote Bandi Jivan, Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb, and Lala Ram Saran Das wrote Dreamland (introduced by Bhagat Singh).

items.src: Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, As
items.s: Which lady is known as the mother of "Indian Revolution"
items.x: Madam Bhikaji Cama, who unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907, is popularly called the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'. Annie Besant led the Home Rule League, and Kanaklata Barua was a 1942 martyr.

items.s: In whose rule Kalidasa lived?
items.x: Kalidasa is traditionally placed at the court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (Gupta age); 'Vikramaditya' alone is the title, not a separate ruler here.

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: The branch of philosophy that is concerned with reasoning is called
items.x: Logic is the branch of philosophy concerned with the principles of correct reasoning (in Indian thought, the Nyaya school).

items.s: Who was the first to circumnavigate the earth?
items.x: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition (1519-22) made the first circumnavigation of the earth; Magellan was killed in the Philippines and Elcano completed it. Cook and Amundsen came much later.

items.s: This leader toured Andhra during the Vande-matharam movement
items.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 during the Vande Mataram movement.

items.s: Who of the following had regarded the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress (1931) as the pinnacle of Mahatma Gandhi’s popularity and prestige?
items.x: Subhas Chandra Bose described the Karachi Congress (1931) as the pinnacle of Gandhi's popularity and prestige.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
items.s:
Match the following correctly:

A. Durgabai Deshmukh - i. 1862

B. Potti Sriramulu - ii. 1880

C. Pattabhi Sitaramaiah - iii. 1901

D. Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu - iv. 1909
Find the correct answer.
items.x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu 1862, Pattabhi Sitaramayya 1880, Potti Sriramulu 1901, Durgabai Deshmukh 1909: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Who was the nationalist poet to use the word Tenugutalli for the first time in Telugu nationalist writings?
items.x: Exam keys credit Rayaprolu Subbarao, the Telugu nationalist poet of Janmabhoomi and Andhravali, with first using 'Tenugu talli' in nationalist verse. Viswanatha, Jashuva and Kodali Venkata Ratnam are distractors. Not found in the library or on the web.

items.s: In a patriarchal society, the principle that the mother's brother plays the most important and ritualistic social role is called this.
items.x: In a patrilineal (patriarchal) society the ritual and social role of the mother's brother reflects complementary filiation (Meyer Fortes) – the tie with the mother's kin; consanguinity is mere blood relationship. Same item as the 'complementary filiations' question (printed key here: A).

items.s: The notion that man is stronger than woman is a
items.x: 'Man is stronger than woman' is a belief, a proposition accepted as true (the same item elsewhere is keyed 'belief'); 'Trust' here translates belief (nammakam). A value is a judgement of what is desirable, not a factual claim (printed key: Value).

items.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
items.s: Declaration of the rights of children took place in
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1959); it is added as option 5.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child on 20 November 1959 (the Geneva Declaration was 1924; the UNCRC 1989). None of 1947, 1951, 1953 or 1958 is correct.

items.s: Divorce occurs when
o: When husband and wife decide to live separately
When both spouses inform their parents
When the society believes that their marriage bond is broken
When the marriage is annulled by the court
items.x: Divorce is the legal dissolution of a marriage by a court (W.P. Scott: an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage); spouses merely deciding to live apart is separation, not divorce.

items.s: The government of Andhra Pradesh had signed an MoU with NDMA on 13 August 2021 for ERSS implementation in the state. What is the full form of ERSS
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Emergency Response Support System); it is added as option 5.
ERSS is the Emergency Response Support System (single number 112). None of the printed options is the correct expansion: option (d) swaps 'Response' and 'Support', and the others are invented.

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: Which of the following is a better way of protecting reserve forests?
o: Keeping them out of bounds for locals
Allowing limited rights like grazing rights to locals
Privatization of forest management through big corporates
items.x: Allowing limited rights such as grazing gives locals a stake in protecting reserve forests; total exclusion, unlimited rights or corporate privatisation do not.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about East Asia Summit?

a. 13th East Asia Summit held in Singapore.

b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum.

c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN Member.

d. East Asia Summit comprises the ten member states of the ASEAN.
items.x: a, b and c are correct: 13th EAS in Singapore (2018), ASEAN-centred, chaired only by an ASEAN member. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members, not just the ten ASEAN states; so 'all of the above' is wrong.

items.s: Tribal economic relations mainly depended on this
items.x: Tribal economic relations depended mainly on barter; the jajmani system links castes in a village, not tribes (printed key: jajmani).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
items.s: The gender focal points, gender desks, gender budgeting cells set up in Ministries, State Government Departments, Panchayats and Urban local bodies serve as a focal point for
o: Advancing data collection on various issues affecting women that require immediate attention and intervention
items.x: The gender focal points, gender desks and gender budgeting cells are meant as focal points for advancing gender-disaggregated data collection on issues needing immediate intervention (Draft National Policy for Women 2016 approach).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Who can dissolve the Gram Panchayat, if the constitutional powers are misused
o: Panchayat cannot be dissolved before its term
items.x: If a Gram Panchayat abuses its powers the State Government (through the administration) can dissolve it; a panchayat can be dissolved before its term, with fresh polls within six months.

items.s: What do you call a family where there is division between 'Biological father' and 'social father'?
items.x: Separation of the biological father (genitor) from the social father (pater) occurs in polyandrous, i.e. polygamous, families, as among the Toda, where a rite fixes the social father (printed key: Patriarchal family).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: The 10th BRICS summit Declaration was named as
items.x: The 10th BRICS Summit (Johannesburg, South Africa, July 2018) adopted the Johannesburg Declaration.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: The Halifax Summit was the meeting of
o: Countries in favour of a common currency in Europe
items.x: The Halifax Summit (Canada, June 1995) was a G7 summit.

items.s: What is a radical cultural movement arising when there is evolution called?
items.x:
Printed keys split: transformational (this copy) vs millenarian (the 1996 copy); the stem is a garbled translation and the original key could not be found.
Garbled stem: a movement promising radical cultural change in times of extreme upheaval is usually called a millenarian movement; the two printings of this question carry different keys (transformational / millenarian).

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Which of the following was prepared and released by the NITI Aayog?
items.x: NITI Aayog prepared and released 'Strategy for New India @ 75' (December 2018).

items.s: English is the official language of the following state in India.
items.x: English is the official language of Nagaland; Goa uses Konkani, Uttarakhand Hindi (and Sanskrit), Assam Assamese.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Inter Board 2012
items.s: When did Indian Penal Code come into effect?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1862); it is added as option 5.
The IPC was enacted on 6 October 1860 but came into force on 1 January 1862; 1860 is the year of enactment, and 1852, 1854, 1857 are wrong.

items.s: In May 2023, the Supreme Court said that "it can exercise its powers under Article ___ of the constitution to grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of a marriage" even if one of the parties opposes it.
items.x: In May 2023 (Shilpa Sailesh) the Supreme Court held it can use Article 142(1) to grant divorce on irretrievable breakdown of marriage even if one party opposes.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Education & Data Processing Sec
items.s: These rights enable men to have a reasonable and legal source of livelihood.
items.x: Economic rights secure a person a reasonable and legal source of livelihood (work, wages, leisure). Liberty and religion are civil rights; education is a social-cultural right.

items.s: Which of the following is an example of a community ?
items.x: No key can be settled: in MacIver's sociology a club and a religious establishment are associations (organised for specific interests), not communities, so the printed key 'a club related to sports' contradicts the textbook distinction; family and kinship groups are treated as both community and association by different authors, so the question has no single defensible answer.

items.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
items.s: From which of the following countries were 4000 Indian nationals evacuated, due to the civil war, by launching the operation called 'Rahat'
items.x: Operation Rahat (April 2015) evacuated over 4,000 Indians and many foreigners from war-torn Yemen through Aden and Al Hudaydah via Djibouti.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: A cash book is used to:
items.at: Record receipts and payments of cash
items.x: A cash book records all cash receipts and cash payments in order of date, the cash counterpart of the ledger account. (Moved: Panchayati Raj finances.)

items.s: Which one of the following is NOT matched correctly with regard to the Governing Board of the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK)?
o: Minister of State, Women & Child Development: Member (Ex-officio)
Minister of Women & Child Development: Chairperson (Ex-officio)
items.x: The Prime Minister has no post on the RMK Governing Board: the Union Minister of Women and Child Development chairs it (ex officio) and the Executive Director is Member-Secretary. So 'PM: Honorary President' is the wrong pair.

items.s: It is said that marriage is a source of kinship. Who said this?
items.x: The printed key credits Westermarck (History of Human Marriage) with the view that marriage is a source of kinship; Radcliffe-Brown defined kinship as dynamic relations regulated by social usage.

items.s:
Sukanya Samriddhi Account is a scheme having which of the following

a) To promote the welfare of the girl child

b) A minimum deposit is Rs. 10,000

c) A savings account can be opened by the parent or legal guardian of a girl child less than 10 years

d) The interest that is provided on the deposited amount is tax free
items.x: Sukanya Samriddhi (2015, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao) promotes the girl child; a parent or guardian can open it for a girl under 10; interest is tax-free (EEE). The minimum deposit was ₹1,000 at launch (now ₹250), not ₹10,000, so it is a, c and d.

items.s: Who among the following proposed the tribe-caste model to explain the process of tribal amalgamation?
items.x: Surajit Sinha proposed the tribe-caste (tribe-peasant) continuum model to explain how tribes were absorbed into caste society; N.K. Bose gave the 'Hindu method of tribal absorption'.

items.s: In India 'Rythu' (Peasant) means
o: Own land and cultivate it with hired labour
Own land and cultivate it with the labor of family members.
Those who use traditional farming practices
items.x: A peasant (rythu, kisan) owns or holds land and cultivates it mainly with family labour – Thorner's 'kisan'; one who cultivates through hired labour is a landlord-farmer (malik) (printed key: A).

items.s: Which of the following is true about sociology?
o: It is the scientific study of society
It is concerned with the behavior of individuals in society
It studies groups and their organizations
Its purpose is to eliminate evils in the society
items.x: Sociology is the scientific study of society (A), the standard definition; it studies groups and behaviour in society too, but its aim is not to eliminate evils (printed key: B, which is only part of its scope).

items.s: The Godavari river water dispute is going on among the following states:
o: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra
Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh
items.x: The Godavari basin States – Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Karnataka (and MP) – are the parties; Bihar is not in the basin.

items.s: The head quarters of International Labour Organization (ILO) is
items.x: The ILO (1919) has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

items.s: False consciousness in caste stratification is due to
o: They are hindered in awareness of their role in the system
They are hindered awareness of their demands
items.x: In the Marxian sense, false consciousness in caste means the lower castes are kept from seeing their real status (their exploitation) in the system. Option 3 says this; the options are loose translations, and the printed key was missing.

items.s:
Which of the following tribes practice couvade?

A. Khasi

B. Toda

C. Spoon

D. Ho
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: Couvade (kuhana prasuti – the husband imitating his wife's pregnancy and birth taboos) is reported among the Khasi and the Toda, i.e. A and B; 'Spoon' is a garbled item and the Ho are not the textbook example (printed key: B, C, D).

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Welfare & Development Secret
items.s: Recently enacted the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2019 allows ethical altruistic surrogacy to the intending infertile Indian married couple between the age of
o: 21-50 years and 26 - 55 years for female and male, respectively
18-45 years and 21 - 50 years for female and male, respectively
23 - 50 years and 26 - 55 years for female and male, respectively
21- 46 years and 21 - 50 years for female and male, respectively
items.x: The Surrogacy (Regulation) Bill 2019 (Act 2021) permits altruistic surrogacy for a married Indian couple with the wife aged 23-50 and the husband 26-55.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: The District level Administrative Authority of the Gram Panchayat
items.x: The district-level administrative authority over gram panchayats is the Collector (Panchayat Raj) – printed key.

items.s: Levirate is practiced in which societies?
items.x: Levirate - a widow marrying her dead husband's brother - keeps the widow, her children and property within the husband's lineage, so it belongs to patriarchal (patrilineal) societies. (Moved to the marriage row of Society.)

items.s: To which Agency, Supreme Court entrusted the probe of alleged cases of forcible conversion and marriage referred as 'Love Jihad' cases?
items.x: In August 2017 (Hadiya case) the Supreme Court asked the National Investigation Agency to probe the alleged 'love jihad' conversion and marriage in Kerala.

items.s: Robert Redfield while defining little community talks about four characteristics. Three of them aredistinctiveness, smallness, and self-sufficiency. Which one is the fourth?
items.x: Redfield's little community has four traits: distinctiveness, smallness, homogeneity and self-sufficiency. Heterogeneity is an urban trait.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: Which of the following is not a source of funds for Gram Panchayat?
items.x: Taxes, Central grants and loans are all GP funding sources; fees on services to SHGs are not one (SHGs are partners, not a revenue base).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: Who has the primary responsibility to report outbreak of an epidemic in a village?
o: All the given answers are correct
items.x: The Panchayat Secretary has the primary responsibility to report an epidemic outbreak in the village (printed key).

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: Which of the following States has the lowest concentration of tribal population?
items.x: Tripura has about 32% STs (Census 2011), the lowest share among the North-Eastern tribal States, which are tribal-majority (Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Arunachal). If Assam were an option it would be lower (about 12%); the app shows no options.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Who exercises control over the Panchayat Secretary?
o: All the given answers are correct
items.x: The Sarpanch, as executive head, exercises control over the Panchayat Secretary.

items.s: Who is the head of National Mission on Rastriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan?
items.at: MHRD minister as head and secretary of Department of School Education and Literacy as vice-chairperson
items.x: The RMSA National Mission was headed by the Union HRD Minister, with the Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, as vice-chairperson.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: For selection of beneficiary in PMAY (Gramin), who would conduct verification of housing deprivation data?
items.x: Under PMAY-G the SECC-based list of housing-deprived households is verified by the Gram Sabha before beneficiaries are finalised.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which country is NOT a part of the BIMSTEC organisation?
items.x: BIMSTEC has seven members – Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand; China is not one.

items.s:
Which of the following problems are associated with transgenders?

A. Denial of access to education

B. Absence of special healthcare services for transgender people

C. Denial and lack of access to food and clothing

D. Lack of identity and social acceptance transgenders

E. Forced to make a living by begging and working as sex workers
Select the correct answer:
o: A, B, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
items.x: Transgender persons commonly face denial of education, lack of special healthcare, lack of identity and social acceptance, and are forced into begging or sex work; denial of food and clothing is not among the standard listed problems. Off-topic, moved to transgender persons.

items.s: What is a group of relatives who are all consanguineous relatives called?
items.x: A group of kin all related by blood (consanguineous) is a cognatic (cognate) group: cognates are blood relatives through both lines, agnates only through males, uterine kin only through females. 'Homogeneous group' is not a kinship term (printed key: Homogeneous group, probably a mistranslation).

items.s: Jan Bremen's work on village studies focused on
items.x: Jan Breman's village studies in south Gujarat focused on the Halpati labourers bound as hali to Anavil landowners (Patronage and Exploitation).

items.s: A national Curricular and Pedagogical Framework for Early Childhood Care and Education for children up to the age of 8 prepared by NCERT is in:
items.x: NCERT's National Curricular and Pedagogical Framework for ECCE (up to 8 years) has two parts: 0–3 and 3–8 years.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Application of principles of sociology to education is known as?
items.x: Educational sociology is the application of the general principles and findings of sociology to the process and administration of education (F.J. Brown). Sociology of education, a later field, is the sociological analysis of education as a social institution, so the 'application' definition points to educational sociology (printed key: Sociology of education).

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The process of keeping a carefull watch on specific events or activities, which constitute the main components of the programme is called
items.x: Monitoring is keeping a careful watch on the specific events or activities that make up a programme while it runs; evaluation judges its results.

items.s: Who said 'Religion is a heart for the heartless'?
items.x: Marx called religion 'the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world' and 'the opium of the people' (1844).

items.s: Excluding Uttar Pradesh, the state which sends maximum number of representatives to the Lok Sabha is
items.x:

Geographic territory and uniformity of conduct
Likeness and differences between the group members
Geographic territory and sense of solidarity

items.x: 'Culture is the man-made part of the environment' is M.J. Herskovits's definition (Man and His Works, 1948). Tylor defined culture as a 'complex whole' of knowledge, belief, art, morals, law and custom, and Malinowski as inherited artefacts, goods and ideas, so 'None of the above'.

items.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016

items.x: The 'we-feeling' is the mark of primary groups (Cooley), and the family is the primary group where it is strongest. The printed key (class) contradicts this: class is a loose, impersonal stratum. Strictly it depends on the source book's framing; the owner should check.

items.s: Economic relations between tribes are mostly based on what?

items.s: When a group of people gets excited and engages in or prepares to engage in violent action, what is the group called?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mob); it is added as option 5.
An excited crowd that engages in or prepares for violent action is a mob. A crowd is any temporary gathering, a gang is a small organised group and an aggregation is a mere collection, so no printed option fits.

items.s:
Which of the following statement is True about Government of India Act, 1919?

A. It was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom.

B. It made provision for dilution of Central and Provincial subjects.

C. The Act covered 10 years from 1909 to 1919.

D. The Act made Central Legislature Bicameral, with Lower House having 145 members serving 5 years term.
items.x: Only A is correct: the 1919 Act was passed by the UK Parliament. B is loose (it classified/devolved central and provincial subjects); C is wrong (a commission was to review it after 10 years, not cover 1909-1919); D is wrong (the Legislative Assembly of 145 had a 3-year term). items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
items.s: Regarding schedule Caste and schedule tribe reservation choose the correct answer
o: Reservation on the basis of domicile is not impermissible in terms of clause of Article 15 of the Constitution of India
Children born to inter caste Marriage of which either father or mother belongs to SC/ST category can claim reservation benefits unconditionally
A person by reason of marriage alone ipso facto become a member of SC or ST
Reservations are available at the time of appointments and promotions even for solitary post
items.x: Only statement (a) is right: Article 15 does not bar residence (domicile) as such – only 'place of birth' – and the Supreme Court has allowed limited domicile preference (Pradeep Jain, 1984). Children of inter-caste marriages cannot claim SC/ST benefits automatically (Rameshbhai Naika, 2012); marriage alone does not make a person SC/ST (Valsamma Paul, 1996); a solitary post cannot be reserved.

items.s:

items.x: In September 2022 the MHA notified the rules under the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022 (which replaced the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920), letting police collect physical and biological samples of arrested and convicted persons.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: The President of India is a/an:
items.x: The office of the President is created by the Constitution (Art. 52), so the President is a constitutional authority, not a statutory or merely administrative one.

items.s: The 62nd Amendment Bill of the Indian Constitution deals with
o: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes
items.x: The 62nd Amendment (1989) extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies (Art. 334) for ten more years; Nagarpalika and Panchayati Raj were the 65th/64th Bills.

items.s: An untouchable, converting to Christianity, is an example of which of the following?
items.x: Changing religion without a change in rank is horizontal mobility (Sorokin's example: moving between religious groups). An untouchable converting to Christianity keeps his social level. The printed key was vertical.

items.s:
In the context of Central Government programmes, which one of the following statement/statements is/are incorrect?
I. The objective of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) is aimed at reducing poverty of the ST communities by generating additional employment opportunities. II
III.
IV. Sel
II. Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana (PM-SYM), monthly contribution is payable by the beneficiary, the State Government and the Central Government. III. Under the 'FutureSkills Prime' Programme, Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C- DAC) is the key implementing agency. IV. Mission Karmayogi comprises of eight key 46. Wi pillars that are intended to create functional and behavioural competencies among the civil servants. Select the answer using the codes given below:
items.x: All four are incorrect. PM-AJAY is for SC (not ST) communities. PM-SYM is funded by the beneficiary and the Centre only. FutureSkills Prime is a MeitY-NASSCOM programme, with C-DAC only a resource centre. Mission Karmayogi has six pillars, not eight. The stem is garbled in the scan.

items.s: Who became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh three times during 1983-1994?
items.x: N.T. Rama Rao (TDP) was Chief Minister in 1983, 1984 and 1985 and again in 1994.

items.s: Special Category Status (SCS) was first introduced in India in 1969 on the recommendation of which body?
items.x:
Most books: the Fifth Finance Commission (1969). Strictly: SCS was an NDC decision under the Gadgil Formula for Plan assistance (general knowledge, not checked).
SCS was introduced in 1969, as most books say, on the recommendation of the Fifth Finance Commission. The NDC approved the Gadgil Formula that gave these States preferential Plan assistance.

items.s: L.B.S. is one of the economic measures taken by the Government of India for financial inclusion. What is L.B.S. in this context?
items.x: LBS is the Lead Bank Scheme (written 'Lead Banking Scheme' in the stem), a district-level financial inclusion measure; the other expansions do not exist.

An artificial island in a city with heating system for use by shelterless
A part of a city experiencing hot climate compared to other parts
A city experiencing much warmer temperatures than nearby rural areas

items.x: In January 2000 the Standing Committee of State Finance Ministers recommended uniform floor rates of sales tax across the States.

items.src: AP Forest Beat Officers Screening Test 2019

items.x: Before demonetisation India's cash (currency) to GDP ratio was about 12%, high by international standards. (Moved: money supply, row 81.)

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A

items.x: Ranikhet (Newcastle) disease shows respiratory signs (gasping), nervous signs (twisted neck, paralysis) and gastrointestinal signs (greenish diarrhoea) – all of these.

items.s: The theoretical distribution used for testing whether a population follows a specific theoretical distribution or not:
items.x: Whether data fit a specified theoretical distribution is tested with the chi-square goodness-of-fit test; Z, t and F test means and variances. Printed key (Z) was wrong. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

items.s: The recent statement made by the Indian Prime Minister that the Higher Education in India can be developed through adopting approach of:
o: Earmarking 60% of the national income for higher education
items.x: The Prime Minister's statement was that higher education can be expanded through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) approach, which combines government support with private investment. Outright privatisation, relying on foreign providers, and spending 60% of national income on higher education (an impossible share) were not the approach suggested.

items.s: Indian rupee devaluation proves successful only if the prices of
items.x: Devaluation succeeds only if export prices abroad fall in proportion to the devaluation, so that exports become cheaper to importers and volumes rise; if domestic prices rise and cancel the cut, it fails (printed key; compare CDS 2017 'exports become cheaper to importers').

In the last quarter of the same year based on audit report for 3 quarters
Would be released in the next year based on audited accounts of the year
Would be released in the last year of the five year period based on audited accounts of four years

items.x: The AP government planned its high-end IT skills university (AI, ML, data analytics) at Visakhapatnam.

items.x: Handloom weaving is India's largest cottage industry, ahead of sericulture and soap making.

items.x: DAY-NULM is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; PMRPY, PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan and the National Child Labour Project are Labour Ministry schemes.

items.s:
Which of the following reasons are mainly responsible for slow growth of Real Per Capita Income in India :
1. Rapid increase in population
2. High increase in prices
3. Slow growth in agriculture and industrial sectors
4. Unavailablity of foreign exchange Find the correct answer using following codes :
Codes :
items.x:
Most keys (UPPCS 2001): all four. Since foreign exchange is no longer scarce, some guides now give 1, 2 and 3 only (the app's earlier key).
All four slowed real per capita income growth in India up to the question period: rapid population growth, high inflation, slow agricultural and industrial growth and (before 1991) chronic scarcity of foreign exchange for imports of capital goods.

items.s: Managing Agency method which contributed for industrial development during the initial stages of industrialization was abolished in the year
items.x: The managing agency system was abolished from 3 April 1970 by the Companies (Amendment) Act 1969, so 1970 is right; 1968, 1972 and 1974 are wrong.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2019
items.s: What are the cards that have been issued to the tenant farmers through the Department of Agriculture in AP to facilitate the availability of institutional credit, crop insurance, farm implements and input subsidy?
items.x:
COC / Loan Eligibility Cards — now Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRCs) under the AP Crop Cultivators Rights Act 2019; 9,13,283 issued by 3 Jan 2025 (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.56)
AP issued Certificates of Cultivation (COC) cards, with Loan Eligibility Cards, so tenant farmers could get institutional credit, insurance and input subsidy (now Crop Cultivator Rights Cards under the 2019 Act). Soil Health Cards only give nutrient advice.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Section Officer (ASO) Mains General Studies

items.x: Between Oct 2014 and the exam, about 5 crore+ rural household toilets had been built under SBM(G) (the nearest option; about 10 crore by 2019).

items.x: The Cauvery is the most exploited river, with almost all of its utilisable water already abstracted.

items.s: Which of the following crops is not covered under the National Food Security Mission ?
items.x: NFSM (2007) covered rice, wheat and pulses; coarse cereals were added only from 2014-15, so in 2010 coarse cereals were not covered.

items.x: The most remarkable feature of Indian industry since Independence is its diversification – from a narrow consumer-goods base to a wide range of capital and basic goods. (Printed: no key.)

items.x: The Economic Survey 2018-19 (4 July 2019) proposed a behavioural shift so that repaying debt is seen as a 'pious obligation'.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: The empirical relationship among mean, median and mode is:
items.x: From Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean: Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean), which is option 4. Option 3 (Mode − Median = 2(Median − Mean)) is the same identity rearranged, so it is also true; options 1 and 2 are false.

items.s: Which one of the following constitutes the single largest export item from India?
items.x: Around 2012 gems and jewellery was the single largest export item among the options, ahead of readymade garments, leather and chemicals (petroleum products, not offered, were larger).

items.s: Money laundering is closely related to
o: Transfer of money from one account to another account
items.x: Money laundering is the process of turning the proceeds of crime – drug trafficking, smuggling, corruption – into apparently legitimate money; mere exchange or transfer of money is not laundering.

items.x:

The scarcity definition – economics studies the relation between unlimited ends and scarce means – is Lionel Robbins' (1932). Keynes, Marx, Weber and Adam Smith (wealth definition) did not give it.

items.s: Which of the following groups constitutes the largest items of export from India?

items.x: Malnutrition results from all the listed causes together: inadequate diet, disease and poverty/food insecurity.

items.s: 11th Finance Commission has recommended that in the tax revenue collected by the Union, the shareable part of States will be :
items.x: The 11th Finance Commission fixed the States' share at 29.5% of the net proceeds of all shareable Central taxes (10th: 29%; 12th: 30.5%).

items.s: Assuming demand curves are elastic, a surplus balance of payments can be eliminated by
o: Strengthening direct controls over imports of goods and services and capital outflows
Convincing other nations that they should follow inflationary domestic policies
items.x: With elastic demand, appreciating the currency makes exports dearer and imports cheaper, removing the surplus; import controls, devaluation or inflation abroad would widen it.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Word Association test for assessing personality was first used by Jung in which year?
items.x: Jung presented his word association method in English at Clark University in 1909, published in 1910; of the options 1910 fits (Galton had used word association earlier).

items.s: Economic Survey 2011-12 of Govt. of India has highlighted that the country's engineering industry accounts for ..... of India's GDP.
items.x: The Economic Survey 2011-12 put the engineering sector, the largest segment of Indian industry, at about 3% of GDP; no source supports 4, 4½ or 2.

items.s: How many Municipalities are there in Andhra Pradesh at present:
items.x:
AP now has 123 ULBs – 17 municipal corporations, 79 municipalities, 27 nagar panchayats (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.263-264)
The APPSC key gives 71 municipalities for the question period. (now 79 municipalities among 123 ULBs)

items.s: Which of the following States has the highest growth in Gross State Domestic Product in 2010-11?
items.x: Among these, Bihar recorded the highest GSDP growth in 2010-11 (about 14.8% at constant prices), well above Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

items.s:
With reference to Central Bank digital currencies, consider the following statements :

a. It is possible to make payments in a digital currency without using US dollar or SWIFT system.

b. A digital currency can be distributed with a condition programmed into it such as a time-frame for spending it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: A CBDC can be used for payments without routing through the US dollar or SWIFT, and being programmable it can carry conditions such as a time limit for spending – both statements are correct.

items.s: The Largest urban agglomeration of the world is :
items.x:
WUP 2025 changed the city definition – now Jakarta is the largest, Dhaka 2nd, Tokyo 3rd (UN World's Cities in 2025, as quoted in the PYQ explanation)
Tokyo(-Yokohama) has been the world's largest urban agglomeration in every UN World Urbanization Prospects list from the 1960s to 2018 (Mexico City and New York well below it); the printed key Mexico City is wrong. (now Jakarta, by the new WUP 2025 method)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: Time required to recover the initial cash outlay in a project
items.x: The payback period is the time a project takes to recover its initial cash outlay from its net cash inflows, a simple capital-budgeting yardstick.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer & Analyst Grade-II (A
items.s:
Identify the option that arranges the following major policy moves by the Union Government in chronological order of their announcement.

1. Expansion of PLI (Production-Linked Incentive) Scheme - A move to extend incentives to more sectors, boosting domestic manufacturing and exports

2. Introduction of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Framework - A policy aimed at enhancing digital governance and promoting seamless digital transactions

3. National Logistics Policy 2.0 - An updated policy designed to improve supply chain efficiency and reduce logistics costs

4. FDI Policy Reforms 2024 - Amendments to foreign direct investment (FDI) rules to attract more global investments into key sectors
items.x:
The stem's 'National Logistics Policy 2.0' is not a recognised policy name; the key assumes it means the National Logistics Policy 2022. Strictly the question is loosely framed.
Taking 'National Logistics Policy 2.0' as the National Logistics Policy of September 2022: PLI expansion (Nov 2020) → logistics policy (2022) → DPI framework (G20, 2023) → FDI reforms (2024), i.e. 1-3-2-4. Moved to row 72 (reform record since 2014).

items.s: Social goods are goods which are consumed by all citizens and increase the
items.x: Social (public) goods are consumed by all citizens and raise the welfare of society. (Moved: public expenditure, row 102.)

items.s: The standing committee of State Finance Ministers recommended in January, 2000 uniform rate across the states in respect of
items.x: In January 2000 the Standing Committee of State Finance Ministers recommended uniform floor rates of sales tax across the States.

items.s: Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the "fiscal stimulus"?
o: It is a massive investment by the Government in manufacturing sector to ensure the supply of goods to meet the demand surge caused by rapid economic growth
It is an intense affirmative action of the Government to boost economic activity in the country
It is Government's intensive action on financial institutions to ensure disbursement of loans to agriculture and allied sectors to promote greater food production and contain food inflation
It is an extreme affirmative action by the Government to pursue its policy of financial inclusion.
items.x: A fiscal stimulus is an intense affirmative action of the Government (tax cuts, higher spending) to boost economic activity, as in the 2008-09 packages; it is not tied to manufacturing, farm credit or financial inclusion. (Official UPSC key: b.)

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What grazing management practice involves moving livestock through six or more paddocks in sequence several times during the season?
items.x: Moving livestock through a sequence of paddocks (six or more) several times a season, so each rests and regrows, is rotational grazing; leader-follower and creep grazing are special forms.

items.s: The percentage of net area cultivated to the total geographical area of Andhra Pradesh State in 2006-07 is
items.x: In 2006-07 undivided AP's net area sown was about 37% of its geographical area, so 37.2; 22.6-27.2 are too low.

items.s: Emotional intelligence is―
o: The ability to score high in IQ tests
The ability to monitor one's own and others ' feelings and one's thinking and actions
The ability to avoid emotional responses in decision-making
The ability to manipulate others ' emotions
items.x: Emotional intelligence is the ability to perceive and monitor one's own and others' feelings and to use that to guide thinking and action. It is not IQ, avoiding emotions or manipulating others.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Welfare Secretary
items.s: Which of the following is true regarding percentage of seasonal and chronic hunger in India?
items.x: NSSO rounds show the share of households reporting seasonal or chronic hunger (not getting two square meals) has fallen steadily since the 1980s - it has decreased. (Moved to the food-security row.)

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: On Which side of Godavari is Bhadrachalam Town located?
o: Partly of Telangana side and partly on Andhra side.
items.x: Bhadrachalam town lies on the bank of the Godavari whose surrounding mandals went to AP (the 'Andhra side'); the temple town itself stayed in Telangana. Printed key kept.

items.s: At present in Andhra Pradesh there is
o: two IIITs in whole of Andhra Pradesh
three IIITs in whole of Andhra Pradesh
items.x: Cannot be settled: IIIT Hyderabad existed, and RGUKT's three IIITs (Basar, Nuzvid, RK Valley) opened in 2008, so the count (one, three or four) depends on the exam date and on what is counted. (Moved to AP education.)

items.s: Which one of the following denotes the size of an operational holding in Indian agriculture?
items.x: An operational holding is the land actually operated: owned land plus land leased in, minus land leased out.

items.s: Canfina is associated with:
items.x: Canfina (Canfin Homes / Canbank Financial Services) belongs to the Canara Bank group.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: What is the name of the ingenious construction designed to harvest surface run off water for agriculture since 15th Century in Jaisalmer area?
items.x: Khadins are runoff-harvesting embankments built across slopes in the Jaisalmer region from the 15th century (Paliwal Brahmins); the moistened bed is cropped. Kunds are covered pits, and johads/baandhis are other structures.

items.s: The Pradhan Mantri Vayo Vandana Yojana has been launched by the government aims to
o: To provide housing for individuals above the age of 60 years
To provide social security to elderly people during old age
To provide a bank loan for senior citizens
To provide life time pension to senior citizens
items.x: PMVVY (LIC) gives senior citizens an assured pension for 10 years – social security in old age; it is not housing, a bank loan or a lifetime pension.

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: As part of rationalization of Centrally Sponsored Schemes, the Central Government categorized the schemes into the following 3 categories?
o: Core of the Core, Core and Optional
Central funded, Jointly funded and State funded
items.x: In 2015-16 the Sub-Group of Chief Ministers (NITI Aayog) grouped Centrally Sponsored Schemes into Core of the Core, Core and Optional schemes.

items.s: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana?
items.x: PMKSY lists renovation of water bodies, rainwater-harvesting structures and recharge of aquifers among its works; 'construction of wells' is the item the keys treat as not listed.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s: How did import substitution industrialization (ISI) impact India's trade policies initially?
items.x: Import substitution industrialisation aimed to reduce import dependence by producing substitutes at home; it meant inward-looking, not open, trade policies.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Falling out of any part of the womb of pregnant cattle either before or after calving is called as
items.x: Falling out of part of the womb (uterus or vagina) before or after calving is prolapse; pyometra is pus in the uterus and involution its return to normal size.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: In which of the following years was the introduction of GST (Goods and Services Tax) announced in the Union Budget?
items.x: The introduction of GST (target 1 April 2010) was first announced by P. Chidambaram in the Union Budget 2006-07; it was finally introduced on 1 July 2017.

items.x: CLAP = Clean Andhra Pradesh and VUDA = Visakhapatnam Urban Development Authority are correct; OWMS is not 'Online water management services' → I and III.

items.x: AP had 27 notified SEZs as of July 2021.

items.x: As per AP Socio-Economic Survey 2016-17 each fair price shop served on average about 450 ration cards.

items.s: Merchandise exports from India (MEIS) has been replaced by which of the existing scheme
o: All the given answers are correct
items.x: MEIS (FTP 2015-20) replaced five earlier reward schemes – Focus Product, Focus Market, Market Linked Focus Product, Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojana and the Agri Infrastructure Incentive Scrip – so all the given answers are correct.

items.src: APPSC AP Municipal Junior Accounts Officers 2012
items.s: Funds which flow into a country to take advantage of favourable rates of interest in that country are called
items.x: Short-term funds that move into a country to take advantage of higher interest rates (or expected exchange-rate gains) are called hot money. (Moved to the FDI/FPI row.)

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: In the early 1960s, at a time when most distinguished development economists were talking about the virtues of import substitution, it was ____ who has pointed out, through a detailed empirical analysis, that trade would be an important factor for the development of a less developed country such as India.
items.x: Manmohan Singh's Oxford thesis (published 1964 as 'India's Export Trends and Prospects for Self-Sustained Growth') argued that trade was important for India's development, against the import-substitution consensus.

items.s: Director-General of WTO
items.x:
Azevedo left in August 2020 — now Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria), DG since 1 March 2021 (app notes 3:77 sub 2)
In 2017 the WTO Director-General was Roberto Azevedo of Brazil (6th DG, 2013-2020) (now Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala); the other names are distractors.

items.s:
Consider the following items imported by India :
1. Capital goods
2. Petroleum
3. Pearls and precious stones
4. Chemicals
5. Iron and Steel The correct sequence of the decreasing order of these items (as per 94-95 figures), in terms of value is:
items.x:
1994-95 order 2, 1, 3, 4, 5 — now 2, 1, 4, 3, 5 (chemicals ahead of pearls and precious stones, 2024-25; printed explanation citing Economic Survey 2025-26)
In 1994-95 the order was petroleum > capital goods > pearls and precious stones > chemicals > iron and steel, i.e. 2, 1, 3, 4, 5 (now 2, 1, 4, 3, 5 as chemicals overtook pearls).

items.src: Divisional Accounts Officer (Works), Asst. Public Relation O

items.x: Jalayagnam (2004) envisaged 86 irrigation projects – major and medium projects, flood banks and modernisation – mainly on the Krishna, Godavari and Pennar.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Annamayya district is carved from parts of erstwhile
items.x: Annamayya district (HQ Rayachoti, 2022) was carved from parts of YSR Kadapa and Chittoor districts.

items.x: The nine priorities of Budget 2024-25 included agriculture productivity and resilience, employment and skilling and energy security, but not 'sustainable development'.

items.s: The largest percentage share in India's export trade is of :
items.x:
gems and jewellery led in 2003 — now electronic goods (9.5% of exports) are ahead of gems and jewellery (6.5%) (2024-25, printed explanation of PYQ yc70fa39fe66 citing Economic Survey 2025-26)
In 2003 gems and jewellery had the largest share of India's exports (about 17%); electronic goods were then only 2-3% (now electronics, 9.5%, lead the four).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: The following places in Andhra Pradesh are famous for decorative hand crocheted lace work?
items.x: Narsapur and Palakollu (West Godavari) are famous for hand-crocheted lace (Narsapur crochet lace has a GI tag).

items.s: With reference to the Edgeworth model, determine which of the following statements is correct
o: Each duopolist assumes the other keeps its price constant
Each duopolist assumes the other keeps its quantity constant
items.x: Edgeworth's model, like Bertrand's, assumes each duopolist expects the rival to keep its price constant; the solution oscillates and the duopolists do not recognise interdependence.

items.s: Toll is a

items.x: In 2016-17 PMGSY built about 130 km of road per day.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: The primary cotton research center in Andhra Pradesh is located at
items.x: ANGRAU's Regional Agricultural Research Station at Lam, Guntur is the main centre of the All India Coordinated Research Project on Cotton in AP (the LRA cotton varieties are named after Lam). RARS Nandyal is only a cotton sub-centre; its main mandates are millets, sorghum and chickpea. Kadapa and Visakhapatnam are not cotton research centres.

items.s: Swayamsidha Scheme launched in the year 2002 was dedicated to:
items.x: Swayamsiddha was an integrated, SHG-based scheme for women's empowerment (launched 2001), not a literacy or health scheme.

items.s: The objective of Jawahar Rojgar Yojna is to :

Strengthen the rural economic and social structure
items.x: JRY (1989) aimed at employment for the rural unemployed and underemployed and at strengthening the rural economic and social structure, so all of the above.

items.x: Life insurance policies are liabilities of insurers (LIC etc.), not of the Government. Provident funds, NSCs (small savings) and long-term government bonds are all Government liabilities and so part of national (public) debt in the wide sense.

items.src: Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fisheries

items.x: Indira Awaas Yojana began in 1985-86 as a sub-scheme of RLEGP (later JRY) and became an independent programme from 1 January 1996.

items.x: Bokaro was the public-sector steel plant of the Third Plan (incorporated 1964, built from 1965 with Soviet help); Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were Second Plan plants.

items.x: School-infrastructure modernisation is the Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu programme (2019); Amma Vodi is a cash aid to mothers, not infrastructure.

items.x: Air India and Indian Airlines merged in 2007 to form a single entity called Air India.

Secure the Core Areas of the forests to protect important wildlife
Strategically allow mining for important minerals within forests with minimum changes to the area
Promote Wildlife tourism for both economic and educational benefit of the country

much higher than government lands assignments
forest lands share is much higher
items.x: In AP land distributed to the poor came overwhelmingly from government (assigned) land, so it is not 'much higher' from ceiling surplus (a) or forest land (c), and (b) reverses the fact – none of them.

items.s:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I : In the post-pandemic recent past, many Central Banks worldwide had carried out interest rate hikes.
Statement-II : Central Banks generally assume that they have the ability to counteract the rising consumer prices via monetary policy means.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
items.x: Both are correct and II explains I: central banks raised rates after the pandemic because they assume monetary tightening can counter rising consumer prices (UPSC official key A).

items.s: Where was the Mega Seed Park proposed to be established in Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: AP's Mega Seed Park was proposed at Tangadancha in Kurnool district.

items.s: The scheme that has entered the Guinness World Record for opening the most bank accounts in a single week

items.s: Share of labour force in agriculture sector in AP

items.x: By 31 March 2017 the SHG-bank linkage programme covered about 10 crore families (about 85 lakh SHGs).

In urban India, malnutrition is not a problem
Compared to rural areas, higher percentage of population in Urban India suffer from malnutrition
Malnutrition levels are equal both in urban and Rural India

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

items.x:

items.s:

II. India is the first country in the world to develop hybrid cotton variety leading to increased production.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St

items.x: Sudden onset of a contagious disease that affects health, disrupts services and businesses and brings high economic and social costs is the definition of a pandemic emergency, one of the four types (natural disasters, environmental emergencies, complex emergencies, pandemic emergencies). items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment

items.x: Maize came from the Americas and reached India only after the 16th century, so it is not an ancient cereal; rice, wheat and barley were grown in ancient India.

items.x: The jaguar is native to the Americas – Central and South America; it does not live in Africa (Nigeria, Ghana) or Siberia.

items.s: Which of the following industrial towns is located on the Chota Nagpur plateau?
items.x: Ranchi stands on the Ranchi plateau, part of the Chota Nagpur plateau; Bhilai is in the Chhattisgarh plain and Asansol–Durgapur in the Damodar valley.

items.s:
Government of India encourages the cultivation of ‘sea buckthorn’. What is the importance of this plant?

I. It helps in controlling soil erosion and preventing desertification.

II. It is a rich source of biodiesel.

III. It has nutritional value and is well adapted to live in cold areas of high altitudes.

IV. Its timber is of great commercial value.
Which of the following statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Sea buckthorn is a cold-desert, high-altitude shrub that checks soil erosion and desertification and has nutritional value (I and III). It is no biodiesel source and its timber has no commercial value.

items.s: Which of the following cities is known by the name of the City of Smoke?
items.x: London, long smothered in coal smoke and smog, is called the 'Big Smoke' / City of Smoke.

items.src: APPSC 2022 Various posts under Group-IV Services(Limited Rec
items.s: The construction of which major infrastructure project in the 19th century helped facilitate transportation and trade in Andhra Pradesh, particularly for agricultural products?
items.x:
Official key: Visakhapatnam Port. Strictly: Visakhapatnam port was built 1927-33 and opened in 1933 (20th century); of the options only Kakinada and the older Machilipatnam port were active in the 19th century (app notes 4:95 sub 7).
The APPSC key is Visakhapatnam Port, the key outlet for the region's farm and mineral trade.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Identify the correct chronology of the following television networks in India
items.x: Doordarshan (1959) came first; then Star TV (1991), Zee TV (October 1992) and Sony Entertainment Television (1995).

items.s: Name the city of South America which due to its wide road is also known as Venice of America
items.x: Buenos Aires, famed for broad avenues such as 9 de Julio, is the city meant ('Paris of South America'); Santiago, Mexico City and Rio do not fit.

items.s: Which of the following is a lake in the Eastern Coastal plains of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Pulicat Lake lies on AP's eastern coastal plain; Waddepally and Laknavaram are Telangana lakes and Sur Sagar is in Gujarat.

items.s: Sir Edwin Lutyens was the architect of which city?
items.x: Sir Edwin Lutyens (with Herbert Baker) designed New Delhi, the imperial capital; Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier (official key: Chandigarh).

items.s: As per the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2021, ____ was the leading producer of primary gold accounting for 99% production in 2020-21.
items.x: Karnataka (Hutti mines) produced about 99% of India's primary gold in 2020-21 (IMYB 2021).

items.s: Which ministry has launched National Air Sport Policy 2022?
items.x: The National Air Sports Policy 2022 was released by the Ministry of Civil Aviation (June 2022).

items.s: Which country among the following produces the maximum sugar in the world?
items.x: Brazil is the world's largest sugar producer, with India second; India topped only briefly in 2021-22.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
items.s: What does Mayday mean for a sailor?
items.x: 'Mayday' (from French 'm'aidez', help me) is the international radio distress call for a life-threatening emergency at sea or in the air.

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: Which of the following is not a drought prevention measure?
items.x: Check dams, desilting tanks and farm ponds conserve water; Eucalyptus is a water-hungry tree that lowers groundwater, so planting it is not a drought-prevention measure.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, Technical Asst. (Hydrog

items.x: Konaseema is the delta island between the Gautami and Vasishta branches of the Godavari in AP – not the Krishna, Penna or Narmada delta.

items.s: Which of the following is not a vulnerability factor for occurrence of a disaster?
items.x: Disaster vulnerability rises with poverty, population growth and hazardous location; religion is not a vulnerability factor. Off-topic (disaster management), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Isogonic lines pass through points of ____
items.x: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination; isoclinic lines join points of equal dip.

items.s:
From the following, find out the correct statements.

A. Kosi project is the joint venture of India and Bangladesh

B. National Institute of Oceanography is in Goa

C. The Head Quarters of South Western Railways is Hubli

D. One has to cross Gulf of Khambhat while travelling from Nagercoil to Srilanka
items.x: B and C are correct: the National Institute of Oceanography is in Goa, and South Western Railway has its headquarters at Hubballi. A is wrong because the Kosi project is an India–Nepal project. D is wrong because the sea between Nagercoil and Sri Lanka is the Gulf of Mannar, not the Gulf of Khambhat. The printed key (A & D) gave the two wrong statements.

Most books: Kerala. Strictly: Maharashtra has been the largest cashew producer for years and is not offered (general knowledge, not checked).

Technical education has no role in community safety
Awareness campaigns delay immediate relief measures
Educated communities are more likely to follow land-use rules and early warning instructions

items.x: In NHDR 2001 AP was 9th among major States in 1991 (HDI 0.377) and 10th in 2001 (HDI 0.416), so its rank changed from 9 to 10. '10 to 9' reverses the direction; AP showed practically no improvement in rank.

items.x: The UN General Assembly declared 2016 the International Year of Pulses (FAO-led). Off-topic here; moved to Indian geography (crops).

items.x: India's huge dairy sector makes it the largest producer of butter and ghee; it does not lead in meat, pork or cheese.

items.x: 'Big Apple' is the nickname of New York City.

o: a Central Government Organisation of India.
a State Government Organisation of West Bengal.
a Government Organisation represented by both the Central (India) and the State Governments of West Bengal and Jharkhand.
an Organisation of the State Governments of West Bengal and Jharkhand.

items.x: The Malwa Plateau lies on the Deccan Trap lava, so its predominant soil is black soil. Alluvial, red and laterite soils are not dominant there.

items.s: What is the number of union territories in India ?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (8); it is added as option 5.
7 UTs in 2010 (printed key) — now 8 UTs since 26 Jan 2020 (J&K and Ladakh created 31 Oct 2019; DNH and Daman & Diu merged) (MHA).
India now has 8 UTs (since 26 Jan 2020): Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry, Lakshadweep, A&N, DNH and DD, J&K, Ladakh. In 2010 the answer was 7 (printed key); 9 was true only from 31 Oct 2019 to 26 Jan 2020, and 5 and 11 were never right.

about 73 revenue divisions when asked — now 74 (Wikipedia list of revenue divisions in Telangana)
Telangana had about 73 revenue divisions in 33 districts when this was asked (c. 2020); 13, 128 and 33 are wrong (33 is the district count). Now 74.

items.x: Ralegan Siddhi in Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra (Anna Hazare), overcame its water crisis with check dams, tanks and watershed work; Hiware Bazar is a similar model.

items.x: Tors are the rounded granite boulders left standing when granite is weathered and eroded along its joints, a common sight in Andhra Pradesh. Fossils, crystals and particles are not landforms.

items.x: U3O8 is about 84.8% uranium by mass (714/842), so 1.22 lakh t of oxide ≈ 1.04 lakh t of uranium metal.

items.x: Macaroni (durum) wheat is grown in the black-soil areas of central India – Maharashtra, MP, Karnataka – not Punjab, Haryana or UP.

items.s: Which of the following is not the man-made disaster?
items.x: Mud slides are a natural (geological) hazard. Food poisoning and deforestation come from human action, and epidemics are spread by human contact, so mud slides is the one not man-made.

items.s: Which of the following Indian states is vulnerable to Tsunamis?
items.x: Andhra Pradesh, with a long east coast facing the Bay of Bengal, is tsunami-prone (2004 tsunami); the others are landlocked.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &

items.x: The Yukon Plateau (Yukon–Tanana upland) lies between the Brooks Range to the north and the Alaska Range to the south; the Great Basin is in Nevada–Utah, between the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada.

items.x: The reorganised West Godavari district (HQ Bhimavaram, 2022) lost its agency mandals to Eluru and has the lowest ST share of the options.

items.x: Sir Edwin Lutyens was the chief architect of New Delhi; Chandigarh was the work of Le Corbusier (official key: Chandigarh).

items.s: Consider the following statements : Statement-I The soil in tropical rain forests is rich in nutrients. Statement-II The high temperature and moisture of tropical rain forests cause dead organic matter in the soil to decompose quickly. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
items.x: Rain-forest soils are poor in nutrients: heavy rain leaches them and the dense vegetation takes them up at once, so Statement-I is false. Statement-II is true: heat and moisture make dead organic matter decompose quickly.

items.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Currently three waterways have been declared as the National Waterways of India.

II. The Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of river Brahmaputra is the longest National Waterway.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x:
only 3 NWs in 2008 — now 111 NWs under the National Waterways Act 2016, so today neither statement is correct (PMF Human & Economic Geography 02 p31)
In 2008 (before NW-4 and NW-5 were declared at the end of 2008) only three National Waterways existed, so statement I was correct; statement II is wrong because NW-1 Allahabad-Haldia (1,620 km) is longer than NW-2 Sadiya-Dhubri (891 km). (Now 111 NWs, so statement I is no longer true.)

items.s: Which state of the USA is also known as the ‘Blue Grass State’?
items.x: Kentucky is the 'Bluegrass State'; California is the Golden State, Montana the Treasure State, Texas the Lone Star State.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office

items.at: Polavaram district (East Godavari when asked, before the 2022 and 2025 reorganisations)
items.x:
East Godavari lost its agency mandals in the April 2022 reorganisation (to Alluri Sitharama Raju) and the Rampachodavaram–Chinturu area became Polavaram district on 31 Dec 2025 — now Polavaram district (en.wikipedia.org, Polavaram district)
Polavaram district (Rampachodavaram HQ; its Chinturu division faces Sukma in Chhattisgarh) now touches Chhattisgarh. When asked the answer was East Godavari; from April 2022 it was Alluri Sitharama Raju, until Polavaram district was carved out on 31 December 2025 (now Polavaram).
